[P2453|Normal] 
[P2454|Heading 1] Preface
[P2455|Heading 2] Declaration
[P2456|Normal] This document updates at irregular intervals because of product upgrade or other reason.
[P2457|Normal] This document is for your reference only.
[P2458|Heading 2] Audience
[P2459|Normal] This document is for the following audiences:
[P2460|Item List] System maintenance engineers
[P2461|Item List] Debugging and testing engineers
[P2462|Item List] Network monitoring engineers
[P2463|Item List] Field maintenance engineers
[P2464|Heading 2] Conventions
[P2465|Table Description] Command syntax convention table

[TABLE 1] rows=9 cols=2
R1	Syntax	Description
R2	Italic type with capital letters	Use italic type with capital letters for the parameters of the commands. Parameters are the parts which need to replace with the actual value.
R3	(x\|y\|…)	Select one among the choices.
R4	(x\|y\|…\|)	Select one or none among the choices.
R5	[x\|y\|…]	Select one or more among the choices. The choices can be selected repeatedly.
R6	[x\|y\|…\|]	Select one or more or none among the choices. The choices can be selected repeatedly.
R7	{x\|y\|…}	Select one or more among the choices. The choices can be selected only once.
R8	{x\|y\|…\|}	Select one or more or none among the choices. The choices can be selected only once.
R9	<x-y>	Select a number between x and y.

[P2466|Heading 1] Basic Commands
[P2467|Heading 2] System Configuration Commands
[P2468|Heading 3] hostname
[P2469|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P2470|Normal] To specify or modify the host name for the network server, use the “hostname” command in Global Configuration.
[P2471|Heading 5] To restore the configuration to the default, use the “no hostname” command.
[P2472|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P2473|Normal] hostname NAME
[P2474|Body Text] no hostname

[TABLE 2] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	NAME	New host name for the network server	Host name is a string with 1-63 characters

[P2475|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P2476|Normal] Global Configuration
[P2477|Heading 4] Default
[P2478|Normal] The default host name is Switch.
[P2479|Heading 4] Usage
[P2480|Normal] The host name is used in prompts and default configuration filenames.
[P2481|Body Text] The name must also follow the rules for ARPANET host names. They have as interior characters only letters, digits, hyphens, and underline. Names must be 64 characters or fewer.
[P2482|Heading 4] Examples
[P2483|Normal] The following example changes the host name to “sandbox”:
[P2484|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# hostname sandbox
sandbox(config)#
[P2485|Normal] The following example unsets the configured hostname:
[P2486|Terminal Display] sandbox# configure terminal 
sandbox(config)# no hostname 
Switch(config)#
[P2487|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P2488|Normal] None
[P2489|Heading 3] management ip address
[P2490|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P2491|Normal] Use this command to set the management IP address on the Switch.
[P2492|Body Text] To remove the management IP address, use the no form of this command.
[P2493|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P2494|Normal] management ip address ( A.B.C.D/M | A.B.C.D mask ) ( gateway A.B.C.D | )
[P2495|Body Text] no management ip address
[P2496|Body Text] management ipv6 address ( X:X::X:X/M | X:X::X:X mask ) ( gateway X:X::X:X | )
[P2497|Body Text] no management ipv6address

[TABLE 3] rows=7 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	A.B.C.D/M	The management IPv4 address with mask length configured	IPv4 address with mask length 1-32
R3	A.B.C.D mask	The management IPv4 address and mask configured	IPv4 address and mask
R4	X:X::X:X/M	The management IPv6 address with mask length configured	IPv4 address with mask length 1-128
R5	X:X::X:X mask	The management IPv6 address and mask configured	IPv6 address and mask
R6	gateway A.B.C.D	Add IPv4 gateway	IPv4 address
R7	gateway X:X::X:X	Add IPv6 gateway	IPv6 address

[P2498|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P2499|Normal] Global Configuration
[P2500|Heading 4] Default
[P2501|Normal] None
[P2502|Heading 4] Usage
[P2503|Normal] None
[P2504|Heading 4] Examples
[P2505|Normal] The following example sets the management ipv4 address:
[P2506|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal

[P2616|Heading 3] terminal length
[P2617|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P2618|Normal] To set the number of lines on the current terminal screen for the current session, use the terminal length command in EXEC mode. To restore the configuration to the default, use the no form of this command.
[P2619|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P2620|Normal] terminal length LENGTH
[P2621|Body Text] terminal no length

[TABLE 6] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	LENGTH	Number of lines on the screen	The value is a number from 0 to 512. A value of zero disables pausing between screens of output

[P2622|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P2623|Normal] Privileged EXEC
[P2624|Heading 4] Default
[P2625|Normal] Automatically detected by terminal screen length by default
[P2626|Heading 4] Usage
[P2627|Normal] The system uses the length value to determine when to pause during multiple-screen output. A value of zero prevents the switch from pausing between screens of output.
[P2628|Body Text] Some types of terminal sessions do not require you to specify the screen length because the screen length specified can be learned by some remote hosts. For example, the rlogin protocol uses the screen length to set up terminal parameters on a remote UNIX host.
[P2629|Heading 4] Examples
[P2630|Normal] In the following example, the system is configured to prevent output from pausing if it exceeds the length of the screen:
[P2631|Terminal Display] Switch# terminal length 0
[P2632|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P2633|Normal] service terminal-length
[P2634|Heading 3] service terminal-length
[P2635|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P2636|Normal] To set the number of lines on the current terminal screen for all sessions, use the service terminal-length command in Global Configuration. To restore the configuration to the default, use the no form of this command.
[P2637|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P2638|Normal] service terminal-length LENGTH
[P2639|Body Text] no service terminal-length

[TABLE 7] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	LENGTH	Number of lines on the screen	The value is a number from 0 to 512. A value of zero disables pausing between screens of output

[P2640|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P2641|Normal] Global Configuration
[P2642|Heading 4] Default
[P2643|Normal] None
[P2644|Heading 4] Usage
[P2645|Normal] The system uses the length value to determine when to pause during multiple-screen output. A value of zero prevents the switch from pausing between screens of output.
[P2646|Body Text] Some types of terminal sessions do not require you to specify the screen length because the screen length specified can be learned by some remote hosts. For example, the rlogin protocol uses the screen length to set up terminal parameters on a remote UNIX host.
[P2647|Heading 4] Examples
[P2648|Normal] In the following example, the system is configured to prevent output from pausing if it exceeds the length of the screen:
[P2649|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# service terminal-length 0

[P2954|Heading 3] show processes cpu sorted
[P2955|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P2956|Normal] To display CPU utilization information about the active processes sorted by percentage in a device, use the show processes cpu sorted command in Privileged EXEC mode.The first line displays the CPU usage in 5 seconds/interrupted CPU usage in 5 seconds, CPU usage in 1 minute, and CPU usage in 5 minutes. The meanings of the fields in the second row are as follows:
[P2957|Body Text] PID: the process ID
[P2958|Body Text] Runtime(ms) : the time taken by a process from startup to execution
[P2959|Body Text] 5Sec: the CPU usage of the process within five seconds
[P2960|Body Text] 1 minute: the CPU usage of a process in one minute
[P2961|Body Text] 5 minutes: the CPU usage of a process within five minutes
[P2962|Body Text] Process: the process name
[P2963|Body Text] Note: It takes about 10 seconds after the system starts to collect running information about all processes. Therefore, process information isn’t displayed except the first line within 10 seconds after the system starts
[P2964|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P2965|Normal] show process cpu sorted
[P2966|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P2967|Normal] Privileged EXEC
[P2968|Heading 4] Default
[P2969|Normal] None

[P3026|Heading 3] configure terminal
[P3027|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P3028|Normal] To enter Global Configuration, use configure terminal command in Privileged EXEC mode.
[P3029|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P3030|Normal] configure terminal
[P3031|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P3032|Normal] Privileged EXEC
[P3033|Heading 4] Default
[P3034|Normal] None
[P3035|Heading 4] Usage
[P3036|Normal] Use this command to enter Global Configuration. Note that commands in this mode are written to the running configuration file as soon as you enter them (using the Enter key/Carriage Return).
[P3037|Body Text] After you enter the configure command, the system prompt changes from # to (config)#, indicating that the switch is in Global Configuration. To leave Global Configuration and return to Privileged EXEC mode, type end or press Ctrl-Z.
[P3038|Heading 4] Examples
[P3039|Normal] In the following example, the user enters Global Configuration:
[P3040|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)#
Enter configuration commands， one per line. End with CNTL/Z.
Switch(config)#
[P3041|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P3042|Normal] enable
[P3043|Body Text] disable
[P3044|Heading 3] disable
[P3045|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P3046|Normal] To exit Privileged EXEC mode and return to user EXEC mode, enter the disable command in EXEC mode.
[P3047|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P3048|Normal] disable
[P3049|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P3050|Normal] Privileged EXEC
[P3051|Heading 4] Default
[P3052|Normal] None
[P3053|Heading 4] Usage
[P3054|Normal] None
[P3055|Heading 4] Examples
[P3056|Normal] In the following example, the user enters Privileged EXEC mode using the enable command, then exits back to user EXEC mode using the disable command. Note that the prompt for user EXEC mode is >, and the prompt for Privileged EXEC mode is #:
[P3057|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch> enable
Password: <password>
Switch# disable
Switch>
[P3058|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P3059|Normal] enable
[P3060|Heading 3] enable
[P3061|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P3062|Normal] To enter Privileged EXEC mod, use the enable command in user EXEC or Privileged EXEC mode.
[P3063|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P3064|Normal] enable
[P3065|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P3066|Normal] User EXEC
[P3067|Body Text] Privileged EXEC
[P3068|Heading 4] Default
[P3069|Normal] None
[P3070|Heading 4] Usage
[P3071|Normal] None
[P3072|Heading 4] Examples
[P3073|Normal] In the following example, the user enters Privileged EXEC mode using the enable command. The system prompts the user for a password before allowing access to the Privileged EXEC mode. The password is not printed to the screen. The user then exits back to user EXEC mode using the disable command. Note that the prompt for user EXEC mode is the greater than symbol (>), and the prompt for Privileged EXEC mode is the number sign (#).:
[P3074|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch> enable
Password: <password>
Switch# disable
Switch>
[P3075|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P3076|Normal] disable
[P3077|Heading 3] end
[P3078|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P3079|Normal] To end the current configuration session and return to Privileged EXEC mode, use the end command in Global Configuration.
[P3080|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P3081|Normal] end
[P3082|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P3083|Normal] Global Configuration
[P3084|Heading 4] Default
[P3085|Normal] None
[P3086|Heading 4] Usage
[P3087|Normal] This command will bring you back to Privileged EXEC mode regardless of what configuration mode or configuration sub-mode you are in.
[P3088|Body Text] This global configuration command can be used in any configuration mode.
[P3089|Body Text] Use this command when you are done configuring the system and you want to return to EXEC mode to perform verification steps.
[P3090|Heading 4] Examples
[P3091|Normal] In the following example, the end command is used to exit from interface configuration mode and return to Privileged EXEC mode. A show command is used in Privileged EXEC mode to verify the configuration:
[P3092|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# end
Switch# show interface eth-0-1
[P3093|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P3094|Normal] exit
[P3095|Heading 3] exit (global)
[P3096|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P3097|Normal] To exit any configuration mode to the lower mode in the CLI mode hierarchy, use the exit command in any configuration mode.
[P3098|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P3099|Normal] exit
[P3100|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P3101|Normal] All Configuration Mode
[P3102|Heading 4] Default
[P3103|Normal] None
[P3104|Heading 4] Usage
[P3105|Normal] The exit command is used in the CLI to exit from the current command mode to the lower mode in the CLI mode hierarchy.
[P3106|Body Text] For example, use the exit command in Global Configuration to return to Privileged EXEC mode. Use the exit command in interface, line, or router configuration mode to return to Global Configuration.
[P3107|Heading 4] Examples
[P3108|Normal] The following example displays an exit from the interface configuration mode to return to the Global Configuration:
[P3109|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config-if)# exit
Switch(config)#

[P3113|Heading 3] exit (EXEC)
[P3114|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P3115|Normal] To close an active terminal session by logging off the switch, use the exit command in EXEC mode.
[P3116|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P3117|Normal] exit
[P3118|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P3119|Normal] Privileged EXEC
[P3120|Heading 4] Default
[P3121|Normal] None
[P3122|Heading 4] Usage
[P3123|Normal] Use the exit command in EXEC mode to exit the active session (log off the device). This command can be used in any EXEC mode (such as User EXEC mode or Privileged EXEC mode) to exit from the EXEC process.
[P3124|Heading 4] Examples
[P3125|Normal] In the following example, the exit (global) command is used to move from Global Configuration to Privileged EXEC mode, the disable command is used to move from Privileged EXEC mode to user EXEC mode, and the exit (EXEC) command is used to log off (exit the active session):
[P3126|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# exit
Switch# disable
Switch> exit

[P3134|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P3135|Normal] All Configuration Mode
[P3136|Heading 4] Default
[P3137|Normal] None
[P3138|Heading 4] Usage
[P3139|Normal] Use the quit command in EXEC mode to exit the active session (log off the device). This command can be used in any EXEC mode (such as User EXEC mode or Privileged EXEC mode) to exit from the EXEC process.
[P3140|Heading 4] Examples
[P3141|Normal] In the following example, the quit command is used to move from Global Configuration to Privileged EXEC mode, the disable command is used to move from Privileged EXEC mode to user EXEC mode, and the quit command is used to log off (exit the active session):
[P3142|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# quit
Switch# disable
Switch> quit
[P3143|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P3144|Normal] exit
[P3145|Heading 3] cd
[P3146|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P3147|Normal] Change the current directory to dir, use the cd command in EXEC mode.
[P3148|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P3149|Normal] cd ( dir | )

[TABLE 23] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	dir	(Optional) The directory or file systems followed by a colon. If flash: argument is specified, change the current directory to flash: . If udisk: argument is specified, change the current directory to udisk:. If you don’t use USB device, failed to cd udisk	-

[P3150|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P3151|Normal] Privileged EXEC
[P3152|Heading 4] Default
[P3153|Normal] The initial default file system is flash:. If you do not specify a directory on a file system, the default is the root directory on that file system.
[P3154|Heading 4] Usage
[P3155|Normal] For all EXEC commands that have an optional file system argument, the system uses the file system specified by the cd command when you omit the optional file system argument. For example, the dir EXEC command, which displays a list of files on a file system, contain an optional file system argument. When you omit this argument, the system lists the files on the file system specified by the cd command.
[P3156|Heading 4] Examples
[P3157|Normal] In the following example, the cd command is used to set the default file system to the Flash memory.:
[P3158|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
DUT1# cd
DUT1# pwd
flash:/
[P3159|Normal] In the following example, the cd command is used to set the default file system to the USB device:
[P3160|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
storage device
DUT1# cd udisk:
DUT1# pwd
udisk:/
[P3161|Normal] In the following example, the cd command is used to set the file system without plug in the USB mass storage device:
[P3162|Terminal Display] Switch# cd udisk:
% Failed to cd udisk:: No such file or directory
In the following example, the cd command is used to set the file system with plug in the USB mass storage device

[P3165|Body Text] ls
[P3166|Body Text] pwd

[TABLE 24] rows=3 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	source-name	The location URL of the source file to be copied. The source can be either local or remote	-
R3	destination-name	The destination URL of the copied file. The destination can be either local or remote	-

[P3172|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P3173|Normal] Privileged EXEC
[P3174|Heading 4] Default
[P3175|Normal] None
[P3176|Heading 4] Usage
[P3177|Normal] The exact format of the source and destination URLs varies according to the file or directory location. You may enter a particular file or a filename that follows the standard file system syntax (filesystem:[/filepath][/filename]).
[P3178|Heading 4] Examples
[P3179|Normal] The following example shows how to get image from TFTP server through in band management interface.:
[P3180|Terminal Display] Switch# copy tftp://192.168.0.1/image flash:/boot/image
Download from URL to temporary file.
Get file from tftp://192.168.0.1/image
..............................................................................................................
Received 15591515 bytes in 16.6 seconds
Copy the temporary file to its destination.
..............................................................................................................
15591515 bytes in 69.8 seconds, 218 kbytes/second
[P3181|Normal] The following example shows how to get image from TFTP server through out band management interface:
[P3182|Terminal Display] Switch# copy mgmt-if tftp://192.168.0.1/image flash:/boot/image

[P3902|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P3903|Normal] Global Configuration
[P3904|Heading 4] Default
[P3905|Normal] None
[P3906|Heading 4] Usage
[P3907|Normal] You can use this command to modify the address which FTP server works on, and specify a vrf to provide FTP server. The source address can only be 0.0.0.0 or loopback interface’s address, 0.0.0.0 indicates that the SSH server address is not specified.

[P4511|Heading 2] Time&Timezone Commands
[P4512|Heading 3] clock set datetime
[P4513|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P4514|Normal] Use this command to set system current date and time on the Switch.
[P4515|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P4516|Normal] clock set datetime HH:MM:SS MONTH DAY YEAR

[TABLE 89] rows=5 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	HH:MM:SS	Specify the time in hours (24-hour format), minutes, and seconds. The time specified is relative to the configured time zone	HH:MM:SS in 24-hour format.
R3	MONTH	Specify the month by name	Should be in range 1 to 12
R4	DAY	Specify the day by date in the month	Should be in range 1 to 31
R5	YEAR	Specify the year	Should be in range 1993 to 2035

[P4517|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P4518|Normal] Global Configuration
[P4519|Heading 4] Default
[P4520|Normal] The default time is based from UTC.
[P4521|Heading 4] Usage
[P4522|Normal] If no other source of time is available, you can manually configure the time and date after the system is restarted. The time remains accurate until the next system restart. We recommend that you use manual configuration only as a last resort. If you have an outside source to which the switch can synchronize, you do not need to manually set the system clock.
[P4523|Heading 4] Examples
[P4524|Normal] This example shows how to manually set the system clock to 1：32 p.m. on July 23, 2014:
[P4525|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# clock set 13:32:00 23 7 2014
[P4526|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P4527|Normal] show clock
[P4528|Heading 3] clock set timezone
[P4529|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P4530|Normal] Use this command to set the time zone on the Switch.
[P4531|Body Text] To restore to the default time of UTC, use the no form of this command.
[P4532|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P4533|Normal] clock set timezone ZONE ( add | minus ) hours-offset [ minutes-offset ] [ seconds-offset ]
[P4534|Body Text] no clock set timezone

[TABLE 90] rows=7 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	ZONE	Specify the zone name	the length should be [3, 32), and only [a-zA-Z_] is supported, and the first and last character must be alphabet.
R3	add	Specify the time offset is positive from UTC	-
R4	minus	Specify the time offset is negative from UTC	-
R5	HOUR_OFFSET	Specify the time offset in hours	0-18
R6	MINUTES_OFFSET	[optional]Specify the time offset in minutes, should be in range 0 to 59	0-59
R7	SECCONDS_OFFSET	[optional]Specify the time offset in seconds	0-59

[P4535|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P4536|Normal] Global Configuration
[P4537|Heading 4] Default

[P4539|Heading 4] Usage
[P4540|Normal] None
[P4541|Heading 4] Examples
[P4542|Normal] The following example sets the Atlantic Canada time zone is 3.5 hours less than UTC:
[P4543|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# clock set timezone Canada minus 3 30
[P4544|Normal] The following example sets the time zone named ZZZ is 5 hours faster than UTC:
[P4545|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# clock set timezone ZZZ add 5
[P4546|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P4547|Normal] show clock (detail)
[P4548|Heading 3] clock set summer-time
[P4549|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P4550|Normal] Use this command to set summer time (daylight saving time) in areas where it starts and ends on a particular day each year(recurring) or on specified year(date).
[P4551|Body Text] To restore to the default time of UTC, use the no form of this command.
[P4552|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P4553|Normal] clock set summer-time ZONE recurring start-time end-time offset
[P4554|Body Text] clock set summer-time ZONE date start-time end-time offset
[P4555|Body Text] no clock set summer-time

[TABLE 91] rows=7 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	ZONE	Specify the summer zone name	The length should be [3, 32), and only [a-zA-Z_] is supported, and the first and last character must be alphabet.
R3	recurring	Specify that summer time starts and ends on a particular day of the week each year	-
R4	date	Specify that summer time starts and ends on a particular day of the specified year	-
R5	START_TIME	Specify the start time of summer time	For recurring summer time, the format should be month, day, hh:mm:ss or (first \| second \| third \| fourth \| last) DAY <1-12> HH:MM:SS, while for date summer time, the format should be month, day, year, hh:mm:ss
R6	END_TIME	Specify the end time of summer time	For recurring summer time, the format should be month, day, hh:mm:ss or (first \| second \| third \| fourth \| last) DAY <1-12> HH:MM:SS, while for date summer time, the format should be month, day, year, hh:mm:ss
R7	OFFSET	For offset, specify the number of minutes to add during summer time. The default is 60.	1-120 minutes

[P4556|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P4557|Normal] Global Configuration
[P4558|Heading 4] Default
[P4559|Normal] Summer time should be disabled by default.
[P4560|Heading 4] Usage
[P4561|Normal] The first part of the clock summer-time global configuration command specifies when summer time begins, and the second part specifies when it ends. All times are relative to the local time zone. The start time is relative to standard time. The end time is relative to summer time. If the starting month is after the ending month, the system assumes that you are in the southern hemisphere.
[P4562|Heading 4] Examples
[P4563|Normal] This example shows how to specify that summer time starts on june 1st at 0200 and ends on the October 31 at 0200:
[P4564|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# clock set summer-time stime recurring 6 1 02:00:00 10 31 02:00:00 120
[P4565|Normal] This example shows how to specify that summer time starts on March the second Wednesday at 0200 and ends on the August the last Friday at 0100:
[P4566|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# clock set summer-time stime recurring second Wed 3 02:0:0 last Fri 8 01:0:0 60

[P5008|Heading 3] duplex
[P5009|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P5010|Normal] Use the duplex interface configuration command to specify the duplex mode of operation for a port. Use the no form of this command to return the port to its default value.
[P5011|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P5012|Normal] duplex ( auto | full | half )
[P5013|Body Text] no duplex

[TABLE 113] rows=4 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	auto	Enable automatic duplex configuration; port automatically detects whether it should run in full-duplex or half-duplex mode, depending on the attached device mode	-
R3	full	Enable full-duplex mode	-
R4	half	Enable half-duplex mode (only for interfaces operating at 10 or 100 Mb/s). You can not configure half-duplex mode for interfaces operating at 1000 or10,000 Mb/s	-

[P5014|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P5015|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P5016|Heading 4] Default
[P5017|Normal] auto
[P5018|Heading 4] Usage
[P5019|Normal] The command is not allowed to be set on 10G port or optical mode of combo port.
[P5020|Heading 4] Examples
[P5021|Normal] The following example sets the duplex mode to auto:
[P5022|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# duplex auto
[P5023|Normal] The following example sets the duplex mode to full:
[P5024|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# duplex full
[P5025|Normal] The following example returns the duplex mode to default:
[P5026|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# no duplex

[P5719|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P5720|Normal] Global Configuration
[P5721|Heading 4] Default
[P5722|Normal] Disabled
[P5723|Heading 4] Usage
[P5724|Normal] The change of reason will not affect those interfaces have already enter errdisable state.

[P5726|Normal] This example shows how to enable link flap errdisable recovery:
[P5727|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# errdisable recovery reason link-flap
[P5728|Normal] This example shows how to disable link flap errdisable recovery:
[P5729|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal

[P5732|Body Text] show errdisable recovery
[P5733|Heading 3] errdisable flap
[P5734|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P5735|Normal] Use this command to set the parameters for link-flap error disable. Use the no form of this command to restore to default value.
[P5736|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P5737|Normal] errdisable flap reason link-flap COUNT SECONDS
[P5738|Body Text] no errdisable flap reason link-flap COUNT SECONDS

[TABLE 143] rows=4 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	link-flap	Configure link flap conditions	-
R3	COUNT	Max flap count	1-100, unit:times
R4	SECONDS	Flap count time in seconds	1-120, unit:second

[P5739|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P5740|Normal] Global Configuration
[P5741|Heading 4] Default
[P5742|Normal] count : 10, seconds :10
[P5743|Heading 4] Usage
[P5744|Normal] Only the link flap can be detected. <1-100> is the threshold of flap count, and <1-120> is the count time in seconds for flap count. If the errdisable detect link flap is enabled, will result in link flap errdisable, otherwise, will only print a message in log.
[P5745|Heading 4] Examples
[P5746|Normal] This example shows how to set link flap conditions to 20 times in 60 seconds:
[P5747|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# errdisable flap reason link-flap 20 60
[P5748|Normal] This example shows how to disable link flap conditions to default:
[P5749|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# no errdisable flap reason link-flap

[P5837|Heading 2] MAC Address Table Commands
[P5838|Heading 3] mac-address-table aging-time
[P5839|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P5840|Normal] Use the mac-address-table aging-time global configuration command on the switch to set the length of time that a dynamic entry remains in the MAC address table after the entry is used or updated. Use the no form of this command to return to the default setting. The aging time applies to all VLANs.
[P5841|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P5842|Normal] mac_address-table aging-time SECONDS
[P5843|Body Text] no mac_address-table aging-time

[TABLE 144] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	SECONDS	Aging time.	0，10-1000000, 0 means that MAC aging function does not work， unit:second

[P5844|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P5845|Normal] Global Configuration
[P5846|Heading 4] Default
[P5847|Normal] The default is 300 seconds
[P5848|Heading 4] Usage
[P5849|Normal] If packets are not received continuously, user can increase the aging time to make the system recording the dynamic entries for a longer time. Increasing the time can reduce the possibility of flooding when the hosts send again.
[P5850|Heading 4] Examples
[P5851|Normal] This example shows how to set the aging time to 200 seconds for all VLANs:
[P5852|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# mac-address-table aging-time 200
[P5853|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P5854|Normal] show mac address-table aging-time
[P5855|Heading 3] mac-address-table hardware-learning

[P5858|Heading 4] Command Syntax

[P5860|Body Text] no mac_address-table hardware-learning enable
[P5861|Heading 4] Command Mode

[P5864|Normal] Disable
[P5865|Heading 4] Usage

[P5867|Heading 4] Examples
[P5868|Normal] This example shows how to enable hardware learning:
[P5869|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# mac-address-table hardware-learning enable

[P5872|Heading 3] mac-address-table forward
[P5873|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P5874|Normal] Use the mac-address-table forward global configuration command on the switch to add static addresses to the MAC address table. Use the no form of this command to remove static entries from the table.
[P5875|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P5876|Normal] mac_address-table MAC_ADDR forward ( IFNAME | eps EPS_ID | remote-vtep REMOTE_VTEP_ID | smart-link SMART_LINK_ID ) vlan VLAN_ID
[P5877|Body Text] no mac_address-table MAC_ADDR forward ( IFNAME | eps EPS_ID | remote-vtep REMOTE_VTEP_ID | smart-link SMART_LINK_ID ) vlan VLAN_ID

[TABLE 145] rows=7 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	MAC_ADDR	Destination MAC address (unicast or multicast) to add to the address table. Packets with this destination address received in the specified VLAN are forwarded to the specified interface	Mac address in HHHH.HHHH.HHHH format
R3	IFNAME	Interface to which the received packet is forwarded.	Valid interfaces include physical ports and link aggregation ports
R4	VLAN_ID	Specify the VLAN for which the packet with the specified MAC address is received.	1-4094
R5	EPS_ID	EPS protection group.	1-2048
R6	REMOTE_VTEP_ID	Remote VTEP	1-65535
R7	SMART_LINK_ID	Smart-Link Group	1-16

[P5878|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P5879|Normal] Global Configuration
[P5880|Heading 4] Default
[P5881|Normal] None
[P5882|Heading 4] Usage
[P5883|Normal] The static address entries which are added by this command are not aged.
[P5884|Heading 4] Examples
[P5885|Normal] This example shows how to add the static address c2f3220a12f4 to the MAC address table When a packet is received in VLAN 4 with this MAC address as its destination, the packet is forwarded to the specified interface:
[P5886|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# mac-address-table c2f3.220a.12f4 forward eth-0-1 vlan 4

[P5898|Normal] None

[P5900|Normal] Follow these guidelines when using this feature:

[P6100|Heading 2] VLAN Commands
[P6101|Heading 3] vlan database
[P6102|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P6103|Normal] Use this command to enter VLAN configure mode.
[P6104|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P6105|Normal] vlan database
[P6106|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P6107|Normal] Global Configuration
[P6108|Heading 4] Default
[P6109|Normal] None
[P6110|Heading 4] Usage
[P6111|Normal] When you try to create or remove VLAN, you must use this command to enter VLAN configure mode first. To exit VLAN configure mode, use exit command.
[P6112|Heading 4] Examples
[P6113|Normal] This example shows how to enter VLAN configure mode:
[P6114|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# vlan database
Switch(config-vlan)# 
[P6115|Normal] This example shows how to exit VLAN configure mode:
[P6116|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# vlan database
Switch(config-vlan)# exit
Switch(config)# 
[P6117|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P6118|Normal] exit
[P6119|Heading 3] vlan
[P6120|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P6121|Normal] Use the vlan VLAN configuration command to configure VLAN characteristics for a VLAN in the VLAN database. Use the no form of this command to delete a VLAN.
[P6122|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P6123|Normal] vlan VLAN_ID ( name NAME | ) ( state ( enable | disable ) | )
[P6124|Body Text] no vlan VLAN_ID

[TABLE 151] rows=5 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	VLAN_ID	Vlan id	1-4094
R3	NAME	the name for specific vlan,	A string with no more than 128 characters
R4	enable	set the operational state of the VLAN to enable, and it is enabled by default	-
R5	disable	set the operational state of the VLAN to disable	-

[P6125|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P6126|Normal] VLAN Configuration
[P6127|Heading 4] Default
[P6128|Normal] VLAN 1 is the default VLAN and all ports have been added to it by default.
[P6129|Heading 4] Usage
[P6130|Normal] Default VLAN 1 can not be removed.
[P6131|Heading 4] Examples
[P6132|Normal] This example shows how to create VLAN 11 and named it to “vlan11”:
[P6133|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# vlan database
Switch(config-vlan)# vlan 11 name vlan11 state enable
[P6134|Normal] This example shows how to remove VLAN 11:
[P6135|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# vlan database
Switch(config-vlan)# no vlan 11
[P6136|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P6137|Normal] vlan VLAN_LIST
[P6138|Body Text] show vlan vlan
[P6139|Body Text] show vlan all
[P6140|Heading 3] vlan VLAN_LIST
[P6141|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P6142|Normal] Use the vlan VLAN_LIST configuration command to add a normal-range VLANs to the VLAN database.
[P6143|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P6144|Normal] vlan VLAN_LIST
[P6145|Body Text] no vlan VLAN_LIST

[P6146|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P6147|Normal] VLAN Configuration
[P6148|Heading 4] Default
[P6149|Normal] Vlan 1 is the default vlan and all ports have been added to it by default.
[P6150|Heading 4] Usage
[P6151|Normal] The vlan list should be connected with ‘-’ and ‘,’, the value should be in the range of <1-4094> and should be ascending order.
[P6152|Body Text] Default VLAN 1 can not be removed.
[P6153|Heading 4] Examples
[P6154|Normal] This example shows how to add vlans of “100,200,300-400”:
[P6155|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# vlan database
Switch(config-vlan)# vlan 100,200,300-400
[P6156|Normal] This example shows how to remove vlans of “100,200,300-400”:
[P6157|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# vlan database
Switch(config-vlan)# no vlan 100,200,300-400

[P6525|Heading 4] Command Mode

[P6527|Heading 4] Default

[P6531|Body Text] 00d0-1e00-0000 Pingtel phone

[P6533|Body Text] 00e0-bb00-0000 3Com phone

[P6620|Heading 4] Default
[P6621|Normal] 1
[P6622|Heading 4] Usage
[P6623|Normal] Distribute-weight is only supported in non-selfing-healing of static load-balance-mode member port, and the total weights of member ports cannot exceed the maximum number of member ports.

[P7095|Heading 2] VLAN Classification Commands
[P7096|Heading 3] vlan classifier activate
[P7097|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P7098|Normal] Use this command to apply vlan classifier group to an interface.
[P7099|Body Text] To remove it, use the no form of this command.
[P7100|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P7101|Normal] vlan classifier activate GROUP_NUMBER based ( ip | mac | protocol )
[P7102|Body Text] no vlan classifier activate

[TABLE 195] rows=5 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	GROUP_NUMBER	VLAN classifier group id	0-31, only group id 31 can be used for protocol
R3	ip	Based on ip	-
R4	mac	Based on MAC	-
R5	protocol	Based on protocol	-

[P7103|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P7104|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P7105|Heading 4] Default
[P7106|Normal] None
[P7107|Heading 4] Usage
[P7108|Normal] An interface can only be applied by one vlan classifier group.
[P7109|Body Text] One vlan classifier group can apply more than one interface.
[P7110|Body Text] This command applies vlan classifier group to interface, and the interface can classify packets to different vlan according to the rule in vlan classifier group.
[P7111|Body Text] To create the rule, refer to vlan classifier rule command.
[P7112|Body Text] To create the group, refer to vlan classifier group command.
[P7113|Heading 4] Examples
[P7114|Normal] This example shows how to apply vlan classifier group 1 to the interface:
[P7115|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# vlan classifier activate 1 based ip
[P7116|Normal] This example shows how to remove the vlan classifier group 1 from the interface:
[P7117|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# no vlan classifier activate
[P7118|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P7119|Normal] vlan classifier group
[P7120|Body Text] vlan classifier rule
[P7121|Heading 3] vlan classifier group
[P7122|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P7123|Normal] Use this command to add or delete rule to vlan classifier group. Use the no form of this command to delete the group.
[P7124|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P7125|Normal] vlan classifier group GROUP_NUMBER ( add | delete ) rule RULE
[P7126|Body Text] no vlan classifier group group

[TABLE 196] rows=5 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	GROUP_NUMBER	VLAN classifier group id	0-31, only group id 31 can be used for protocol
R3	add	Add rule to vlan classifier group	-
R4	delete	Delete rule to vlan classifier group	-
R5	RULE	The id of rule	0-4095

[P7127|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P7128|Normal] Global Configuration
[P7129|Heading 4] Default
[P7130|Normal] None
[P7131|Heading 4] Usage
[P7132|Normal] To create the rule, refer to vlan classifier rule command.
[P7133|Body Text] To apply the vlan classifier group to an interface, refer to vlan classifier activate command.
[P7134|Body Text] When add a rule to the group by this command, the rule will be active immediately if the group has been applied to an interface already.
[P7135|Body Text] When delete a rule from the group by this command, the rule on this interface will be inactive immediately if the group is still applied to that interface.
[P7136|Body Text] The vlan classifier group will be deleted when the last rule on this group is deleted.
[P7137|Heading 4] Examples
[P7138|Normal] This example shows how to add rule1 to vlan classifier group 1:
[P7139|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# vlan classifier group 1 add rule 1
[P7140|Normal] This example shows how to delete rule1 from vlan classifier group 1:
[P7141|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# vlan classifier group 1 delete rule 1
[P7142|Normal] This example shows how to delete vlan classifier group 1:
[P7143|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# no vlan classifier group 1
[P7144|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P7145|Normal] vlan classifier activate
[P7146|Body Text] vlan classifier rule
[P7147|Heading 3] vlan classifier rule
[P7148|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P7149|Normal] Use this command to create vlan classifier rule.
[P7150|Body Text] To remove the vlan classifier rule, use the no form of this command.
[P7151|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P7152|Normal] vlan classifier rule RULE ( ip IP_ADDR | ip IP_ADDR/PREFIX-LENGTH | ipv6 IPV6_ADDR | mac MAC_ADDR | protocol ( arp | ip | mpls | mpls-mcast | pppoe | rarp ) ) vlan VLAN_ID
[P7153|Body Text] no vlan classifier rule RULE

[TABLE 197] rows=14 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	RULE	The id of vlan classifier rule	0-4095
R3	IP_ADDR	The source of ipv4 address in packets	IPv4 address
R4	PREFIX-LENGTH	Prefix length for the ip address.	1-32
R5	IPV6_ADDR	The source of ipv6 address in packets	IPv6 address
R6	MAC_ADDR	The source of mac address in packets	Mac address in HHHH.HHHH.HHHH format
R7	protocol	Specify an ethernet protocol classification	-
R8	arp	Specifiy ARP protocol	-
R9	ip	Specifiy IP protocol	-
R10	mpls	Specifiy MPLS protocol	-
R11	mpls-mcast	Specifiy MPLS multi cast protocol	-
R12	pppoe	Specifiy PPPOE protocol	-
R13	rarp	Specifiy RARP protocol	-
R14	VLAN_ID	The vlan id to be assigned	1-4094

[P7154|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P7155|Normal] Global Configuration
[P7156|Heading 4] Default
[P7157|Normal] None
[P7158|Heading 4] Usage
[P7159|Normal] The rule will be effective only in inbound on interface.
[P7160|Body Text] The vlan id assigned by vlan classifier rule will be appended to the packets which match the rule.
[P7161|Body Text] To add this rule to vlan classifier group or apply the group to an interface, refer to vlan classifier group and vlan classifier activate command.
[P7162|Heading 4] Examples
[P7163|Normal] This example shows how to create rule1 which will classify all ipv4 packets to vlan11:
[P7164|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# vlan classifier rule 1 protocol ip vlan 11
[P7165|Normal] This example shows how to delete rule1:
[P7166|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# no vlan classifier rule 1
[P7167|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P7168|Normal] vlan classifier group
[P7169|Body Text] vlan classifier activate
[P7170|Heading 3] vlan classifier default-action
[P7171|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P7172|Normal] Use this command to set action when not hit vlan classifier rule. Use the no form of this command to restore default action.
[P7173|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P7174|Normal] vlan classifier default-action drop
[P7175|Body Text] no vlan classifier default-action drop
[P7176|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P7177|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P7178|Heading 4] Default
[P7179|Normal] None
[P7180|Heading 4] Usage
[P7181|Normal] When packet input the port which enable vlan classifier and not hit any vlan classifier rule, the packet will be dropped.
[P7182|Heading 4] Examples
[P7183|Normal] This example shows how to set default action drop:
[P7184|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# vlan classifier default-action drop
[P7185|Normal] This example shows how to set default action not drop:
[P7186|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# no vlan classifier default-action drop

[P7615|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P7616|Normal] show spanning-stree
[P7617|Heading 3] spanning-tree priority
[P7618|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P7619|Normal] Use this command to set the bridge priority for the common instance for the default bridge. Using a lower priority indicates a higher likelihood of the bridge becoming root. Use the no parameter with this command to reset it to the default value.
[P7620|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P7621|Normal] spanning-tree priority PRIORITY
[P7622|Body Text] no spanning-tree priority

[TABLE 215] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	PRIORITY	Bridge priority	0-61440

[P7623|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P7624|Normal] Global Configuration
[P7625|Heading 4] Default
[P7626|Normal] The default priority is 32678 (or hex 0x8000)
[P7627|Heading 4] Usage
[P7628|Normal] This command is used to set the priority of the bridge. The priority values must be in multiples of 4096.
[P7629|Heading 4] Examples
[P7630|Normal] This example shows how to set the bridge priority.:
[P7631|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# spanning-tree priority 4096
[P7632|Normal] This example shows how to reset the bridge priority to default value:
[P7633|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# no spanning-tree priority
[P7634|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P7635|Normal] show spanning-stree
[P7636|Heading 3] spanning-tree instance priority
[P7637|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P7638|Normal] Use this command to set the default bridge priority for an MST instance to the value specified. Use the no parameter with this command to restore the default value of the default bridge priority.
[P7639|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P7640|Normal] spanning-tree instance INSTANCE_ID priority PRIORITY
[P7641|Body Text] no spanning-tree instance INSTANCE_ID priority

[TABLE 216] rows=3 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	INSTANCE_ID	Specify the instance ID	1-4094
R3	PRIORITY	Specify the bridge priority	0-61440

[P7642|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P7643|Normal] Global Configuration
[P7644|Heading 4] Default
[P7645|Normal] The default value of port priority for each instance is 32768.
[P7646|Heading 4] Usage
[P7647|Normal] The lower the priority of the bridge, there is higher likelihood that the bridge becomes a root bridge or a designated bridge for the LAN. The permitted range of values is 0-61440. The priority values must be in multiples of 4096.
[P7648|Heading 4] Examples
[P7649|Normal] This example shows how to set the priority for instance 1:
[P7650|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# spanning-tree instance 1 priority 0
[P7651|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P7652|Normal] show spanning-stree
[P7653|Heading 3] spanning-tree forward-time
[P7654|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P7655|Normal] Use this command to set the time after which (if this bridge is the root bridge) each port in the default bridge changes states to learning and forwarding. This value is used by all instances. Use the no parameter with this command to restore the default value of 15 seconds.
[P7656|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P7657|Normal] spanning-tree forward-time SECONDS
[P7658|Body Text] no spanning-tree forward-time

[TABLE 217] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	SECONDS	Forwarding time delay, in seconds, for the default bridge	2018/4/30

[P7659|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P7660|Normal] Global Configuration
[P7661|Heading 4] Default
[P7662|Normal] The default value is 15 seconds
[P7663|Heading 4] Usage
[P7664|Normal] The allowable range for the forward time is 4-30 seconds. It is not advisable to set the value below 7 seconds.
[P7665|Heading 4] Examples
[P7666|Normal] This example shows how to set the forward time to 16 seconds:
[P7667|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# spanning-tree forward-time 16
[P7668|Normal] This example shows how to reset the forward time to default value:
[P7669|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# no spanning-tree forward-time
[P7670|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P7671|Normal] show spanning-stree
[P7672|Heading 3] spanning-tree hello-time
[P7673|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P7674|Normal] Use this command to set the hello-time, the time in seconds after which (if this bridge is the root bridge) all the default bridges in a bridged LAN exchange Bridge Protocol Data Units (BPDUs). A very low value of this parameter leads to excessive traffic on the network, while a higher value delays the detection of topology change. This value is used by all instances.
[P7675|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P7676|Normal] spanning-tree hello-time SECONDS
[P7677|Body Text] no spanning-tree hello-time

[TABLE 218] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	SECONDS	Hello BPDU interval	1-10, unit:second

[P7678|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P7679|Normal] Global Configuration
[P7680|Heading 4] Default
[P7681|Normal] The default hello-time value is 2
[P7682|Heading 4] Usage
[P7683|Normal] The allowable range of values is 1-10 seconds.
[P7684|Heading 4] Examples
[P7685|Normal] This example shows how to set the hello time to 5 seconds:
[P7686|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# spanning-tree hello-time 5
[P7687|Normal] This example shows how to reset the hello-time to default value:
[P7688|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# no spanning-tree hello-time
[P7689|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P7690|Normal] show spanning-stree
[P7691|Heading 3] spanning-tree max-age
[P7692|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P7693|Normal] Use this command to set the maximum age for the default bridge. Use the no parameter with this command to restore the default value of the maximum age.
[P7694|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P7695|Normal] spanning-tree max-age SECONDS
[P7696|Body Text] no spanning-tree max-age

[TABLE 219] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	SECONDS	The maximum time, in seconds, to listen for the root bridge	6-40

[P7697|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P7698|Normal] Global Configuration
[P7699|Heading 4] Default
[P7700|Normal] The default value of bridge maximum age is 20 seconds.
[P7701|Heading 4] Usage
[P7702|Normal] Maximum age is the maximum time for which (if a bridge is the root bridge) a message is considered valid. This prevents the frames from looping indefinitely. The value of maximum age should be greater than twice the value of hello time plus 1, and less than twice the value of forward delay minus 1. The allowable range for maximum age is 6-40 seconds. Configure this value sufficiently high, so that a frame generated by root can be propagated to the leaf nodes without exceeding the maximum age.
[P7703|Heading 4] Examples
[P7704|Normal] This example shows how to set the max age to 12 seconds:
[P7705|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# spanning-tree max-age 12
[P7706|Normal] This example shows how to reset the max age to default value:
[P7707|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# no spanning-tree max-age
[P7708|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P7709|Normal] show spanning-tree
[P7710|Heading 3] spanning-tree max-hops
[P7711|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P7712|Normal] Use this command to specify the maximum allowed hops for a BPDU in an MST region. This parameter is used by all the instances of the MST. To restore the default value, use the no parameter with this command.
[P7713|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P7714|Normal] spanning-tree max-hops NUMBER
[P7715|Body Text] no spanning-tree max-hops

[TABLE 220] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	NUMBER	Max hops	1-40

[P7716|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P7717|Normal] Global Configuration
[P7718|Heading 4] Default
[P7719|Normal] The default maximum hops in an MST region are 20
[P7720|Heading 4] Usage
[P7721|Normal] Specifying the maximum hops for a BPDU prevents the messages from looping indefinitely in the network. When a bridge receives an MST BPDU that has exceeded the allowed maximum hops, it discards the BPDU packets.
[P7722|Body Text] The configuration should be shown when the bridge is MSTP mode.
[P7723|Heading 4] Examples
[P7724|Normal] This example shows how to set the max hops to 25:
[P7725|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# spanning-tree max-hops 25
[P7726|Normal] This example shows how to reset the max hops to default value:
[P7727|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# no spanning-tree max-hops

[P7741|Normal] None

[P7929|Heading 3] spanning-tree guard root
[P7930|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P7931|Normal] Use this command to enable the Root Guard feature for the port. This feature disables reception of superior BPDUs. Use the no parameter with this command to disable the root guard feature for the port.
[P7932|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P7933|Normal] spanning-tree guard root
[P7934|Body Text] no spanning-tree guard root
[P7935|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P7936|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P7937|Heading 4] Default
[P7938|Normal] Root guard is disabled
[P7939|Heading 4] Usage
[P7940|Normal] The Root Guard feature makes sure that the port on which it is enabled is a designated port. If a port with Root Guard enabled receives a superior BPDU, it goes to a Listening state (for STP) or discarding state (for RSTP and MSTP).
[P7941|Heading 4] Examples
[P7942|Normal] This example shows how to enable the Root Guard feature for the port:
[P7943|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# spanning-tree guard root
[P7944|Normal] This example shows how to disable the Root Guard feature for the port:
[P7945|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# no spanning-tree guard root
[P7946|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P7947|Normal] None
[P7948|Heading 3] spanning-tree guard loop
[P7949|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P7950|Normal] Use this command to enable the loop guard feature for the port. This feature provides additional protection against Layer 2 forwarding loops. Use the no parameter with this command to disable the loop guard feature for the port.
[P7951|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P7952|Normal] spanning-tree guard loop
[P7953|Body Text] no spanning-tree guard loop
[P7954|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P7955|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P7956|Heading 4] Default
[P7957|Normal] Loop guard is disabled
[P7958|Heading 4] Usage
[P7959|Normal] The loop guard feature should be enabled on the non-designated ports. When a port enables loop guard, and BPDUs are not received on a non-designated port after max_age, the port should move into the STP loop-inconsistent blocking state, instead of the listening / learning / forwarding state, and should not pass user traffic.
[P7960|Heading 4] Examples
[P7961|Normal] This example shows how to enable the loop guard on the port:
[P7962|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# spanning-tree guard loop
[P7963|Normal] This example shows how to disable the loop guard on the port:
[P7964|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# no spanning-tree guard loop
[P7965|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P7966|Normal] spanning-tree guard root
[P7967|Heading 3] spanning-tree bpdu-loop
[P7968|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P7969|Normal] Use this command to enable the bpdu loop feature for the port. This feature provides additional protection against BPDU packet forwarding loops. Use the no parameter with this command to disable the loop guard feature for the port.
[P7970|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P7971|Normal] spanning-tree bpdu-loop
[P7972|Body Text] no spanning-tree bpdu-loop
[P7973|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P7974|Normal] Global Configuration
[P7975|Heading 4] Default
[P7976|Normal] BPDU loop is enabled
[P7977|Heading 4] Usage
[P7978|Normal] When bpdu-loop enable, If an interface receives more than three bpdu packets in one second whose MACSA is interface’s MAC, errdisable this interface by bpdu loop reason.
[P7979|Heading 4] Examples
[P7980|Normal] This example shows how to enable the bpdu-loop:
[P7981|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# spanning-tree bpdu-loop
[P7982|Normal] This example shows how to disable the bpdu-loop:
[P7983|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# no spanning-tree bpdu-loop
[P7984|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P7985|Normal] None
[P7986|Heading 3] spanning-tree force-version
[P7987|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P7988|Normal] Use this command to specify the version. A version identifier of less than a value of 2 enforces the spanning tree protocol. Although the command supports an input range of 0-3, for RSTP, the valid range is 0-2. Use the no parameter with this command to set the default protocol version.
[P7989|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P7990|Normal] spanning-tree force-version NUMBER
[P7991|Body Text] no spanning-tree force-version

[TABLE 229] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	NUMBER	Version identifier.	0 - STP, 1- Not supported, 2 - RSTP, 3 - MSTP

[P7992|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P7993|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P7994|Heading 4] Default
[P7995|Normal] STP default 0, RSTP default 2, MSTP default 3
[P7996|Heading 4] Usage
[P7997|Normal] None
[P7998|Heading 4] Examples
[P7999|Normal] This example shows how to specify the version:
[P8000|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# spanning-tree force-version 1
[P8001|Normal] This example shows how to reset the default version:
[P8002|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# no spanning-tree force-version

[P8097|Heading 3] spanning-tree instance port-priority
[P8098|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P8099|Normal] Use this command to set the port priority for a bridge group. Use the no parameter with this command to restore the default priority value.
[P8100|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P8101|Normal] spanning-tree instance INSTANCE_ID port-priority PRIORITY
[P8102|Body Text] no spanning-tree instance INSTANCE_ID port-priority

[TABLE 232] rows=3 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	INSTANCE_ID	Specify the identifier	1-4094
R3	PRIORITY	Specify the port priority (a lower priority indicates greater likelihood of the interface becoming a root). The range is 0~240	0-240

[P8103|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P8104|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P8105|Heading 4] Default
[P8106|Normal] The default priority is 128
[P8107|Heading 4] Usage
[P8108|Normal] The Multiple Spanning Tree Protocol uses port priority as a tiebreaker to determine which port should forward frame for a particular instance on a LAN, or which port should be the root port for an instance. A lower value implies a better priority. In the case of the same priority, the interface index will serve as the tiebreaker, with the lower-numbered interface being preferred over others.
[P8109|Body Text] The permitted range is 0-240. The priority values can only be set in increments of 16.
[P8110|Heading 4] Examples
[P8111|Normal] This example shows how to set the port priority to 112 for instance 3:
[P8112|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# spanning-tree instance 3 port-priority 112
[P8113|Normal] This example shows how to reset the port priority to defaule value for instance 3:
[P8114|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# no spanning-tree instance 3 port-priority
[P8115|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P8116|Normal] None
[P8117|Heading 3] spanning-tree instance path-cost
[P8118|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P8119|Normal] Use this command to set the cost of a path associated with an interface. Use the no parameter with this command to restore the default cost value of the path.
[P8120|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P8121|Normal] spanning-tree instance INSTANCE_ID path-cost COST
[P8122|Body Text] no spanning-tree instance INSTANCE_ID path-cost

[TABLE 233] rows=3 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	INSTANCE_ID	Specify the identifier	1-4094
R3	COST	Specify the cost of path	<1-200000000> for dot1t and <1-65535> for dot1d-1998 (a lower path-cost indicates a greater likelihood of the specified interface becoming a root)

[P8123|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P8124|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P8125|Heading 4] Default
[P8126|Normal] Assuming a 10 Mb/s link speed, the default value is configured as 2,000,000
[P8127|Heading 4] Usage
[P8128|Normal] Before you can use this command to set a path-cost in a VLAN configuration, you must explicitly add an MST instance to a port using the bridge-group instance command (see the example below).
[P8129|Heading 4] Examples
[P8130|Normal] This example shows how to set the cost of a path associated with an interface:
[P8131|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# spanning-tree mst configuration
Switch(config-mst)# instance 3 vlan 3
Switch(config-mst)# exit
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# switchport mode trunk
Switch(config-if)# switchport trunk allowed vlan add 3
Switch(config-if)# spanning-tree instance 3 path-cost 1000
Switch(config-mst)# exit
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# switchport mode access
Switch(config-if)# switchport access vlan 3
Switch(config-if)# spanning-tree instance 3 path-cost 1000

[P8720|Body Text] When forwarding PDUs in L2PT, the destination MAC address of the PDU can be modified instead of adding a layer of encapsulation, using this name to replace the destination multicast MAC address specified in the protocol configuration. [P8747|Heading 3] port storm-control
[P8748|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P8749|Normal] Use the storm-control interface configuration command to enable broadcast, multicast, or unicast storm control and to set threshold levels on an interface. Use the no form of this command to return to the default setting.
[P8750|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P8751|Normal] storm-control ( broadcast | multicast | unicast ) ( level LEVEL | pps PPS )
[P8752|Body Text] no storm-control ( broadcast | multicast | unicast )

[TABLE 259] rows=6 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	broadcast	Enable broadcast storm control on the interface	-
R3	multicast	Enable multicast storm control on the interface	-
R4	unicast	Enable unicast storm control on the interface	-
R5	level LEVEL	Specify the rising and falling suppression levels as a percentage of total bandwidth of the port.	0.00-100.00
R6	pps PPS	Specify the rising and falling suppression levels as a rate in packets per second at which traffic is received on the port.	0-1000000000

[P8838|Heading 2] Loopback Detection Commands
[P8839|Heading 3] loopback-detect enable
[P8840|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P8841|Normal] Using the loopback-detect enable command, you can enable loopback detection on an interface.
[P8842|Body Text] Using the no loopback-detect enable command, you can disable loopback detection on an interface. By default, loopback detection is disabled on an interface.
[P8843|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P8844|Normal] loopback-detect enable
[P8845|Body Text] no loopback-detect enable
[P8846|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P8847|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P8848|Heading 4] Default
[P8849|Normal] Disable
[P8850|Heading 4] Usage
[P8851|Normal] The loopback-detect enable command enables loopback detection on an interface. This function enables the system to detect a loopback on the interface quickly and minimizes impact of the loopback on the entire network. After loopback detection is enabled on an interface, the interface sends loopback detection packets at intervals. Loopback detection occupies CPU resources; therefore, disable this function when it is not required.
[P8852|Heading 4] Examples
[P8853|Normal] This example shows how to enable loopback detect on port eth-0-1:
[P8854|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# loopback-detect enable
[P8855|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P8856|Normal] show loopback-detect
[P8857|Heading 3] loopback-detect packet-interval
[P8858|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P8859|Normal] Using the loopback-detect packet-interval command, you can set the interval for sending loopback detection packets on all interfaces.
[P8860|Body Text] Using the no loopback-detect packet-interval command, you can restore the default interval for sending loopback detection packets on all interfaces.
[P8861|Body Text] By default, the interval for sending loopback detection packets is 5s
[P8862|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P8863|Normal] loopback-detect packet-interval INTERVAL
[P8864|Body Text] no loopback-detect packet-interval

[TABLE 262] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	INTERVAL	loopback detect packet send interval	1-300, unit:second

[P8865|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P8866|Normal] Global Configuration
[P8867|Heading 4] Default
[P8868|Normal] 5 seconds
[P8869|Heading 4] Usage
[P8870|Normal] The loopback-detect packet-interval command is used to adjust the interval for sending loopback detection packets. After loopback detection is enabled on an interface, the interface sends loopback detection packets at the interval specified by the loopback-detect packet-interval command. If a shorter interval is set, the system sends more loopback detection packets in a certain period. This enables the system to detect loopbacks more quickly and accurately, but more system sources are consumed.
[P8871|Heading 4] Examples
[P8872|Normal] This example shows how to set the interval for sending loopback detection packets to 10s:
[P8873|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# loopback-detect packet-interval 10
[P8874|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P8875|Normal] show loopback-detect
[P8876|Heading 3] loopback-detect recovery-time
[P8877|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P8878|Normal] Using the loopback-detect recovery-time command, you can set the time for interface recovery from abnormal status.
[P8879|Body Text] Using the no loopback-detect recovery-time command, you can restore the default time.
[P8880|Body Text] By default, the value for recovery time is the packet-interval * 3
[P8881|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P8882|Normal] loopback-detect recovery-time TIME
[P8883|Body Text] no loopback-detect recovery-time

[TABLE 263] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	TIME	recovery time in seconds	1-255, unit:second

[P8884|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P8885|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P8886|Heading 4] Default
[P8887|Normal] recovery-time is packet-interval * 3
[P8888|Heading 4] Usage
[P8889|Normal] If the interface is shutdown, this command is useless.
[P8890|Heading 4] Examples
[P8891|Normal] This example shows how to set the value for recoverying time to 10s:
[P8892|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# loopback-detect recovery-time 10
[P8893|Heading 4] Related Commands

[P8901|Body Text] no loopback-detect delay-time

[TABLE 264] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	TIME	delay time	1-255, unit:second

[P8902|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P8903|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P8904|Heading 4] Default
[P8905|Normal] None
[P8906|Heading 4] Usage
[P8907|Normal] The no loopback-detect delay-time command is used to set on the interface, if received loopback-detect packet, then set action that set on the interface.
[P8908|Heading 4] Examples
[P8909|Normal] This example shows how to set the value for delay time set action to 5s:
[P8910|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# loopback-detect delay-time 5
[P8911|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P8912|Normal] show loopback-detect
[P8913|Heading 3] loopback-detect action
[P8914|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P8915|Normal] Using the loopback-detect action command, you can configure an action to perform when a loopback is detected on an interface.
[P8916|Body Text] Using the no loopback-detect action command, you can restore the default action.
[P8917|Body Text] By default, an interface is blocked when a loopback is detected on the interface.
[P8918|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P8919|Normal] loopback-detect action { shutdown | trap | block }
[P8920|Body Text] no loopback-detect action

[TABLE 265] rows=4 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	shutdown	Shuts down an interface when a loopback is detected on the interface.	-
R3	Trap	Only sends a trap message when a loopback is detected.	-
R4	block	Block the interface and continue to send loopback-detect packets	-

[P8921|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P8922|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P8923|Heading 4] Default
[P8924|Normal] Trap
[P8925|Heading 4] Usage
[P8926|Normal] After loopback detection is enabled on an interface, the interface sends loopback detection packets at intervals. When a loopback is detected on the interface, the system performs an action to minimize the impact on the entire network. The loopback-detect action command configures the action.
[P8927|Heading 4] Examples
[P8928|Normal] This example shows how to configure the system action to shutdown interface eth-0-1 when a loopback occurs:
[P8929|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)#interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# loopback-detect action shutdown
[P8930|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P8931|Normal] show loopback-detect
[P8932|Body Text] loopback-detect enable
[P8933|Heading 3] loopback-detect packet vlan
[P8934|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P8935|Normal] Using the loopback-detect packet vlan command, you can specify the VLAN IDs of loopback detection packets on an interface.
[P8936|Body Text] Using the no loopback-detect packet vlan command, you can cancel the configuration.
[P8937|Body Text] By default, detection packets do not have a VLAN ID.
[P8938|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P8939|Normal] loopback-detect packet vlan VID
[P8940|Body Text] no loopback-detect packet vlan VID

[TABLE 266] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	VID	VLAN ID	1-4094

[P8941|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P8942|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P8943|Heading 4] Default
[P8944|Normal] No vlan id.
[P8945|Heading 4] Usage
[P8946|Normal] By default, loopback detection packets do not contain VLAN IDs. After the loopback-detect packet vlan command is executed on an interface, the interface sends an untagged loopback detection packet and the loopback detection packets with the specified VLAN tags. The specified VLANs exist and the interface has been added to the VLANs in tagged mode. If you run the loopback-detect packet vlan command multiple times in the same interface view, multiple VLAN IDs are specified.
[P8947|Body Text] You can specify a maximum of eight VLAN IDs
[P8948|Heading 4] Examples
[P8949|Normal] This example shows how to set the VLAN ID of loopback detection packets sent by interface eth-0-1 to 30:
[P8950|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)#interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# loopback-detect packet vlan 30

[P8970|Heading 3] loopback-detect in-loop-enable
[P8971|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P8972|Normal] Using the loopback-detect in-loop enable, you can enable in-loop mode.
[P8973|Body Text] Using the no loopback-detect in-loop-enable,you can disable in-loop mode.
[P8974|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P8975|Normal] loopback-detect in-loop-enable
[P8976|Body Text] no loopback-detect in-loop-enable
[P8977|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P8978|Normal] Global Configuration
[P8979|Heading 4] Default
[P8980|Normal] Disable
[P8981|Heading 4] Usage
[P8982|Normal] Using this command can switch loopback-detect to the in-loop mode in global configuration mode. In this mode, a loop alarm is triggered when the port receives the packets from the same port, and when the port receives the packets from other ports on the same board, the loop alarm is triggered.
[P8983|Heading 4] Examples
[P8984|Normal] This example shows how to enable in-loop mode in global configration:
[P8985|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# loopback-detect in-loop-enable

[P9036|Heading 4] Usage
[P9037|Normal] The peer-address command specifies the peer IPv4 address for a MLAG domain. MLAG control traffic is sent to the peer IPv4 address.

[P9045|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P9046|Normal] The peer-link command specifies the interface that connects MLAG peers.
[P9047|Body Text] The no peer-link command removes the peer link by deleting the peer-link command from running-config
[P9048|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P9049|Normal] peer-link IFNAME
[P9050|Body Text] no peer-link

[P9051|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P9052|Normal] MLAG Configuration
[P9053|Heading 4] Default
[P9054|Normal] None
[P9055|Heading 4] Usage
[P9056|Normal] The peer-link command specifies the interface that connects MLAG peers. To form an MLAG, two switches are connected through an interface called a apeer link. The peer link carries control and data traffic between the two switches.
[P9057|Body Text] The no peer-link command removes the peer link by deleting the peer-link command from running-config.
[P9058|Heading 4] Examples
[P9059|Normal] This example shows how to specify the interface that connects MLAG peers:
[P9060|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# mlag configuration
Switch(config-mlag)# peer-link eth-0-9 
Switch(config-mlag)#

[P9063|Heading 3] timers mlag
[P9064|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P9065|Normal] The timers mlag command specifies the keepalive interval and holdtime timers.
[P9066|Body Text] The no timers mlag command removes the specified timer and returns it to default value.
[P9067|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P9068|Normal] timers mlag keepalive holdtime
[P9069|Body Text] no timers mlag

[TABLE 271] rows=3 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	keepalive	keepalive time interval	1-65535, unit:second
R3	holdtime	holdtime time interval	4-65535, unit:second

[P9070|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P9071|Normal] MLAG Configuration
[P9072|Heading 4] Default
[P9073|Normal] Default keepalive interval is 1 seconds and default holdtime is 5 seconds.
[P9074|Heading 4] Usage
[P9075|Normal] The timers mlag command specifies the keepalive interval and holdtime timers. It will be take effective by next time when the peer goes to established. Between the locally configured keepalive timer and the calculated value by the remote holdtime/4 carried in open message, system uses the smaller one in actual calculation.
[P9076|Body Text] The no timers mlag command removes the specified timer and returns it to default value.
[P9077|Heading 4] Examples
[P9078|Normal] This example shows how to specify the keeepalive interval and holdtime timers:
[P9079|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# mlag configuration
Switch(config-mlag)# timers mlag 10 100
Switch(config-mlag)#

[P9082|Heading 3] reload-delay
[P9083|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P9084|Normal] The reload-delay command specifies the period that non-peer links are disabled after an MLAG peer reboots.
[P9085|Body Text] The no reload-delay command restores the default value of 300 by deleting the reload-delay mlag statement from running-config.
[P9086|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P9087|Normal] reload-delay ( auto | period )
[P9088|Body Text] no reload-delay

[TABLE 272] rows=3 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	period	Disable link interval. The number 0 means that interface not enter into errdisable	0-86400, unit:second
R3	auto	Auto recovery from errdisable after MLAG peer build successful.	-

[P9089|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P9090|Normal] MLAG Configuration
[P9091|Heading 4] Default
[P9092|Normal] 300 seconds.
[P9093|Heading 4] Usage
[P9094|Normal] When an MLAG peer reboots, all ports except those in peer-link port-channel remain in errdisabled state for a specified period. This period allows all topology states to stabilize before the switch begins forwarding traffic. The specified period is configured by this command.
[P9095|Heading 4] Examples
[P9096|Normal] This example shows how to specify the dealy interval:
[P9097|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# mlag configuration
Switch(config-mlag)# reload-delay 100
Switch(config-mlag)#

[P9163|Normal] None
[P9164|Heading 4] Usage
[P9165|Normal] The mlag command assigns an MLAG ID to a port-channel. MLAG peer switches form an MLAG when each switch configures the same MLAG ID to a port-channel interface. Only one MLAG ID can be assigned to an interface. An individual MLAG number cannot be assigned to more than one interface.

[P9169|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal

Switch(config-if)# mlag 1

[P9252|Normal] The following example shows how to delete the user-defined hash field named user:
[P9253|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# no hash-field user

[P9926|Heading 4] Usage

[P9930|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
