[P9936|Heading 2] ARP Commands
[P9937|Heading 3] arp
[P9938|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P9939|Normal] To add a permanent entry in the Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) cache, use the arp command in global configuration mode.
[P9940|Body Text] To remove an entry from the ARP cache, use the no form of this command.
[P9941|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P9942|Normal] arp ( vrf VRF-NAME | ) IP-ADDRESS HARDWARE-ADDRESS
[P9943|Body Text] no arp ( vrf VRF-NAME | ) IP-ADDRESS

[TABLE 306] rows=4 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	vrf VRF-NAME	Virtual Routing and Forwarding (VRF) instance. The vrf-name argument is the name of the VRF table	String with up to 31 characters
R3	IP-ADDRESS	IP address in four-part dotted decimal format corresponding to the local data-link address	IPv4 Address
R4	HARDWARE-ADDRESS	Local data-link address (a 48-bit address)	MAC Address

[P9944|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P9945|Normal] Global Configuration
[P9946|Heading 4] Default
[P9947|Normal] No entries are permanently installed in the ARP cache.
[P9948|Heading 4] Usage
[P9949|Normal] Because most hosts support dynamic resolution, you generally need not specify static ARP cache entries.
[P9950|Body Text] To remove all none static entries from the ARP cache, use the clear arp-cache privileged EXEC command.
[P9951|Heading 4] Examples
[P9952|Normal] The following is an example of add a static ARP entry for a typical Ethernet host:
[P9953|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# arp 10.31.7.19 0800.0900.1834
[P9954|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P9955|Normal] clear arp-cache
[P9956|Heading 3] arp retry-interval
[P9957|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P9958|Normal] When an interface requests a mapping for an address not in the cache, system will send ARP request message on the associated network requesting the address mapping. Usually, 3 request messages will be sent until the system got a response. To configure the ARP request delay interval between 2 messages, use arp retry-interval command in interface configuration mode. To restore the default value, use the no form of this command.
[P9959|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P9960|Normal] arp retry-interval SECONDS
[P9961|Body Text] no arp retry-interval

[TABLE 307] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	SECONDS	Time (in seconds) that an ARP request delay to interface	0-3 seconds

[P9962|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P9963|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P9964|Heading 4] Default
[P9965|Normal] 1 second
[P9966|Heading 4] Usage
[P9967|Normal] This command is ignored when issued on interfaces that do not use ARP. The show interface EXEC command displays the ARP retry interval value. The value as seen in the following example from the show interface command:
[P9968|Body Text] ARP timeout 01:00:00, ARP retry interval 1s
[P9969|Heading 4] Examples
[P9970|Normal] The following example sets the ARP retry interval to 3 seconds:
[P9971|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# no switchport
Switch(config-if)# arp retry-interval 3
[P9972|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P9973|Normal] show interface

[P9977|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P9978|Normal] arp timeout SECONDS
[P9979|Body Text] no arp timeout

[TABLE 308] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	SECONDS	Time (in seconds) that an entry remains in the ARP cache. <1-2147483>	1-2147483 seconds

[P9980|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P9981|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P9982|Heading 4] Default
[P9983|Normal] 3600 seconds (1 hour)
[P9984|Heading 4] Usage
[P9985|Normal] This command is ignored when issued on interfaces that do not use ARP. The show interface EXEC command displays the ARP timeout value. The value as seen in the following example from the show interface command:
[P9986|Body Text] ARP timeout 01:00:00, ARP retry interval 1s
[P9987|Heading 4] Examples
[P9988|Normal] The following example sets the ARP timeout to 1200 seconds to allow entries to time out more quickly than the default:
[P9989|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# no switchport
Switch(config-if)# arp timeout 1200

[P10038|Heading 4] Usage
[P10039|Normal] If enable, the interface receive IP packets that not match any ARP entry will create an fake ARP entry. [P10062|Heading 3] clear arp-cache
[P10063|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P10064|Normal] To refresh dynamically created entries from the Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) cache, use the clear arp-cache command in privileged EXEC mode.
[P10065|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P10066|Normal] clear arp-cache ( ( vrf VRF-NAME | ) interface IFNAME | )

[TABLE 310] rows=3 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	vrf VRF-NAME	(Optional) Refreshes only the ARP table entries for the specified Virtual Private Network (VPN) routing and forwarding (VRF) instance	String with up to 31 characters
R3	IFNAME	(Optional) Refreshes only the ARP table entries associated with this interface	Support physical/aggregation/loopback/vlan/tunnel ports

[P10067|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P10068|Normal] Privileged EXEC
[P10069|Heading 4] Default
[P10070|Normal] No default behavior or values.
[P10071|Heading 4] Usage
[P10072|Normal] This command updates the dynamically learned IP address and MAC address mapping information in the ARP table to ensure the validity of those entries. If the refresh operation encounters any stale entries (dynamic ARP entries that have expired but have not yet been aged out by an internal, timer-driven process), those entries are aged out of the ARP table immediately as opposed to at the next refresh interval.
[P10073|Body Text] Use this command without any arguments or keywords to refresh all ARP cache entries for all enabled interfaces.
[P10074|Heading 4] Examples
[P10075|Normal] The following example shows how to refresh all dynamically learned ARP cache entries for all enabled interfaces:
[P10076|Terminal Display] Switch# clear arp-cache
[P10077|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P10078|Normal] show ip arp
[P10079|Heading 3] clear ip arp

[P10175|Heading 3] proxy-arp enable
[P10176|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P10177|Normal] The switch uses proxy ARP to help hosts determine MAC addresses of hosts on other networks or subnets.
[P10178|Body Text] To enable proxy Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) on an interface, use the proxy-arp enable command in interface configuration mode. To disable proxy ARP on the interface, use the no form of this command.
[P10179|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P10180|Normal] proxy-arp enable 
[P10181|Body Text] no proxy-arp enable
[P10182|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P10183|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P10184|Heading 4] Default
[P10185|Normal] Proxy ARP is disabled by default.
[P10186|Heading 4] Usage
[P10187|Normal] When proxy ARP is disabled, a device will respond to ARP requests received on its interface only if the target IP address is the same as its IP address.
[P10188|Heading 4] Examples
[P10189|Normal] The following example enables proxy ARP on interface eth-0-1:
[P10190|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)#interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)#no switchport
Switch(config-if)#no shutdown
Switch(config-if)#ip address 1.1.1.1/24
Switch(config-if)# proxy-arp enable
[P10191|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P10192|Normal] local-proxy-arp enable
[P10193|Heading 3] local-proxy-arp enable
[P10194|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P10195|Normal] The local proxy ARP feature allow the L3 Device to response ARP request whose ARP Target address is in the same subnet the as the ARP request comes from (No Routing is required).
[P10196|Body Text] To enable local proxy Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) on an interface, use the local-proxy-arp enable command in interface configuration mode.
[P10197|Body Text] To disable proxy ARP on the interface, use the no form of this command.
[P10198|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P10199|Normal] local-proxy-arp enable 
[P10200|Body Text] no local-proxy-arp enable
[P10201|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P10202|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P10203|Heading 4] Default
[P10204|Normal] Local proxy ARP is disabled by default.
[P10205|Heading 4] Usage
[P10206|Normal] Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP) redirects are disabled on interfaces when the local proxy ARP feature is enabled. The main condition we need to enable local ARP proxy is that the switch enables port isolate.
[P10207|Heading 4] Examples
[P10208|Normal] The following example enables local proxy ARP on interface eth-0-1:
[P10209|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# no switchport
Switch(config-if)# no shutdown
Switch(config-if)# ip address 1.1.1.1/24
Switch(config-if)# local-proxy-arp enable
[P10210|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P10211|Normal] proxy-arp enable

[P10263|Heading 2] DHCP Client Commands
[P10264|Heading 3] ip address dhcp
[P10265|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P10266|Normal] To acquire an IP address from Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol(DHCP), use the ip address dhcp command in interface configuration mode.
[P10267|Body Text] To disable the function, use the no form of this command.
[P10268|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P10269|Normal] ip address dhcp
[P10270|Body Text] no ip address dhcp
[P10271|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P10272|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P10273|Heading 4] Default
[P10274|Normal] DHCP Client is not enabled on interface.
[P10275|Heading 4] Usage
[P10276|Normal] Once this command was enabled on an UP interface, it will acquire IP address immediately, otherwise the DHCP function of the interface will be in SUSPEND status.
[P10277|Body Text] The no ip address dhcp command will send a DHCPRELEASE message to server and remove any IP address.
[P10278|Heading 4] Examples
[P10279|Normal] The following example shows how to enable dhcp client function:
[P10280|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config-if)# ip address dhcp
[P10281|Normal] The following example shows how to disable dhcp client function:
[P10282|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config-if)# no ip address dhcp
[P10283|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P10284|Normal] dhcp client request

[P10286|Body Text] dhcp client class-id

[P10289|Body Text] management ip address dhcp
[P10290|Body Text] show dhcp client
[P10291|Heading 3] management ip address dhcp
[P10292|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P10293|Normal] To acquire an IP address for management interface from by DHCP, use the management IP address dhcp command in global configuration mode.
[P10294|Body Text] To disable the function, use the no form of this command.
[P10295|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P10296|Normal] management ip address dhcp
[P10297|Body Text] no management ip address dhcp
[P10298|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P10299|Normal] Global Configuration
[P10300|Heading 4] Default
[P10301|Normal] DHCP Client is not enabled on management interface.
[P10302|Heading 4] Usage
[P10303|Normal] Use this command like IP address dhcp.
[P10304|Heading 4] Examples
[P10305|Normal] The following example shows how to enable dhcp client function on management interface:
[P10306|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# management ip address dhcp
[P10307|Normal] The following example shows how to disable dhcp client function on management interface:
[P10308|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# no management ip address dhcp
[P10309|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P10310|Normal] show dhcp client
[P10311|Heading 3] dhcp client request
[P10312|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P10313|Normal] To request configuration parameters by DHCP, use the dhcp client request command in interface configuration mode. To cancel the request, use the no form of this command.
[P10314|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P10315|Normal] dhcp client request ( router | static-route | classless-static-route | classless-static-route-ms | tftp-server-address | dns-nameserver | domain-name | netbios-nameserver | vendor-specific )
[P10316|Body Text] no dhcp client request ( router | static-route | classless-static-route | classless-static-route-ms | tftp-server-address | dns-nameserver | domain-name | netbios-nameserver | vendor-specific )

[TABLE 318] rows=10 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	router	Default router option (3)	-
R3	static-route	Static route option (33)	-
R4	classless-static-route	Classless static route option (121)	-
R5	classless-static-route-ms	Microsoft classless static route option (249)	-
R6	tftp-server-address	TFTP server ip address option (150)	-
R7	dns-nameserver	DNS name server option (6)	-
R8	domain-name	Domain name option (15)	-
R9	netbios-nameserver	NetBIOS name server option (44)	-
R10	vendor-specific	Vendor specific option (43)	-

[P10317|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P10318|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P10319|Heading 4] Default
[P10320|Normal] static-route, classless-static-route, classless-static-route-ms, tftp-server-address and router is requested as default.
[P10321|Heading 4] Usage
[P10322|Normal] Use this command to request configuration form DHCP server. It can be typed many times with each option or one time with all options wanted. Note that when Option 249 coexist with option 121 then the option 121 should have high priority and option 249 should be ignored. when option 121 or option 249 coexist with option 33 then the option 33 should be ignored. This command should be issued before ip address dhcp command. If you issued ip address dhcp before, this command will take effect after next ip address dhcp command.
[P10323|Heading 4] Examples
[P10324|Normal] The following example shows how to request dhcp option static-route and tftp-server-address:
[P10325|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config-if)# no management ip address dhcp
[P10326|Normal] The following example shows how to request dhcp option router:
[P10327|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config-if)# dhcp client request router
[P10328|Normal] The following example shows how to cancel request of dhcp option router:
[P10329|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config-if)# no dhcp client request router
[P10330|Normal] The following example shows how to request tftp server address:
[P10331|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config-if)# dhcp client request static-route tftp-server-address

[P10355|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P10356|Normal] To specify a class-id for DHCP server and client, use the dhcp client class-id command in interface configuration mode. To remove this configuration, use the no form of this command.
[P10357|Heading 4] Command Syntax

[P10359|Body Text] no dhcp client class-id

R3	hex	Hex type	-

[P10360|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P10361|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P10362|Heading 4] Default
[P10363|Normal] No class-id is set.
[P10364|Heading 4] Usage
[P10365|Normal] Class-id used by DHCP clients to optionally identify the type and configuration of a DHCP client. Vendors and sites may choose to define specific class identifiers to convey particular configuration or other identification information about a client. This command should be issued before ip address dhcp command. If you issued ip address dhcp before, this command will take effect after next ip address dhcp command.
[P10366|Heading 4] Examples

[P10370|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# no dhcp client class-id

[P10433|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P10434|Normal] To specify the broadcast-flag in the DHCP message, use the dhcp client broadcast-flag command in global configuration mode.
[P10435|Body Text] To remove this configuration, use the no form of this command.
[P10436|Heading 4] Command Syntax

[P10439|Heading 4] Command Mode

[P10441|Heading 4] Default
[P10442|Normal] Broadcast-flag will be set in DHCP message sent by client for request IP address.
[P10443|Heading 4] Usage
[P10444|Normal] This flag tell DHCP server that client can’t receive unicast IP datagrams until been configured with an IP address. Thus server or relay agent will broadcast any messages to the client on the client’s subnet.

[P10649|Heading 3] dhcp relay information trust-all
[P10650|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P10651|Normal] To configure all interfaces as trusted sources of the DHCP relay agent information option, use the dhcp relay information trust-all command in global configuration mode. To restore these interfaces to their default behavior, use the no form of this command.
[P10652|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P10653|Normal] dhcp relay information trust-all
[P10654|Body Text] no dhcp relay information trust-all
[P10655|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P10656|Normal] Global Configuration
[P10657|Heading 4] Default
[P10658|Normal] All interfaces on the switch are considered entrusted.
[P10659|Heading 4] Usage
[P10660|Normal] By default, if the gateway address is set to all zeros in the DHCP packet and the relay information option is already present in the packet, the DHCP relay agent will discard the packet. If the dhcp relay information trust-all command is configured globally, the DHCP relay agent will not discard the packet even if the gateway address is set to all zeros. Instead, the received DHCPDISCOVER or DHCPREQUEST messages will be forwarded to the addresses configured by the dhcp-server command as in normal DHCP relay operation.
[P10661|Heading 4] Examples
[P10662|Normal] The following example shows how to configure dhcp relay information trust globally:
[P10663|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# dhcp relay information trust-all
[P10664|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P10665|Normal] dhcp relay information trusted
[P10666|Heading 3] dhcp relay information trusted

[P10669|Heading 4] Command Syntax

[P10671|Body Text] no dhcp relay information trusted
[P10672|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P10673|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P10674|Heading 4] Default
[P10675|Normal] All interfaces on the router are considered entrusted.
[P10676|Heading 4] Usage
[P10677|Normal] By default, if the gateway address is set to all zeros in the DHCP packet and the relay information option is already present in the packet, the DHCP relay agent will discard the packet. If the dhcp relay information trusted command is configured globally, the DHCP relay agent will not discard the packet even if the gateway address is set to all zeros. Instead, the received DHCPDISCOVER or DHCPREQUEST messages will be forwarded to the addresses configured by the dhcp-server command as in normal DHCP relay operation.
[P10678|Heading 4] Examples

[P10680|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal

[P10701|Heading 3] dhcp relay address cycle
[P10702|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P10703|Normal] Use “dhcp relay address cycle” command to enable DHCP relay cycle feature.
[P10704|Body Text] Use “no dhcp relay address cycle” to disable the feature.
[P10705|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P10706|Normal] dhcp relay address cycle
[P10707|Body Text] no dhcp relay address cycle
[P10708|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P10709|Normal] Global Configuration
[P10710|Heading 4] Default
[P10711|Normal] DHCP relay cycle is disabled by default.
[P10712|Heading 4] Usage
[P10713|Normal] This command is used for DHCP relay. When more than one DHCP servers are configured on a DHCP relay device, relay device should send DHCP DISCOVER packets to all servers by default. In this way, the servers should deal with too much packet and might be overload. To resolve this problem use this command to enable DHCP relay cycle. After configure this command, DHCP relay device send to only one server when it receive the DHCP DISCOVER packet, and it will change a server to send packet every time after it sent one. Use this method to make all servers to achieve load balance.
[P10714|Heading 4] Examples
[P10715|Normal] Enable DHCP relay cycle feature :
[P10716|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# dhcp relay address cycle
[P10717|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P10718|Normal] None

[P10994|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P10995|Normal] To specify the DNS IP servers available to a DHCP client, use the dns-server DHCP pool configuration command. To remove the DNS server list, use the no form of this command.
[P10996|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P10997|Normal] dns-server A.B.C.D ( A.B.C.D… A.B.C.D )
[P10998|Body Text] no dns-server

[TABLE 336] rows=3 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	A.B.C.D	Specifies the IP address of a DNS server. One IP address is required, although you can specify up to eight addresses in one command line.	IPv4 Address
R3	A.B.C.D… A.B.C.D (Optional)	Specifies up to eight addresses in the command line.	IPv4 Address

[P10999|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P11000|Normal] DHCP pool Configuration
[P11001|Heading 4] Default
[P11002|Normal] The default value is none DNS IP servers specified.
[P11003|Heading 4] Usage
[P11004|Normal] You can specify up to eight servers in the list, Servers are listed in order of preference (address1 is the most preferred server, address2 is the next most preferred server, and so on).
[P11005|Heading 4] Examples
[P11006|Normal] The following is sample output from the dns-server command:
[P11007|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# dhcp pool test
Switch(config-dhcp)#  dns-server 1.1.1.1 2.2.2.2
[P11008|Heading 4] Related Commands

[P11011|Heading 4] Command Purpose

[P11015|Body Text] no domain-name

[TABLE 337] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	WORD	specify a domain name suffix in each DHCP address pool on the DHCP server for the clients.	1) The length range should be [1, 64) 2) The characters can only include [0-9a-zA-Z.-_], specify a domain name suffix in each DHCP address pool on the DHCP server for the clients. 1) The length range should be [1, 64) 2) The characters can only include [0-9a-zA-Z.-_], 3) The string must starting with alphabetic, ending with alphanumeric or digit

[P11016|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P11017|Normal] DHCP pool Configuration
[P11018|Heading 4] Default
[P11019|Normal] The default value is none domain-name specified.
[P11020|Heading 4] Usage
[P11021|Normal] You can specify a domain name suffix in each DHCP address pool on the DHCP serverfor the clients. With this suffix assigned, the client needs only input part of a domainname, and the system will add the domain name suffix for name resolution.
[P11022|Heading 4] Examples
[P11023|Normal] The following is sample output from the domain-name command:
[P11024|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# dhcp pool test
Switch(config-dhcp)#  domain-name switch.org
[P11025|Heading 4] Related Commands

[P11027|Heading 3] bootfile-name
[P11028|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P11029|Normal] To specify the name of the default boot image for a DHCP client, use the bootfile-name DHCP pool configuration command. To delete the boot image name, use the no form of this command.
[P11030|Heading 4] Command Syntax

[P11033|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P11034|Normal] DHCP pool Configuration
[P11035|Heading 4] Default
[P11036|Normal] The default value is none boot file specified.
[P11037|Heading 4] Usage
[P11038|Normal] This task is to specify the IP address and name of a TFTP server and the bootfile name in the DHCP address pool. The DHCP clients use these parameters to contact the TFTP server, requesting the configuration file used for system initialization, which is called autoconfiguration.
[P11039|Heading 4] Examples

Switch(config)# dhcp pool test
Switch(config-dhcp)# bootfile dhclient_startup_config

[P11116|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P11117|Normal] To configure the subnet number and mask for a DHCP address pool on a DHCP Server, use the network DHCP pool configuration command.

[P11121|Body Text] no network

R4	prefix-length	Prefix length for the network.	0-32

[P11122|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P11123|Normal] DHCP pool Configuration
[P11124|Heading 4] Default
[P11125|Normal] The default value is none subnet number and mask specified.
[P11126|Heading 4] Usage
[P11127|Normal] This command is valid for DHCP subnetwork address pools only.The DHCP server assumes that all host addresses are available. The system administrator can exclude subsets of the address space by using the ip dhcp excluded-address command.Network for one pool cann’t the same with other pool’s network and can’t configure manual bindings within the same pool that is configured with the network command.

[P11138|Body Text] no lease

R3	HOURS (Optional)	Specifies the number of hours in the lease. A days value must be supplied before you can configure an hours value.	0-23 hours
R4	MINUTES (Optional)	Specifies the number of minutes in the lease. A day’s value and an hours value must be supplied before you can configure a minute’s value.	0-59 minutes

[P11139|Heading 4] Command Mode

[P11154|Heading 3] option
[P11155|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P11156|Normal] To configure DHCP Server options, use the option DHCP pool configuration command.
[P11157|Body Text] To remove the options, use the no form of this command.
[P11158|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P11159|Normal] option { code [ ascii ascii-string | hex hex-string | ip-address ip-address ] }
[P11160|Body Text] no option [ code ]

[TABLE 345] rows=5 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	code	Specifies the DHCP option code，except values 3, 6, 15, 44, 46, 50, 51, 52, 53, 54, 55, 57, 58, 59, 61, 67, 82 and 150.	2-254
R3	ascii-string	Specifies an NVT ASCII character string. ASCII character strings that contain white space must be delaminated by quotation marks.	String with up to 255 characters
R4	hex-string	Specifies dotted-hexadecimal data. Each byte in hexadecimal character strings is two hexadecimal digitse.	String with up to 254 characters， if its length is odd, 0 is added before it.
R5	ip-address	Specifies an IP address.	IPv4 Address, at most 8 IPv4 addresses are supported.

[P11161|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P11162|Normal] DHCP pool Configuration
[P11163|Heading 4] Default
[P11164|Normal] The default value is none DHCP option specified.
[P11165|Heading 4] Usage
[P11166|Normal] DHCP provides a framework for passing configuration information to hosts on a TCP/IP network. Configuration parameters and other control information are carried in tagged data items that are stored in the options field of the DHCP message. The data items themselves are also called options. The current set of DHCP options are documented in RFC 2131, Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol.
[P11167|Body Text] Options with specified command line or options that the dhcp server does not need to support are not supported to be configure by the CLI “option”. These unsupported options are 3, 6, 15, 44, 46, 50, 51, 52, 53, 54, 55, 57, 58, 59, 61, 67, 82 and 150.
[P11168|Heading 4] Examples
[P11169|Normal] The following is sample output from the option command:
[P11170|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# dhcp pool test
Switch(config-dhcp)# option 4 ip-address 10.10.10.10 11.11.11.11
[P11171|Heading 4] Related Commands

[P11174|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P11175|Normal] To specify a single IP address or a range of IP addresses which the DHCP Server is not assign to DHCP clients, use the excluded-address DHCP pool configuration command. To remove the IP addresses, use the no form of this command.
[P11176|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P11177|Normal] dhcp excluded-address A.B.C.D [ A.B.C.D ]
[P11178|Body Text] no dhcp excluded-address A.B.C.D [ A.B.C.D ]

[TABLE 346] rows=3 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	A.B.C.D	The excluded IP address, or low IP address in an excluded address range.	IPv4 Address
R3	A.B.C.D(Optional)	The high IP address in the excluded address range.	IPv4 Address

[P11179|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P11180|Normal] Global Configuration
[P11181|Heading 4] Default
[P11182|Normal] All IP pool addresses are assignable.
[P11183|Heading 4] Usage
[P11184|Normal] The DHCP server assumes that all pool addresses may be assigned to clients. Use this command to exclude a single IP address or a range of IP addresses.
[P11185|Heading 4] Examples
[P11186|Normal] The following example shows how to disallow DHCP server distribute the address in the range of 10.10.1.100 -10.10.1.199:
[P11187|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# dhcp pool test
Switch(config-dhcp)#  ip dhcp excluded-address 10.10.1.100 10.10.1.199

[P11190|Heading 3] show dhcp server conflict
[P11191|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P11192|Normal] To display address conflicts found by a DHCP Server when addresses are offered to the client, use the show dhcp server conflict in privileged EXEC mode.
[P11193|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P11194|Normal] show dhcp server conflict [ ip A.B.C.D | all ]

[TABLE 347] rows=3 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	ip A.B.C.D	Specifies the IP address of the conflict found.	IPv4 Address
R3	all	Specifies all IP address of the conflict found.	-

[P11195|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P11196|Normal] Privileged EXEC
[P11197|Heading 4] Default
[P11198|Normal] None
[P11199|Heading 4] Usage
[P11200|Normal] The server detects conflicts using ping. The client detects conflicts using gratuitous Address Resolution Protocol (ARP). If an address conflict is detected, the address is removed from the pool and the address will not be assigned until an administrator resolves the conflict.
[P11201|Heading 4] Examples
[P11202|Normal] The following example displays the detection method and detection time for all IP addresses the DHCP server has offered that have conflicts with other devices:
[P11203|Terminal Display] Switch# show ip dhcp conflict all

[P11206|Body Text] dhcp ping packets

[P11320|Heading 2] DNS Commands
[P11321|Heading 3] ip host
[P11322|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P11323|Normal] To define static hostname-to-address mappings in the Domain Name System (DNS) hostname cache for a DNS view, use the ip host command in global configuration mode. If the hostname cache does not exist yet, it is automatically created.
[P11324|Body Text] To remove a hostname-to-address mapping, use the no form of this command.
[P11325|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P11326|Normal] ip host HOSTNAME IP_ADDR
[P11327|Body Text] no ip host hostname

[TABLE 352] rows=3 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	HOSTNAME	Name of the host	String with up to 63 characters
R3	IP_ADDR	Associated host IP address	IPv4 Address

[P11328|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P11329|Normal] Global Configuration
[P11330|Heading 4] Default
[P11331|Normal] No static hostname-to-address mapping is added to the DNS hostname cache for a DNS view.
[P11332|Heading 4] Usage
[P11333|Normal] None
[P11334|Heading 4] Examples
[P11335|Normal] The following example shows how to add a mapping entry to the global hostname cache and then remove one of those entries from the global hostname cache:
[P11336|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ip host www.example1.com 192.0.2.141
[P11337|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P11338|Normal] show ip host
[P11339|Heading 3] dns domain
[P11340|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P11341|Normal] To specify the default domain for a Domain Name System (DNS) view to use to complete unqualified hostnames (names without a dotted-decimal domain name), use the dns domain command in global configuration mode.
[P11342|Body Text] To remove the specification of the default domain name for a DNS view, use the no form of this command.
[P11343|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P11344|Normal] dns domain DOMAIN-NAME
[P11345|Body Text] no dns domain DOMAIN-NAME

[TABLE 353] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	DOMAIN-NAME	Name of the domain	String with up to 63 characters

[P11346|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P11347|Normal] Global Configuration
[P11348|Heading 4] Default
[P11349|Normal] No default domain name is defined for the DNS view.
[P11350|Heading 4] Usage
[P11351|Normal] None
[P11352|Heading 4] Examples
[P11353|Normal] The following example shows how to specify the default domain for DNS:
[P11354|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# dns domain www.example1.com
[P11355|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P11356|Normal] show dns domain
[P11357|Heading 3] dns server
[P11358|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P11359|Normal] To add a name server to the list of Domain Name System (DNS) name servers, use the dns server command in global configuration mode. To remove a DNS name server from the list, use the no form of this command.
[P11360|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P11361|Normal] dns server IP_ADDR ( source-interface IFNAME | source-ip A.B.C.D | )
[P11362|Body Text] no dns server IP_ADDR

[TABLE 354] rows=4 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	IP_ADDR	IP address of a DNS name server	Support IPv4/IPv6 Address
R3	IFNAME	Name of source interface	Support physical/aggregation/loopback/tunnel/vlan ports
R4	A.B.C.D	Source IP address	IPv4 Address

[P11363|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P11364|Normal] Global Configuration
[P11365|Heading 4] Default
[P11366|Normal] No IP address is explicitly added to the list of resolving name servers for this view.
[P11367|Heading 4] Usage
[P11368|Normal] This command can be entered multiple times to specify a maximum of three resolving name servers. After three resolving name servers have been specified, additional resolving name servers cannot be specified unless an existing entry is removed.
[P11369|Body Text] If the source interface or source IP address is specified, the packet transmit will use the related IP address as source address.
[P11370|Heading 4] Examples
[P11371|Normal] The following example shows how to specify the DNS server list:
[P11372|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# dns server 10.10.1.1
Switch(config)# dns server 20.20.2.2
[P11373|Heading 4] Related Commands

[P11409|Heading 2] Tunnel Commands
[P11410|Heading 3] interface
[P11411|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P11412|Normal] Use this command to create a new tunnel interface.
[P11413|Body Text] Use the no form of this command to destroy the tunnel interface.
[P11414|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P11415|Normal] interface tunnel TUNNEL-ID
[P11416|Body Text] no interface tunnel TUNNEL-ID

[TABLE 356] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	TUNNEL-ID	The tunnel id	0-1023

[P11417|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P11418|Normal] Global Configuration
[P11419|Heading 4] Default
[P11420|Normal] None
[P11421|Heading 4] Usage
[P11422|Normal] Before connect 2 IPv6 networks by an IPv4 network, a tunnel interface is required. The tunnel is available after set some attributes. After IPv6 is enabled the tunnel interface can forward IPv6 packets.
[P11423|Heading 4] Examples
[P11424|Normal] This example shows how to create a tunnel interface:
[P11425|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface tunnel 1
[P11426|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P11427|Normal] show interface tunnel
[P11428|Heading 3] tunnel mode
[P11429|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P11430|Normal] Use this command to specify the IPv6 transition tunnel protocol.
[P11431|Body Text] Use the no form of this command to unset the tunnel protocol.
[P11432|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P11433|Normal] tunnel mode tunnel mode ( erspan ( ecmp-dst-gre | ) | gre | ipv6ip ) ( 6to4 | isatap | )
[P11434|Body Text] no tunnel mode

[TABLE 357] rows=5 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	6to4	Set the tunnel as automatic tunnel 6to4, which use 2002::/16 as its prefix	-
R3	isatap	Set the tunnel as automatic tunnel ISATAP, which use ::5efe:a.b.c.d as its suffix	-
R4	gre	When the destination of tunnel is single, the mode of the tunnel	-
R5	ecmp-dst-gre	When the destinations of tunnel are multi, the mode of the tunnel	-

[P11435|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P11436|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P11437|Heading 4] Default
[P11438|Normal] None
[P11439|Heading 4] Usage
[P11440|Normal] This command specifies a tunnel encapsulation mode for IPv6 in IPv4. When the keywords “6to4” or “isatap” is not specified, then it is a manual tunnel. Tunnel mode is not allowed to change from 6to4 to ISATAP when 6to4 relay routes are configured. Users should unset the tunnel destination before change from manual tunnel to automatic tunnel.
[P11441|Heading 4] Examples
[P11442|Normal] This example shows how to create a 6to4 Tunnel:
[P11443|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface tunnel 1
Switch(config-if)# tunnel mode ipv6ip 6to4
[P11444|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P11445|Normal] tunnel source
[P11446|Body Text] tunnel destination
[P11447|Heading 3] tunnel source

[P11453|Heading 4] Command Mode

[P11537|Heading 3] tunnel extend-header
[P11538|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P11539|Normal] Before the mirror traffic passes through the tunnel, encapsulate the traffic with the extend header.
[P11540|Body Text] Use no the form of this command to unset this configuration.
[P11541|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P11542|Normal] tunnel extend-header
[P11543|Body Text] no tunnel extend-header
[P11544|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P11545|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P11546|Heading 4] Default
[P11547|Normal] None
[P11548|Heading 4] Usage
[P11549|Normal] spanExtendHeaderCopyHash, using the new hash or not;
[P11550|Normal] PacketInfo.skipTimeInfoUpdate, fixed with 1;
[P11551|Normal] if spanExtendHeaderCopyHash is 1, the filed consist with hash (8 bit) and 0 (8 bit); if spanExtendHeaderCopyHash is 0, the filed consist with source port of the mirror (16 bit).
[P11552|Normal] Without dst-load-balance parameter, spanExtendHeaderCopyHash will be 0, and extend-header field does not contain the hash value;
[P11553|Body Text] with dst-load-balance parameter, spanExtendHeaderCopyHash will be 1, and extend-header field contain the hash value.
[P11554|Heading 4] Examples
[P11555|Normal] This example shows how to enable extend-header hash for load balance:
[P11556|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface tunnel 1
Switch(config-if)# tunnel extend-header
Switch(config-if)# tunnel extend-header dst-load-balance
[P11557|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P11558|Normal] show running-config interface tunnel

[P11671|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P11672|Normal] Global Configuration
[P11673|Heading 4] Default
[P11674|Normal] By default, there is not any static ipv6 neighbor entry exist.
[P11675|Heading 4] Usage
[P11676|Normal] Use this command to configure a static neighbor entry. If the IPv6 address is link-local, the interface name must be specified.

[P11678|Heading 4] Examples

[P11821|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P11822|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P11823|Heading 4] Default
[P11824|Normal] By default, MAX interval should be 600 second; MIN interval should be 0.33*MAX.
[P11825|Heading 4] Usage
[P11826|Normal] The valid range should be between 4 and 1800 second for the max value. The valid range should be between 3 and 0.75 * MAX for the minimum value.
[P11827|Body Text] If the minimum value is not specified, it should be 0.33*MAX when MAX >= 9, and it should be equal to the MAX when MAX < 9.

[P11829|Normal] This example shows how to set the RA interval:
[P11830|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal

R3	VALID_TIME	Valid lifetime.	0-4294967295 second
R4	PERFERRED_TIME	Preferred lifetime.	0-4294967295 second

[P11917|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P11918|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P11919|Heading 4] Default
[P11920|Normal] The valid range of valid life time should be between 0 and 4294967295 seconds. User can also use the keyword “infinite” to indicate the value 4294967295(0xFFFFFFFF）. The default value should be 2592000 seconds (30 days).
[P11921|Body Text] The valid range of preferred life time should be between 0 and 4294967295 seconds. User can also use the keyword “infinite” to indicate the value 4294967295（0xFFFFFFFF）. The default value should be 604800 seconds (7 days).
[P11922|Heading 4] Usage
[P11923|Normal] None

[P12243|Heading 1] IP Routing Commands
[P12244|Heading 2] IP Unicast-Routing Commands
[P12245|Heading 3] ip address
[P12246|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P12247|Normal] To set a primary or secondary IP address for an interface, use the ip address command in interface configuration mode. To remove an IP address or disable IP processing, use the no form of this command.
[P12248|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P12249|Normal] ip address ( ADDRESS WILDCARD-MASK | ADDRESS /PREFIX-LENGTH ) ( secondary | )

[TABLE 387] rows=5 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	ADDRESS	IPv4 address of the interface	IPv4 address
R3	WILDCARD-MASK	Mask for the associated IP subnet	Mask in IPv4 address format
R4	PREFIX-LENGTH	Prefix length of the address	1-32
R5	secondary	(Optional) Specifies that the configured address is a secondary IP address. If this keyword is omitted, the configured address is the primary IP address	-

[P12250|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P12251|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P12252|Heading 4] Default
[P12253|Normal] No IP address is defined for the interface.
[P12254|Heading 4] Usage
[P12255|Normal] An interface can have one primary IP address and multiple secondary IP addresses. Packets generated by the switch always use the primary IP address. Therefore, all switches and access servers on a segment should share the same primary network number.
[P12256|Body Text] Hosts can determine subnet masks using the Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP) mask request message. Switch respond to this request with an ICMP mask reply message.
[P12257|Body Text] You can disable IP processing on a particular interface by removing its IP address with the no ip address command. If the software detects another host using one of its IP addresses, it will print an error message on the console.
[P12258|Body Text] The optional secondary keyword allows you to specify up to 8 secondary addresses. Secondary addresses are treated like primary addresses, except the system never generates datagrams other than routing updates with secondary source addresses. IP broadcasts and Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) requests are handled properly, as are interface routes in the IP routing table.
[P12259|Body Text] Secondary IP addresses can be used in a variety of situations. The following are the most common applications:
[P12260|Body Text] There may not be enough host addresses for a particular network segment. For example, your subnet allows up to 254 hosts per logical subnet, but on one physical subnet you need 300 host addresses. Using secondary IP addresses on the switches or access servers allows you to have two logical subnets using one physical subnet.
[P12261|Body Text] Many older networks were built using Level 2 bridges. The judicious use of secondary addresses can aid in the transition to a subnet and router-based network. Switches on an older, bridged segment can be easily made aware that many subnets are on that segment.
[P12262|Body Text] Two subnets of a single network might otherwise be separated by another network. This situation is not permitted when subnets are in use. In these instances, the first network is extended, or layered on top of the second network using secondary addresses.
[P12263|Heading 4] Examples
[P12264|Normal] In the following example, 10.108.1.27 is the primary address and 192.31.7.17 and 192.31.8.17 are secondary addresses for eth-0-1:
[P12265|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# ip address 10.108.1.27 255.255.255.0
Switch(config-if)# ip address 192.31.7.17/24 secondary
Switch(config-if)# ip address 192.31.8.17 255.255.255.0 secondary
[P12266|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P12267|Normal] None

[P12392|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P12393|Normal] To establish static routes, use the ip route command in global configuration mode. To remove static routes, use the no form of this command.
[P12394|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P12395|Normal] ip route vrf VRF-NAME ( PREFIX MASK | PREFIX/PREFIX-LENGTH ) ( NH-ADDRESS public | ( vrf VRF-NAME | ) NH-ADDRESS | IFNAME ( NH-ADDRESS | ) | IFNULL ) ( DISTANCE | ) ( bind bfd BFD-NAME | track NUMBER | ) 
[P12396|Body Text] no ip route vrf VRF-NAME ( PREFIX MASK | PREFIX/PREFIX-LENGTH ) ( NH-ADDRESS public | ( vrf VRF-NAME | ) NH-ADDRESS | IFNAME ( NH-ADDRESS | ) | IFNULL | ) ( bind bfd | track | )
[P12397|Body Text] ip route ( PREFIX MASK | PREFIX/PREFIX-LENGTH ) ( ( vrf VRF-NAME | ) NH-ADDRESS | IFNAME ( NH-ADDRESS | ) | IFTUNNEL | IFNULL ) ( DISTANCE | ) ( bind ( bfd | sbfd ) BFD-NAME | track NUMBER | ) 
[P12398|Body Text] no ip route ( PREFIX MASK | PREFIX/PREFIX-LENGTH ) ( ( vrf VRF-NAME | ) NH-ADDRESS | IFNAME ( NH-ADDRESS | ) | IFTUNNEL | IFNULL | ) ( bind ( bfd | sbfd ) | track | )

[TABLE 391] rows=12 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	VRF-NAME	VRF instance name	A string up to 31 characters
R3	PREFIX	IP route prefix for the destination	IPv4 address
R4	MASK	Prefix mask for the destination	Mask in IPv4 address format
R5	PREFIX-LENGTH	Prefix length for the destination	1-32
R6	IFNAME	Interface name of the next hop that can be used to reach that network	-
R7	IFTUNNEL	tunnel port	-
R8	IFNULL	NULL 0 port	-
R9	NH-ADDRESS	IP address of the next hop that can be used to reach that network	IPv4 address
R10	DISTANCE	(Optional) An administrative distance. The default administrative distance for a static route is 1	1-255
R11	track NUMBER	Specify the ID of track object	1-500
R12	BFD-NAME	Specify the name of bfd	A string up to 16 characters

[P12399|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P12400|Normal] Global Configuration
[P12401|Heading 4] Default
[P12402|Normal] No static routes are established.
[P12403|Heading 4] Usage
[P12404|Normal] The establishment of a static route is appropriate when the switch cannot dynamically build a route to the destination.
[P12405|Heading 4] Examples
[P12406|Normal] The following example establishes a static route:
[P12407|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ip route 172.31.0.0 255.255.0.0 172.31.6.6

[P12660|Heading 2] RIP Commands
[P12661|Heading 3] default-information originate (RIP)
[P12662|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P12663|Normal] To generate a default route into Routing Information Protocol (RIP), use the default-information originate command in router configuration mode. To disable this feature, use the no form of this command.
[P12664|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P12665|Normal] default-information originate ( route-map | )
[P12666|Body Text] no default-information originate ( route-map | )

[TABLE 400] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	route-map	Route map reference	-

[P12667|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P12668|Normal] Router Configuration
[P12669|Heading 4] Default
[P12670|Normal] None
[P12671|Heading 4] Usage
[P12672|Normal] The route orginated will only be learned by RIP neighbor, and this route is not configured in FIB.
[P12673|Heading 4] Examples
[P12674|Normal] The following example originates a default route:
[P12675|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router rip
Switch(config-router)# version 2
Switch(config-router)# network 192.168.16.0/24
Switch(config-router)# default-information originate
[P12676|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P12677|Normal] None
[P12678|Heading 3] default-metric (RIP)
[P12679|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P12680|Normal] To set default metric values for Routing Information Protocol (RIP), use the default-metric command in router configuration mode. To return to the default state, use the no form of this command.
[P12681|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P12682|Normal] default-metric NUMBER-VALUE
[P12683|Body Text] no default-metric

[TABLE 401] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	NUMBER-VALUE	Default metric value	1-16

[P12684|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P12685|Normal] Router Configuration
[P12686|Heading 4] Default
[P12687|Normal] By default, the metric is set to 0.
[P12688|Heading 4] Usage
[P12689|Normal] The default-metric command is used in conjunction with the redistribute router configuration command to cause the current routing protocol to use the same metric value for all redistributed routes. A default metric helps solve the problem of redistributing routes with incompatible metrics. Whenever metrics do not convert, using a default metric provides a reasonable substitute and enables the redistribution to proceed.
[P12690|Heading 4] Examples
[P12691|Normal] The following example shows a switch using both the RIP and the Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) routing protocols. The example advertises OSPF-derived routes using RIP and assigns the OSPF-derived routes a RIP metric of 10:
[P12692|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router rip
Switch(config-router)# default-metric 10
Switch(config-router)# redistribute ospf
[P12693|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P12694|Normal] redistribute (RIP)
[P12695|Heading 3] distance (RIP)
[P12696|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P12697|Normal] To define an administrative distance for routes that are inserted into the routing table, use the distance command in router configuration mode. To return the administrative distance to its default distance definition, use the no form of this command.
[P12698|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P12699|Normal] distance DISTANCE PREFIX/PREFIX-LENGTH ( ACCESSS-LIST-NAME | )
[P12700|Body Text] no distance

[TABLE 402] rows=5 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	DISTANCE	Administrative distance	Administrative distance, an integer from 1 to 255 (routes with a distance value of 255 are not installed in the routing table)
R3	PREFIX	IP prefix for the originator of the imcoming routing updates	IPv4 Address
R4	PREFIX-LENGTH	Prefix length for the originator	1-32
R5	ACCESSS-LIST-NAME	(Optional) Named access list to be applied to incoming routing updates	Up to 40 characters

[P12701|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P12702|Normal] Router Configuration
[P12703|Heading 4] Default
[P12704|Normal] By default, the distance is 120.
[P12705|Heading 4] Usage
[P12706|Normal] An administrative distance is a rating of the trustworthiness of a routing information source, such as an individual switch or a group of switches. Numerically, an administrative distance is an integer from 0 to 255. In general, the higher the value, the lower the trust rating. An administrative distance of 255 means the routing information source cannot be trusted at all and should be ignored.
[P12707|Body Text] When this command is configured, it is applied when a network is being inserted into the routing table. It filters routing updates according to the IP address of the switch that supplies the routing information. It could be used, for example, to filter possibly incorrect routing information from switches that are not under your administrative control. The optional access list name is used to filter router entries in routing update.
[P12708|Heading 4] Examples
[P12709|Normal] The following example set administrative distance 200 for routes that are inserted from 20.20.0.0 network segment :
[P12710|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router rip
Switch(config-router)# network 10.10.0.0/24
Switch(config-router)# network 20.20.0.0/24
Switch(config-router)# distance 200 20.20.0.0/24
[P12711|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P12712|Normal] distance (OSPF)
[P12713|Heading 3] ip rip authentication
[P12714|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P12715|Normal] To enable authentication for Routing Information Protocol (RIP) Version 2 packets and to specify the set of keys that can be used on an interface, use the ip rip authentication command in interface configuration mode. To prevent authentication, use the no form of this command.
[P12716|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P12717|Normal] ip rip authentication ( key-chain NAME-OF-CHAIN | string STRING )
[P12718|Body Text] no ip rip authentication ( key-chain | string )

[TABLE 403] rows=3 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	key-chain NAME-OF-CHAIN	Enables authentication and specifies the group of keys that are valid	A String of key chain name
R3	string STRING	Enables authentication and specifies the authentication string	Up to 16 characters

[P12719|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P12720|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P12721|Heading 4] Default
[P12722|Normal] No authentication is provided for RIP packets.
[P12723|Heading 4] Usage
[P12724|Normal] If neither key chain is configured with the key-chain command nor string is configured with the authentication string command, no authentication is performed on the interface (not even the default authentication). Key chain and authentication string can not be configured on the same interface. If you want configure one, make sure the other is not configured.
[P12725|Heading 4] Examples
[P12726|Normal] The following example configures the interface to accept and send any key belonging to the key chain named trees:
[P12727|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# no switchport

[P12730|Heading 3] ip rip authentication mode
[P12731|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P12732|Normal] To specify the type of authentication used in Routing Information Protocol (RIP) Version 2 packets, use the ip rip authentication mode command in interface configuration mode. To restore clear text authentication, use the no form of this command.
[P12733|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P12734|Normal] ip rip authentication mode ( text | md5 )
[P12735|Body Text] no ip rip authentication mode

R3	md5	Keyed Message Digest 5 (MD5) authentication	-

[P12736|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P12737|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P12738|Heading 4] Default
[P12739|Normal] Clear text authentication is provided for RIP packets.
[P12740|Heading 4] Usage
[P12741|Normal] RIP Version 1 does not support authentication.
[P12742|Heading 4] Examples
[P12743|Normal] The following example configures the interface to use MD5 authentication:
[P12744|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# no switchport
Switch(config-if)# ip rip authentication mode md5

[P12747|Heading 3] ip rip receive version
[P12748|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P12749|Normal] To specify a Routing Information Protocol (RIP) version to receive on an interface basis, use the ip rip receive version command in interface configuration mode. To follow the global version rules, use the no form of this command.
[P12750|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P12751|Normal] ip rip receive version [ 1 | 2 ]
[P12752|Body Text] no ip rip receive version

[TABLE 405] rows=3 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	1	(Optional) Accepts only RIP Version 1 packets on the interface	-
R3	2	(Optional) Accepts only RIP Version 2 packets on the interface	-

[P12753|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P12754|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P12755|Heading 4] Default
[P12756|Normal] Only RIPv2 packet should be received.
[P12757|Heading 4] Usage
[P12758|Normal] Use this command to override the default behavior of RIP as specified by the version command. This command applies only to the interface being configured. You can configure the interface to accept both RIP versions.
[P12759|Heading 4] Examples
[P12760|Normal] The following example configures the interface to receive both RIP Version 1 and Version 2 packets:
[P12761|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# no switchport
Switch(config-if)# ip rip receive version 1 2
[P12762|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P12763|Normal] version (RIP)
[P12764|Heading 3] ip rip receive-packet
[P12765|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P12766|Normal] To enable the interface to receive Routing Information Protocol (RIP) packets, use the ip rip receive-packet command in interface configuration mode. To disable to receive RIP packets, use the no form of this command.
[P12767|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P12768|Normal] ip rip receive-packet
[P12769|Body Text] no ip rip receive-packet
[P12770|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P12771|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P12772|Heading 4] Default
[P12773|Normal] Receive packet is enabled by default.
[P12774|Heading 4] Usage
[P12775|Normal] Use this command to enable or disable the capability of receiving RIP packets, whether the network of this interface is added into RIP or not.
[P12776|Heading 4] Examples

[P12778|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# no switchport
Switch(config-if)# ip rip receive-packet
[P12779|Heading 4] Related Commands

[P12815|Heading 3] ip rip split-horizon
[P12816|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P12817|Normal] To enable the split horizon mechanism for Routing Information Protocol (RIP), use the ip rip split-horizon command in interface configuration mode. To disable the split horizon mechanism, use the no form of this command.
[P12818|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P12819|Normal] ip rip split-horizon ( poisoned | )
[P12820|Body Text] no ip rip split-horizon

[P12821|Heading 4] Command Mode

[P12823|Heading 4] Default
[P12824|Normal] This command is enabled with poisoned reverse by default.
[P12825|Heading 4] Usage
[P12826|Normal] In general, changing the state of the default for the ip rip split-horizon command is not recommended, unless you are certain that your application requires a change in order to properly advertise routes.
[P12827|Heading 4] Examples
[P12828|Normal] The following example enables split horizon without poisoned reverse:
[P12829|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal

[P12832|Heading 3] network (RIP)
[P12833|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P12834|Normal] To specify a list of networks for the Routing Information Protocol (RIP) routing process, use the network command in router configuration mode. To remove an entry, use the no form of this command.
[P12835|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P12836|Normal] network ( PREFIX / PREFIX-LENGTH )
[P12837|Body Text] no network ( PREFIX / PREFIX-LENGTH )

[TABLE 408] rows=3 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	PREFIX	IP route prefix for the network	IPv4 Address
R3	PREFIX-LENGTH	Prefix length for the network	1-32

[P12838|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P12839|Normal] Router Configuration
[P12840|Heading 4] Default
[P12841|Normal] No networks are specified.
[P12842|Heading 4] Usage
[P12843|Normal] There is no limit to the number of network commands you can use on the switch. RIP routing updates will be sent and received only through interfaces on this network.
[P12844|Body Text] RIP sends updates to the interfaces in the specified networks. Also, if the network of an interface is not specified, the interface will not be advertised in any RIP update.
[P12845|Heading 4] Examples
[P12846|Normal] The following example defines RIP as the routing protocol to be used on all interfaces connected to networks 10.99.0.0/16 and 192.168.7.0/24:
[P12847|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router rip
Switch(config-router)# network 10.99.0.0/16
Switch(config-router)# network 192.168.7.0/24
[P12848|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P12849|Normal] router rip
[P12850|Heading 3] neighbor (RIP)
[P12851|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P12852|Normal] To define a neighboring switch with which to exchange routing information, use the neighbor command in router configuration mode. To remove an entry, use the no form of this command.
[P12853|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P12854|Normal] neighbor IP-ADDRESS
[P12855|Body Text] no neighbor IP-ADDRESS

[TABLE 409] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	IP-ADDRESS	IP address of a peer switch with which routing information will be exchanged	IPv4 Address

[P12856|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P12857|Normal] Router Configuration
[P12858|Heading 4] Default
[P12859|Normal] No neighboring switches are defined.
[P12860|Heading 4] Usage
[P12861|Normal] This command permits the point-to-point (non-broadcast) exchange of routing information. When it is used in combination with the passive-interface router configuration command, routing information can be exchanged between a subset of switches and access servers on a LAN.
[P12862|Body Text] Multiple neighbor commands can be used to specify additional neighbors or peers.
[P12863|Heading 4] Examples
[P12864|Normal] In the following example, RIP updates are sent to all interfaces on network 10.108.0.0 except eth-0-1. However, in this case a neighbor switch configuration command is included. This command permits the sending of routing updates to specific neighbors. One copy of the routing update is generated per neighbor:
[P12865|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router rip
Switch(config-router)# network 10.108.0.0/16
Switch(config-router)# passive-interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-router)# neighbor 10.108.20.4
[P12866|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P12867|Normal] router rip
[P12868|Heading 3] offset-list (RIP)
[P12869|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P12870|Normal] To add an offset to incoming and outgoing metrics to routes learned via Routing Information Protocol (RIP), use the offset-list command in router configuration mode. To remove an offset list, use the no form of this command.
[P12871|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P12872|Normal] offset-list ACCESSS-LIST-NAME ( in | out ) METRIC-OFFSET ( IFNAME | )
[P12873|Body Text] no offset-list ( in | out ) ( IFNAME | )

[TABLE 410] rows=6 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	ACCESSS-LIST-NAME	Named access list to be applied	Up to 40 characters
R3	in	Applies the access list to incoming metrics	-
R4	out	Applies the access list to outgoing metrics	-
R5	METRIC-OFFSET	Positive offset to be applied to metrics for networks matching the access list. If the offset is 0, no action is taken	0-16
R6	IFNAME	Interface name to which the offset list is applied	Support physical/aggregation/loopback/vlan/tunnel ports

[P12874|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P12875|Normal] Router Configuration
[P12876|Heading 4] Default
[P12877|Normal] This command is disabled by default.
[P12878|Heading 4] Usage
[P12879|Normal] The offset value is added to the routing metric. An offset list with an interface is considered extended and takes precedence over an offset list that is not extended. Therefore, if an entry passes the extended offset list and the normal offset list, the offset of the extended offset list is added to the metric.
[P12880|Heading 4] Examples
[P12881|Normal] In the following example, the switch applies an offset to the delay component of a switch only to access list 21:
[P12882|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router rip
Switch(config-router)# offset-list 21 out 10
[P12883|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P12884|Normal] None
[P12885|Heading 3] passive-interface (RIP)
[P12886|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P12887|Normal] To disable sending routing updates for the Routing Information Protocol (RIP) on an interface, use the passive-interface command in router configuration mode. To re-enable the sending of routing updates, use the no form of this command.
[P12888|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P12889|Normal] passive-interface IFNAME
[P12890|Body Text] no passive-interface IFNAME

[TABLE 411] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	IFNAME	The interface name	Support physical/aggregation/loopback/vlan/tunnel ports

[P12891|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P12892|Normal] Router Configuration
[P12893|Heading 4] Default
[P12894|Normal] Routing updates are sent on the interface.
[P12895|Heading 4] Usage
[P12896|Normal] If you disable the sending of routing updates on an interface, the particular subnet will continue to be advertised to other interfaces, and updates from other switches on that interface continue to be received and processed.
[P12897|Heading 4] Examples
[P12898|Normal] The following example sets the interface eth-0-1 as passive:
[P12899|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router rip
Switch(config-router)# network 10.108.0.0/16
Switch(config-router)# passive-interface eth-0-1
[P12900|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P12901|Normal] router rip
[P12902|Heading 3] redistribute (RIP)
[P12903|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P12904|Normal] To redistribute routes from one routing domain into RIP routing domain, use the redistribute command in router configuration mode. To disable redistribution, use the no form of this command.
[P12905|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P12906|Normal] redistribute PROTOCOL { [ metric VALUE ] | route-map WORD }
[P12907|Body Text] no redistribute PROTOCOL

[TABLE 412] rows=5 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	PROTOCOL	(Optional) The name of a routing protocol, or the keyword connected, or static. If you specify a routing protocol, use one of the following keywords: bgp, and ospf，connected,isis	bgp/ospf/connected/isis/static/isis
R3	metric VALUE	(Optional) When redistributing other routing process to the RIP process, the default metric is 0 if no metric value is specified	1-16
R4	route-map	Route map reference	-
R5	WORD	Pointer to route-map entries	Up to 20 characters

[P12908|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P12909|Normal] Router Configuration
[P12910|Heading 4] Default
[P12911|Normal] Route redistribution is disabled.
[P12912|Body Text] Metric metric-value: 0
[P12913|Heading 4] Usage
[P12914|Normal] The metric value specified in the redistribute command supersedes the metric value specified using the default-metric command.
[P12915|Heading 4] Examples
[P12916|Normal] The following examples redistribute the static routes into RIP with metric 10:
[P12917|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router rip
Switch(config-router)# network 10.108.0.0/16
Switch(config-router)# redistribute static metric 10

[P12924|Normal] router rip
[P12925|Body Text] no router rip

[P12927|Normal] Global Configuration

[P12929|Normal] None
[P12930|Heading 4] Usage
[P12931|Normal] None

[P12933|Normal] The following example shows how to enter the RIP routing configuration:

[P12936|Normal] network (RIP)
[P12937|Heading 3] timers basic (RIP)
[P12938|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P12939|Normal] To adjust Routing Information Protocol (RIP) network timers, use the timers basic command in router configuration mode. To restore the default timers, use the no form of this command.
[P12940|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P12941|Normal] timers basic UPDATE TIMEOUT INVALID
[P12942|Body Text] no timers basic

[TABLE 413] rows=4 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	UPDATE	Rate (in seconds) at which updates are sent. This is the fundamental timing parameter of the routing protocol.	<5-2147483647>, default 30s
R3	TIMEOUT	Time (in seconds) after which a route is declared invalid without updates that refresh the route. The route then enters into an invalid state and is not used for forwarding packets.	It is marked inaccessible and advertised as unreachable. <5-2147483647>, default 180s
R4	INVALID	Time after which an invalid route is removed from RIP routing database.	<5-2147483647>, default 120s

[P12943|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P12944|Normal] Router Configuration
[P12945|Heading 4] Default
[P12946|Normal] update: 30 seconds
[P12947|Body Text] timeout: 180 seconds
[P12948|Body Text] invalid: 120 seconds
[P12949|Heading 4] Usage
[P12950|Normal] The basic timing parameters for RIP are adjustable. Because RIP is executing a distributed, asynchronous routing algorithm, these timers must be the same for all switches and access servers in the network.
[P12951|Body Text] In addition, an address family can have explicitly specified timers that apply to that address-family only. The timers basic command must be specified for an address family or the system Default for the timers basic command are used regardless of what is configured for RIP routing.
[P12952|Heading 4] Examples
[P12953|Normal] The following example sets updates to be broadcast every 5 seconds. If a switch is not heard from in 15 seconds, the route is declared unusable. And after 15 seconds the invalid route will be removed from RIP routing database:
[P12954|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router rip
Switch(config-router)# timers basic 5 15 15
