[P13122|Heading 2] OSPF Commands
[P13123|Heading 3] area authentication
[P13124|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P13125|Normal] To enable authentication for an Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) area, use the area authentication command in router configuration mode. To remove an authentication specification of an area or a specified area from the configuration, use the no form of this command.
[P13126|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P13127|Normal] area AREA-ID authentication ( message-digest | )
[P13128|Body Text] no area AREA-ID authentication

[TABLE 421] rows=3 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	AREA-ID	Identifier of the area for which authentication is to be enabled. The identifier can be specified as either a decimal value or an IP address	IP address or number in the range of 0-4294967295
R3	message-digest	(Optional) Enables Message Digest 5 (MD5) authentication on the area specified by the area-id argument	-

[P13129|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P13130|Normal] Router Configuration
[P13131|Heading 4] Default
[P13132|Normal] Type 0 authentication (no authentication)
[P13133|Heading 4] Usage
[P13134|Normal] Specifying authentication for an area sets the authentication to Type 1 (simple password) as specified in RFC 1247. If this command is not included in the configuration file, authentication of Type 0 (no authentication) is assumed.
[P13135|Body Text] The authentication type must be the same for all routers and access servers in an area. The authentication password for all OSPF routers on a network must be the same if they are to communicate with each other via OSPF. Use the ip ospf authentication-key interface command to specify this password.
[P13136|Body Text] If you enable MD5 authentication with the message-digest keyword, you must configure a password with the ip ospf message-digest-key interface command.
[P13137|Body Text] To remove the authentication specification for an area, use the no form of this command with the authentication keyword.
[P13138|Heading 4] Examples
[P13139|Normal] The following example mandates authentication for areas 0 and 10.0.0.0 of OSPF routing process 201. Authentication keys are also provided:
[P13140|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# no switchport
Switch(config-if)# ip address 192.168.251.201/24
Switch(config-if)# ip ospf authentication-key adcdefgh
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-2
Switch(config-if)# no switchport
Switch(config-if)# ip address 10.56.0.201/16
Switch(config-if)# ip ospf authentication-key ijklmnop
Switch(config)# router ospf 201
Switch(config-router)# network 10.0.0.0 0.255.255.255 area 10.0.0.0
Switch(config-router)# network 192.168.0.0/16 area 0
Switch(config-router)# area 10.0.0.0 authentication
Switch(config-router)# area 0 authentication
[P13141|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P13142|Normal] ip ospf authentication-key
[P13143|Heading 3] area default-cost
[P13144|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P13145|Normal] To specify a cost for the default summary route sent into a stub, use the area default-cost command in router configuration mode. To remove the assigned default route cost, use the no form of this command.
[P13146|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P13147|Normal] area AREA-ID default-cost COST
[P13148|Body Text] no area AREA-ID default-cost

[TABLE 422] rows=3 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	AREA-ID	Identifier of the area for which authentication is to be enabled. The identifier can be specified as either a decimal value or an IP address	IP address or number in the range of 0-4294967295
R3	COST	default cost value	0-16777214

[P13149|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P13150|Normal] Router Configuration
[P13151|Heading 4] Default
[P13152|Normal] COST: 1
[P13153|Heading 4] Usage
[P13154|Normal] The command is used only on an Area Border Router (ABR) attached to a stub.
[P13155|Body Text] There are two stub area router configuration commands: the stub and default-cost options of the area command. In all routers and access servers attached to the stub area, the area should be configured as a stub area using the stub option of the area command. Use the default-cost option only on an ABR attached to the stub area. The default-cost option provides the metric for the summary default route generated by the ABR into the stub area.
[P13156|Heading 4] Examples
[P13157|Normal] The following example shows how to configure a stub area and set its COST value:
[P13158|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# no switchport
Switch(config-if)# ip address 10.56.0.201/16
Switch(config)# router ospf 201
Switch(config-router)# network 10.0.0.0/8 area 10.0.0.0
Switch(config-router)# area 10.0.0.0 stub
Switch(config-router)# area 10.0.0.0 default-cost 20
[P13159|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P13160|Normal] None
[P13161|Heading 3] area filter-list
[P13162|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P13163|Normal] To filter prefixes advertised in type 3 link-state advertisements (LSAs) between Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) areas of an Area Border Router (ABR), use the area filter-list command in router configuration mode. To change or cancel the filter, use the no form of this command.
[P13164|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P13165|Normal] area AREA-ID filter-list ( access ACCESSS-LIST-NAME | prefix PREFIX-LIST-NAME ) ( in | out )
[P13166|Body Text] no area AREA-ID filter-list ( access ACCESSS-LIST-NAME | prefix PREFIX-LIST-NAME ) ( in | out )

[TABLE 423] rows=8 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	AREA-ID	Identifier of the area for which authentication is to be enabled. The identifier can be specified as either a decimal value or an IP address	IP address or number in the range of 0-4294967295
R3	access	Indicates that an accesslist is used	-
R4	ACCESSS-LIST-NAME	Name of an access list	A string with 1-20 characters
R5	prefix	Indicates that a prefix list is used	-
R6	PREFIX-LIST-NAME	Name of a prefix list	A string with 1-20 characters
R7	in	Access list or prefix list applied to prefixes advertised to the specified area from other areas	-
R8	out	Access list or prefix list applied to prefixes advertised out of the specified area to other areas	-

[P13167|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P13168|Normal] Router Configuration
[P13169|Heading 4] Default
[P13170|Normal] This command has no default behavior.
[P13171|Heading 4] Usage
[P13172|Normal] With this feature enabled in the “in” direction, all type 3 LSAs originated by the ABR to this area, based on information from all other areas, are filtered by the prefix list. Type 3 LSAs that were originated as a result of the area range command in another area are treated like any other type 3 LSA that was originated individually. Any prefix that does not match an entry in the prefix list is implicitly denied.
[P13173|Body Text] With this feature enabled in the “out” direction, all type 3 LSAs advertised by the ABR, based on information from this area to all other areas, are filtered by the prefix list. If the area range command has been configured for this area, type 3 LSAs that correspond to the area range are sent to all other areas, only if at least one prefix in the area range matches an entry in the prefix list.
[P13174|Body Text] If all specific prefixes are denied by the prefix list, type 3 LSAs that correspond to the area range command will not be sent to any other area. Prefixes that are not permitted by the prefix list are implicitly denied.
[P13175|Heading 4] Examples
[P13176|Normal] The following example filters prefixes that are sent from all other areas to area 1:
[P13177|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router ospf 201
Switch(config-router)# area 1 filter-list prefix AREA_1 in
[P13178|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P13179|Normal] area range
[P13180|Heading 3] area range
[P13181|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P13182|Normal] To consolidate and summarize routes at an area boundary, use the area range command in router configuration mode. To disable this function, use the no form of this command.
[P13183|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P13184|Normal] area AREA-ID range ( ADDRESS MASK | ADDRESS / PREFIX-LENGTH ) ( advertise | not-advertise | )
[P13185|Body Text] no area AREA-ID range ( ADDRESS MASK | ADDRESS / PREFIX-LENGTH }

[TABLE 424] rows=6 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	AREA-ID	Identifier of the area for which authentication is to be enabled. The identifier can be specified as either a decimal value or an IP address	IP address or number in the range of 0-4294967295
R3	ADDRESS	IPv4 address	IPv4 Address
R4	PREFIX-LENGTH	Prefix length of the address	1-32
R5	advertise	Advertise this range (default)	-
R6	not-advertise	Do not advertise this range	-

[P13186|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P13187|Normal] Router Configuration
[P13188|Heading 4] Default
[P13189|Normal] This command is disabled by default.
[P13190|Heading 4] Usage
[P13191|Normal] The area range command is used only with Area Border Routers (ABRs). It is used to consolidate or summarize routes for an area. The result is that a single summary route is advertised to other areas by the ABR. Routing information is condensed at area boundaries. External to the area, a single route is advertised for each address range. This behavior is called route summarization.
[P13192|Body Text] Multiple area router configuration commands specifying the range option can be configured. Thus, OSPF can summarize addresses for many different sets of address ranges.
[P13193|Heading 4] Examples
[P13194|Normal] The following example specifies one summary route to be advertised by the ABR to other areas for all subnets on network 10.0.0.0 and for all hosts on network 192.168.110.0:
[P13195|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# no switchport
Switch(config-if)# ip address 192.168.110.201/24
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-2
Switch(config-if)# no switchport
Switch(config-if)# ip address 192.168.120.201/24
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-3
Switch(config-if)# no switchport
Switch(config-if)# ip address 10.0.0.0/8
Switch(config)# router ospf 201
Switch(config-router)# network 192.168.110.0/24 area 0
Switch(config-router)# area 10.0.0.0 range 10.0.0.0/8
Switch(config-router)# area 0 range 192.168.110.0 255.255.0.0
[P13196|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P13197|Normal] None
[P13198|Heading 3] area stub
[P13199|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P13200|Normal] To define an area as a stub area, use the area stub command in router configuration mode. To disable this function, use the no form of this command.
[P13201|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P13202|Normal] area AREA-ID stub ( no-summary | )
[P13203|Body Text] no area AREA-ID stub ( no-summary | )

[TABLE 425] rows=3 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	AREA-ID	Identifier of the area for which authentication is to be enabled. The identifier can be specified as either a decimal value or an IP address	IP address or number in the range of 0-4294967295
R3	no-summary	(Optional) Prevents an Area Border Router (ABR) from sending summary link advertisements into the stub area	-

[P13204|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P13205|Normal] Router Configuration
[P13206|Heading 4] Default
[P13207|Normal] No stub area is defined.
[P13208|Heading 4] Usage
[P13209|Normal] You must configure the area stub command on all routers and access servers in the stub area. Use the area router configuration command with the default-cost keyword to specify the cost of a default internal router sent into a stub area by an ABR.
[P13210|Body Text] There are two stub area router configuration commands: the stub and default-cost options of the area router configuration command. In all routers attached to the stub area, the area should be configured as a stub area using the stub keyword of the area command. Use the default-cost keyword only on an ABR attached to the stub area. The default-cost keyword provides the metric for the summary default route generated by the ABR into the stub area.
[P13211|Body Text] To further reduce the number of link-state advertisements (LSAs) sent into a stub area, you can configure the no-summary keyword on the ABR to prevent it from sending summary LSAs (LSA type 3) into the stub area.
[P13212|Heading 4] Examples
[P13213|Normal] The following example shows how to configure a stub area and set its COST value:
[P13214|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# no switchport
Switch(config-if)# ip address 10.56.0.201/16
Switch(config)# router ospf 201
Switch(config-router)# network 10.0.0.0/8 area 10.0.0.0
Switch(config-router)# area 10.0.0.0 stub
Switch(config-router)# area 10.0.0.0 default-cost 20
[P13215|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P13216|Normal] None
[P13217|Heading 3] area nssa
[P13218|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P13219|Normal] To define an area as a NSSA area, use the area nssa command in router configuration mode. To disable this function, use the no form of this command.
[P13220|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P13221|Normal] area AREA-ID nssa ( translator-role ( candidate | never | always ) | ) ( no-summary | ) ( no-redistribution | ) ( default-information-originate { metric METRIC_VALUE | metric-type TYPE-VALUE | } | )
[P13222|Body Text] no area AREA-ID nssa ( translator-role | ) ( no-summary | ) ( no-redistribution | ) ( default-information-originate | )

[TABLE 426] rows=10 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	AREA-ID	Identifier of the area for which authentication is to be enabled. The identifier can be specified as either a decimal value or an IP address	IP address or number in the range of 0-4294967295
R3	candidate	(Optional) Configure the role for ABR in NSSA area as candidate for the translator router	-
R4	never	(Optional) Configure the role for ABR in NSSA area as non-translator router	-
R5	always	(Optional) Configure the role for ABR in NSSA area as the specified translator router	-
R6	no-summary	(Optional) Prevents an Area Border Router (ABR) from sending Summary LSAs into the NSSA area	-
R7	no-redistribution	(Optional) Prevents an Area Border Router (ABR) from importing routes into the NSSA area	-
R8	default-information-originate	(Optional) Configure an ASBR to send default type 7 LSA into the NSSA area	-
R9	metric METRIC_VALUE	(Optional) Configure metric for the default originate route	0-16777214
R10	metric-type TYPE-VALUE	(Optional) Configure metric type for the default originate route	1-2

[P13223|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P13224|Normal] Router Configuration
[P13225|Heading 4] Default
[P13226|Normal] No NSSA area is defined.
[P13227|Heading 4] Usage
[P13228|Normal] No NSSA area is configured as default. You must configure the area nssa command on all routers and access servers in the NSSA area.
[P13229|Body Text] There are many similarities between NSSA and stub area, neither of which propagates external routes from other area. The difference is that NSSA area can introduce and propagate external routes to the OSPF autonomous domain, while STUB area can not introduce external routes.
[P13230|Heading 4] Examples
[P13231|Normal] The following example shows how to configure a NSSA area :
[P13232|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# no switchport
Switch(config-if)# ip address 10.56.0.201/16
Switch(config)# router ospf 201
Switch(config-router)# network 10.0.0.0/8 area 10.0.0.0
Switch(config-router)# area 10.0.0.0 nssa
[P13233|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P13234|Normal] None
[P13235|Heading 3] auto-cost
[P13236|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P13237|Normal] To control how Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) calculates default metrics for the interface, use the auto-cost command in router configuration mode. To assign cost based only on the interface type, use the no form of this command.
[P13238|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P13239|Normal] auto-cost reference-bandwidth RATE
[P13240|Body Text] no auto-cost reference-bandwidth

[TABLE 427] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	RATE	Rate in Mbps (bandwidth).	1-4294967

[P13241|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P13242|Normal] Router Configuration
[P13243|Heading 4] Default
[P13244|Normal] 100 Mbps
[P13245|Heading 4] Usage
[P13246|Normal] The value set by the ip ospf cost command overrides the cost resulting from the auto-cost command.Bandwidth dividing port rate is cost.
[P13247|Heading 4] Examples
[P13248|Normal] The following example changes the cost of the cost link to 1GBps:
[P13249|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router ospf 1
Switch(config-router)# auto-cost reference-bandwidth 1000
[P13250|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P13251|Normal] ip ospf cost
[P13252|Heading 3] clear ip ospf
[P13253|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P13254|Normal] To clear redistribution based on the Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) routing process ID, use the clear ip ospf command in privileged EXEC mode.
[P13255|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P13256|Normal] clear ip ospf ( PID | ) process

[TABLE 428] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	PID	(Optional) Process ID	0-65535

[P13257|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P13258|Normal] Privileged EXEC
[P13259|Heading 4] Default
[P13260|Normal] None
[P13261|Heading 4] Usage
[P13262|Normal] Use the PID argument to clear only one OSPF process. If the PID argument is not specified, all OSPF processes are cleared.
[P13263|Heading 4] Examples
[P13264|Normal] The following example clears all OSPF processes:
[P13265|Terminal Display] Switch# clear ip ospf process
[P13266|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P13267|Normal] None
[P13268|Heading 3] compatible rfc1583
[P13269|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P13270|Normal] To restore the method used to calculate summary route costs per RFC 1583, use the compatible rfc1583 command in router configuration mode. To disable RFC 1583 compatibility, use the no form of this command.
[P13271|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P13272|Normal] compatible rfc1583
[P13273|Body Text] no compatible rfc1583
[P13274|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P13275|Normal] Router Configuration
[P13276|Heading 4] Default
[P13277|Normal] Not compatible with RFC 1583.
[P13278|Heading 4] Usage
[P13279|Normal] To minimize the chance of routing loops, all Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) routers in an OSPF routing domain should have RFC compatibility set identically.
[P13280|Body Text] Because of the introduction of RFC 2328, OSPF Version 2, the method used to calculate summary route costs has changed. Use the no compatible rfc1583 command to enable the calculation method used per RFC 2328.
[P13281|Heading 4] Examples
[P13282|Normal] The following example specifies that the router process is compatible with RFC 1583:
[P13283|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router ospf 1
Switch(config-router)# compatible rfc1583
[P13284|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P13285|Normal] None
[P13286|Heading 3] default-information originate (OSPF)
[P13287|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P13288|Normal] To generate a default external route into an Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) routing domain, use the default-information originate command in router configuration mode. To disable this feature, use the no form of this command.
[P13289|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P13290|Normal] default-information originate ( route-map WORD | always | metric METRIC-VALUE | metric-type TYPE-VALUE | )
[P13291|Body Text] no default-information originate ( route-map WORD | always | metric | metric-type | )

[TABLE 429] rows=5 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	always	(Optional) Always advertises the default route regardless of whether the system has a default route	-
R3	metric METRIC-VALUE	metric-value (Optional) Metric used for generating the default route. If you omit a value and do not specify a value using the default-metric router configuration command, the default metric value is 1.	0-16777214
R4	metric-type TYPE-VALUE	(Optional) External link type associated with the default route advertised into the OSPF routing domain.It can be type 1 or type 2 LSA	1-2
R5	route-map WORD	Route map reference	A string with 1-20 characters

[P13292|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P13293|Normal] Router Configuration
[P13294|Heading 4] Default
[P13295|Normal] This command is disabled by default.
[P13296|Heading 4] Usage
[P13297|Normal] Whenever you use the redistribute or the default-information router configuration command to redistribute routes into an OSPF routing domain, the switch automatically becomes an autonomous System Boundary Router (ASBR). However, an ASBR does not, by default, generate a default route into the OSPF routing domain. The system still must have a default route for itself before it generates one, except when you have specified the always keyword.
[P13298|Heading 4] Examples
[P13299|Normal] The following example specifies a metric for the default route redistributed into the OSPF routing domain and an external metric type:
[P13300|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router ospf 109
Switch(config-router)# redistribute rip metric 100
Switch(config-router)# default-information originate metric 100 metric-type 1
[P13301|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P13302|Normal] redistribute (OSPF)
[P13303|Heading 3] default-metric (OSPF)
[P13304|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P13305|Normal] To set default metric values for the Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) routing protocol, use the default-metric command in router configuration mode. To return to the default state, use the no form of this command.
[P13306|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P13307|Normal] default-metric METRIC-VALUE
[P13308|Body Text] no default-metric

[TABLE 430] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	METRIC-VALUE	Default metric value appropriate for the specified routing protocol.	0-16777214

[P13309|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P13310|Normal] Router Configuration
[P13311|Heading 4] Default
[P13312|Normal] 1 for BGP routes
[P13313|Body Text] 20 for others
[P13314|Heading 4] Usage
[P13315|Normal] The default-metric command is used in conjunction with the redistribute router configuration command to cause the current routing protocol to use the same metric value for all redistributed routes.
[P13316|Heading 4] Examples
[P13317|Normal] The example advertises OSPF-derived routes using RIP and assigns the Internal Gateway Protocol (IGP)-derived routes a RIP metric of 10.:
[P13318|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router ospf
Switch(config-router)# default-metric 10
Switch(config-router)# redistribute rip
[P13319|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P13320|Normal] redistribute (OSPF)
[P13321|Heading 3] distance (OSPF)
[P13322|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P13323|Normal] To define Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) route administrative distances based on route type, use the distance command in router configuration mode. To restore the default value, use the no form of this command.
[P13324|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P13325|Normal] distance { DISTANCE | ospf [ external DIST1 ] [ inter-area DIST2 ] | [ intra-area DIST3 ] }
[P13326|Body Text] no distance { DISTANCE | ospf }

[TABLE 431] rows=5 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	DISTANCE	Administrative distance. An integer from 1 to 255. (Routes with a distance value of 255 are not installed in the routing table.)	1-255
R3	external DIST1	(Optional) Sets the distance for routes from other routing domains, learned by redistribution. Range is 1 to 255.	1-255
R4	inter-area DIST2	(Optional) Sets the distance for all routes from one area to another area. Range is 1 to 255.	1-255
R5	intra-area DIST3	(Optional) Sets the distance for all routes within an area. Range is 1 to 255.	1-255

[P13327|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P13328|Normal] Router Configuration
[P13329|Heading 4] Default
[P13330|Normal] DIST1: 110
[P13331|Body Text] DIST2: 110
[P13332|Body Text] DIST3: 110
[P13333|Heading 4] Usage
[P13334|Normal] You may specify one of the keywords or use distance only to apply to all types of routes.
[P13335|Body Text] The distance command allows you to set a distance for an entire group of routes, rather than a specific route that passes an access list.
[P13336|Body Text] A common reason to use the distance command is when you have multiple OSPF processes with mutual redistribution, and you want to prefer internal routes from one over external routes from the other.
[P13337|Heading 4] Examples
[P13338|Normal] The example advertises OSPF-derived routes using RIP and assigns the Internal Gateway Protocol (IGP)-derived routes a RIP distance of 90:
[P13339|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router ospf
Switch(config-router)# distance 90
Switch(config-router)# redistribute rip
[P13340|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P13341|Normal] None
[P13342|Heading 3] distribute-list (OSPF)
[P13343|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P13344|Normal] To filter networks received in updates or suppress networks from being advertised in updates, use the distribute-list command in router configuration mode. To cancel this function, use the no form of this command.
[P13345|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P13346|Normal] distribute-list prefix PREIFX-LIST-NAME ( in | out )

[TABLE 432] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	PREFIX-LIST-NAME	Name of a prefix list to be applied	A string with 1-20 characters

[P13347|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P13348|Normal] Router Configuration
[P13349|Heading 4] Default
[P13350|Normal] None
[P13351|Heading 4] Usage
[P13352|Normal] This command must specify an access list.
[P13353|Heading 4] Examples
[P13354|Normal] In the following example, OSPF process 1 is configured to accept network 20.0.0.0/8.:
[P13355|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal

Switch(config)# ip prefix-list plist permit 20.0.0.0/8


Switch(config)# router ospf
Switch(config-router)# network 20.0.0.0/8 area 0
Switch(config-router)# distribute-list prefix plist in
[P13356|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P13357|Normal] None
[P13358|Heading 3] distribute-list (OSPF)
[P13359|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P13360|Normal] To filter networks received in updates or suppress networks from being advertised in updates, use the distribute-list command in router configuration mode. To cancel this function, use the no form of this command.
[P13361|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P13362|Normal] distribute-list ACCESSS-LIST-NAME ( in | out )
[P13363|Body Text] no distribute-list ACCESSS-LIST-NAME ( in | out )

[TABLE 433] rows=4 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	ACCESSS-LIST-NAME	Name of an access list to be applied	A string with 1-20 characters
R3	in	Filter networks received in updates	-
R4	out	Suppress networks from being advertised in updates	-

[P13364|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P13365|Normal] Router Configuration
[P13366|Heading 4] Default
[P13367|Normal] None
[P13368|Heading 4] Usage
[P13369|Normal] This command must specify an access list.
[P13370|Heading 4] Examples
[P13371|Normal] In the following example, OSPF process 1 is configured to accept two networks, network 20.0.0.0 and network 10.108.0.0:
[P13372|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ip access-list acl1
Switch(config-ip-acl)# permit any 20.0.0.0 0.0.255.255 any
Switch(config-ip-acl)# permit any 10.108.0.0 0.0.255.255 any
Switch(config-ip-acl)# deny any any any
Switch(config)# router ospf 1
Switch(config-router)# network 10.108.0.0/16 area 1
Switch(config-router)# distribute-list acl1 in

[P13375|Heading 3] ip ospf authentication
[P13376|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P13377|Normal] To specify the authentication type for an interface, use the ip ospf authentication command in interface configuration mode. To remove the authentication type for an interface, use the no form of this command.
[P13378|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P13379|Normal] ip ospf authentication ( message-digest | null | )
[P13380|Body Text] no ip ospf authentication

[TABLE 434] rows=3 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	message-digest	(Optional) Specifies that message-digest authentication will be used	-
R3	null	(Optional) No authentication is used. Useful for overriding password or message-digest authentication if configured for an area	-

[P13381|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P13382|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P13383|Heading 4] Default
[P13384|Normal] The area default is no authentication (null authentication).
[P13385|Heading 4] Usage
[P13386|Normal] Before using the ip ospf authentication command, configure a password for the interface using the ip ospf authentication-key command. If you use the ip ospf authentication message-digest command, configure the message-digest key for the interface with the ip ospf message-digest-key command.
[P13387|Heading 4] Examples
[P13388|Normal] The following example enables message-digest authentication:
[P13389|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# ip ospf authentication message-digest

[P13394|Heading 3] ip ospf authentication-key
[P13395|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P13396|Normal] To assign a password to be used by neighboring routers that are using the Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) simple password authentication, use the ip ospf authentication-key command in interface configuration mode. To remove a previously assigned OSPF password, use the no form of this command.
[P13397|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P13398|Normal] ip ospf authentication-key ( 8 | ) PASSWORD
[P13399|Body Text] no ip ospf authentication-key

[TABLE 435] rows=3 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	PASSWORD	Any continuous printable string of characters that can be entered from the keyboard up to 8 bytes in length	A string with 8 characters
R3	(8\|)	Specifies a hidden password will follow	-

[P13400|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P13401|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P13402|Heading 4] Default
[P13403|Normal] No password is specified.
[P13404|Heading 4] Usage
[P13405|Normal] The password created by this command is used as a “key” that is inserted directly into the OSPF header when the switch originates routing protocol packets. A separate password can be assigned to each network on a per-interface basis. All neighboring routers on the same network must have the same password to be able to exchange OSPF information.
[P13406|Heading 4] Examples
[P13407|Normal] The following example enables the authentication key with the string yourpass:
[P13408|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# no switchport
Switch(config-if)# ip ospf authentication-key yourpass
[P13409|Normal] The following example enables the authentication key with the encrypt password 91c38996a1aa5699:
[P13410|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-2
Switch(config-if)# no switchport
Switch(config-if)# ip ospf authentication-key 8 91c38996a1aa5699
[P13411|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P13412|Normal] area authentication
[P13413|Body Text] ip ospf authentication
[P13414|Heading 3] ip ospf cost
[P13415|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P13416|Normal] To explicitly specify the cost of sending a packet on an interface, use the ip ospf cost command in interface configuration mode. To reset the path cost to the default value, use the no form of this command.
[P13417|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P13418|Normal] ip ospf cost INTERFACE-COST
[P13419|Body Text] no ip ospf cost

[TABLE 436] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	INTERFACE-COST	The cost of sending a packet on an interface	1-65535

[P13420|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P13421|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P13422|Heading 4] Default
[P13423|Normal] Different port rate has different default cost.
[P13424|Heading 4] Usage
[P13425|Normal] You can set the metric manually using this command, if you need to change the default. Using the bandwidth command changes the link cost as long as this command is not used.
[P13426|Heading 4] Examples
[P13427|Normal] The following example sets the interface cost value to 65:
[P13428|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# no switchport
Switch(config-if)# ip ospf cost 65
[P13429|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P13430|Normal] auto-cost reference bandwidth
[P13431|Heading 3] ip ospf database-filter all out
[P13432|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P13433|Normal] To filter outgoing link-state advertisements (LSAs) to an Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) interface, use the ip ospf database-filter all out command in interface configuration mode. To restore the forwarding of LSAs to the interface, use the no form of this command.
[P13434|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P13435|Normal] ip ospf database-filter all out
[P13436|Body Text] no ip ospf database-filter
[P13437|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P13438|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P13439|Heading 4] Default
[P13440|Normal] This command is disabled by default. All outgoing LSAs are flooded to the interface.
[P13441|Heading 4] Usage
[P13442|Normal] OSPF floods new LSAs over all interfaces in an area, except the interface on which the LSA arrives. This redundancy ensures robust flooding. However, too much redundancy can waste bandwidth and might lead to excessive link and CPU usage in certain topologies, resulting in destabilizing the network. To avoid this, use the database-filter command to block flooding of LSAs over specified interfaces.
[P13443|Heading 4] Examples
[P13444|Normal] The following example prevents flooding of OSPF LSAs to broadcast, nonbroadcast, or point-to-point networks reachable through the interface eth-0-1:
[P13445|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# no switchport
Switch(config-if)# ip ospf database-filter all out
[P13446|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P13447|Normal] None
[P13448|Heading 3] ip ospf dead-interval
[P13449|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P13450|Normal] To set the interval during which at least one hello packet must be received from a neighbor before the router declares that neighbor down, use the ip ospf dead-interval command in interface configuration mode. To restore the default value, use the no form of this command.
[P13451|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P13452|Normal] ip ospf dead-interval SECONDS
[P13453|Body Text] no ip ospf dead-interval

[TABLE 437] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	SECONDS	The interval during which at least one hello packet must be received from a neighbor before the router declares that neighbor down. The value must be the same for all nodes on the network	1-65535

[P13454|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P13455|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P13456|Heading 4] Default
[P13457|Normal] SECONDS: The neighbor is been considered as dead in 40s by default.
[P13458|Heading 4] Usage
[P13459|Normal] The dead interval is advertised in OSPF hello packets. This value must be the same for all networking devices on a specific network.
[P13460|Body Text] Specifying a smaller dead interval (seconds) will give faster detection of a neighbor being down and improve convergence, but might cause more routing instability.
[P13461|Heading 4] Examples
[P13462|Normal] The following example sets the OSPF dead interval to 20 seconds:
[P13463|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# no switchport
Switch(config-if)# ip ospf dead-interval 20
[P13464|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P13465|Normal] ip ospf hello-interval
[P13466|Body Text] show ip ospf interface
[P13467|Heading 3] ip ospf hello-interval
[P13468|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P13469|Normal] To specify the interval between hello packets that the switch sends on the interface, use the ip ospf hello-interval command in interface configuration mode. To return to the default time, use the no form of this command.
[P13470|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P13471|Normal] ip ospf hello-interval SECONDS
[P13472|Body Text] no ip ospf hello-interval

[TABLE 438] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	SECONDS	Interval (in seconds) during which the router must receive at least one hello packet from a neighbor or else that neighbor is removed from the peer list and does not participate in routing. The range is 1 to 65535. The value must be the same for all nodes on the network	1-65535

[P13473|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P13474|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P13475|Heading 4] Default
[P13476|Normal] 10 seconds (Ethernet)
[P13477|Body Text] 30 seconds (non-broadcast)
[P13478|Heading 4] Usage
[P13479|Normal] This value is advertised in the hello packets. The smaller the hello interval, the faster topological changes will be detected, but more routing traffic will ensue. This value must be the same for all routers and access servers on a specific network.
[P13480|Heading 4] Examples
[P13481|Normal] The following example sets the interval between hello packets to 15 seconds:
[P13482|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# no switchport
Switch(config-if)# ip ospf hello-interval 15
[P13483|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P13484|Normal] ip ospf dead-interval
[P13485|Heading 3] ip ospf message-digest-key md5
[P13486|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P13487|Normal] To enable Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) Message Digest 5 (MD5) authentication, use the ip ospf message-digest-key command in interface configuration mode. To remove an old MD5 key, use the no form of this command.
[P13488|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P13489|Normal] ip ospf message-digest-key KEY-ID md5 ( 8 | ) KEY
[P13490|Body Text] no ip ospf message-digest-key KEY-ID

[TABLE 439] rows=4 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	KEY-ID	An identifier in the range from 1 to 255	1-255
R3	(8\|)	Specifies a hidden password will follow	-
R4	KEY	Alphanumeric password of up to 16 bytes	A string with 1-16 characters

[P13491|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P13492|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P13493|Heading 4] Default
[P13494|Normal] OSPF MD5 authentication is disabled.
[P13495|Heading 4] Usage
[P13496|Normal] All routers access the same network/sub network share the same password when using this type of authentication. For every OSPF packet, the password is used for generating/examining the “message digest” which is at the tail of the OSPF packet. This “message digest” is processed by OSPF packet and password. There may multiple password be activated on the same interface, this command line always used to transit smoothly to the new password from the old one.
[P13497|Heading 4] Examples
[P13498|Normal] The following example sets a new key 19 with the password 8ry4222:
[P13499|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# no switchport
Switch(config-if)# ip ospf message-digest-key 10 md5 xvv560qle
Switch(config-if)# ip ospf message-digest-key 19 md5 8ry4222
[P13500|Normal] The following example sets a new key 2 with the encrypt password 91c38996a1aa5699:
[P13501|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# no switchport
Switch(config-if)# ip ospf message-digest-key 2 md5 8 91c38996a1aa5699

[P13504|Body Text] service password-encryption

[P13506|Heading 3] ip ospf mtu
[P13507|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P13508|Normal] To set the MTU value when sending Database Descriptor (DD) packets, use the ip ospf mtu command in interface configuration mode. To restore a default value, use the no form of this command.
[P13509|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P13510|Normal] ip ospf mtu MTU-VALUE
[P13511|Body Text] no ip ospf mtu

[TABLE 440] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	MTU-VALUE	MTU value	576-65535

[P13512|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P13513|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P13514|Heading 4] Default
[P13515|Normal] Decided by interface mtu
[P13516|Heading 4] Usage
[P13517|Normal] Whenever OSPF constructs packets, it uses interface MTU size as Maximum IP packet size. This command forces OSPF to use the specified value overriding the actual interface MTU size.
[P13518|Body Text] This command allows an administrator to configure the MTU size recognized by the OSPF protocol. It does not configure the MTU settings on the kernel. OSPF will not recognize MTU size configuration changes made to the kernel until the MTU size is updated through the CLI.
[P13519|Heading 4] Examples
[P13520|Normal] The following example sets a new MTU value when sending OSPF DD packets:
[P13521|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# no switchport
Switch(config-if)# ip ospf mtu 1280
[P13522|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P13523|Normal] ip ospf mtu-ignore
[P13524|Heading 3] ip ospf mtu-ignore
[P13525|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P13526|Normal] To disable Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) maximum transmission unit (MTU) mismatch detection on receiving Database Descriptor (DD) packets, use the ip ospf mtu-ignore command in interface configuration mode. To reset to default, use the no form of this command.
[P13527|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P13528|Normal] ip ospf mtu-ignore
[P13529|Body Text] no ip ospf mtu-ignore
[P13530|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P13531|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P13532|Heading 4] Default
[P13533|Normal] OSPF MTU mismatch detection is enabled.
[P13534|Heading 4] Usage
[P13535|Normal] OSPF checks whether neighbors are using the same MTU on a common interface. This check is performed when neighbors exchange DD packets. If the receiving MTU in the DD packet is higher than the IP MTU configured on the incoming interface, OSPF adjacency will not be established.
[P13536|Heading 4] Examples
[P13537|Normal] The following example disables MTU mismatch detection on receiving DD packets:
[P13538|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# no switchport
Switch(config-if)# ip ospf mtu-ignore
[P13539|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P13540|Normal] ip ospf mtu
[P13541|Heading 3] ip ospf priority
[P13542|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P13543|Normal] To set the router priority, which helps determine the designated router for this network, use the ip ospf priority command in interface configuration mode. To return to the default value, use the no form of this command.
[P13544|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P13545|Normal] ip ospf priority NUMBER-VALUE
[P13546|Body Text] no ip ospf priority

[TABLE 441] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	NUMBER-VALUE	A number value that specifies the priority of the router.	0-255

[P13547|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P13548|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P13549|Heading 4] Default
[P13550|Normal] Priority of 1
[P13551|Heading 4] Usage
[P13552|Normal] When two routers attached to a network both attempt to become the designated router, the one with the higher router priority takes precedence. If there is a tie, the router with the higher router ID takes precedence. A router with a router priority set to zero is ineligible to become the designated router or backup designated router. Router priority is configured only for interfaces to multi-access networks (in other words, not to point-to-point networks).
[P13553|Body Text] This priority value is used when you configure Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) for non-broadcast networks using the neighbor router configuration command for OSPF.
[P13554|Heading 4] Examples
[P13555|Normal] The following example sets the router priority value to 4:
[P13556|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# no switchport
Switch(config-if)# ip ospf priority 4
[P13557|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P13558|Normal] ip ospf network
[P13559|Body Text] neighbor (OSPF)
[P13560|Heading 3] ip ospf retransmit-interval
[P13561|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P13562|Normal] To specify the time between link-state advertisement (LSA) retransmissions for adjacencies belonging to the interface, use the ip ospf retransmit-interval command in interface configuration mode. To return to the default value, use the no form of this command.
[P13563|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P13564|Normal] ip ospf retransmit-interval SECONDS
[P13565|Body Text] no ip ospf retransmit-interval

[TABLE 442] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	SECONDS	Time (in seconds) between retransmissions. The default is 5 seconds	1-65535 seconds

[P13566|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P13567|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P13568|Heading 4] Default
[P13569|Normal] 5 seconds
[P13570|Heading 4] Usage
[P13571|Normal] When a router sends an LSA to its neighbor, it keeps the LSA until it receives back the acknowledgment message. If the router receives no acknowledgment, it will resend the LSA. The setting of this parameter should be conservative, or needless retransmission will result. The value should be larger for serial lines and virtual links.
[P13572|Heading 4] Examples
[P13573|Normal] The following example sets the retransmit interval value:
[P13574|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# no switchport
Switch(config-if)# ip ospf retransmit-interval 8
[P13575|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P13576|Normal] None
[P13577|Heading 3] ip ospf transmit-delay
[P13578|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P13579|Normal] To set the estimated time required to send a link-state update packet on the interface, use the ip ospf transmit-delay command in interface configuration mode. To return to the default value, use the no form of this command.
[P13580|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P13581|Normal] ip ospf transmit-delay SECONDS
[P13582|Body Text] no ip ospf transmit-delay

[TABLE 443] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	SECONDS	Time (in seconds) of link state transmit delay. The default is 1 seconds	1-65535

[P13583|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P13584|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P13585|Heading 4] Default
[P13586|Normal] 1 second
[P13587|Heading 4] Usage
[P13588|Normal] Link-state advertisements (LSAs) in the update packet must have their ages incremented by the amount specified in the seconds argument before transmission. The value assigned should take into account the transmission and propagation delays for the interface.
[P13589|Body Text] If the delay is not added before transmission over a link, the time in which the LSA propagates over the link is not considered. This setting has more significance on very low-speed links.
[P13590|Heading 4] Examples
[P13591|Normal] The following example sets the retransmit delay value to 3 seconds:
[P13592|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# no switchport
Switch(config-if)# ip ospf transmit-delay 3
[P13593|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P13594|Normal] None
[P13595|Heading 3] ip ospf network
[P13596|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P13597|Normal] To configure the Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) network type to a type other than the default for a given medium, use the ip ospf network command in interface configuration mode. To return to the default value, use the no form of this command.
[P13598|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P13599|Normal] ip ospf network ( broadcast | non-broadcast | point-to-multipoint [ non-broadcast ] | point-to-point )
[P13600|Body Text] no ip ospf network

[TABLE 444] rows=5 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	broadcast	Sets the network type to broadcast.(Such as Ethernet,FDDI)	-
R3	non-broadcast	Sets the network type to non-broadcast multi-access (NBMA)	-
R4	point-to-multipoint	Sets the network type to point-to-multipoint.	-
R5	point-to-point	Sets the network type to point-to-point	-

[P13601|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P13602|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P13603|Heading 4] Default
[P13604|Normal] Depends on the network type.
[P13605|Heading 4] Usage
[P13606|Normal] Using this feature, you can configure broadcast networks as NBMA networks when, for example, routers in your network do not support multicast addressing. You can also configure non-broadcast multi-access networks as broadcast networks. This feature saves you from needing to configure neighbors.
[P13607|Body Text] Configuring NBMA networks as either broadcast or non-broadcast assumes that there are virtual circuits from every router to every router or fully meshed networks. However, there are other configurations where this assumption is not true. For example, a partially meshed network. In these cases, you can configure the OSPF network type as a point-to-multipoint network. Routing between two routers that are not directly connected will go through the router that has virtual circuits to both routers. You need not configure neighbors when using this feature.
[P13608|Body Text] If this command is issued on an interface that does not allow it, this command will be ignored.
[P13609|Body Text] OSPF has two features related to point-to-multipoint networks. One feature applies to broadcast networks; the other feature applies to non-broadcast networks:
[P13610|Body Text] On point-to-multipoint, broadcast networks, you can use the neighbor command, and you must specify a cost to that neighbor.
[P13611|Body Text] On point-to-multipoint, non-broadcast networks, you must use the neighbor command to identify neighbors. Assigning a cost to a neighbor is optional.
[P13612|Heading 4] Examples
[P13613|Normal] The following example sets your OSPF network as a non-broadcast network:
[P13614|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# no switchport
Switch(config-if)# ip address 192.168.77.17/24
Switch(config-if)# ip ospf network non-bradcast
[P13615|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P13616|Normal] Neighbor (OSPF)
[P13617|Heading 3] neighbor (OSPF)
[P13618|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P13619|Normal] To configure Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) routers interconnecting to non-broadcast networks, use the neighbor command in router configuration mode. To remove a configuration, use the no form of this command.
[P13620|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P13621|Normal] neighbor IP_ADDR { priority NUMBER | poll-interval SECONDS }
[P13622|Body Text] neighbor IP_ADDR ( cost COST | )
[P13623|Body Text] no neighbor IP_ADDR { priority | poll-interval }
[P13624|Body Text] no neighbor IP_ADDR ( cost | )

[TABLE 445] rows=5 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	IP_ADDR	Interface IP address of the neighbor	IPv4 Address
R3	priority NUMBER	(Optional) A number that indicates the router priority value of the non-broadcast neighbor associated with the IP address specified. The default is 0. This keyword does not apply to point-to-multipoint interfaces	0-255
R4	poll-interval		-
R5	cost		-

[P13625|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P13626|Normal] Router Configuration
[P13627|Heading 4] Default
[P13628|Normal] No configuration is specified.
[P13629|Heading 4] Usage
[P13630|Normal] One neighbor entry must be included in the switch configuration for each known non-broadcast network neighbor. The neighbor address must be the the primary address of the interface.
[P13631|Body Text] If a neighboring router has become inactive (hello packets have not been received for the Router Dead Interval period), it may still be necessary to send hello packets to the dead neighbor. These hello packets will be sent at a reduced rate called Poll Interval.
[P13632|Body Text] When the router first starts up, it sends only hello packets to those routers with nonzero priority, that is, routers that are eligible to become designated routers (DRs) and backup designated routers (BDRs). After the DR and BDR are selected, DR and BDR will then start sending hello packets to all neighbors in order to form adjacencies.
[P13633|Heading 4] Examples
[P13634|Normal] The following example declares a router at address 192.168.3.4 on a non-broadcast network, with a priority of 1 and a poll interval of 180 seconds:
[P13635|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router ospf
Switch(config-router)# neighbor 192.168.3.4 priority 1 poll-interval 180
[P13636|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P13637|Normal] ip ospf priority
[P13638|Heading 3] network area (OSPF)
[P13639|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P13640|Normal] To define the interfaces on which Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) runs and to define the area ID for those interfaces, use the network area command in router configuration mode. To disable OSPF routing for interfaces defined with the address wildcard-mask pair, use the no form of this command.
[P13641|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P13642|Normal] network { IP_ADDR WILDCARD-MASK | IP-ADDRESS/PREFIX-LENGTH } area AREA-ID 
[P13643|Body Text] no network { IP-ADDRESS WILDCARD-MASK | IP-ADDRESS/PREFIX-LENGTH } area AREA-ID

[TABLE 446] rows=5 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	IP_ADDR	Interface IP address of the neighbor	IPv4 Address
R3	WILDCARD-MASK	IP-address-type mask that includes “don’t care” bits	IPv4 mask
R4	PREFIX-LENGTH	Prefix length for the network	1-32
R5	AREA-ID	Area that is to be associated with the OSPF address range. It can be specified as either a decimal value or as an IP address	IP address or number in the range of 0-4294967295

[P13644|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P13645|Normal] Router Configuration
[P13646|Heading 4] Default
[P13647|Normal] This command is disabled by default.
[P13648|Heading 4] Usage
[P13649|Normal] The IP-ADDRESS and WILDCARD-MASK arguments together allow you to define one or multiple interfaces to be associated with a specific OSPF area using a single command.
[P13650|Heading 4] Examples
[P13651|Normal] The following partial example initializes OSPF routing process 109, and defines four OSPF areas 10.9.50.0, 2, 3, and 0. Areas 10.9.50.0, 2, and 3 mask specific address ranges, and area 0 enables OSPF for all other networks:
[P13652|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# no switchport
Switch(config-if)# ip address 10.108.20.1/24
Switch(config)# router ospf 109
Switch(config-router)# network 10.108.20.0/24  area 10.9.50.0
Switch(config-router)# network 10.108.0.0/16  area 2
Switch(config-router)# network 10.109.10.0/24  area 3
Switch(config-router)# network 0.0.0.0/0 area 0
[P13653|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P13654|Normal] router ospf
[P13655|Heading 3] overflow database external
[P13656|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P13657|Normal] Use this command to configure the size of the external database and the time the router waits before its entries to exit the overflow state.
[P13658|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to revert to default.
[P13659|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P13660|Normal] overflow database external MAXLSAS RECOVERTIME
[P13661|Body Text] no overflow database external

[TABLE 447] rows=3 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	MAXLSAS	The maximum number of LSAs. Note that this value should be the same	0-2147483647
R3	RECOVERTIME	The number of seconds the router waits before trying to exit the database	0-65535

[P13662|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P13663|Normal] Router Configuration
[P13664|Heading 4] Default
[P13665|Normal] None.
[P13666|Heading 4] Usage
[P13667|Normal] Use this command to limit the number of AS-external-LSAs a router can receive, once it is in the wait state. It takes the number of seconds specified as the RECOVERTIME to recover from this state.
[P13668|Heading 4] Examples
[P13669|Normal] The following example shows setting the maximum number of LSAs and the time to recover from overflow state:
[P13670|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router ospf 200
Switch(config-router)# network 10.108.0.0/16 area 0
Switch(config-router)# overflow database external 5 3
[P13671|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P13672|Normal] router ospf
[P13673|Heading 3] passive-interface (OSPF)
[P13674|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P13675|Normal] To disable sending routing updates for the Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) on an interface, use the passive-interface command in router configuration mode. To re-enable the sending of routing updates, use the no form of this command.
[P13676|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P13677|Normal] passive-interface IFNAME
[P13678|Body Text] no passive-interface IFNAME

[TABLE 448] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	IFNAME	The interface name	Support physical/aggregation/loopback/tunnel/vlan interfaces

[P13679|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P13680|Normal] Router Configuration
[P13681|Heading 4] Default
[P13682|Normal] Routing updates are sent on the interface.
[P13683|Heading 4] Usage
[P13684|Normal] If you disable the sending of routing updates on an interface, the particular subnet will continue to be advertised to other interfaces, and updates from other switches on that interface continue to be received and processed.
[P13685|Heading 4] Examples
[P13686|Normal] The following example sets the interface eth-0-1 as passive:
[P13687|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router ospf 200
Switch(config-router)# network 10.108.0.0/16 area 0
Switch(config-router)# passive-interface eth-0-1
[P13688|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P13689|Normal] router ospf
[P13690|Heading 3] redistribute (OSPF)
[P13691|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P13692|Normal] To redistribute routes from one routing domain into Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) routing domain, use the redistribute command in router configuration mode. To disable redistribution, use the no form of this command.
[P13693|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P13694|Normal] redistribute PROTOCOL [ route-map WORD ] [ tag TAG-VALUE ] [ metric METRIC-VALUE ] [ metric-type TYPE-VALUE ]
[P13695|Body Text] no redistribute PROTOCOL [ metric METRIC -VALUE ] [ metric-type TYPE-VALUE ]

[TABLE 449] rows=6 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	route-map WORD	Route map reference.	A string with 1-20 characters
R3	PROTOCOL	(Optional) The name of a routing protocol, or the keyword connected, or static. If you specify a routing protocol	use one of the following keywords: static，connected， bgp, and rip
R4	tag TAG-VALUE	Set tag for routes redistributed into OSPF	0-4294967295
R5	metric METRIC-VALUE	(Optional) When redistributing other processes to an OSPF process, the default metric is 20 when no metric value is specified	0-16777214
R6	metric-type TYPE-VALUE	For OSPF, the external link type associated with the default route advertised into the OSPF routing domain. It can be one of two values	1-2

[P13696|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P13697|Normal] Router Configuration
[P13698|Heading 4] Default
[P13699|Normal] Route redistribution is disabled.
[P13700|Body Text] metric metric-value: 20
[P13701|Body Text] metric-type TYPE-VALUE: Type 2 external route
[P13702|Heading 4] Usage
[P13703|Normal] The metric value specified in the redistribute command supersedes the metric value specified using the default-metric command.
[P13704|Heading 4] Examples
[P13705|Normal] The following example redistribute the static routes into OSPF with metric 10:
[P13706|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router ospf 119
Switch(config-router)# network 10.108.0.0/16 area 100
Switch(config-router)# redistribute static metric 10
[P13707|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P13708|Normal] default-metric
[P13709|Heading 3] router-id (OSPF)
[P13710|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P13711|Normal] To use a fixed router ID, use the router-id command in router configuration mode. To force Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) to use the previous OSPF router ID behavior, use the no form of this command.
[P13712|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P13713|Normal] router-id IP_ADDR
[P13714|Body Text] no router-id

[TABLE 450] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	IP_ADDR	Router ID in IP address format	IPv4 Address

[P13715|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P13716|Normal] Router Configuration
[P13717|Heading 4] Default
[P13718|Normal] No OSPF routing process is defined.
[P13719|Heading 4] Usage
[P13720|Normal] You can configure an arbitrary value in the IP address format for each router. However, each router ID must be unique.
[P13721|Body Text] If this command is used on an OSPF router process which is already active (has neighbors), the new router-ID is used at the next reload or at a manual OSPF process restart. To manually restart the OSPF process, use the clear ip ospf command.
[P13722|Heading 4] Examples
[P13723|Normal] The following example specifies a fixed router-id:
[P13724|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router ospf 119
Switch(config-router)# router-id 10.1.1.1
[P13725|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P13726|Normal] clear ip ospf
[P13727|Body Text] router ospf
[P13728|Heading 3] router ospf
[P13729|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P13730|Normal] To configure an Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) routing process, use the router ospf command in global configuration mode. To terminate an OSPF routing process, use the no form of this command.
[P13731|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P13732|Normal] router ospf [ PROCESS-ID [ vrf VPN-NAME ] ]
[P13733|Body Text] no router ospf [ PROCESS-ID ]

[TABLE 451] rows=3 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	PROCESS-ID	Internally used identification parameter for an OSPF routing process.If you don’t assign a PROCESS-ID, it enter process ID 0. Process ID 0 will be closed if you use the no form of this command and don’t assign PORCESS-ID.	1-65535
R3	vrf VPN-NAME	(Optional) Specifies the name of the VPN routing and forwarding (VRF) instance to associate with OSPF VRF processes	A string with 1-31 characters

[P13734|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P13735|Normal] Global Configuration
[P13736|Heading 4] Default
[P13737|Normal] No OSPF routing process is defined.
[P13738|Heading 4] Usage
[P13739|Normal] You can specify multiple OSPF routing processes in each router. If you do not specify the process-id, the process-id will be the default 0.
[P13740|Heading 4] Examples
[P13741|Normal] The following example configures an OSPF routing process and assign a process number of 109:
[P13742|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router ospf 109
Switch(config-router)# 
[P13743|Heading 4] Related Commands

[P13796|Heading 3] summary-address (OSPF)
[P13797|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P13798|Normal] To create aggregate addresses for Open Shortest Path First (OSPF), use the summary-address command in router configuration mode. To restore the default, use the no form of this command.
[P13799|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P13800|Normal] summary-address PREFIX/PREFIX-LENGTH ( not-advertise | tag TAG-VALUE | )
[P13801|Body Text] no summary-address PREFIX/PREFIX-LENGTH ( not-advertise | tag TAG-VALUE | )

[TABLE 453] rows=5 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	PREFIX	IP route prefix for the destination	IPv4 Address
R3	PREFIX-LENGTH	Prefix length for the network	1-32
R4	not-advertise	(Optional) Suppress routes that match the specified prefix/mask pair. This keyword applies to OSPF only	-
R5	tag TAG-VALUE	Route tag value. The default tag is 0.	0-4294967295

[P13802|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P13803|Normal] Router Configuration
[P13804|Heading 4] Default
[P13805|Normal] This command is disabled by default.
[P13806|Heading 4] Usage
[P13807|Normal] Routes learned from other routing protocols can be summarized. The metric used to advertise the summary is the largest metric of all the more specific routes. This command helps reduce the size of the routing table.
[P13808|Body Text] Using this command for OSPF causes an OSPF Autonomous System Boundary Router (ASBR) to advertise one external route as an aggregate for all redistributed routes that are covered by the address. For OSPF, this command summarizes only routes from other routing protocols that are being redistributed into OSPF. Use the area range command for route summarization between OSPF areas.
[P13809|Body Text] OSPF does not support the summary-address 0.0.0.0/0 command.
[P13810|Heading 4] Examples
[P13811|Normal] In the following example, the summary address 10.1.0.0 includes address 10.1.1.0, 10.1.2.0, 10.1.3.0, and so on. Only the address 10.1.0.0 is advertised in an external link-state advertisement:
[P13812|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router ospf 
Switch(config-router)# summary-address 10.1.0.0/16

[P14031|Heading 3] ip ospf bfd
[P14032|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P14033|Normal] Use this command to enable IP BFD for ospf on an interface.
[P14034|Body Text] Use the “no” form of this command to disable IP BFD for ospf on an interface.
[P14035|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P14036|Normal] ip ospf bfd
[P14037|Body Text] no ip ospf bfd
[P14038|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P14039|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P14040|Heading 4] Default
[P14041|Normal] By default IP BFD for ospf is disabled on the interface.
[P14042|Heading 4] Usage
[P14043|Normal] Use this command to enable IP BFD for ospf on an interface.
[P14044|Body Text] The IP BFD session should be created when ospf neighbor is created and the neighbor’s state is large than “two-way”.
[P14045|Body Text] The IP BFD session should be destroyed when ospf neighbor is delete or the neighbor’s state is not large than “two-way”.
[P14046|Heading 4] Examples
[P14047|Normal] In the following example, IP BFD for ospf is enabled on this interface:
[P14048|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config-if)# ip ospf bfd

[P14236|Heading 2] Route Map Commands
[P14237|Heading 3] route-map
[P14238|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P14239|Normal] To define the conditions for redistributing routes from one routing protocol into another, or to enable policy routing in bgp, use the route-map command in global configuration mode and the match and set command in route-map configuration modes. To delete an entry, use the no form of this command.
[P14240|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P14241|Normal] route-map MAP_TAG ( deny | permit | ) ( SEQUENCE-NUMBER | )
[P14242|Body Text] no route-map MAP_TAG ( deny | permit | ) ( SEQUENCE-NUMBER | )

[TABLE 472] rows=5 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	MAP_TAG	A meaningful name for the route map. The redistribute router configuration command uses this name to reference this route map. Multiple route maps may share the same map tag name. The length of route-map name should not greater than 20 and the first character should be ‘a’-‘z’, ‘A’-‘Z’ or ‘0’-‘9’	-
R3	permit	(Optional) If the match criteria are met for this route map, and the permit keyword is specified, the route is redistributed as controlled by the set actions. (Optional) If the match criteria are met for this route map, and the permit keyword is specified, the route is redistributed as controlled by the set actions. If the match criteria are not met, and the permit keyword is specified, the next route map with the same map tag is tested. If a route passes none of the match criteria for the set of route maps sharing the same name, it is not redistributed by that set.	-
R4	deny	(Optional) If the match criteria are met for the route map and the deny keyword is specified, the route is not redistributed	-
R5	SEQUENCE-NUMBER	(Optional) Number that indicates the position a new route map will have in the list of route maps already configured with the same name. If given with the no form of this command, the position of the route map should be deleted	1-65535

[P14278|Heading 3] match as-path
[P14279|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P14280|Normal] Use this command to match an autonomous system path access list.
[P14281|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to remove a path list entry.
[P14282|Body Text] The match as-path command specifies the autonomous system path to be matched. If there is a match for the specified AS path, and permit is specified, the route is redistributed or controlled, as specified by the set action. If the match criteria are met, and deny is specified, the route is not redistributed or controlled. If the match criteria are not met then the route is neither accepted nor forwarded, irrespective of permit or deny specifications.
[P14283|Body Text] The route specified by the policies might not be the same as specified by the routing protocols. Setting policies enable packets to take different routes, depending on their length or content. Packet forwarding based on configured policies overrides packet forwarding specified in routing tables.
[P14284|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P14285|Normal] match as-path LISTNAME
[P14286|Body Text] no match as-path

[P14302|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P14303|Normal] Use this command to specify the community to be matched.
[P14304|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to remove the community list entry.
[P14305|Body Text] Communities are used to group and filter routes. They are designed to provide the ability to apply policies to large numbers of routes by using match and set commands. Community lists are used to identify and filter routes by their common attributes.
[P14306|Body Text] Use the match community command to allow matching based on community lists.
[P14307|Body Text] The values set by the match community command overrides the global values. The route that does not match at least one match clause is ignored.

[P14477|Heading 3] match origin
[P14478|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P14479|Normal] Use this command to match origin code.
[P14480|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to disable this matching.
[P14481|Body Text] The origin attribute defines the origin of the path information. The egp parameter is indicated as an e in the routing table, and it indicates that the origin of the information is learned via Exterior Gateway Protocol. The igp parameter is indicated as i in the routing table, and it indicates the origin of the path information is interior to the originating AS.
[P14482|Body Text] The incomplete parameter is indicated as a ? in the routing table, and indicates that the origin of the path information is unknown or learned through other means. If a static route is redistributed into BGP, the origin of the route is incomplete.
[P14483|Body Text] The match origin command specifies the origin to be matched. If there is a match for the specified origin, and permit is specified, the route is redistributed or controlled as specified by the set action. If the match criteria are met, and deny is specified, the route is not redistributed or controlled. If the match criteria are not met, the route is neither accepted nor forwarded, irrespective of permit or deny specifications.
[P14484|Body Text] The route specified by the policies might not be the same as specified by the routing protocols. Setting policies enable packets to take different routes depending on their length or content. Packet forwarding based on configured policies overrides packet forwarding specified in routing tables.
[P14485|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P14486|Normal] match origin { egp | igp | incomplete }
[P14487|Body Text] no match origin

[TABLE 482] rows=4 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	egp	learned from EGP	-
R3	igp	Local IGP	-
R4	incomplete	Unknown heritage	-

[P14535|Heading 3] set aggregator
[P14536|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P14537|Normal] Use this command to set the AS number for the route map and router ID.
[P14538|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to disable this function.
[P14539|Body Text] An Autonomous System (AS) is a collection of networks under a common administration sharing a common routing strategy. It is subdivided by areas, and is assigned a unique 16-bit number. Use the set aggregator command to
[P14540|Body Text] assign an AS number for the aggregator.
[P14541|Body Text] To use the set aggregator command, you must first have a match clause. Match and set commands set the conditions for redistributing routes from one routing protocol to another. The match command specifies the match criteria under which redistribution is allowed for the current route-map. The set command specifies the set redistribution actions to be performed, if the match criteria are met.
[P14542|Body Text] If the packets do not match any of the defined criteria, they are routed through the normal routing process.
[P14543|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P14544|Normal] set aggregator as ASNUM IPADDRESS
[P14545|Body Text] no set aggregator

[TABLE 485] rows=3 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	ASNUM	Specifies the AS number of aggregator	1-65535
R3	IPADDRESS	Specifies the IP address of aggregator	-

[P14557|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P14558|Normal] Use this command to modify an autonomous system path for a route.
[P14559|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to disable this function.
[P14560|Body Text] Use the set as-path command to specify an autonomous system path. By specifying the length of the AS-Path, the router influences the best path selection by a neighbor. this command to prepend an AS path string to routes increasing the AS path length.
[P14561|Body Text] To use the set as-path command, you must first have a match clause. Match and set commands set the conditions for redistributing routes from one routing protocol to another. The match command specifies the match criteria under which redistribution is allowed for the current route-map. The set command specifies the set redistribution actions to be performed, if the match criteria are met.
[P14562|Body Text] If the packets do not match any of the defined criteria, they are routed through the normal routing process.

[P14598|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to disable this feature.

R5	delete	Delete matching communities	-

[P14612|Heading 3] set community
[P14613|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P14614|Normal] Use this command to set the communities attribute.
[P14615|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to delete the entry.
[P14616|Body Text] Use this command to set the community attribute and group destinations in a certain community, as well as, apply routing decisions according to those communities.
[P14617|Body Text] To use the set community command, you must first have a match clause. Match and set commands set the conditions for redistributing routes from one routing protocol to another. The match command specifies the match criteria under which redistribution is allowed for the current route-map. The set command specifies the set redistribution actions to be performed, if the match criteria are met.
[P14618|Body Text] If the packets do not match any of the defined criteria, they are routed through the normal routing process.
[P14619|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P14620|Normal] set community [ AA:NN | internet | local-AS | no-advertise | no-export ]
[P14621|Body Text] set community none
[P14622|Body Text] no set community

[TABLE 488] rows=7 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	AA:NN	AA:NN: Specifies the community number in this format AA = The AS number NN = The number assigned to community	AA is in the range 1-65535 NN is in the range of 1-65535
R3	internet	Specifies the Internet (well-known community)	-
R4	local-AS	Specifies no sending outside the local AS (well-known community)	-
R5	no-advertise	Specifies no advertisement of this route to any peer (well-known community)	-
R6	no-export	Specifies no advertisement of this route to next AS (well-known community)	-
R7	none	Removes the community attribute from the prefixes that pass the route-map	-

[P14623|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P14624|Normal] Route-map Configuration
[P14625|Heading 4] Default
[P14626|Normal] No set community is specified by default.
[P14627|Heading 4] Usage
[P14628|Normal] This command is valid for BGP only.
[P14629|Heading 4] Examples
[P14630|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# route-map rmap1 permit 3
Switch(config-route-map)# set community no-export no-advertise
Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# route-map rmap1 permit 3
Switch(config-route-map)# set community no-advertise
Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# route-map rmap1 permit 3
Switch(config-route-map)# set community 10:01 23:34 12:14 no-export

[P14633|Heading 3] set dampening
[P14634|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P14635|Normal] Use this command to enable route-flap dampening and set parameters.
[P14636|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to disable it.
[P14637|Body Text] Set the unreachability half-life time to be equal to, or greater than, reachability half-life time. The suppress-limit value must be greater than or equal to the reuse limit value.
[P14638|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P14639|Normal] set dampening REACHTIME REUSE SUPPRESS MAXSUPPRESS [ UNREACHTIME ]
[P14640|Body Text] no set dampening

[TABLE 489] rows=6 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	REACHTIME	Specifies the reachability half-life time in minutes. The time for the penalty to decrease to one-half of its current value. The default is 15 minutes	1-45
R3	REUSE	Specifies the reuse-limit value. When the penalty for a suppressed route decays below the reuse value, the routes become unsuppressed. The default reuse limit is 750	1-20000
R4	SUPPRESS	Specifies the suppress-limit value. When the penalty for a route exceeds the suppress value, the route is suppressed. The default suppress limit is 2000	1-20000
R5	MAXSUPPRESS	Specifies the max-suppress-time. Maximum time that a dampened route is suppressed. The default max-suppress value is 4 times the half-life time (60 minutes)	1-255
R6	UNREACHTIME	Specifies the un-reachability half-life time for penalty, in minutes. The default value is 15 minutes	1-45

[P14727|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# track 1 interface eth-0-1 linkstate 
Switch(config-track)# quit
Switch(config)# route-map mymap permit 3
Switch(config-route-map)# set ip next-hop 10.10.0.67 track 1

[P14807|Heading 3] set metric
[P14808|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P14809|Normal] Use this command to set a metric value for a route.
[P14810|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to disable this function.
[P14811|Body Text] This command sets the metric value for a route, and influences external neighbors about the preferred path into an Autonomous System (AS). The preferred path is the one with a lower metric value. A router compares metrics for paths from neighbors in the same ASs. To compare metrics from neighbors coming from different ASs, use the bgp always-compare-med command.
[P14812|Body Text] To use the set metric command, you must first have a match clause. Match and set commands set the conditions for redistributing routes from one routing protocol to another. The match command specifies the match criteria under which redistribution is allowed for the current route-map. The set command specifies the set redistribution actions to be performed, if the match criteria are met.
[P14813|Body Text] If the packets do not match any of the defined criteria, they are routed through the normal routing process.
[P14814|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P14815|Normal] set metric METRICVAL
[P14816|Body Text] no set metric

[TABLE 498] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	METRICVAL	The metric value	0-4294967295

[P14817|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P14818|Normal] Route-map Configuration
[P14819|Heading 4] Default
[P14820|Normal] No set metric is specified by default.
[P14821|Heading 4] Usage
[P14822|Normal] This command is valid for BGP, OSPF and RIP.
[P14823|Heading 4] Examples
[P14824|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# route-map rmap1 permit 3
Switch(config-route-map)# set metric 600
