[P14845|Heading 3] set origin
[P14846|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P14847|Normal] Use this command to set the BGP origin code.
[P14848|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to delete an entry.
[P14849|Body Text] The origin attribute defines the origin of the path information. The three parameters with this command indicate three different values. IGP is interior to the originating AS. This happens if IGP is redistributed into the BGP. EGP is learned through an Exterior Gateway Protocol. Incomplete is unknown or learned through some other means. This happens when static route is redistributed in BGP and the origin of the route is incomplete.
[P14850|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P14851|Normal] set origin { egp | igp | incomplete }
[P14852|Body Text] no set origin

[TABLE 500] rows=4 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	egp	Specifies a remote EGP system	-
R3	igp	A local IGP system	-
R4	incomplete	Specifies a system of unknown heritage	-

[P14882|Heading 3] set tag
[P14883|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P14884|Normal] Use this command to set a specified tag value.
[P14885|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to return to the default.
[P14886|Body Text] Tag in this command is the route tag which is labeled by another routing protocol (BGP or other IGP when redistributing), because AS-external-LSA has a route-tag field in its LSAs. Also, with using route-map, ZebOS can tag the LSAs with the appropriate tag value. Sometimes, the tag matches with using route-map, and sometimes, the value
[P14887|Body Text] may be used by another application.

[P14952|Heading 2] Prefix-list Commands
[P14953|Heading 3] ip prefix-list
[P14954|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P14955|Normal] To create a prefix list or add a prefix-list entry, use the ip prefix-list command in global configuration mode. To delete a prefix-list or an entry, use the no form of this command.
[P14956|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P14957|Normal] ip prefix-list WORD ( seq SEQUENCE-NUMBER | ) ( deny | permit ) ( any | A.B.C.D/M ( ge GE-LENGTH | ) ( le LE-LENGTH | ) )
[P14958|Body Text] ( any | A.B.C.D/M ( ge GE-LENGTH | ) ( le LE-LENGTH | ) )
[P14959|Body Text] no ip prefix-list WORD ( seq SEQUENCE-NUMBER | ) ( deny | permit ) ( any | A.B.C.D/M ( ge GE-LENGTH | ) ( le LE-LENGTH | ) )
[P14960|Body Text] no ip prefix-list WORD ( seq SEQUENCE-NUMBER | )

[TABLE 506] rows=8 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	WORD	Config a name to identify the prefix list	Up to 40 characters
R3	seq SEQUENCE-NUMBER	Applies a sequence number to a prefix-list entry. If a sequence number is not entered when configuring this command, a default sequence numbering is applied to the prefix list. The number 5 is applied to the first prefix entry, and subsequent unnumbered entries are incremented by 5	1-65535
R4	deny	Denies access for a matching condition	-
R5	permit	Permits access for a matching condition	-
R6	A.B.C.D/M	Configures the network address, and the length of the network mask in bits. The network number can be any valid IP address or prefix. The bit mask can be a number from 0 to 32	IPv4 Address and mask length in A.B.C.D/M format
R7	ge GE-LENGTH	(Optional)Specifies the lesser value of a range (the “from” portion of the range description) by applying the ge-length argument to the range specified. The ge-length argument represents the minimum prefix length to be matched	1-32
R8	le LE-LENGTH	(Optional)Specifies the greater value of a range (the “to” portion of the range description) by applying the le-length argument to the range specified. The le-length argument represents the maximum prefix length to be matched	1-32

[P14961|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P14962|Normal] Global Configuration
[P14963|Heading 4] Default
[P14964|Normal] No prefix lists are created.
[P14965|Heading 4] Usage
[P14966|Normal] The ip prefix-list command is used to configure IP prefix filtering. Prefix lists are configured with permit or deny keywords to either permit or deny the prefix based on the matching condition. A prefix list consists of an IP address and a bit mask. The IP address can be a classful network, a subnet, or a single host route. The bit mask is entered as a number from 1 to 32. An implicit deny is applied to traffic that does not match any prefix-list entry. Prefix lists are configured to match an exact prefix length or a prefix range. The ge and le keywords are used to specify a range of the prefix lengths to match, providing more flexible configuration than can be configured with just the network/length argument. The prefix list is processed using an exact match when neither the ge nor le keyword is entered. If only the ge value is entered, the range is the value entered for the ge ge-length argument to a full 32-bit length. If only the le value is entered, the range is from value entered for the network/length argument to the le le-length argument. If both the ge ge-length and le le-length keywords and arguments are entered, the range falls between the values used for the ge-length and le-length arguments. The following formula shows this behavior:
[P14967|Body Text] Network/length < ge ge-length < le le-length <= 32.
[P14968|Body Text] A prefix list is configured with a name and/or sequence number. One or the other must be entered when configuring this command. If a sequence number is not entered, a default sequence number of 5 is applied to the prefix list. And subsequent prefix list entries will be increment by 5 (for example, 5, 10, 15, and onwards). If a sequence number is entered for the first prefix list entry but not subsequent entries, then the subsequent entries will also be incremented by 5 (For example, if the first configured sequence number is 3, then subsequent entries will be 8, 13, 18, and onwards). Default sequence numbers can be suppressed by entering the no form of this command with the seq keyword. Prefix lists are evaluated starting with the lowest sequence number and continues down the list until a match is made. Once a match is made that covers the network the permit or deny statement is applied to that network and the rest of the list is not evaluated.
[P14969|Heading 4] Examples
[P14970|Normal] To deny the default route 0.0.0.0/0:
[P14971|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ip prefix-list abc deny 0.0.0.0/0
[P14972|Normal] To permit the prefix10.0.0.0/8:
[P14973|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ip prefix-list abc permit 10.0.0.0/8
[P14974|Normal] To accept a mask length of up to 24 bits in routes with the prefix 192/16:
[P14975|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ip prefix-list abc permit 192.168.0.0/16 le 24
[P14976|Normal] To deny mask lengths greater than 25 bits in routes with the prefix 192/16:
[P14977|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ip prefix-list abc deny 192.168.0.0/16 ge 25

[P15058|Heading 3] ip policy route-map
[P15059|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P15060|Normal] By default, PBR is disabled on the switch. To enable PBR, you must create a route map that specifies the match criteria and the resulting action if all of the match clauses are met. Then, you must enable PBR on a layer3 interface. All packets arriving on the specified interface matching the match clauses are subject to PBR.

[P15062|Normal] ip policy route-map MAP_NAME
[P15063|Body Text] no ip policy route-map

[TABLE 510] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value

[P15064|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P15065|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P15066|Heading 4] Default
[P15067|Normal] disabled
[P15068|Heading 4] Usage
[P15069|Normal] This command can only be configured on routed port, vlan interface and routed agg port.
[P15070|Heading 4] Examples
[P15071|Normal] The following example shows how to configure pbr on an interface:
[P15072|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
switch (config)# ip access-list 1 extend
switch (config-ex-ip-acl)# 10 permit any any any
switch (config-route-map)#exit
switch (config)#route-map richard permit 10
switch (config-route-map)#match ip address 1
switch (config-route-map)#set ip next-hop 10.1.1.1
switch (config-route-map)#exit
switch (config)#interface eth-0-1
switch (config-if)#no switch port
switch (config-if)#no shutdown
switch (config-if)#ip policy route-map richrad

[P15174|Heading 3] aggregate-address
[P15175|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P15176|Normal] Use this command to configure BGP aggregate entries.
[P15177|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to disable this function.
[P15178|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P15179|Normal] aggregate-address IP_PREFIX { summary-only | as-set }
[P15180|Body Text] no aggregate-address IP_PREFIX { summary-only | as-set }

[TABLE 515] rows=4 cols=3

R2	IP_PREFIX	A.B.C.D/M Specifies the aggregate prefix	IPv4 Address and mask length in A.B.C.D/M format
R3	summary-only	Filters more specific routes from updates.	-
R4	as-set	Generates AS set path information	-

[P15181|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P15182|Normal] Router Configuration
[P15183|Heading 4] Default
[P15184|Normal] Disabled
[P15185|Heading 4] Usage
[P15186|Normal] Aggregates are used to minimize the size of routing tables. Aggregation combines the characteristics of several different routes and advertises a single route.The aggregate-address command creates an aggregate entry in the BGP routing table if any more-specific BGP routes are available in the specified range. Using the summary-only parameter advertises the prefix only, suppressing the more-specific routes to all neighbors.
[P15187|Heading 4] Examples
[P15188|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router bgp 100
Switch(config-router)# aggregate-address 10.0.0.0/8 as-set summary-only

[P15191|Heading 3] bgp always-compare-med
[P15192|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P15193|Normal] Use this command to compare the Multi Exit Discriminator (MED) for paths from neighbors in different autonomous systems.
[P15194|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to disallow the comparison.
[P15195|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P15196|Normal] bgp always-compare-med
[P15197|Body Text] no bgp always-compare-med
[P15198|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P15199|Normal] Router Configuration
[P15200|Heading 4] Default
[P15201|Normal] Disabled
[P15202|Heading 4] Usage
[P15203|Normal] Multi Exit Discriminator (MED) is used in best path selection by BGP. MED is compared after BGP attributes weight, local preference, AS-path and origin have been compared and are equal.
[P15204|Body Text] MED comparison is done only among paths from the same autonomous system (AS). Use bgp always-comparemed command to allow comparison of MEDs from different ASs. The MED parameter is used to select the best path. A path with lower MED is preferred.
[P15205|Heading 4] Examples
[P15206|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router bgp 100
Switch(config-router)# bgp always-compare-med
[P15207|Heading 4] Related Commands

[P15209|Body Text] bgp bestpath as-path ignore

[P15233|Body Text] no bgp bestpath as-path ignore
[P15234|Heading 4] Command Mode

[P15237|Normal] Disabled
[P15238|Heading 4] Usage

[P15244|Heading 3] bgp bestpath compare-confed-aspath
[P15245|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P15246|Normal] Use this command to allow comparing of the confederation AS path length.
[P15247|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to revert the selection and ignore AS confederation path length in the BGP best path selection.
[P15248|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P15249|Normal] bgp bestpath compare-confed-aspath
[P15250|Body Text] no bgp bestpath compare-confed-aspath
[P15251|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P15252|Normal] Router Configuration
[P15253|Heading 4] Default
[P15254|Normal] BGP receives routes with identical eBGP paths from eBGP peers and selects the first route received as the best path.
[P15255|Heading 4] Usage
[P15256|Normal] This command specifies that the AS confederation path length must be used, when available, in the BGP best path decision process. It is effective only when bgp bestpath as-path ignore command has not been specified.
[P15257|Heading 4] Examples
[P15258|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config) router bgp 100
Switch(config-router) bgp bestpath compare-confed-aspath
[P15259|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P15260|Normal] bgp bestpath as-path ignore
[P15261|Heading 3] bgp bestpath compare-routerid
[P15262|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P15263|Normal] Use this command to compare router-id for identical eBGP paths.
[P15264|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to disable this function.
[P15265|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P15266|Normal] bgp bestpath compare-routerid
[P15267|Body Text] no bgp bestpath compare-routerid
[P15268|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P15269|Normal] Router Configuration
[P15270|Heading 4] Default
[P15271|Normal] BGP receives routes with identical eBGP paths from eBGP peers and selects the first route received as the best path.
[P15272|Heading 4] Usage
[P15273|Normal] When comparing similar routes from peers the BGP router does not consider router ID of the routes. By default, it selects the first received route. Use this command to include router ID in the selection process; similar routes are compared and the route with lowest router ID is selected. The router-id is the highest IP address on the router, with preference given to loopback addresses. Router-id can be manually set by using the bgp router-id command.
[P15274|Heading 4] Examples
[P15275|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config) router bgp 100
Switch(config-router) bgp bestpath compare-routerid
[P15276|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P15277|Normal] show ip bgp
[P15278|Body Text] show ip bgp neighbors

[P15282|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to allow the router to consider originator-id in choosing a route.

[P15285|Body Text] no bgp bestpath dont-compare-originator-id

[P15288|Heading 4] Default
[P15289|Normal] In the default case, BGP will consider originator-id as a factor in choosing a route.
[P15290|Heading 4] Usage
[P15291|Normal] Use this command to prevent BGP to consider originator-id as a factor in choosing a route.
[P15292|Heading 4] Examples
[P15293|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal 
Switch(config)# router bgp 100
Switch(config-router)# bgp bestpath dont-compare-originator-id

[P15296|Heading 3] bgp bestpath med
[P15297|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P15298|Normal] Use this command to specify Multi Exit Discriminator (MED) attribute comparison.
[P15299|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to prevent BGP from considering the MED attribute in comparing paths.
[P15300|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P15301|Normal] bgp bestpath med confed [ missing-as-worst ]
[P15302|Body Text] bgp bestpath med missing-as-worst [ confed ]
[P15303|Body Text] no bgp bestpath med confed [ missing-as-worst ]
[P15304|Body Text] no bgp bestpath med missing-as-worst [ confed ]

[TABLE 517] rows=3 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	confed	Compares MED among confederation paths	-
R3	missing-as-worst	Treats missing MED as the least preferred one	-

[P15305|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P15306|Normal] Router Configuration
[P15307|Heading 4] Default
[P15308|Normal] MED value is zero.
[P15309|Heading 4] Usage
[P15310|Normal] Use this command to specify two MED attributes–confed and missing-as-worst. The confed attribute enables MED comparison among paths learned from confederation peers. The MEDs are compared only if there is no external autonomous system (an AS not within the confederation) in the path. If there is an external autonomous system in the path, the MED comparison is not made.
[P15311|Body Text] The missing-as-worst attribute to consider a missing MED attribute in a path as having a value of infinity, making the path without a MED value the least desirable path. If missing-as-worst is disabled, the missing MED is assigned the value of 0, making the path with the missing MED attribute the best path.
[P15312|Heading 4] Examples
[P15313|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config) router bgp 100
Switch(config-router) bgp bestpath med missing-as-worst
[P15314|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P15315|Normal] bgp-always-compare-med, bgp bestpath as-path ignore, bgp deterministic-med
[P15316|Heading 3] bgp bestpath tie-break-on-age
[P15317|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P15318|Normal] Use this command to preferentially choose old routes when other condition is the same in the algorithm for choosing a route.
[P15319|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to compare addtional information in route choosing rather than the age of route.
[P15320|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P15321|Normal] bgp bestpath tie-break-on-age
[P15322|Body Text] no bgp bestpath tie-break-on-age
[P15323|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P15324|Normal] Router Configuration
[P15325|Heading 4] Default
[P15326|Normal] In the default case, BGP will preferentially choose an old route when other condition is the same.
[P15327|Heading 4] Usage
[P15328|Normal] When the the information that influence the quality of routing like aspath、local-preference、med is the same，preferentially chose the old route to prevent route flap.
[P15329|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to let BGP compara addtional information like router-id、neighbor’s address，instead of the age of routes.
[P15330|Heading 4] Examples
[P15331|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal 
Switch(config)# router bgp 100
Switch(config-router)# no bgp bestpath tie-break-on-age

[P15335|Heading 4] Command Purpose

[P15337|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to turn off client-to-client reflection.

[P15341|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P15342|Normal] Router Configuration
[P15343|Heading 4] Default
[P15344|Normal] When a router is configured as a route reflector, client-to-client reflection is enabled by default.
[P15345|Heading 4] Usage
[P15346|Normal] The bgp client-to-client reflection command is used to configure routers as route reflectors. Route reflectors are used when all Interior Border Gateway Protocol (iBGP) speakers are not fully meshed. If the clients are fully meshed the route reflector is not required, use no bgp client-to-client reflection command to disable the client-to-client route reflection.
[P15347|Heading 4] Examples

[P15354|Heading 4] Command Purpose

[P15359|Body Text] no bgp cluster-id

R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	CLUSTERID	Specifies the cluster ID of this router acting as a route reflector, either as IP address or as a maximum of 4 bytes.	IPv4 Address in A.B.C.D format or number in range 1-4294967295
R3	A.B.C.D	A.B.C.D Route Reflector Cluster-id in IP address format	IPv4 Address
R4	1-4294967295	Route Reflector cluster-id as a 32 bit quantity	1-4294967295

[P15360|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P15361|Normal] Router Configuration
[P15362|Heading 4] Default
[P15363|Normal] N/A
[P15364|Heading 4] Usage
[P15365|Normal] A cluster includes route reflectors and its clients. Usually, each cluster is identified by the router ID of its single route reflector but to increase redundancy sometimes a cluster may have more than one route reflector. All router reflectors in such a cluster are then identified by a cluster ID. The bgp cluster-id command is used to configure the 4 byte cluster ID for clusters with more than one route reflectors.
[P15366|Heading 4] Examples
[P15367|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config) router bgp 100
Switch(config-router) bgp cluster-id 1.1.1.1

[P15394|Heading 4] Command Mode

[P15398|Heading 4] Usage
[P15399|Normal] A confederation allows an AS to be divided into several ASs. The AS is given a confederation identifier. External routers view only the whole confederation as one AS. [P15404|Heading 3] bgp dampening
[P15405|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P15406|Normal] Use this command to set bgp dampening parameters.
[P15407|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to unset the bgp dampening parameters.
[P15408|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P15409|Normal] bgp dampening REACHTIME
[P15410|Body Text] bgp dampening REACHTIME REUSE
[P15411|Body Text] bgp dampening REACHTIME REUSE SUPPRESS MAXSUPPRESS ( UNREACHTIME | )
[P15412|Body Text] bgp dampening route-map ROUTEMAP
[P15413|Body Text] no bgp dampening REACHTIME
[P15414|Body Text] no bgp dampening REACHTIME REUSE
[P15415|Body Text] no bgp dampening REACHTIME REUSE SUPPRESS MAXSUPPRESS ( UNREACHTIME | )
[P15416|Body Text] no bgp dampening route-map ( ROUTEMAP | )

[TABLE 522] rows=7 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	REACHTIME	Specifies the reachability half-life time in minutes. The time for the penalty to decrease to one-half of its current value. The default is 15 minutes.	1-45
R3	REUSE	Specifies the reuse limit value. When the penalty for a suppressed route decays below the reuse value, the routes become unsuppressed. The default reuse limit is 750 SUPPRESS <1-20000> Specifies the suppress limit value. When the penalty for a route exceeds the suppress value, the route is suppressed. The default suppress limit is 2000.	1-20000
R4	SUPPRESS	Specifies suppress-time.A route dampening more than this value will be suppressd. The default value is 2000.	1-20000
R5	MAXSUPPRESS	Specifies the max-suppress-time. Maximum time that a dampened route is suppressed. The default max-suppress value is 4 times the half-life time (60 minutes).	1-255
R6	UNREACHTIME	Specifies the un-reachability half-life time for penalty, in minutes.	1-45
R7	ROUTEMAP	route-map WORD Route-map to specify criteria for dampening.	Up to 20 characters

[P15417|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P15418|Normal] Router Configuration
[P15419|Body Text] Address Family Configuration
[P15420|Heading 4] Default
[P15421|Normal] N/A
[P15422|Heading 4] Usage
[P15423|Normal] Route dampening minimizes the instability caused by route flapping. A penalty is added for every flap in a flapping route. As soon as the total penalty reaches the suppress limit the advertisement of the route is suppressed. This penalty is decayed according to the configured half time value. Once the penalty is lower than the reuse limit, the route advertisement is un-suppressed.
[P15424|Body Text] The dampening information is purged from the router once the penalty becomes less than half of the reuse limit.
[P15425|Heading 4] Examples
[P15426|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router bgp 100
Switch(config-router)# bgp dampening 20 800 2500 80 25

[P15458|Normal] Local preference indicates the preferred path when there are multiple paths to the same destination. The path having a higher preference is preferred. [P15463|Heading 3] bgp deterministic-med
[P15464|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P15465|Normal] Use this command to compare the Multi Exit Discriminator (MED) variable when choosing among routes advertised by different peers in the same autonomous system.
[P15466|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to disallow this setting.
[P15467|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P15468|Normal] bgp deterministic-med
[P15469|Body Text] no bgp deterministic-med
[P15470|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P15471|Normal] Router Configuration
[P15472|Heading 4] Default
[P15473|Normal] Disabled
[P15474|Heading 4] Usage
[P15475|Normal] "Multi Exit Discriminator (MED) is used in best path selection by BGP. MED is compared after BGP attributes weight, local preference, AS-path and origin have been compared and are equal. Enable bgp deterministic med command on all routers in the local AS, for a correct comparison result. After enabling this command, all paths for the same prefix are grouped together and arranged according to their MED value.
[P15476|Body Text] Based on this comparison, the best path is then chosen.
[P15477|Body Text] This command compares MED variable when choosing routes advertised by different peers in the same AS, to compare MED, when choosing routes from neighbors in different ASs use the bgp always-compare-med command."
[P15478|Heading 4] Examples
[P15479|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config) router bgp 100
Switch(config-router) bgp deterministic-med

[P15550|Heading 3] bgp log-neighbor-changes
[P15551|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P15552|Normal] Use this command to enable logging of status change messages without turning on debug bgp commands.
[P15553|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to disable this feature.
[P15554|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P15555|Normal] bgp log-neighbor-changes
[P15556|Body Text] no bgp log-neighbor-changes
[P15557|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P15558|Normal] Router Configuration
[P15559|Heading 4] Default
[P15560|Normal] Disabled
[P15561|Heading 4] Usage
[P15562|Normal] System implementation provides other kinds of logging services for neighbor status, for example, debug bgp fsm, debug bgp events, etc. However, these commands create a significant hit in the logging performance.
[P15563|Body Text] The bgp log-neighbor-changes command, logs the following events:
[P15564|Body Text] (1)BGP Notification Received
[P15565|Body Text] (2)Erroneous BGP Update Received

[P15791|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P15792|Normal] Router Configuration
[P15793|Heading 4] Default
[P15794|Normal] N/A
[P15795|Heading 4] Usage
[P15796|Normal] Use this command to set the administrative distance for BGP. This distance is a rating of trustworthiness of a router.
[P15797|Body Text] The higher the distance the lower the trust rating.
[P15798|Body Text] The administrative distance can be set for external, internal and local routes. External paths are routes learned from a neighbor out of the AS. The internal routes are routes learned from another router within the same AS. Local routes are for the router that is being redistributed from another process.
[P15799|Body Text] If the administrative distance is changed, it could create inconsistency in the routing table and obstruct routing.
[P15800|Heading 4] Examples
[P15801|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config) router bgp 100
Switch(config-router) distance 34 10.10.0.0/24 mylist
Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config) router bgp 100
Switch(config-router) distance bgp 34 23 15

[P15826|Body Text] no ip as-path access-list LISTNAME ( deny | permit ) LINE

R3	deny	(Optional) Denies access to matching conditions.	-

[P15827|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P15828|Normal] Global Configuration
[P15829|Heading 4] Default
[P15830|Normal] N/A
[P15831|Heading 4] Usage
[P15832|Normal] Named community list is a filter based on regular expressions. If the regular expression matches the specified string representing the AS path of the route, then the permit or deny condition applies. Use this command to define the BGP access list globally, use the neighbor router configuration command to apply a specific access list.
[P15833|Heading 4] Examples
[P15834|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ip as-path access-list mylist deny ^65535$

[P15837|Heading 3] ip community-list
[P15838|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P15839|Normal] Use this command to add a community list entry.
[P15840|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to delete the community list entry.
[P15841|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P15842|Normal] ip community-list LISTNUM ( deny | permit ) COMMUNITY
[P15843|Body Text] no ip community-list LISTNUM ( deny | permit ) COMMUNITY

[TABLE 538] rows=10 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	LISTNUM	Specifies the community ID. 1-99:Standard list 100-199:Expandes list	1-199
R3	deny	Specifies the community to reject.	-
R4	permit	Specifies the community to accept.	-
R5	COMMUNITY	(AA:NN\|internet\|local-AS\|no-advertise\|no-export)	-
R6	AA:NN	Specifies the valid value for the community number. This format represents the 32 bit communities value, where AS is the high order 16 bits and VAL is the low order 16 bits in digit format.	AA is in the range 1-65535 NN is in the range of 1-65535
R7	internet	Specifies routes not to be advertised to the Internet.	-
R8	local-AS	Specifies routes not to be advertised to external BGP peers.	-
R9	no-advertise	Specifies routes not to be advertised to other BGP peers.	-
R10	no-export	Specifies routes not to be advertised outside of Autonomous System boundary.	-

[P15844|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P15845|Normal] Global Configuration
[P15846|Heading 4] Default
[P15847|Normal] N/A
[P15848|Heading 4] Usage
[P15849|Normal] Use the community-lists to specify BGP community attributes. The community attribute is used for implementing policy routing. It is an optional, transitive attribute and facilitates transfer of local policies through different autonomous systems. It includes community values that are 32 bits long.
[P15850|Body Text] There are two kinds of community-lists: the expanded and standard. The standard community-list defines the community attributes in a specified format and not with regular expressions. The expanded community-list defines the communities attributes with regular expressions.
[P15851|Heading 4] Examples
[P15852|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ip community-list 20 permit 7675:80 7675:90

[P15857|Heading 4] Command Purpose

[TABLE 539] rows=6 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value

R3	WORD	Expanded community list name	Up to 20 characters
R4	deny	Specifies community to reject.	-
R5	permit	Specifies community to accept.	-
R6	LINE	Specifies a regular expression to match the BGP AS paths.	A regular expression

[P15863|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P15864|Normal] Global Configuration
[P15865|Heading 4] Default
[P15866|Normal] N/A
[P15867|Heading 4] Usage
[P15868|Normal] Use the community-lists to specify BGP community attributes. The community attribute is used for implementing policy routing. It is an optional, transitive attribute and facilitates transfer of local policies through different autonomous systems. It includes community values that are 32 bits long.
[P15869|Body Text] There are two kinds of community-lists–the expanded and standard. The standard community-list defines the community attributes in a specified format and not with regular expressions. The expanded community-list defines the communities attributes with regular expressions.
[P15870|Heading 4] Examples
[P15871|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ip community-list expanded CLIST permit .*
[P15872|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P15873|Normal] ip community-list
[P15874|Body Text] ip community-list standard
[P15875|Heading 3] ip community-list standard
[P15876|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P15877|Normal] Use this command to add a standard community-list entry.
[P15878|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to delete the standard community-list entry.
[P15879|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P15880|Normal] ip community-list standard WORD ( deny | permit ) COMMUNITY
[P15881|Body Text] no ip community-list standard WORD ( deny | permit ) COMMUNITY

[TABLE 540] rows=11 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	standard	Specifies a standard community list.	-

R4	deny	Specifies community to reject.	-
R5	permit	Specifies community to accept.	-
R6	COMMUNITY	(AA:NN\|internet\|local-AS\|no-advertise\|no-export)	-
R7	AA: NN	Specifies the valid value for the community number. This format represents the 32 bit communities value, where AS is the high order 16 bits and VAL is the low order 16 bits in digit Specifies the valid value for the community number. This format represents the 32 bit communities value, where AS is the high order 16 bits and VAL is the low order 16 bits in digit format.	AA is in the range 1-65535 NN is in the range of 1-65535
R8	internet	Specifies routes not to be advertised to the Internet.	-
R9	local-AS	Specifies routes not to be advertised to external BGP peers.	-
R10	no-advertise	Specifies routes not to be advertised to other BGP peers.	-
R11	no-export	Specifies routes not to be advertised outside of the Autonomous System boundary.	-

[P15882|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P15883|Normal] Global Configuration
[P15884|Heading 4] Default
[P15885|Normal] N/A
[P15886|Heading 4] Usage
[P15887|Normal] Use the community-lists to specify BGP community attributes. The community attribute is used for implementing policy routing. It is an optional, transitive attribute and facilitates transfer of local policies through different autonomous systems. It includes community values that are 32 bits long.
[P15888|Body Text] There are two kinds of community-lists–the expanded and standard. The standard community-list defines the community attributes in a specified format without regular expressions. The expanded community-list defines the communities attributes with regular expressions.
[P15889|Body Text] Use the ip community-list standard command to add a standard community-list entry. The standard community-list is compiled into binary format and is directly compared with the BGP communities attribute in the BGP updates. The comparison is faster than the expanded community-list. Any community value that does not match the standard community value is automatically treated as expanded.
[P15890|Heading 4] Examples
[P15891|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ip community-list standard CLIST permit 7675:80 7675:90 no-export
[P15892|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P15893|Normal] ip community-list
[P15894|Body Text] ip community-list expanded
[P15895|Heading 3] neighbor activate
[P15896|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P15897|Normal] Use this command to enable the exchange of the specified AF routes with a neighboring router.
[P15898|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to disable exchange of information with a neighbor.
[P15899|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P15900|Normal] neighbor NEIGHBORID activate
[P15901|Body Text] no neighbor NEIGHBORID activate

[TABLE 541] rows=4 cols=3

R4	TAG	Name of an existing peer-group. For information on how to create peer groups, refer to the neighbor peer-group and neighbor remote-as commands. When this parameter is used with a command, the command applies on all peers in the specified group.	Up to 20 characters

[P15902|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P15903|Normal] Router Configuration
[P15904|Body Text] Address Family Configuration
[P15905|Heading 4] Default
[P15906|Normal] N/A
[P15907|Heading 4] Usage
[P15908|Normal] After the TCP connection is opened with the neighbor, this command is used to enable or disable the exchange of the specified AF information with a neighboring router.
[P15909|Body Text] To enable the exchange of multicast and VPNv4 address prefix types, neighbors are activated using the neighbor activate command in address family mode.
[P15910|Heading 4] Examples
[P15911|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router bgp 10
Switch(config-router)# neighbor 1.2.3.4 activate

[P15914|Heading 3] neighbor advertisement-interval
[P15915|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P15916|Normal] Use this command to set the minimum interval between sending the BGP routing updates.
[P15917|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to set the interval time to default.
[P15918|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P15919|Normal] neighbor NEIGHBORID advertisement-interval TIME
[P15920|Body Text] no neighbor NEIGHBORID advertisement-interval

[TABLE 542] rows=5 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	NEIGHBORID	(A.B.C.D\|TAG)	-
R3	A.B.C.D	Specifies the address of the BGP neighbor in IPv4 format.	IPv4 Address in A.B.C.D format
R4	TAG	Name of an existing peer-group. For information on how to create peer groups, refer to the neighbor peer-group and neighbor remote-as commands. When this parameter is used with a command, the command applies on all peers in the specified group.	Up to 20 characters
R5	TIME	Advertise -interval value in seconds	0-600

[P15921|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P15922|Normal] Router Configuration
[P15923|Heading 4] Default
[P15924|Normal] N/A
[P15925|Heading 4] Usage
[P15926|Normal] Use this command to set the minimum interval between the sending of BGP routing updates. To reduce the flapping of routes to internet, a minimum advertisement interval is set, so that the BGP routing updates are sent only per interval seconds. bgp dampening can also be used to control the effects of flapping routes. For the originated bgp routes， they would be sent out when as-origination-interval and advertisement-interval expired at the same time.
[P15927|Heading 4] Examples
[P15928|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router bgp 10
Switch(config-router)# neighbor 10.10.0.3 advertisement-interval 45

[P15948|Heading 3] neighbor allowas-in
[P15949|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P15950|Normal] Use this command to configure PE routers to allow re-advertisement of all prefixes containing duplicate Autonomous System Numbers (ASNs).
[P15951|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to disable the readvertisement of a PE router’s ASN.
[P15952|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P15953|Normal] neighbor NEIGHBOR allowas-in [ NUMBER ]
[P15954|Body Text] no neighbor NEIGHBOR allowas-in

[TABLE 544] rows=5 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	NEIGHBORID	(A.B.C.D\|TAG)	-
R3	A.B.C.D	Specifies the address of the BGP neighbor in IPv4 format.	IPv4 Address in A.B.C.D format
R4	TAG	Name of an existing peer-group. For information on how to create peer groups, refer to the neighbor peer-group and neighbor remote-as commands. When this parameter is used with a command, the command applies on all peers in the specified group.	Up to 20 characters
R5	NUMBER	Number of occurances of AS number.Default value is 1	1-10

[P15955|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P15956|Normal] Router Configuration
[P15957|Body Text] Address Family Configuration
[P15958|Heading 4] Default
[P15959|Normal] Disabled
[P15960|Heading 4] Usage
[P15961|Normal] In a hub and spoke configuration, a PE router re-advertises all prefixes containing duplicate ASNs. Use the neighbor allowas-in command to configure two VRFs on each PE router to receive and re-advertise prefixes. One of the VRFs receives prefixes with ASNs from all PE routers and then advertises them to neighboring PE routers. The other VRF receives prefixes with ASNs from the CE router and re-advertises them to all PE routers in the hub and spoke configuration.
[P15962|Body Text] Control the number of times an ASN is advertised, by specifying a number from 1 to 10.
[P15963|Heading 4] Examples
[P15964|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config-router)# address-family ipv4 vrf VRF_A
Switch(config-router-af)# neighbor 10.10.0.1 allowas-in 3

[P16136|Heading 4] Command Mode

[P16139|Heading 4] Default
[P16140|Normal] N/A
[P16141|Heading 4] Usage
[P16142|Normal] The neighbor maximum-prefix command allows the configuration of a specified number of prefixes that a BGP router is allowed to receive from a neighbor. When the warning-only option is not used, if any extra prefixes are received, the router ends the peering. A terminated peer, stays down until the clear ip bgp command is used.
[P16143|Heading 4] Examples
[P16144|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router bgp 10
Switch(config-router)# neighbor 10.10.0.72 maximum-prefix 1244 warning-only

[P16206|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P16207|Normal] Router Configuration
[P16208|Heading 4] Default
[P16209|Normal] N/A
[P16210|Heading 4] Usage
[P16211|Normal] Use this command to Neighbors with the same update policies are grouped into peer groups. This facilitates the updates of various policies, such as, distribute and filter lists. The peer-group is then configured easily with any of the neighbor commands. Any changes made to the peer group affect all members.
[P16212|Body Text] To create a peer-group use the neighbor peer-group create command and then use this command to add neighbors to the group.
[P16213|Heading 4] Examples
[P16214|Normal] This example shows a new peer-group group1 and the adding of a neighbor 10.10.0.63 to the group:
[P16215|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router bgp 10
Switch(config-router)# neighbor group1 peer-group
Switch(config-router)# neighbor 10.10.0.63 peer-group group1

R4	TAG	Name of an existing peer-group. For information on how to create peer groups, refer to the neighbor peer-group and neighbor remote-as commands. When this parameter is used with a command, the command applies on all peers in the specified group.	Up to 20 characters

[P16242|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P16243|Normal] Router Configuration
[P16244|Body Text] Address Family Configuration
[P16245|Heading 4] Default
[P16246|Normal] N/A
[P16247|Heading 4] Usage
[P16248|Normal] Use this command to specify a prefix list for filtering BGP advertisements. Filtering by prefix list matches the prefixes of routes with those listed in the prefix list. If there is a match, the route is used. An empty prefix list permits all prefixes. If a given prefix does not match any entries of a prefix list, the route is denied access. When multiple entries of a prefix list match a prefix, the entry with the smallest sequence number is considered to be a real match.
[P16249|Body Text] The router begins the search at the top of the prefix list, with the sequence number 1. Once a match or deny occurs, the router does not need to go through the rest of the prefix list. For efficiency the most common matches or denies are listed at the top.
[P16250|Body Text] The neighbor distribute-list command is an alternative to the neighbor prefix-list command and only
[P16251|Body Text] one of them can be used for filtering to the same neighbor in any direction.
[P16252|Heading 4] Examples
[P16253|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ip prefix-list list1 deny 30.0.0.0/24
Switch(config)# router bgp 12
Switch(config-router)# neighbor 10.10.10.10 prefix-list list1 in
[P16254|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P16255|Normal] ip prefix-list

[P16285|Normal] The private AS numbers range from <64512-65535>. Private AS numbers are not advertised to the Internet. This command is used with external BGP peers only. [P16297|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P16298|Normal] Router Configuration
[P16299|Body Text] Address Family Configuration
[P16300|Heading 4] Default
[P16301|Normal] N/A
[P16302|Heading 4] Usage
[P16303|Normal] Route reflectors are a solution for the explosion of iBGP peering within an autonomous system. By route reflection the number of iBGP peers within an AS is reduced. Use the neighbor route-reflector-client command to configure the local router as the route reflector and specify neighbors as its client.
[P16304|Body Text] An AS can have more than one route reflector. One route reflector treats the other route reflector as another iBGP speaker.
[P16305|Heading 4] Examples
[P16306|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router bgp 10
Switch(config-router)# neighbor 10.10.0.72 route-reflector-client

[P16356|Heading 4] Usage
[P16357|Normal] Use this command to store updates for inbound soft reconfiguration. Soft-reconfiguration may be used in lieu of BGP route refresh capability. Using this command enables local storage of all the received routes and their attributes. This requires additional memory. When a soft reset (inbound) is done on this neighbor, the locally stored routes are reprocessed according to the inbound policy. The BGP neighbor connection is not affected.

[P16389|Normal] N/A
[P16390|Heading 4] Usage
[P16391|Normal] Keepalive messages are sent by a router to inform another router that the BGP connection between the two is still active. The keepalive interval is the period of time between each keepalive message sent by the router. The holdtime interval is the time the router waits to receive a keepalive message and if it does not receive a message for this period it declares the neighbor dead.
[P16392|Heading 4] Examples
[P16393|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router bgp 12
Switch(config-router)# neighbor 10.10.10.10 timers 60 120

[P16442|Normal] Use this command to specify a weight value to all routes learned from a neighbor. The route with the highest weight gets preference when there are other routes on the network.

[P16466|Heading 3] neighbor collide-established
[P16467|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P16468|Normal] Use this command to configure a BGP neighbor should be included into collision detection even its stats is established.
[P16469|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to disable this function.
[P16470|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P16471|Normal] neighbor NEIGHBORID collide-established
[P16472|Body Text] no neighbor NEIGHBORID collide-established

[TABLE 573] rows=3 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	NEIGHBORID	(A.B.C.D\|TAG)	-
R3	A.B.C.D	Specifies the address of the BGP neighbor in IPv4 format.	IPv4 Address in A.B.C.D format

[P16473|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P16474|Normal] Router Configuration
[P16475|Heading 4] Default
[P16476|Normal] In the default case, if a neighbor’s state is established, it will not be included into collision detection.
[P16477|Heading 4] Usage
[P16478|Normal] When building connection with BGP neighbors, devices on both sides may start TCP connections in the sasme time. There will be two TCP connections in this case. To avoid reduncancy, collision detection is required to shutdown the connection on the side whose router-id or BGP identifier is smaller.
[P16479|Body Text] In the default case, when a BGP neighbor is already established, it will not be included into collision detection, which may causes redundant connections. Therefore, this command should be used to include established neighbors into collision detection.
[P16480|Heading 4] Examples
[P16481|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal 
Switch(config)# router bgp 100
Switch(config-router)# neighbor 10.1.1.2 collide-establishe

[P16484|Heading 3] neighbor disallow-infinite-holdtime
[P16485|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P16486|Normal] Use this command to prohibit BGP neighbor to use infinite holdtime in OPEN message.
[P16487|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to allow BGP neighbor to use infinite holdtime.
[P16488|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P16489|Normal] neighbor NEIGHBORID disallow-infinite-holdtime
[P16490|Body Text] no neighbor NEIGHBORID disallow-infinite-holdtime

[TABLE 574] rows=3 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	NEIGHBORID	(A.B.C.D\|TAG)	-
R3	A.B.C.D	Specifies the address of the BGP neighbor in IPv4 format.	IPv4 Address in A.B.C.D format

[P16491|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P16492|Normal] Router Configuration
[P16493|Heading 4] Default
[P16494|Normal] In the default case, if a neighbor’s state is established, it will not be included into collision detection.
[P16495|Heading 4] Usage
[P16496|Normal] After building connection with BGP neighbors, devices need to send keepalive message to keep the connetion. The interval of sending keepalive message is the holdtime. When a neighbor negotiated the holdtime to be 0(infinite), the two neighbors on both sides will not need keepalive messages anymore.
[P16497|Body Text] Use this command to prohibit the neighbor to neigotiate the holdtime to infinite.
[P16498|Heading 4] Examples
[P16499|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal 
Switch(config)# router bgp 100
Switch(config-router)# neighbor 10.1.1.2 disallow-infinite-holdtime

[P16503|Heading 4] Command Purpose

[P16507|Normal] neighbor NEIGHBORID dont-capability-negotiate

[P16509|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P16510|Normal] Router Configuration
[P16511|Heading 4] Default
[P16512|Normal] In the default case, it is allowed for a BGP neighbor to attach the capability segment in OPEN messages.
[P16513|Heading 4] Usage
[P16514|Normal] In the BGP open messages, neighbors can negotiate capabilities through the capability segment in open messages.
[P16515|Body Text] When the switch received an open message containing capability segment after enabled this function, it will send a notification message and shutdown the connetion with the neighbor.
[P16516|Heading 4] Examples
[P16517|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal 
Switch(config)# router bgp 100
Switch(config-router)# neighbor 10.1.1.2 dont-capability-negotiate

[P16521|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P16522|Normal] Use this command to allow EBGP neighbor to build connection through multihop routes.
[P16523|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to prohibit EBGP neighbor to build connection through multihop routes, which means EBGP neighbor must be directly connected.
[P16524|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P16525|Normal] neighbor NEIGHBORID enforce-multihop
[P16526|Body Text] no neighbor NEIGHBORID enforce-multihop

[TABLE 576] rows=3 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	NEIGHBORID	(A.B.C.D\|TAG)	-
R3	A.B.C.D	Specifies the address of the BGP neighbor in IPv4 format.	IPv4 Address in A.B.C.D format

[P16527|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P16528|Normal] Router Configuration
[P16529|Heading 4] Default
[P16530|Normal] In the default case, it is only allowed to build connection with directly connected EBGP neighbor.
[P16531|Heading 4] Usage
[P16532|Normal] Usually EBGP neighbor connection is built through direct connection. And the TTL of its TCP packets is 1. When build neighbor through non-direct connection like loopback interface, due to the limitation of TTL, the connection will fail. Then this command will be used to allow connection with EBGP neighbor through multihop routes.
[P16533|Heading 4] Examples
[P16534|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal 
Switch(config)# router bgp 100
Switch(config-router)# neighbor 10.1.1.2 enforce-multihop

[P16610|Heading 3] network synchronization
[P16611|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P16612|Normal] Use this command to ensure the exact same static network prefix, specified through any of the network commands, is local or has IGP reachability (in the NSM RIB) before being introduced into the BGP RIB.

[P16618|Normal] Router Configuration
[P16619|Body Text] Address Family Configuration

[P16623|Normal] N/A

[P16626|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal

[P16627|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P16628|Normal] N/A
[P16629|Heading 3] synchronization
[P16630|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P16631|Normal] Use this command to enable IGP synchronization of Internal BGP (iBGP) learned routes with the Internal Gateway Protocol (IGP) system in the router configuration mode or in the address-family configuration mode.
[P16632|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to disable this function.
[P16633|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P16634|Normal] synchronization
[P16635|Body Text] no synchronization
[P16636|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P16637|Normal] Router Configuration
[P16638|Body Text] Address Family Configuration
[P16639|Heading 4] Default
[P16640|Normal] IGP synchronization is disabled.
[P16641|Heading 4] Usage
[P16642|Normal] Synchronization is used when a BGP router should not advertise routes learned from iBGP neighbors, unless those routes are also present in an IGP (for example, OSPF). Synchronization may be enabled when all the routers in an autonomous system do not speak BGP, and the autonomous system is a transit for other autonomous systems. The no synchronization command is used when BGP router can advertise routes learned from its iBGP neighbors without waiting for the IGP reachability to be present.
[P16643|Heading 4] Examples
[P16644|Normal] The following example enables IGP synchronization of BGP static network routes in the IPv4-Unicast address family:
[P16645|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router bgp 11
Switch(config)# address-family ipv4 unicast
Switch(config-af)# network synchronization

[TABLE 585] rows=10 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	TYPE	AA:NN\|local-AS\|no-advertise\|no-export	-
R3	AA:NN	Specifies the valid value for the community number. This format represents the 32 bit communities value, where AS is the high order 16 bits and VAL is the low order 16 bits in digit format.	AA is in the range 1-65535 NN is in the range of 1-65535
R4	local-AS	Do not send outside local AS (well-known community).	-
R5	no-advertise	Do not advertise to any peer (well-known community).	-
R6	no-export	Do not export to next AS (well-known community).	-
R7	exact-match	Specifies that display the exact match of the communities.	-
R8	PREFIX	(multicast\|unicast)	-
R9	multicast	Specifies a IPv4 multicast address family.	-
R10	unicast	Specifies a IPv4 unicast address family. This is the default option.	-

[P17005|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P17006|Normal] Use this command sets the BGP keepalive timer and holdtime timer values.
[P17007|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to reset timers to default value.
[P17008|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P17009|Normal] timers bgp KEEPALIVE HOLDTIME
[P17010|Body Text] no timers bgp

[TABLE 599] rows=3 cols=3

R2	KEEPALIVE	<0-65535> The frequency with which the keepalive messages are sent to the neighbors. The default value is 60 seconds.	0-65535
R3	HOLDTIME	The interval after which the neighbor is considered dead if keepalive messages are not received. The default holdtime value is 180 seconds.	3-65535

[P17017|Heading 4] Examples
[P17018|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router bgp 10
Switch(config-router)# timers bgp 40 120

[P17057|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P17058|Normal] Use this command to specify the time period during which the authentication on a key chain is received as valid.
[P17059|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to negate this command.
[P17060|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P17061|Normal] accept-lifetime HH:MM:SS DAY MONTH YEAR HH1:MM1:SS1 DAY1 MONTH1 YEAR1
[P17062|Body Text] accept-lifetime HH:MM:SS MONTH DAY YEAR infinite
[P17063|Body Text] accept-lifetime HH:MM:SS MONTH DAY YEAR duration <1-2147483646>
[P17064|Body Text] no accept-lifetime

[TABLE 602] rows=10 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	HH:MM:SS	Specify the end time of accept-lifetime in hours, minutes and seconds.	0-23:0-59:0-59
R3	DAY	Specify the day of the month to end.	1-31
R4	MONTH	Specify the month of the year to end as the first three letters of the month, for example, december.	january, february, march, april, may, june, july, august, september, october, november, december
R5	YEAR	Specify the year to end.	1993-2035
R6	HH1:MM1:SS1		0-23:0-59:0-59
R7	DAY1		1-31
R8	MONTH1		january, february, march, april, may, june, july, august, september, october, november, december
R9	YEAR1		1993-2035
R10	<1-2147483646>	Specify the actual end time duration of a key in seconds.	1-2147483646

[P17113|Heading 3] area-password
[P17114|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P17115|Normal] Use this command to set the authentication password for the Level-1 area and to set authentication on Level-1 SNP PDUs. This command enables authentication when receiving and sending LSP and SNP PDU in Level-1 areas. Area password must be the same for all the routers in the same area.
[P17116|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to clear the area password.
[P17117|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P17118|Normal] area-password PASSWORD
[P17119|Body Text] area-password WORD authenticate snp ( send-only | validate )
[P17120|Body Text] no area-password

[TABLE 604] rows=6 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	PASSWORD	Specify the password string.	Up to 254 characters
R3	authenticate	Specify to insert the password into Level-1 SNP PDUs.	-
R4	snp	Specify the sequence number PDU (SNP).	-
R5	send-only	Specify to only insert the password into the Level-1 SNP PDUs, but not check the password in SNP PDUs that it receives. Use this keysword during a software upgrade to ease the transition.	-
R6	validate	Specify to insert the password into the Level-1 SNP PDUs and check the password in SNPs that it receives.	-

[P17121|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P17122|Normal] Router Configuration

[P17129|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal

[P17132|Heading 3] authentication key-chain
[P17133|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P17134|Normal] Use this command to set the key chain to be used for authentication at the instance level. Authentication mode must be set to md5 to configure the key chain. If no key chain is configured with the key-chain command, no key-chain authentication is performed.
[P17135|Body Text] Only one authentication key-chain is applied to an interface at a time. That is, issuing a second isis authentication key-chain command overrides the first isis authentication key-chain command. Authentication can be specified for an individual interface using the isis authentication key-chain command.
[P17136|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to unset the key chain used for authentication.
[P17137|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P17138|Normal] authentication key-chain WORD ( level-1 | level-2 | )
[P17139|Body Text] no authentication key-chain PASSWORD ( level-1 | level-2 | )
[P17140|Body Text] no authentication key-chain ( level-1 | level-2 | )

[TABLE 605] rows=4 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	WORD	Specify the chain name (valid authentication keys).	A String of key chain name
R3	level-1	Specify an authentication key-chain for level-1 PDUs.	-
R4	level-2	Specify an authentication key-chain for level-2 PDUs.	-

[P17141|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P17142|Normal] Router Configuration
[P17143|Heading 4] Default
[P17144|Normal] Disabled
[P17145|Heading 4] Usage
[P17146|Normal] If neither the level-1 nor the level-2 keysword is configured, it applies to both levels.
[P17147|Heading 4] Examples
[P17148|Normal] The following example shows how to set the key chain to be used for authentication at the level-1:
[P17149|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router isis 1
Switch(config-router)# authentication key-chain code1234 level-1
[P17150|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P17151|Normal] None
[P17152|Heading 3] authentication mode md5
[P17153|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P17154|Normal] Use this command to set the MD5 authentication mode at the instance level.
[P17155|Body Text] If clear-text authentication was configured using the area-password or domain-password commands, the authentication mode command overrides both of those commands (based on the level at which MD5 is configured). If the authentication mode command was used first, and subsequently an attempt is made to use the area-password or domain-password commands, the attempt fails. To configure clear-text authentication using the area-password or domain-password commands, first use the no authentication mode command.
[P17156|Body Text] The type of authentication and the level to which it applies can be specified for a single interface, rather than per instance, using the isis authentication mode command.
[P17157|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to unset the MD5 authentication mode.
[P17158|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P17159|Normal] authentication mode ( md5 | text ) ( level-1 | level-2 | )
[P17160|Body Text] no authentication mode ( md5 | text ) ( level-1 | level-2 | )

[TABLE 606] rows=5 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	md5	Keyed message digest	-
R3	text	Text mode	-
R4	level-1	Specify an authentication key-chain for level-1 PDUs.	-
R5	level-2	Specify an authentication key-chain for level-2 PDUs.	-

[P17161|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P17162|Normal] Router Configuration
[P17163|Heading 4] Default
[P17164|Normal] Disabled
[P17165|Heading 4] Usage
[P17166|Normal] If neither the level-1 nor the level-2 keysword is configured, it applies to both levels.
[P17167|Heading 4] Examples
[P17168|Normal] The following example shows how to set the MD5 authentication mode at the level-1:
[P17169|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router isis 1
Switch(config-router)# authentication mode md5 level-1
Switch(config-router)# no authentication mode md5 level-1

[P17171|Normal] None
[P17172|Heading 3] authentication send-only
[P17173|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P17174|Normal] Use this command to set the send-only option at the instance level.
[P17175|Body Text] Use this command before configuring the authentication mode and authentication key-chain, so that the implementation of authentication goes smoothly.
[P17176|Body Text] After all routers that must communicate are configured with this command, enable the authentication mode and key chain on each router. Then, specify the no authentication send-only command to disable the send-only feature.
[P17177|Body Text] If neither the level-1 nor level-2 keysword is configured, the send-only feature applies to both levels.The send-only option applies to both levels if no level is specified.
[P17178|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to unset the send-only option.
[P17179|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P17180|Normal] authentication send-only ( level-1 | level-2 | )
[P17181|Body Text] no authentication send-only ( level-1 | level-2 | )

[TABLE 607] rows=3 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	level-1	Specify an authentication key-chain for level-1 PDUs.	-
R3	level-2	Specify an authentication key-chain for level-2 PDUs.	-

[P17187|Normal] If neither the level-1 nor the level-2 keysword is configured, it applies to both levels.

[P17390|Heading 3] ignore-lsp-errors
[P17391|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P17392|Normal] Use this command to ignore LSPs with checksum errors. By default, validates checksum for LSP whenever it receives LSPs and if the checksum has an error, the LSP will be dropped. Configuring this command to ignore the LSP checksum error and treat it as if checksum is passed.
[P17393|Body Text] Use the no parameter to turn off this function.
[P17394|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P17395|Normal] ignore-lsp-errors
[P17396|Body Text] no ignore-lsp-errors
[P17397|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P17398|Normal] Router Configuration
[P17399|Heading 4] Default
[P17400|Normal] Disabled
[P17401|Heading 4] Usage
[P17402|Normal] None
[P17403|Heading 4] Examples
[P17404|Normal] The following example shows how to ignore LSPs with checksum errors:
[P17405|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router isis bb
Switch(config-router)# ignore-lsp-errors

[P17426|Heading 3] ip router isis
[P17427|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P17428|Normal] Use this command to enable IPv4 routing on the interface. This command is mandatory to configuration. Match the instance tag to one of existing instance’s tags, or a new instance with the tag name should be initiated, otherwise routing will not run on this interface.
[P17429|Body Text] Configuring this command, the router sends Hello with IP address TLV on this interface, and IP reachability information TLV in the LSP will be updated.
[P17430|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to disable IPv4 routing on the interface. This action does not clear the database. To clear the database, unconfigure the routing instance.
[P17431|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P17432|Normal] ip router isis ( INSTANCE | )
[P17433|Body Text] no ip router isis ( INSTANCE | )

[TABLE 617] rows=2 cols=3

[P17464|Heading 3] isis authentication key-chain
[P17465|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P17466|Normal] Use this command to set the key chain to be used for authentication on the interface-related packets.
[P17467|Body Text] Authentication mode must be set to md5 or text to configure the key chain. If no key chain is configured with the key-chain command, no key-chain authentication is performed. Only one authentication key-chain is applied to an interface at a time. That is, issuing a second isis authentication key-chain command overrides the first isis authentication key-chain command.
[P17468|Body Text] If neither the level-1 nor level-2 keysword is configured, the key chain applies to the level(s) on which the authentication mode is configured as md5. Authentication can be specified for an entire, instead of at the interface level, by using the authentication key-chain command.
[P17469|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to unset the key chain used for authentication on the interface-related packets.
[P17470|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P17471|Normal] isis authentication key-chain KEY_NAME ( level-1 | level-2 | )
[P17472|Body Text] no isis authentication key-chain ( level-1 | level-2 | )
[P17473|Body Text] no isis authentication key-chain KEY_NAME ( level-1 | level-2 | )

[TABLE 619] rows=4 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	KEY_NAME	Chain name - valid authentication keys.	A String of key chain name
R3	level-1	Specify an authentication key-chain for level-1 PDUs.	-
R4	level-2	Specify an authentication key-chain for level-2 PDUs.	-

[P17474|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P17475|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P17476|Heading 4] Default
[P17477|Normal] Disabled
[P17478|Heading 4] Usage
[P17479|Normal] The key chain applies to the level(s) on which authentication mode is configured as MD5 if no level is specified.
[P17480|Heading 4] Examples
[P17481|Normal] The following example shows how to set the key chain to be used for authentication on the interface-related packets:
[P17482|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# isis authentication key-chain code1234 level-1
[P17483|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P17484|Normal] None
[P17485|Heading 3] isis authentication mode md5
[P17486|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P17487|Normal] Use this command to set the MD5 authentication mode. If clear text authentication was configured using the isis password command, the isis authentication mode command overrides the isis password command. If the isis authentication mode command was used, then subsequently an attempt is made to use the isis password command, the attempt fails.
[P17488|Body Text] To configure clear text authentication using the isis password command, first use the no isis authentication mode command. The type of authentication and the level to which it applies can be specified for the entire instance, rather than per interface, using the authentication mode command.
[P17489|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to unset the MD5 authentication mode.
[P17490|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P17491|Normal] isis authentication mode ( md5 | text ) ( level-1 | level-2 | )
[P17492|Body Text] no isis authentication mode ( md5 | text ) ( level-1 | level-2 | )

[TABLE 620] rows=5 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	md5	Keyed message digest	-
R3	text	Text mode	-
R4	level-1	Specify an authentication key-chain for level-1 PDUs.	-
R5	level-2	Specify an authentication key-chain for level-2 PDUs.	-

[P17493|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P17494|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P17495|Heading 4] Default
[P17496|Normal] Disabled
[P17497|Heading 4] Usage
[P17498|Normal] The send-only option applies to both levels if no level is specified.
[P17499|Heading 4] Examples
[P17500|Normal] The following example shows how to set the MD5 authentication mode.:
[P17501|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# isis authentication mode md5
[P17502|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P17503|Normal] None
[P17504|Heading 3] isis authentication send-only
[P17505|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P17506|Normal] Use this command to set the send-only option to the interface-related packets.
[P17507|Body Text] Use this command before configuring the ISIS authentication mode and ISIS authentication key-chain, so that the implementation of authentication goes smoothly. That is, the routers will have more time for the keys to be configured on each router if authentication is inserted only on the packets being sent, not checked on packets being received.
[P17508|Body Text] After all routers that must communicate are configured with this command, enable the authentication mode and key chain on each router.
[P17509|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to unset the send-only option to the interface-related packets.
[P17510|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P17511|Normal] isis authentication send-only ( level-1 | level-2 | )
[P17512|Body Text] no isis authentication send-only ( level-1 | level-2 | )

[TABLE 621] rows=3 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	level-1	Specify an authentication key-chain for level-1 PDUs.	-
R3	level-2	Specify an authentication key-chain for level-2 PDUs.	-

[P17513|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P17514|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P17515|Heading 4] Default
[P17516|Normal] Disabled
[P17517|Heading 4] Usage
[P17518|Normal] The send-only option applies to both levels if no level is specified.
[P17519|Heading 4] Examples
[P17520|Normal] The following example shows how to set the send-only option to the interface-related packets.:
[P17521|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# isis authentication send-only

[P17524|Heading 3] isis bfd

[P17526|Normal] Use this command to enable/disable the BFD check on interface.
[P17527|Body Text] The isis bfd command allows a user to enable BFD on an interface. The isis bfd disable command disables BFD checking on an interface. However, the no isis bfd and no isis bfd disable commands both remove the enable/disable configuration, but do not disable/enable BFD.

[P17562|Heading 3] isis csnp-interval
[P17563|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P17564|Normal] Use this command to set CSNP (Complete sequence number PDU) interval in seconds.
[P17565|Body Text] Configuring this command changes the interval between two consecutive CSNP transmission. By default, CSNP is sent every 10 seconds only by LAN DIS. This parameter is only valid on broadcast interface, since periodic CSNP is only sent on broadcast interface, while CSNP on Point-to-Point interface is sent only when adjacency is initiated.
[P17566|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to reset CSNP interval to the default value.
[P17567|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P17568|Normal] isis csnp-interval INTERVAL ( level-1 | level-2 | )

R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	INTERVAL	Specify the CSNP interval in seconds.	1-65535
R3	level-1	Specify Level-1 CSNP.	-
R4	level-2	Specify Level-2 CSNP.	-

[P17571|Heading 4] Command Mode

[P17600|Heading 3] isis hello-interval
[P17601|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P17602|Normal] Use this command to set the Hello interval in seconds. The Hello-interval is set with the hello-multiplier (see isis hello-multiplier command).
[P17603|Body Text] Configuring this command changes the time interval between two consecutive Hello transmissions. If a device receives its own LSP with a maximum sequence number, then it suspends for the hold interval. DIS sends Hello transmissions at three times the rate than non-DIS. If is elected as DIS on this interface, sends Hello every 3.3 seconds.
[P17604|Body Text] If minimal keysword is specified, Holding timer in Hello PDU is set to 1 second and Hello interval is calculated by dividing by the hello-multiplier. For example, if the hello-multiplier is configured as 4 and hello-interval minimal is the command used, an Hello PDU is sent every 250 milliseconds.
[P17605|Body Text] Use the no parameter to set the Hello interval to the default.
[P17606|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P17607|Normal] isis hello-interval INTERVAL ( level-1 | level-2 | )
[P17608|Body Text] isis hello-interval minimal ( level-1 | level-2 | )
[P17609|Body Text] no isis hello-interval ( level-1 | level-2 | )
[P17610|Body Text] no isis hello-interval <1-65535> ( level-1 | level-2 | )
[P17611|Body Text] no isis hello-interval minimal ( level-1 | level-2 | )

[TABLE 626] rows=5 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	INTERVAL	Specify the hello interval in seconds.	1-65535
R3	minimal	Specify the holding-time as 1 second.	-
R4	level-1	Specify Level-1 CSNP.	-
R5	level-2	Specify Level-2 CSNP.	-

[P17612|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P17613|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P17614|Heading 4] Default
[P17615|Normal] By default, uses 10 seconds for the interval and the interval is applied to both level-1 and level-2.
[P17616|Heading 4] Usage
[P17617|Normal] If neither the level-1 nor the level-2 keysword is configured, it applies to both levels.
[P17618|Heading 4] Examples
[P17619|Normal] The following example shows how to set the Hello interval.:
[P17620|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# isis hello-interval 5 level-1

[P17752|Heading 3] isis priority
[P17753|Heading 4] Command Purpose

[P17755|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P17756|Normal] isis priority PRIORITY ( level-1 | level-2 | )
[P17757|Body Text] no isis priority ( level-1 | level-2 | )
[P17758|Body Text] no isis priority <0-127> ( level-1 | level-2 | )

[TABLE 634] rows=4 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	PRIORITY	Priority value	0-127
R3	level-1	Specify a priority for Level-1 hello PDUs.	-
R4	level-2	Specify a priority for Level-2 hello PDUs.	-

[P17759|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P17760|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P17761|Heading 4] Default
[P17762|Normal] By default, uses 64 for the priority value, and the priority is applied to both level-1 and level-2.
[P17763|Heading 4] Usage
[P17764|Normal] If neither the level-1 nor the level-2 keysword is configured, it applies to both levels.
[P17765|Heading 4] Examples
[P17766|Normal] The following example shows how to set the priority for LAN DIS election:
[P17767|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# isis priority 127

[P17973|Heading 3] passive-interface
[P17974|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P17975|Normal] Use this command to suppress routing updates on all interfaces or on a specified interface, which puts the interfaces into passive mode. [P18103|Heading 3] set-overload-bit
[P18104|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P18105|Normal] To configure the router to signal other routers not to use it as an intermediate hop in their shortest path first
[P18106|Body Text] (SPF) calculations, use the set-overload-bit command in router configuration mode. To remove the designation,
[P18107|Body Text] use the noform of this command.
[P18108|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P18109|Normal] set-overload-bit ( { suppress ( external | interlevel | external interlevel | interlevel external ) | on-startup ( TIME | wait-for-bgp ) } | )
[P18110|Body Text] no set-overload-bit

[TABLE 652] rows=7 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	suppress	Specify to suppress specific types of IP prefixes.	-
R3	external	Specify to redistribute external reachability (to prevent the IP prefixes learned from other protocols from being advertised).	-
R4	interlevel	Specify to redistribute interlevel reachability.	-
R5	on-startup	Specify an interval in seconds after which the overload state is exited.	-
R6	TIME	Specify the time in seconds to advertise one self as overloaded after reboot.	5-86400
R7	wait-for-bgp	Specify that BGP determines when to unset the overload bit.	-

[P18111|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P18112|Normal] Router Configuration
[P18113|Heading 4] Default
[P18114|Normal] By default, no overload-bit is set.
[P18115|Heading 4] Usage
[P18116|Normal] None
[P18117|Heading 4] Examples
[P18118|Normal] The following example shows how to set overload bit:
[P18119|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router isis bb
Switch(config-router)# set-overload-bit
[P18120|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P18121|Normal] None
[P18122|Heading 3] spf-interval-exp
[P18123|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P18124|Normal] Use this command to set the minimum and maximum hold intervals between Shortest Path First (SPF) calculations.
[P18125|Body Text] The spf-interval-exp command configures the minimum and maximum interval time between the receipt of a topology change and the calculation of the SPF.
[P18126|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to set the minimum and maximum hold intervals to the default.
[P18127|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P18128|Normal] spf-interval-exp EXP_MIN EXP_MAX
[P18129|Body Text] spf-interval-exp ( level-1 | level-2 ) <0-2147483647> <0-2147483647>
[P18130|Body Text] no spf-interval-exp

[TABLE 653] rows=5 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	EXP_MIN	Specify the minimum delay between receiving a change to the SPF calculation in milliseconds.	0-2147483647
R3	EXP_MAX	Specify the maximum delay between receiving a change to the SPF calculation in milliseconds.	0-2147483647
R4	level-1	Specify an interval for Level-1 IS.	-
R5	level-2	Specify an interval for Level-2 IS.	-

[P18131|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P18132|Normal] Router Configuration
[P18133|Heading 4] Default
[P18134|Normal] By default, uses 500 milliseconds and 50,000 milliseconds for the minimum and maximum hold intervals, respectively. The values are applied to both level-1 and level-2 if the level parameter is omitted.
[P18135|Heading 4] Usage
[P18136|Normal] None
[P18137|Heading 4] Examples
[P18138|Normal] The following example shows how to set the minimum and maximum hold intervals between Shortest Path First (SPF) calculations:
[P18139|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router isis bb
Switch(config-router)# spf-interval-exp level-1 600 60000
Switch(config-router)# no spf-interval-exp level-1
[P18140|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P18141|Normal] None
[P18142|Heading 3] summary-address
[P18143|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P18144|Normal] Use this command to configure Summary Address to summarize IPv4 reachability information.
[P18145|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to unconfigure the summary.
[P18146|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P18147|Normal] summary-address IP_ADDR/IP_MASK_LEN ( level-1 | level-1-2 | level-2 | ) ( metric ) ( METRIC | )
[P18148|Body Text] no summary-address IP_ADDR/IP_MASK_LEN

[TABLE 654] rows=7 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	IP_ADDR/IP_MASK_LEN	Specify the IPv4 prefix to be announced.	IPv4 Address and mask length in A.B.C.D/M format
R3	level-1	Specify the reachability information only for Level-1.	-
R4	level-1-2	Specify the reachability information for both Level-1 and Level-2.	-
R5	level-2	Specify the reachability information only for Level-2.	-
R6	metric	Specify the metric for the summarized address.	-
R7	METRIC	Specify the metric. The default is 0.	1-4294967295

[P18149|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P18150|Normal] Router Configuration
[P18151|Heading 4] Default
[P18152|Normal] By default, does not configure the summary-address. Summary-address is applied to Level-2 IS if level parameter is omitted.
[P18153|Heading 4] Usage
[P18154|Normal] If neither the level-1 nor the level-2 keysword is configured, it applies to level-2
[P18155|Heading 4] Examples
[P18156|Normal] The following example shows how to configure ipv4 Summary Address:
[P18157|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router isis bb
Switch(config-router)# summary-address 10.10.0.0/16
[P18158|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P18159|Normal] None

R3	level-1	Specify the reachability information only for Level-1.	-
