[P18380|Heading 3] area default-cost
[P18381|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P18382|Normal] To specify a cost for the default summary route sent into a stub, use the area default-cost command in router configuration mode.
[P18383|Body Text] To remove the assigned default route cost, use the no form of this command.
[P18384|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P18385|Normal] area AREA-ID default-cost COST
[P18386|Body Text] no area AREA-ID default-cost

[TABLE 664] rows=3 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	AREA-ID	Identifier of the area for which authentication is to be enabled. The identifier can be specified as either a decimal value or an IP address	IP address or number in the range of 0-4294967295
R3	COST	Cost for the default summary route used for a stub.	0-16777215

[P18387|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P18388|Normal] Router Configuration
[P18389|Heading 4] Default
[P18390|Normal] The cost value is 1 by default.
[P18391|Heading 4] Usage
[P18392|Normal] The command is used only on an Area Border Router (ABR) attached to a stub.
[P18393|Body Text] There are two stub area router configuration commands: the stub and default-cost options of the area command. In all routers and access servers attached to the stub area, the area should be configured as a stub area using the stub option of the area command. Use the default-cost option only on an ABR attached to the stub area. The default-cost option provides the metric for the summary default route generated by the ABR into the stub area.
[P18394|Heading 4] Examples
[P18395|Normal] The following example assigns a default cost of 20 to stub network 10.0.0.0:
[P18396|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)#router ipv6 ospf 201
Switch(config-router)#area 10.0.0.0 stub
Switch(config-router)#area 10.0.0.0 default-cost 20
[P18397|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P18398|Normal] None
[P18399|Heading 3] area range
[P18400|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P18401|Normal] To consolidate and summarize routes at an area boundary, use the area range command in router configuration mode.To disable this function, use the no form of this command.
[P18402|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P18403|Normal] area AREA-ID range ADDRESS/PREFIX-LENGTH ( advertise | not-advertise | )
[P18404|Body Text] no area AREA-ID range ADDRESS/PREFIX-LENGTH

[TABLE 665] rows=6 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	AREA-ID	Identifier of the area for which authentication is to be enabled. The identifier can be specified as either a decimal value or an IP address	IP address or number in the range of 0-4294967295
R3	ADDRESS	IPv6 address	IPv6 Address
R4	PREFIX-LENGTH	Prefix length of the address	1-128
R5	advertise	Advertise this range (default)	-
R6	not-advertise	Do Not Advertise this range	-

[P18405|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P18406|Normal] Router Configuration
[P18407|Heading 4] Default
[P18408|Normal] This command is disabled by default.
[P18409|Heading 4] Usage
[P18410|Normal] The area range command is used only with Area Border Routers (ABRs). It is used to consolidate or summarize routes for an area. The result is that a single summary route is advertised to other areas by the ABR. Routing information is condensed at area boundaries. External to the area, a single route is advertised for each address range. This behavior is called route summarization.
[P18411|Body Text] Multiple area router configuration commands specifying the range option can be configured. Thus, OSPF can summarize addresses for many different sets of address ranges.
[P18412|Heading 4] Examples
[P18413|Normal] The following example specifies one summary route to be advertised by the ABR to other areas for all subnets on area 10:
[P18414|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router ipv6 ospf 201
Switch(config-router)#area 10 range 2004::1/16
[P18415|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P18416|Normal] None
[P18417|Heading 3] area stub
[P18418|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P18419|Normal] To define an area as a stub area, use the area stub command in router configuration mode.
[P18420|Body Text] To disable this function, use the no form of this command.
[P18421|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P18422|Normal] area AREA-ID stub ( no-summary | )
[P18423|Body Text] no area AREA-ID stub ( no-summary | )

[TABLE 666] rows=3 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	AREA-ID	Identifier of the area for which authentication is to be enabled. The identifier can be specified as either a decimal value or an IP address	IP address or number in the range of 0-4294967295
R3	no-summary	(Optional) Prevents an Area Border Router (ABR) from sending summary link advertisements into the stub area	-

[P18424|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P18425|Normal] Router Configuration
[P18426|Heading 4] Default
[P18427|Normal] No stub area is defined.
[P18428|Heading 4] Usage
[P18429|Normal] You must configure the area stub command on all routers and access servers in the stub area. Use the area router configuration command with the default-cost keyword to specify the cost of a default internal router sent into a stub area by an ABR.
[P18430|Body Text] There are two stub area router configuration commands: the stub and default-cost options of the area router configuration command. In all routers attached to the stub area, the area should be configured as a stub area using the stub keyword of the area command. Use the default-cost keyword only on an ABR attached to the stub area. The default-cost keyword provides the metric for the summary default route generated by the ABR into the stub area.
[P18431|Body Text] To further reduce the number of link-state advertisements (LSAs) sent into a stub area, you can configure the no-summary keyword on the ABR to prevent it from sending summary LSAs (LSA type 3) into the stub area.
[P18432|Heading 4] Examples
[P18433|Normal] The following example assigns a default cost of 20 to stub network 10.0.0.0:
[P18434|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router ipv6 ospf 201
Switch(config-router)#area 10.0.0.0 stub
Switch(config-router)#area 10.0.0.0 default-cost 20
[P18435|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P18436|Normal] None
[P18437|Heading 3] auto-cost
[P18438|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P18439|Normal] To control how Open Shortest Path First Version3 (OSPFv3) calculates default metrics for the interface; use the auto-cost command in router configuration mode.
[P18440|Body Text] To assign cost based only on the interface type, use the no form of this command.
[P18441|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P18442|Normal] auto-cost reference-bandwidth RATE
[P18443|Body Text] no auto-cost reference-bandwidth

[TABLE 667] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	RATE	Rate in Mbps (bandwidth). The default is 100	1 - 4294967 Mbps

[P18444|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P18445|Normal] Router Configuration
[P18446|Heading 4] Default
[P18447|Normal] 100 Mbps
[P18448|Heading 4] Usage
[P18449|Normal] The value set by the ipv6 ospf cost command overrides the cost resulting from the auto-cost command.
[P18450|Heading 4] Examples
[P18451|Normal] The following example changes the cost of the cost link to 1GBps:
[P18452|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router ipv6 ospf 1
Switch(config-router)#auto-cost reference-bandwidth 1000
[P18453|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P18454|Normal] ipv6 ospf cost
[P18455|Heading 3] clear ipv6 ospf
[P18456|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P18457|Normal] To clear routing information based on the Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) routing process ID, use the clear ipv6 ospf command in privileged EXEC mode.
[P18458|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P18459|Normal] clear ipv6 ospf ( PID | ) process

[TABLE 668] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	PID	(Optional) Process ID	0-65535

[P18460|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P18461|Normal] Privileged EXEC
[P18462|Heading 4] Default
[P18463|Normal] None
[P18464|Heading 4] Usage
[P18465|Normal] Use the PID argument to clear only one OSPFv3 process. If the PID argument is not specified, all OSPFv3 processes are cleared.
[P18466|Heading 4] Examples
[P18467|Normal] The following example clears all OSPFv3 processes:
[P18468|Terminal Display] Switch# clear ipv6 ospf process
[P18469|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P18470|Normal] None
[P18471|Heading 3] default-information originate (OSPFv3)
[P18472|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P18473|Normal] To generate a default external route into an Open Shortest Path First Version3 (OSPFv3) routing domain, use the default-information originate command in router configuration mode.
[P18474|Body Text] To disable this feature, use the no form of this command.
[P18475|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P18476|Normal] default-information originate
[P18477|Body Text] default-information originate { metric METRIC | metric-type TYPE ) | route-map ROUTE_MAP | always }
[P18478|Body Text] no default-information originate
[P18479|Body Text] no default-information originate { metric | metric-type | route-map | always }

[TABLE 669] rows=5 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	always	(Optional) Always advertises the default route regardless of whether the system has a default route	Up to 20 characters
R3	METRIC	metric-value (Optional) Metric used for generating the default route. If you omit a value and do not specify a value using the default-metric router configuration command, the default metric value is 10. The value used is specific to the protocol	0-16777214
R4	TYPE	(Optional) External link type associated with the default route advertised into the OSPF routing domain. It can be one of the following values	1,2
R5	ROUTE_MAP	Route map reference	-

[P18480|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P18481|Normal] Router Configuration
[P18482|Heading 4] Default
[P18483|Normal] This command is disabled by default.
[P18484|Heading 4] Usage
[P18485|Normal] Whenever you use the redistribute or the default-information router configuration command to redistribute routes into an OSPFv3 routing domain, the switch automatically becomes an autonomous System Boundary Router (ASBR). However, an ASBR does not, by default, generate a default route into the OSPFv3 routing domain. The system still must have a default route for itself before it generates one, except when you have specified the always keyword.
[P18486|Heading 4] Examples
[P18487|Normal] The following example specifies a metric of 100 for the default route redistributed into the OSPFv3 routing domain and an external metric type of Type 1:
[P18488|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router ipv6 ospf 109
Switch(config-router)# redistribute rip metric 100
Switch(config-router)#default-information originate metric 100 metric-type 1
[P18489|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P18490|Normal] redistribute (OSPFv3)
[P18491|Heading 3] default-metric (OSPFv3)
[P18492|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P18493|Normal] To set default metric values for the Open Shortest Path First Version3 (OSPFv3) routing protocol, use the default-metric command in router configuration mode.
[P18494|Body Text] To return to the default state, use the no form of this command.
[P18495|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P18496|Normal] default-metric METRIC-VALUE
[P18497|Body Text] no default-metric ( METRIC-VALUE )

[TABLE 670] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	METRIC-VALUE	Default metric value appropriate for the specified routing protocol. Default metric value appropriate for the specified routing protocol. Built-in, automatic metric translations, as appropriate for each routing protocol. The metric of redistributed connected and static routes is set to 0	0-16777214

[P18498|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P18499|Normal] Router Configuration
[P18500|Heading 4] Default
[P18501|Normal] 1 for BGP routes
[P18502|Body Text] 20 for others
[P18503|Heading 4] Usage
[P18504|Normal] The default-metric command is used in conjunction with the redistribute router configuration command to cause the current routing protocol to use the same metric value for all redistributed routes. A default metric helps solve the problem of redistributing routes with incompatible metrics. Whenever metrics do not convert, using a default metric provides a reasonable substitute and enables the redistribution to proceed.
[P18505|Heading 4] Examples
[P18506|Normal] The following example shows a router in autonomous system using both the Routing Information Protocol (RIPng) and the OSPFv3 routing protocols. The example advertises OSPFv3-derived routes using RIPng and assigns the Internal Gateway Protocol (IGP)-derived routes a RIPng metric of 10:
[P18507|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router ipv6 ospf
Switch(config-router)#default-metric 10
Switch(config-router)# redistribute ripng
[P18508|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P18509|Normal] redistribute (OSPFv3)
[P18510|Heading 3] distance (OSPFv3)
[P18511|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P18512|Normal] To define Open Shortest Path First Version3 (OSPFv3) route administrative distances based on route type, use the distance command in router configuration mode.
[P18513|Body Text] To restore the default value, use the no form of this command.
[P18514|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P18515|Normal] distance { DISTANCE | ospfv3 [ external DIST1 ] [ inter-area DIST2 ] | [ intra-area DIST3 ] }
[P18516|Body Text] no distance { DISTANCE | ospfv3 }

[TABLE 671] rows=5 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	DISTANCE	Administrative distance.	1-254.(routes with a distance value of 255 are not installed in the routing table)
R3	external DIST1	(Optional) Sets the distance for routes from other routing domains, learned by redistribution. Range is 1 to 255. The default value is 110	1-254
R4	inter-area DIST2	(Optional) Sets the distance for all routes from one area to another area. Range is 1 to 255. The default value is 110	1-254
R5	intra-area DIST3	(Optional) Sets the distance for all routes within an area. Range is 1 to 255. The default value is 110	1-254

[P18517|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P18518|Normal] Router Configuration
[P18519|Heading 4] Default
[P18520|Normal] DIST1: 110
[P18521|Body Text] DIST2: 110
[P18522|Body Text] DIST3: 110
[P18523|Heading 4] Usage
[P18524|Normal] You may specify one of the keywords or use distance only to apply to all types of routes.
[P18525|Body Text] The distance command allows you to set a distance for an entire group of routes, rather than a specific route that passes an access list.
[P18526|Body Text] A common reason to use the distance command is when you have multiple OSPFv3 processes with mutual redistribution, and you want to prefer internal routes from one over external routes from the other.
[P18527|Heading 4] Examples
[P18528|Normal] The following example shows a router in autonomous system using both the Routing Information Protocol (RIPng) and the OSPFv3 routing protocols. The example advertises OSPFv3-derived routes using RIPng and assigns the Internal Gateway Protocol (IGP)-derived routes a RIPng distance of 90:
[P18529|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router ipv6 ospf
Switch(config-router)#distance 90
Switch(config-router)# redistribute ripng
[P18530|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P18531|Normal] None
[P18532|Heading 3] distribute-list (OSPFv3)
[P18533|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P18534|Normal] To filter networks received in updates or suppress networks from being advertised in updates, use the distribute-list command in router configuration mode.
[P18535|Body Text] To cancel this function, use the no form of this command.
[P18536|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P18537|Normal] distribute-list ACCESSS-LIST-NAME ( in | out ( bgp | connected | ospfv3 | ripng | static ) )
[P18538|Body Text] no distribute-list ACCESSS-LIST-NAME ( in | out ( bgp | connected | ospfv3 | ripng | static ) )

[TABLE 672] rows=4 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	ACCESSS-LIST-NAME	Name of an access list to be applied	Up to 20 characters
R3	in	Filter networks received in updates	-
R4	out	Suppress networks from being advertised in updates	-

[P18539|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P18540|Normal] Router Configuration
[P18541|Heading 4] Default
[P18542|Normal] This command is disabled by default.
[P18543|Heading 4] Usage
[P18544|Normal] This command must specify an access list.
[P18545|Heading 4] Examples
[P18546|Normal] In the following example, OSPFv3 process 1 is configured to accept two prefixes, prefix 2001:1:1::1/32 and prefix 3001:1:1::1/32:
[P18547|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ipv6 access-list fiter-as-router
Switch(config-ip-acl)# permit any 2001:1:1::1/32 any
Switch(config-ip-acl)# permit any 3001:1:1::1/32 any
Switch(config-ip-acl)#deny any any any
Switch(config)# router ipv6 ospf 1
Switch(config-router)#distribute-list acl1 in
[P18548|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P18549|Normal] ipv6 access-list
[P18550|Heading 3] enable db-summary-opt
[P18551|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P18552|Normal] Use this command to enable optimize the process when building ospfv3 neighbor ship.
[P18553|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P18554|Normal] enable db-summary-opt
[P18555|Body Text] no enable db-summary-opt
[P18556|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P18557|Normal] Router Configuration
[P18558|Heading 4] Default
[P18559|Normal] Disable
[P18560|Heading 4] Usage
[P18561|Normal] After this function enabled, if the router receives a DD packet which has newer LSA, the router should delete the LSA in the database summary list, and should not send this LSA to its neighbor.
[P18562|Heading 4] Examples
[P18563|Normal] The following example enables this optimization:
[P18564|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router ipv6 ospf 1
Switch(config-if)# enable db-summary-opt

Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router ipv6 ospf 1
Switch(config-router)# enable db-summary-opt
[P18565|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P18566|Normal] None
[P18567|Heading 3] ipv6 ospf cost
[P18568|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P18569|Normal] To explicitly specify the cost of sending a packet on an interface, use the ipv6 ospf cost command in interface configuration mode. To reset the path cost to the default value, use the no form of this command.
[P18570|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P18571|Normal] ipv6 ospf cost INTERFACE-COST ( instance ID | )
[P18572|Body Text] no ipv6 ospf cost ( instance ID | )

[TABLE 673] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	INTERFACE-COST	Unsigned integer value expressed as the link-state metric.	1-65535

[P18573|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P18574|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P18575|Heading 4] Default
[P18576|Normal] No default cost is predefined.
[P18577|Heading 4] Usage
[P18578|Normal] You can set the metric manually using this command, if you need to change the default. Using the bandwidth command changes the link cost as long as this command is not used.
[P18579|Body Text] The link-state metric is advertised as the link cost in the router link advertisement.
[P18580|Body Text] In general, the path cost is calculated using the following formula:
[P18581|Body Text] Reference Bandwidth / bandwidth
[P18582|Heading 4] Examples
[P18583|Normal] The following example sets the interface cost value to 65:
[P18584|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# no switchport
Switch(config-if)# ipv6 ospf cost 65
[P18585|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P18586|Normal] auto-cost reference bandwidth
[P18587|Heading 3] ipv6 ospf dead-interval
[P18588|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P18589|Normal] To set the interval during which at least one hello packet must be received from a neighbor before the router declares that neighbor down, use the ipv6 ospf dead-interval command in interface configuration mode. To restore the default value, use the no form of this command.
[P18590|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P18591|Normal] ipv6 ospf dead-interval SECONDS ( instance ID | )
[P18592|Body Text] no ipv6 ospf dead-interval ( instance ID | )

[TABLE 674] rows=3 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	SECONDS	Interval (in seconds) during which the router must receive at least one hello packet from a neighbor or else that neighbor is removed from the peer list and does not participate in routing. The value must be the same for all nodes on the network	1-65535
R3	ID	Instance ID, the default value is 0.	0-255

[P18593|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P18594|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P18595|Heading 4] Default
[P18596|Normal] The neighbor is considered as dead in 40s by default.
[P18597|Heading 4] Usage
[P18598|Normal] The dead interval is advertised in OSPFv3 hello packets. This value must be the same for all networking devices on a specific network.
[P18599|Body Text] Specifying a smaller dead interval (seconds) will give faster detection of a neighbor being down and improve convergence, but might cause more routing instability.
[P18600|Heading 4] Examples
[P18601|Normal] The following example sets the OSPFv3 dead interval to 20 seconds:
[P18602|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# no switchport
Switch(config-if)# ipv6 ospf dead-interval 20
[P18603|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P18604|Normal] ipv6 ospf hello-interval
[P18605|Body Text] show ipv6s ospf interface
[P18606|Heading 3] ipv6 ospf hello-interval
[P18607|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P18608|Normal] To specify the interval between hello packets that the switch sends on the interface, use the ip ospf hello-interval command in interface configuration mode.
[P18609|Body Text] To return to the default time, use the no form of this command.
[P18610|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P18611|Normal] ip ospf hello-interval SECONDS ( instance ID | )
[P18612|Body Text] no ip ospf hello-interval ( instance ID | )

[TABLE 675] rows=3 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	SECONDS	Interval (in seconds) during which the router must receive at least one hello packet from a neighbor or else that neighbor is removed from the peer list and does not participate in routing. The value must be the same for all nodes on the network	1-65535
R3	ID	Instance ID, the default value is 0.	0-255

[P18613|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P18614|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P18615|Heading 4] Default
[P18616|Normal] 10 seconds (Ethernet)
[P18617|Body Text] 30 seconds (non-broadcast)
[P18618|Heading 4] Usage
[P18619|Normal] This value is advertised in the hello packets. The smaller the hello interval, the faster topological changes will be detected, but more routing traffic will ensue. This value must be the same for all routers and access servers on a specific network.
[P18620|Heading 4] Examples
[P18621|Normal] The following example sets the interval between hello packets to 15 seconds:
[P18622|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# no switchport
Switch(config-if)# ipv6 ospf hello-interval 15
[P18623|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P18624|Normal] ipv6 ospf dead-interval
[P18625|Heading 3] ipv6 ospf mtu-ignore
[P18626|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P18627|Normal] To disable Open Shortest Path First Version3 (OSPFv3) maximum transmission unit (MTU) mismatch detection on receiving Database Descriptor (DBD) packets, use the ipv6 ospf mtu-ignore command in interface configuration mode.
[P18628|Body Text] To reset to default, use the no form of this command.
[P18629|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P18630|Normal] ipv6 ospf mtu-ignore ( instance ID | )
[P18631|Body Text] no ipv6 ospf mtu-ignore ( instance ID | )

[TABLE 676] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	ID	Instance ID, the default value is 0.	0-255

[P18632|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P18633|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P18634|Heading 4] Default
[P18635|Normal] OSPFv3 MTU mismatch detection is enabled.
[P18636|Heading 4] Usage
[P18637|Normal] OSPFv3 checks whether neighbors are using the same MTU on a common interface. This check is performed when neighbors exchange DBD packets. If the receiving MTU in the DBD packet is higher than the IP MTU configured on the incoming interface, OSPFv3 adjacency will not be established.
[P18638|Heading 4] Examples
[P18639|Normal] The following example disables MTU mismatch detection on receiving DBD packets:
[P18640|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# no switchport
Switch(config-if)# ipv6 ospf mtu-ignore
[P18641|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P18642|Normal] None
[P18643|Heading 3] ipv6 ospf priority
[P18644|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P18645|Normal] To set the router priority, which helps determine the designated router for this network, use the ip ospf priority command in interface configuration mode.
[P18646|Body Text] To return to the default value, use the no form of this command.
[P18647|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P18648|Normal] ipv6 ospf priority NUMBER-VALUE ( instance ID | )
[P18649|Body Text] no ipv6 ospf priority ( instance ID | )

[TABLE 677] rows=3 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	NUMBER-VALUE	A number value that specifies the priority of the router.	0-255
R3	ID	Instance ID, the default value is 0.	0-255

[P18650|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P18651|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P18652|Heading 4] Default
[P18653|Normal] Priority of 1
[P18654|Heading 4] Usage
[P18655|Normal] When two routers attached to a network both attempt to become the designated router, the one with the higher router priority takes precedence. If there is a tie, the router with the higher router ID takes precedence. A router with a router priority set to zero is ineligible to become the designated router or backup designated router. Router priority is configured only for interfaces to multi-access networks (in other words, not to point-to-point networks).
[P18656|Body Text] This priority value is used when you configure Open Shortest Path First Version3 (OSPFv3) for non-broadcast networks using the neighbor router configuration command for OSPFv3.
[P18657|Heading 4] Examples
[P18658|Normal] The following example sets the router priority value to 4:
[P18659|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# no switchport
Switch(config-if)# ipv6 ospf priority 4
[P18660|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P18661|Normal] None
[P18662|Heading 3] ipv6 ospf retransmit-interval
[P18663|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P18664|Normal] To specify the time between link-state advertisement (LSA) retransmissions for adjacencies belonging to the interface, use the ipv6 ospf retransmit-interval command in interface configuration mode.
[P18665|Body Text] To return to the default value, use the no form of this command.
[P18666|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P18667|Normal] ipv6 ospf retransmit-interval SECONDS ( instance ID | )
[P18668|Body Text] no ipv6 ospf retransmit-interval ( instance ID | )

[TABLE 678] rows=3 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	SECONDS	Time (in seconds) between retransmissions. It must be greater than the expected round-trip delay between any two routers on the attached network.	1-65535 seconds
R3	ID	Instance ID, the default value is 0.	0-255

[P18669|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P18670|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P18671|Heading 4] Default
[P18672|Normal] 5 seconds
[P18673|Heading 4] Usage
[P18674|Normal] When a router sends an LSA to its neighbor, it keeps the LSA until it receives back the acknowledgment message. If the router receives no acknowledgment, it will resend the LSA. The setting of this parameter should be conservative, or needless retransmission will result. The value should be larger for serial lines and virtual links.
[P18675|Heading 4] Examples
[P18676|Normal] The following example sets the retransmit interval value to 8 seconds:
[P18677|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# no switchport
Switch(config-if)# ipv6 ospf retransmit-interval 8
[P18678|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P18679|Normal] None
[P18680|Heading 3] ipv6 ospf transmit-delay
[P18681|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P18682|Normal] To set the estimated time required to send a link-state update packet on the interface, use the ipv6 ospf transmit-delay command in interface configuration mode. To return to the default value, use the no form of this command.
[P18683|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P18684|Normal] ipv6 ospf transmit-delay SECONDS ( instance ID | )
[P18685|Body Text] no ipv6 ospf transmit-delay ( instance ID | )

[TABLE 679] rows=3 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	SECONDS	Time (in seconds) between retransmissions. It must be greater than the expected round-trip delay between any two routers on the attached network.	1-65535 seconds
R3	ID	Instance ID, the default value is 0.	0-255

[P18686|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P18687|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P18688|Heading 4] Default
[P18689|Normal] 1 second
[P18690|Heading 4] Usage
[P18691|Normal] Link-state advertisements (LSAs) in the update packet must have their ages incremented by the amount specified in the seconds argument before transmission. The value assigned should take into account the transmission and propagation delays for the interface.
[P18692|Body Text] If the delay is not added before transmission over a link, the time in which the LSA propagates over the link is not considered. This setting has more significance on very low-speed links.
[P18693|Heading 4] Examples
[P18694|Normal] The following example sets the retransmit delay value to 3 seconds:
[P18695|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# no switchport
Switch(config-if)# ipv6 ospf transmit-delay 3
[P18696|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P18697|Normal] None
[P18698|Heading 3] ipv6 ospf network
[P18699|Heading 4] Command Purpose

[P18701|Heading 4] Command Syntax

[P18703|Body Text] no ipv6 ospf network ( instance <0-255> | )

R3	non-broadcast	Specify NBMA network	-
R4	point-to-multipoint	Specify point-to-multipoint network	non-broadcast
R5	point-to-point	Specify point-to-point network	-
R6	instance	Instance ID, the default value is 0.	0-255

[P18704|Heading 4] Command Mode

[P18707|Normal] broadcast
[P18708|Heading 4] Usage
[P18709|Normal] None

Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# no switchport
Switch(config-if)# ipv6 ospf network point-to-point

R4	priority	Priority of non-broadcast neighbor	0-255
R5	cost	Cost for point-to-multipoint neighbor	1-65535
R6	instance	Instance ID, the default value is 0.	0-255

[P18721|Heading 4] Command Mode

[P18725|Heading 4] Usage

[P18732|Heading 3] passive-interface (OSPF)
[P18733|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P18734|Normal] To disable sending routing updates for the Open Shortest Path First Version3 (OSPFv3) on an interface, use the passive-interface command in router configuration mode. To re-enable the sending of routing updates, use the no form of this command.
[P18735|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P18736|Normal] passive-interface IFNAME
[P18737|Body Text] no passive-interface IFNAME

[TABLE 682] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	IFNAME	The interface name	Support physical/aggregation/loopback/vlan/tunnel ports

[P18738|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P18739|Normal] Router Configuration
[P18740|Heading 4] Default
[P18741|Normal] Routing updates are sent on the interface.
[P18742|Heading 4] Usage
[P18743|Normal] If you disable the sending of routing updates on an interface, the particular subnet will continue to be advertised to other interfaces, and updates from other switches on that interface continue to be received and processed.
[P18744|Heading 4] Examples
[P18745|Normal] The following example sets the interface eth-0-1 as passive:
[P18746|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router ipv6 ospf 200
Switch(config-router)# passive-interface eth-0-1
[P18747|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P18748|Normal] router ipv6 ospf
[P18749|Heading 3] redistribute (OSPFv3)
[P18750|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P18751|Normal] To redistribute routes from one routing domain into Open Shortest Path First Version3 (OSPFv3) routing domain, use the redistribute command in router configuration mode. To disable redistribution, use the no form of this command.
[P18752|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P18753|Normal] redistribute PROTOCOL [ route-map WORD ] [ tag TAG-VALUE ] [ metric METRIC-VALUE ] [ metric-type TYPE-VALUE ]
[P18754|Body Text] no redistribute PROTOCOL [ metric METRIC-VALUE ] [ metric-type TYPE-VALUE ]

[TABLE 683] rows=6 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	route-map WORD	Route map name	Up to 20 characters
R3	PROTOCOL	(Optional) The name of a routing protocol, or the keyword connected, or static. If you specify a routing protocol, use one of the following keywords: bgp, and ripng	connected/static/bgp/ripng
R4	tag TAG-VALUE	Set tag for routes redistributed into OSPF	0-4294967295
R5	metric METRIC-VALUE	(Optional) When redistributing other processes to an OSPF process, the default metric is 20 when no metric value is specified	0-16777214
R6	metric-type TYPE-VALUE	For OSPF, the external link type associated with the default route advertised into the OSPF routing domain. It can be one of two values	1-2

[P18755|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P18756|Normal] Router Configuration
[P18757|Heading 4] Default
[P18758|Normal] Route redistribution is disabled.
[P18759|Body Text] metric metric-value: 20
[P18760|Body Text] metric-type TYPE-VALUE: Type 2 external route
[P18761|Heading 4] Usage
[P18762|Normal] The metric value specified in the redistribute command supersedes the metric value specified using the default-metric command.
[P18763|Heading 4] Examples
[P18764|Normal] The following example redistribute the static routes into OSPFv3 with metric 10:
[P18765|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router ospf 119
Switch(config-router)# redistribute static metric 10
[P18766|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P18767|Normal] default-metric
[P18768|Heading 3] router-id (OSPF)
[P18769|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P18770|Normal] To use a fixed router ID, use the router-id command in router configuration mode.
[P18771|Body Text] To force Open Shortest Path First Version3 (OSPFv3) use the previous OSPF router ID behavior, use the no form of this command.
[P18772|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P18773|Normal] router-id IP-ADDRESS
[P18774|Body Text] no router-id

[TABLE 684] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	IP-ADDRESS	Router ID in IP address format	IPv6 Address

[P18775|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P18776|Normal] Router Configuration
[P18777|Heading 4] Default
[P18778|Normal] No OSPF routing process is defined.
[P18779|Heading 4] Usage
[P18780|Normal] You can configure an arbitrary value in the IP address format for each router. However, each router ID must be unique.
[P18781|Body Text] If this command is used on an OSPFv3 router process which is already active (has neighbors), the new router-ID is used at the next reload or at a manual OSPFv3 process restart. To manually restart the OSPFv3 process, use the clear ip ospf command.
[P18782|Heading 4] Examples
[P18783|Normal] The following example specifies a fixed router-id:
[P18784|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router ipv6 ospf 119
Switch(config-router)# router-id 10.1.1.1
[P18785|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P18786|Normal] clear ipv6 ospf
[P18787|Body Text] router ipv6 ospf
[P18788|Heading 3] router ipv6 ospf
[P18789|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P18790|Normal] To configure an Open Shortest Path First Version3 (OSPFv3) routing process, use the router ipv6 ospf command in global configuration mode. To terminate an OSPFv3s routing process, use the no form of this command.
[P18791|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P18792|Normal] router ipv6 ospf [ PROCESS-ID [ vrf VPN-NAME ] ]
[P18793|Body Text] no router ipv6 ospf [ PROCESS-ID ]

[TABLE 685] rows=3 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	PROCESS-ID	Internally used identification parameter for an OSPF routing process. It is locally assigned and can be any positive integer. A unique value is assigned for each OSPF routing process	1-65535
R3	vrf VPN-NAME	(Optional) Specifies the name of the VPN routing and forwarding (VRF) instance to associate with OSPFv3 VRF processes	A string with 1-31 characters

[P18794|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P18795|Normal] Global Configuration
[P18796|Heading 4] Default
[P18797|Normal] No OSPF routing process is defined.
[P18798|Heading 4] Usage
[P18799|Normal] You can specify multiple OSPFv3 routing processes in each router. If you do not specify the process-id, the process-id will be the default 0.
[P18800|Heading 4] Examples
[P18801|Normal] The following example configures an OSPFv3 routing process and assigns a process number of 109:
[P18802|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router ipv6 ospf 109
[P18803|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P18804|Normal] None
[P18805|Heading 3] capability vrf-lite
[P18806|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P18807|Normal] To disable ospf dn-bit check,calculate all ospf route.
[P18808|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P18809|Normal] capability vrf-lite
[P18810|Body Text] no capability vrf-lite
[P18811|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P18812|Normal] Router Configuration
[P18813|Heading 4] Default
[P18814|Normal] Disable capability vrf-lite
[P18815|Heading 4] Usage
[P18816|Normal] It only supports configure under ospfv3 vrf view.
[P18817|Heading 4] Examples
[P18818|Normal] The following example enables ospfv3 capability vrf-lite.:
[P18819|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ip vrf a
Switch(config-vrf)# exit
Switch(config)# router ipv6 ospf 1 vrf a
Switch(config-router)# capability vrf-lite
[P18820|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P18821|Normal] None
[P18822|Heading 3] dn-bit-check disable
[P18823|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P18824|Normal] To disable ospfv3 dn-bit-check for special type LSA,and calculate it’s route.
[P18825|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P18826|Normal] dn-bit-check LSA-Type
[P18827|Body Text] no dn-bit-check disable

[TABLE 686] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	LSA-type	Specail type of ospfv3 LSA	(summary\|ase\|nssa)

[P18828|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P18829|Normal] Router Configuration
[P18830|Heading 4] Default
[P18831|Normal] Default enable LSA DN-bit check.
[P18832|Heading 4] Usage
[P18833|Normal] It only supports configure under ospfv3 vrf view.
[P18834|Heading 4] Examples
[P18835|Normal] The following example configures don’t check DN-bit of ospfv3 summary LSA.:
[P18836|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ip vrf a
Switch(config-vrf)# exit
Switch(config)# router ipv6 ospf 1 vrf a
Switch(config-router)# dn-bit-check disable summary
[P18837|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P18838|Normal] None
[P18839|Heading 3] summary-address (OSPFv3)
[P18840|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P18841|Normal] To create aggregate addresses for Open Shortest Path First Version3 (OSPFv3), use the summary-address command in router configuration mode. To restore the default, use the no form of this command.
[P18842|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P18843|Normal] summary-address PREFIX / PREFIX-LENGTH [ not-advertise ] [ tag TAG-VALUE ]
[P18844|Body Text] no summary-address PREFIX / PREFIX-LENGTH [ not-advertise ] [ tag TAG-VALUE ]

[TABLE 687] rows=5 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	PREFIX	IP route prefix for the destination	IPv6 Address
R3	PREFIX-LENGTH	Prefix length for the network	1-128
R4	not-advertise	(Optional) Suppress routes that match the specified prefix/mask pair. This keyword applies to OSPFv3 only	-
R5	tag TAG-VALUE	Route tag value	0-4294967295

[P18845|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P18846|Normal] Router Configuration
[P18847|Heading 4] Default
[P18848|Normal] This command is disabled by default.
[P18849|Heading 4] Usage
[P18850|Normal] Routes learned from other routing protocols can be summarized. The metric used to advertise the summary is the largest metric of all the more specific routes. This command helps reduce the size of the routing table.
[P18851|Body Text] Using this command for OSPFv3 causes an OSPFv3 Autonomous System Boundary Router (ASBR) to advertise one external route as an aggregate for all redistributed routes that are covered by the address. For OSPFv3, this command summarizes only routes from other routing protocols that are being redistributed into OSPFv3. Use the area range command for route summarization between OSPF areas.
[P18852|Body Text] OSPFv3 does not support the summary-address 0.0.0.0/0 command.
[P18853|Heading 4] Examples
[P18854|Normal] In the following example, the summary address 2001:1:1::/48 includes address 2001:1:1:1::/64, 2001:1:1:2::/64, and so on. Only the address 2001:1:1::/48 is advertised in an external link-state advertisement:
[P18855|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router ipv6 ospf 
Switch(config-router)# summary-address 2001:1:1::/48
[P18856|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P18857|Normal] area range

[P19190|Heading 3] area nssa
[P19191|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P19192|Normal] Use this command to set the specified area as NSSA area, and use the keyword 'no' to cancel the setting of this area as stub area.
[P19193|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P19194|Normal] area AREA-ID nssa ( translator-role ( candidate | never | always ) | ) ( no-summary | ) ( no-redistribution | ) ( default-information-originate { metric METRIC_VALUE | metric-type TYPE-VALUE | } | )
[P19195|Body Text] no area AREA-ID nssa ( translator-role | ) ( no-summary | ) ( no-redistribution | ) ( stability-interval | ) ( default-information-originate | )

[TABLE 704] rows=10 cols=3
R1	参数	参数说明	参数取值
R2	AREA-ID	区域标识符，标识符可以是十进制的或者是IP地址	IP地址或0-4294967295的整数
R3	candidate	(可选)配置ABR在NSSA区域中的角色为候选转换路由器	-
R4	always	(可选)配置ABR在NSSA区域中的角色为指定转换路由器	-
R5	no-summary	(可选)如果指定了此项，则禁止ABR向此区域发送Summary LSAs	-
R6	no-redistribution	(可选)如果指定了此项，则禁止向此区域引入外部路由	-
R7	default-information-originate	(可选)如果指定了此项，则ASBR将产生默认的type 7 LSA到NSSA区域	-
R8	metric METRIC_VALUE	(可选)配置生成的默认路由的metric值	0-16777214
R9	metric-type TYPE-VALUE	(可选)配置生成的默认路由的metric类型	1-2
R10	stability-interval INTERVAL-VALUE	(可选)配置失效时间	0-2147483647 seconds

[P19196|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P19197|Normal] 路由模式
[P19198|Heading 4] Default
[P19199|Normal] 默认无NSSA区域
[P19200|Heading 4] Usage
[P19201|Normal] 缺省情况下，没有区域被设置为NSSA区域。NSSA区域的所有路由器都必须用area nssa进行设置。 NSSA区域与STUB区域有许多相似的地方，两者都不传播来自其它OSPF区域的外部路由。差别在于NSSA区域能够将外部路由引入并传播到整个OSPF自治域中，而STUB区域不能引入外部路由。
[P19202|Heading 4] Examples
[P19203|Normal] 下面例子讲述了如何配置NSSA区域
[P19204|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router ipv6 ospf 201
Switch(config-router)# area 10.0.0.0 nssa
[P19205|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P19206|Normal] none
[P19207|Normal]

[P19209|Heading 3] router ipv6 rip
[P19210|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P19211|Normal] To enable or configure the Routing Information Protocol next generation (RIPng) routing process, use the router ipv6 rip command in global configuration mode.
[P19212|Body Text] To disable the RIPng routing process, use the no form of this command.
[P19213|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P19214|Normal] router ipv6 rip
[P19215|Body Text] no router ipv6 rip
[P19216|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P19217|Normal] Global Configuration
[P19218|Heading 4] Default
[P19219|Normal] No RIPng routing process is defined.
[P19220|Heading 4] Usage
[P19221|Normal] None
[P19222|Heading 4] Examples
[P19223|Normal] The following example shows how to enable RIPng routing process:
[P19224|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router ipv6 rip
[P19225|Heading 4] Related Commands

[P19227|Heading 3] ipv6 router rip
[P19228|Heading 4] Command Purpose

[P19230|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to disable RIPng routing process on interface.
[P19231|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P19232|Normal] ipv6 router rip
[P19233|Body Text] no ipv6 router rip
[P19234|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P19235|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P19236|Heading 4] Default
[P19237|Normal] None.
[P19238|Heading 4] Usage
[P19239|Normal] None
[P19240|Heading 4] Examples
[P19241|Normal] The following example shows how to enable RIPng on the interface eth-0-1:
[P19242|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# no switchport
Switch(config-if)# ipv6 router rip
[P19243|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P19244|Normal] None
[P19245|Heading 3] ipv6 rip metric-offset
[P19246|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P19247|Normal] Use this command to set RIP metric offset in interface mode.
[P19248|Body Text] To restore the default metric, use the no form of this command.
[P19249|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P19250|Normal] ipv6 rip metric-offset NUMBER-VALUE
[P19251|Body Text] no ipv6 rip metric-offset NUMBER-VALUE

[P19252|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P19253|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P19254|Heading 4] Default
[P19255|Normal] Metric offset value is 1.
[P19256|Heading 4] Usage
[P19257|Normal] Metric offset value is used to add the metric of the network on which the message arrived (as the RFC describes).
[P19258|Heading 4] Examples
[P19259|Normal] The following example shows how to set metric offset as 2:
[P19260|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal

[P19263|Heading 3] ipv6 rip split-horizon
[P19264|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P19265|Normal] To enable the split horizon mechanism for Routing Information Protocol next generation (RIPng), use the ipv6 rip split-horizon command in interface configuration mode.
[P19266|Body Text] To disable the split horizon mechanism, use the no form of this command.
[P19267|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P19268|Normal] ipv6 rip split-horizon ( poisoned | )
[P19269|Body Text] no ipv6 rip split-horizon

[TABLE 706] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	poisoned	Split horizon with poisoned reverse	-

[P19270|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P19271|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P19272|Heading 4] Default
[P19273|Normal] This command is enabled with poisoned reverse by default.
[P19274|Heading 4] Usage
[P19275|Normal] In general, changing the default state for the ipv6 rip split-horizon command is not recommended, unless you are certain that your application requires a change in order to properly advertise routes.
[P19276|Heading 4] Examples
[P19277|Normal] The following example enables split horizon without poisoned reverse:
[P19278|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# ipv6 rip split- horizon

[P19294|Heading 4] Examples
[P19295|Normal] The following example originates a default route (0::0/0) into RIPng:

[P19297|Heading 4] Related Commands

[P19299|Heading 3] default-metric (RIPng)
[P19300|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P19301|Normal] To specify the metrics to be assigned to redistributed routers for Routing Information Protocol next generation (RIPng), use the default-metric command in router configuration mode.
[P19302|Body Text] To return to the default state, use the no form of this command.
[P19303|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P19304|Normal] default-metric NUMBER-VALUE
[P19305|Body Text] no default-metric

[TABLE 708] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	NUMBER-VALUE	Metric value	1-16

[P19306|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P19307|Normal] Router Configuration
[P19308|Heading 4] Default
[P19309|Normal] By default, the metric is set to 0.
[P19310|Heading 4] Usage
[P19311|Normal] The default-metric command is used in conjunction with the redistribute router configuration command to cause the current routing protocol to use the same metric value for all redistributed routes. A default metric helps solve the problem of redistributing routes with incompatible metrics. Whenever metrics do not convert, using a default metric provides a reasonable substitute and enables the redistribution to proceed.
[P19312|Heading 4] Examples
[P19313|Normal] The following example shows a switch using both the RIPng and the Open Shortest Path First (OSPFv3) routing protocols. The example advertises OSPFv3-derived routes using RIPng and assigns the OSPFv3-derived routes a RIPng metric of 10:
[P19314|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router ipv6 rip
Switch(config-router)#default-metric 10
Switch(config-router)#redistribute ospfv3
[P19315|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P19316|Normal] redistribute (RIPng)
[P19317|Heading 3] distance (RIPng)
[P19318|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P19319|Normal] To define an administrative distance for routes that are inserted into the routing table, use the distance command in router configuration mode.
[P19320|Body Text] To return the administrative distance to its default distance definition, use the no form of this command.
[P19321|Body Text] An administrative distance is a rating of the trustworthiness of a routing information source, such as an individual switch or a group of switches. Numerically, an administrative distance is an integer from 0 to 255. In general, the higher the value is, the lower the trust rating. An administrative distance of 255 means the routing information source cannot be trusted at all and should be ignored.
[P19322|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P19323|Normal] distance DISTANCE
[P19324|Body Text] no distance

[TABLE 709] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	DISTANCE	Administrative distance	1-255.(routes with a distance value of 255 are not installed in the routing table)

[P19325|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P19326|Normal] Router Configuration
[P19327|Heading 4] Default
[P19328|Normal] By default, the distance is 120.
[P19329|Heading 4] Usage

[TABLE 710] rows=8 cols=2
R1	Route Source	Default Distance
R2	Connected interface	0
R3	Static route	1
R4	External Border Gateway Protocol (eBGP)	20
R5	Open Shortest Path First (OSPF)	110
R6	Routing Information Protocol (RIP)/ Routing Information Protocol next generation (RIPng)	120
R7	Internal BGP	200
R8	Unknown	255

[P19330|Heading 4] Examples
[P19331|Normal] The following example set the distance of RIPng 投200:
[P19332|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)#router ipv6 rip
Switch(config-router)#distance 200
[P19333|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P19334|Normal] None
[P19335|Heading 3] neighbor (RIPng)
[P19336|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P19337|Normal] To specify a neighboring router to which to notify routing updating information, use the neighbor command in router configuration mode.
[P19338|Body Text] To remove the neighbor, use the no form of this command.
[P19339|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P19340|Normal] neighbor IPV6_ADDR IFNAME
[P19341|Body Text] no neighbor IP-ADDRESS IFNAME

[TABLE 711] rows=3 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	IPV6_ADDR	Link-local IP address of a peer switch with which routing information will be notified	IPv6 Address
R3	IFNAME	Interface name to which the neighbor is specified	Support physical/aggregation/loopback/vlan/tunnel ports

[P19342|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P19343|Normal] Router Configuration
[P19344|Heading 4] Default
[P19345|Normal] No neighboring switches are defined.
[P19346|Heading 4] Usage
[P19347|Normal] Especially use the neighbor command in conjunction with the passive-interface command to send routing updates to specific neighbors. This command permits the point-to-point (non-multicast) notification of routing update information. Multiple neighbors can be configured
[P19348|Heading 4] Examples
[P19349|Normal] In the following example, RIPng updates are sent to all interfaces which have been enabled RIPng routing except eth-0-1. However, in this case a neighbor switch configuration command is included. This command permits the sending of routing updates to specific neighbors:
[P19350|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)#router ipv6 rip
Switch(config-router)# passive-interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-router)# neighbor fe80:db8::1 eth-0-1
[P19351|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P19352|Normal] router rip
[P19353|Heading 3] offset-list (RIPng)
[P19354|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P19355|Normal] To add an offset to incoming and outgoing metrics to routes exchanging via Routing Information Protocol next generation (RIPng), use the offset-list command in router configuration mode.
[P19356|Body Text] To remove an offset list, use the no form of this command.
[P19357|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P19358|Normal] offset-list ACCESSS-LIST-NAME ( in | out ) METRIC-OFFSET ( IFNAME | )
[P19359|Body Text] no offset-list ( in | out ) ( IFNAME | )

[TABLE 712] rows=6 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	ACCESSS-LIST-NAME	Named access list to be applied	Up to 40 characters
R3	in	Applies the access list to incoming metrics	-
R4	out	Applies the access list to outgoing metrics	-
R5	METRIC- OFFSET	Positive offset to be applied to metrics for networks matching the access list. The meric-offset range is 0 to 16	0-16
R6	IFNAME	Interface name to which the offset list is applied	Support physical/aggregation/loopback/vlan/tunnel ports

[P19360|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P19361|Normal] Router Configuration
[P19362|Heading 4] Default
[P19363|Normal] This command is configured by default.
[P19364|Heading 4] Usage
[P19365|Normal] Especially if the offset value is added to the routing metric by offset-list, the default action where the metric updates when RIPng message arrives (as RFC defined) is ignored, but outputs will be added.
[P19366|Body Text] The offset value is added to the routing metric. An offset list with an interface is considered extended and takes precedence over an offset list that is not extended. Therefore, if an entry passes the extended offset list and the normal offset list, the offset of the extended offset list is added to the metric.
[P19367|Heading 4] Examples
[P19368|Normal] In the following example, the switch applies an offset of 10 if access list 21 permits:
[P19369|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router ipv6 rip
Switch(config-router)# offset-list 21 out 10
[P19370|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P19371|Normal] None
[P19372|Heading 3] passive-interface (RIPng)
[P19373|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P19374|Normal] To disable sending routing updates for the Routing Information Protocol next generation (RIPng) on an interface, use the passive-interface command in router configuration mode.
[P19375|Body Text] To enable the sending of routing updates, use the no form of this command.
[P19376|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P19377|Normal] passive-interface IFNAME
[P19378|Body Text] no passive-interface IFNAME

[TABLE 713] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	IFNAME	The interface name	Support physical/aggregation/loopback/vlan/tunnel ports

[P19379|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P19380|Normal] Router Configuration
[P19381|Heading 4] Default
[P19382|Normal] Interface is active by default.
[P19383|Heading 4] Usage
[P19384|Normal] The command disable the sending of routing updates and ignore the request message from neighbor on an interface, but updates from other routers on that interface should be received and processed.
[P19385|Heading 4] Examples
[P19386|Normal] The following example sets the interface eth-0-1 as passive:
[P19387|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)#router ipv6 rip
Switch(config-router)# passive-interface eth-0-1

[P19390|Heading 3] redistribute (RIPng)
[P19391|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P19392|Normal] To redistribute routes from one routing domain into RIPng routing domain, use the redistribute command in router configuration mode.
[P19393|Body Text] To disable redistribution, use the no form of this command.
[P19394|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P19395|Normal] redistribute PROTOCOL { [ metric VALUE ] | route-map NAME }
[P19396|Body Text] no redistribute PROTOCOL

[TABLE 714] rows=4 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	PROTOCOL	The name of a routing protocol, or the keyword connected, or static. If you specify a routing protocol, use one of the following keywords: bgp, and ospfv3, static, connected,isis	connected/static/bgp/ospf/isis
R3	metric VALUE	(Optional) When redistributing other routing process to the RIP process, the default metric is 1 if no metric value is specified	1-16
R4	route-map NAME	Route map reference, name of route-map entry	Up to 20 characters

[P19397|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P19398|Normal] Router Configuration
[P19399|Heading 4] Default
[P19400|Normal] Route redistribution is disabled.
[P19401|Body Text] Metric-value: 0
[P19402|Heading 4] Usage
[P19403|Normal] The metric value specified in the redistribute command supersedes the metric value specified using the default-metric command.
[P19404|Heading 4] Examples
[P19405|Normal] The following example redistributes the static routes into RIPng with metric 10:
[P19406|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)#router ipv6 rip
Switch(config-router)#redistribute static metric 10
[P19407|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P19408|Normal] default-metric
[P19409|Heading 3] timers basic (RIPng)
[P19410|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P19411|Normal] To adjust Routing Information Protocol next generation (RIPng) network timers, use the timers basic command in router configuration mode.
[P19412|Body Text] To restore the default timers, use the no form of this command.
[P19413|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P19414|Normal] timers basic UPDATE TIMEOUT INVALID
[P19415|Body Text] no timers basic

[TABLE 715] rows=4 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	UPDATE	Rate (in seconds) at which updates are sent. This is the fundamental timing parameter of the routing protocol	5-2147483647 seconds
R3	TIMEOUT	Time (in seconds) after which a route is declared invalid without updates that refresh the route. The route then enters into an invalid state and is not used for forwarding packets. It is marked inaccessible and advertised as unreachable	5-2147483647 seconds
R4	INVALID	Time after which an invalid route is removed from RIPng routing database	5-2147483647 seconds

[P19416|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P19417|Normal] Router Configuration
[P19418|Heading 4] Default
[P19419|Normal] Update timer: 30 seconds
[P19420|Body Text] Timeout timer: 180 seconds
[P19421|Body Text] Invalid timer: 120 seconds
[P19422|Heading 4] Usage
[P19423|Normal] The basic timing parameters for RIPng are adjustable. Because RIPng is executing a distributed, asynchronous routing algorithm, these timers must be the same for all switches and access servers in the network.
[P19424|Heading 4] Examples
[P19425|Normal] The following example sets updates to every 5 seconds. If a switch is not learned from in 15 seconds, the route is declared unusable. And after 15 seconds the invalid route will be removed from RIPng routing database:
[P19426|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)#router ipv6 rip
Switch(config-router)#timers basic 5 15 15

[P19448|Heading 4] Command Purpose

[P19454|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P19455|Normal] Router Configuration
[P19456|Heading 4] Default

[P19458|Heading 4] Usage
[P19459|Normal] If the routing info is suppressed by aggregate-address, it is still stored in RIPng database, but willn’t be notified to neighbor. On the other hand the aggregate-address will be notified to neighbor.
[P19460|Body Text] The command only be useful when the interface is L3.

[P19462|Normal] In the following example, RIPng specify an aggregate address into RIPng database:
[P19463|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal

Switch(config-router)# aggregate-address 2001:db8::/32

R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	GOLBAL_FREFIX	Global IPv6 address and prefix length. In X:X::X:X/M format	IPv6 Address and mask length in X:X::X:X/M format
R3	LINK-LOCAL	Link-local IPv6 address. In X:X::X:X format	IPv6 Address in X:X::X:X format

[P19696|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P19697|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P19698|Heading 4] Default
[P19699|Normal] There is not any ipv6 address on the interface by default.
[P19700|Heading 4] Usage
[P19701|Normal] Use this command to configure ipv6 address on the interface. Use the no form of this command to remove the ipv6 address. This configuration should not affect the ipv4 functions and other ipv6 configuration on the interface.
[P19702|Body Text] The maximum count of the Link-local address is 1; the maximum count of the global address address is 8.
[P19703|Body Text] Use this command with the keyword “auto link-local” to automatically generate a link-local address, if there is no link-local address on this interface. Use the no form of this command with the keyword “auto link-local” to remove the automatically generated link-local address, if there is only that automatically generated link-local address left on this interface.
[P19704|Body Text] Use this command with a specified ipv6 address (e.g. 3ffe:506::1/48) to configure a global unicast ipv6 address. Use this command with the keyword “eui-64” to generate interface id automatically by the eui-64 algorithm. The global address should not be same. Use the no form of this command the remove the specified ipv6 global unicast address.
[P19705|Body Text] If there is no link-local address on the interface, system should automatically generate one when configure a global unicast ipv6 address.
[P19706|Body Text] Use this command with a specified ipv6 address (e.g. fe80::1) and a keyword “link-local” to configure a link-local address. Use the no form of this command with the specified ipv6 address and the keyword “link-local” to remove the specified ipv6 link-local address. The specified link-local address has a higher priority than the automatically generated the link-local address, that can overwrite the automatically generated one.
[P19707|Body Text] Use the no form of this command without any parameters or keywords to remove all ipv6 addresses on the interface, include ipv6 global addresses and link-local addresses.
[P19708|Heading 4] Examples
[P19709|Normal] The following example shows how to configure link local address and global unicast address:
[P19710|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# ipv6 address fe80::1233 link-local 
Switch(config-if)# ipv6 address 3001:1::1234/64

[P19801|Heading 2] Ipv6 Prefix-list Commands
[P19802|Heading 3] ipv6 prefix-list
[P19803|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P19804|Normal] To create a ipv6 prefix list or add a prefix-list entry, use the ipv6 prefix-list command in global configuration mode.
[P19805|Body Text] To delete a prefix-list or an entry, use the no form of this command.
[P19806|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P19807|Normal] ipv6 prefix-list WORD [ seq SEQUENCE-NUMBER ] ( deny | permit ) ( any | IPv6-ADDRESS/M [ ge GE-LENGTH ] [ le LE-LENGTH ] )
[P19808|Body Text] no ipv6 prefix-list WORD [ seq SEQUENCE-NUMBER ] ( deny | permit ) ( any | IPv6-ADDRESS/M [ ge GE-LENGTH ] [ le LE-LENGTH ] )
[P19809|Body Text] no ipv6 prefix-list WORD [ seq SEQUENCE-NUMBER ]

[TABLE 729] rows=8 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	WORD	Config a name to identify the prefix list	Up to 40 characters
R3	seq SEQUENCE-NUMBER	Applies a sequence number to a prefix-list entry. The range of sequence number that can be entered is from 1 to 65535. If a sequence number is not entered when configuring this command, a default sequence numbering is applied to the prefix list. The number 5 is applied to the first prefix entry, and subsequent unnumbered entries are incremented by 5	1-65535
R4	deny	Denies access for a matching condition	-
R5	permit	Permits access for a matching condition	-
R6	IPv6-ADDRESS /M	Configures the network address, and the length of the network mask in bits. The network number can be any valid IPv6 address or prefix. The bit mask can be a number from 0 to 128	IPv6 address and mask length between 1-128
R7	ge GE-LENGTH	(Optional)Specifies the lesser value of a range (the “from” portion of the range description) by applying the ge-length argument to the range specified. The ge-length argument represents the minimum prefix length to be matched	1-128
R8	le LE-LENGTH	(Optional)Specifies the greater value of a range (the “to” portion of the range description) by applying the le-length argument to the range specified. The le-length argument represents the maximum prefix length to be matched	1-128

[P19810|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P19811|Normal] Global Configuration
[P19812|Heading 4] Default
[P19813|Normal] No prefix lists are created.
[P19814|Heading 4] Usage
[P19815|Normal] The ipv6 prefix-list command is used to configure IPv6 prefix filtering. Prefix lists are configured with permit or deny keywords to either permit or deny the prefix based on the matching condition. A prefix list consists of an IPv6 address and a bit mask. The IPv6 address can be global address, or a link-local address. The bit mask is entered as a number from 1 to 128. An implicit deny is applied to traffic that does not match any prefix-list entry. Prefix lists are configured to match an exact prefix length or a prefix range. The ge and le keywords are used to specify a range of the prefix lengths to match, providing more flexible configuration than can be configured with just the network/length argument. The prefix list is processed using an exact match when neither the ge nor le keyword is entered. If only the ge value is entered, the range is the value entered for the ge ge-length argument to a full 128-bit length. If only the le value is entered, the range is from value entered for the network/length argument to the le le-length argument. If both the ge ge-length and le le-length keywords and arguments are entered, the range falls between the values used for the ge-length and le-length arguments. The following formula shows this behavior:
[P19816|Body Text] network/length < ge ge-length < le le-length <= 128 .
[P19817|Body Text] A prefix list is configured with a name and/or sequence number. One or the other must be entered when configuring this command. If a sequence number is not entered, a default sequence number of 5 is applied to the prefix list. And subsequent prefix list entries will be increment by 5 (for example, 5, 10, 15, and onwards). If a sequence number is entered for the first prefix list entry but not subsequent entries, then the subsequent entries will also be incremented by 5 (For example, if the first configured sequence number is 3, then subsequent entries will be 8, 13, 18, and onwards). Default sequence numbers can be suppressed by entering the no form of this command with the seq keyword. Prefix lists are evaluated starting with the lowest sequence number and continues down the list until a match is made. Once a match is made that covers the network the permit or deny statement is applied to that network and the rest of the list is not evaluated.
[P19818|Heading 4] Examples
[P19819|Normal] The following example shows how to configure ipv6 prefix-list: To deny the default route ::/0:
[P19820|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ipv6 prefix-list abc deny ::/0
[P19821|Normal] To permit the prefix 2001:db8::/64:
[P19822|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ipv6 prefix-list abc permit 2001:db8::/64
[P19823|Normal] To accept a mask length of up to 64 bits in routes with the prefix 2001:db8::/32:
[P19824|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ipv6 prefix-list abc permit 2001:db8::/32 le 64
[P19825|Normal] To deny mask lengths greater than 64 bits in routes with the prefix 2001:db8::/32:
[P19826|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ipv6 prefix-list abc deny 2001:db8::/32 ge 64

[P19906|Heading 2] Route Map Commands
[P19907|Heading 3] route-map
[P19908|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P19909|Normal] To define the conditions for redistributing routes from one routing protocol into another, or to enable policy routing in bgp, use the route-map command in global configuration mode and the match and set command in route-map configuration modes.
[P19910|Body Text] To delete an entry, use the no form of this command.
[P19911|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P19912|Normal] route-map MAP-TAG [ permit | deny ] [ SEQUENCE_NUMBER ]
[P19913|Body Text] no route-map MAP-TAG [ permit | deny ] [ SEQUENCE_NUMBER ]

[TABLE 733] rows=5 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	MAP-TAG	A meaningful name for the route map. The redistribute router configuration command uses this name to reference this route map. Multiple route maps may share the same map tag name.	The length of route-map name should not greater than 20 and the first character should be ‘a’-‘z’, ‘A’-‘Z’ or ‘0’-‘9’.
R3	permit	(Optional) If the match criteria are met for this route map, and the permit keyword is specified, the route is redistributed as controlled by the set actions. If the match criteria are not met, and the permit keyword is specified, the next route map with the same map tag is tested. If a route passes none of the match criteria for the set of route maps sharing the same name, it is not redistributed by that set.	-
R4	deny	(Optional) If the match criteria are met for the route map and the deny keyword is specified, the route is not redistributed	-
R5	SEQUENCE_NUMBER	(Optional) Number that indicates the position a new route map will have in the list of route maps already configured with the same name. If given with the no form of this command, the position of the route map should be deleted	1-65535

[P19914|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P19915|Normal] Global Configuration
[P19916|Heading 4] Default
[P19917|Normal] The permit keyword is the default.
[P19918|Heading 4] Usage
[P19919|Normal] None
[P19920|Heading 4] Examples
[P19921|Normal] The following example shows how to create a route-map and enter route-map configuration mode:
[P19922|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# route-map rip-to-ospf permit
Switch(config-route-map)# match metric 1
Switch(config-route-map)# set metric 2

[P19949|Heading 3] match as-path
[P19950|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P19951|Normal] Use this command to match an autonomous system path access list.
[P19952|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to remove a path list entry.
[P19953|Body Text] The match as-path command specifies the autonomous system path to be matched. If there is a match for the specified AS path, and permit is specified, the route is redistributed or controlled, as specified by the set action. If the match criteria are met, and deny is specified, the route is not redistributed or controlled. If the match criteria are not met then the route is neither accepted nor forwarded, irrespective of permit or deny specifications.
[P19954|Body Text] The route specified by the policies might not be the same as specified by the routing protocols. Setting policies enable packets to take different routes, depending on their length or content. Packet forwarding based on configured policies overrides packet forwarding specified in routing tables.
[P19955|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P19956|Normal] match as-path LISTNAME
[P19957|Body Text] no match as-path

[TABLE 734] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	LISTNAME	Specifies as autonomous system path access list name	Up to 20 characters

[P19958|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P19959|Normal] Route-map Configuration
[P19960|Heading 4] Default
[P19961|Normal] No match as-path is specified by default.
[P19962|Heading 4] Usage
[P19963|Normal] This command is valid only for BGP.
[P19964|Heading 4] Examples
[P19965|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# route-map myroute deny 34
Switch(config-route-map)# match as-path myaccesslist

[P19973|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P19974|Normal] Use this command to specify the community to be matched.
[P19975|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to remove the community list entry.
[P19976|Body Text] Communities are used to group and filter routes. They are designed to provide the ability to apply policies to large numbers of routes by using match and set commands. Community lists are used to identify and filter routes by their common attributes.
[P19977|Body Text] Use the match community command to allow matching based on community lists.
[P19978|Body Text] The values set by the match community command overrides the global values. The route that does not match at least one match clause is ignored.

[P19980|Normal] match community WORD

[P20149|Heading 3] match origin
[P20150|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P20151|Normal] Use this command to match origin code.
[P20152|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to disable this matching.
[P20153|Body Text] The origin attribute defines the origin of the path information. The egp parameter is indicated as an e in the routing table, and it indicates that the origin of the information is learned via Exterior Gateway Protocol. The igp parameter is indicated as an i in the routing table, and it indicates the origin of the path information is interior to the originating AS.
[P20154|Body Text] The incomplete parameter is indicated as a ? in the routing table, and indicates that the origin of the path information is unknown or learned through other means. If a static route is redistributed into BGP, the origin of the route is incomplete.
[P20155|Body Text] The match origin command specifies the origin to be matched. If there is a match for the specified origin, and permit is specified, the route is redistributed or controlled as specified by the set action. If the match criteria are met, and deny is specified, the route is not redistributed or controlled. If the match criteria are not met, the route is neither accepted nor forwarded, irrespective of permit or deny specifications.
[P20156|Body Text] The route specified by the policies might not be the same as specified by the routing protocols. Setting policies enable packets to take different routes depending on their length or content. Packet forwarding based on configured policies overrides packet forwarding specified in routing tables.
[P20157|Body Text] This command is valid for BGP only.
[P20158|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P20159|Normal] match origin { egp | igp | incomplete }
[P20160|Body Text] no match origin

[TABLE 743] rows=4 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	egp	learned from EGP	-
R3	igp	Local IGP	-
R4	incomplete	Unknown heritage	-

[P20161|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P20162|Normal] Route-map Configuration
[P20163|Heading 4] Default
[P20164|Normal] No match origin is specified by default.
[P20165|Heading 4] Usage
[P20166|Normal] None
[P20167|Heading 4] Examples
[P20168|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# route-map myroute deny 34
Switch(config-route-map)# match origin egp

[P20208|Heading 3] set ipv6 aggregator
[P20209|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P20210|Normal] Use this command to set the AS number for the route map and router ID.
[P20211|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to disable this function.
[P20212|Body Text] An Autonomous System (AS) is a collection of networks under a common administration sharing a common routing strategy. It is subdivided by areas, and is assigned a unique 16-bit number. Use the set aggregator command to
[P20213|Body Text] assign an AS number for the aggregator.
[P20214|Body Text] To use the set aggregator command, you must first have a match clause. Match and set commands set the conditions for redistributing routes from one routing protocol to another. The match command specifies the match criteria under which redistribution is allowed for the current route-map. The set command specifies the set redistribution actions to be performed, if the match criteria are met.
[P20215|Body Text] If the packets do not match any of the defined criteria, they are routed through the normal routing process.
[P20216|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P20217|Normal] set ipv6 aggregator as ASNUM IPV6_ADDR
[P20218|Body Text] no set ipv6 aggregator

[TABLE 746] rows=3 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	ASNUM	Specifies the AS number of aggregator	1-65535
R3	IPV6_ADDR	Specifies the IPv6 address of aggregator	IPv6 Address

[P20220|Normal] Route-map Configuration

[P20224|Normal] This command is valid for BGP only.
[P20225|Heading 4] Examples
[P20226|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# route-map myroute permit 3
Switch(config-route-map)# set aggregator as 43 2001:db8::1

[P20229|Heading 3] set as-path
[P20230|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P20231|Normal] Use this command to modify an autonomous system path for a route.
[P20232|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to disable this function.
[P20233|Body Text] Use the set as-path command to specify an autonomous system path. By specifying the length of the AS-Path, the router influences the best path selection by a neighbor. Use the prepend parameter with this command to prepend an AS path string to routes increasing the AS path length.
[P20234|Body Text] To use the set as-path command, you must first have a match clause. Match and set commands set the conditions for redistributing routes from one routing protocol to another. The match command specifies the match criteria under which redistribution is allowed for the current route-map. The set command specifies the set redistribution actions to be performed, if the match criteria are met.
[P20235|Body Text] If the packets do not match any of the defined criteria, they are routed through the normal routing process.
[P20236|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P20237|Normal] set as-path prepend ASN [ …ASN ]
[P20238|Body Text] no set as-path

[P20285|Heading 3] set community
[P20286|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P20287|Normal] Use this command to set the communities attribute.
[P20288|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to delete the entry.
[P20289|Body Text] Use this command to set the community attribute and group destinations in a certain community, as well as, apply routing decisions according to those communities.
[P20290|Body Text] To use the set community command, you must first have a match clause. Match and set commands set the conditions for redistributing routes from one routing protocol to another. The match command specifies the match criteria under which redistribution is allowed for the current route-map. The set command specifies the set redistribution actions to be performed, if the match criteria are met.
[P20291|Body Text] If the packets do not match any of the defined criteria, they are routed through the normal routing process.
[P20292|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P20293|Normal] set community [ AA:NN | internet | local-AS | no-advertise | no-export ]

R3	internet	Specifies the Internet (well-known community)	-
R4	local-AS	Specifies no sending outside the local AS (well-known community)	-
R5	no-advertise	Specifies no advertisement of this route to any peer (well-known community)	-
R6	no-export	Specifies no advertisement of this route to next AS (well-known community)	-
R7	none	Removes the community attribute from the prefixes that pass the route-map	-
