[P20307|Heading 3] set dampening
[P20308|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P20309|Normal] Use this command to enable route-flap dampening and set parameters.
[P20310|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to disable it.
[P20311|Body Text] Set the unreachability half-life time to be equal to, or greater than, reachability half-life time. The suppress-limit value must be greater than or equal to the reuse limit value.
[P20312|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P20313|Normal] set dampening REACHTIME REUSE SUPPRESS MAXSUPPRESS [ UNREACHTIME ]
[P20314|Body Text] no set dampening

[TABLE 750] rows=6 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	REACHTIME	Specifies the reachability half-life time in minutes. The time for the penalty to decrease to one-half of its current value. The default is 15 minutes	1-45
R3	REUSE	Specifies the reuse-limit value. When the penalty for a suppressed route decays below the reuse value, the routes become unsuppressed. The default reuse limit is 750	1-20000
R4	SUPPRESS	Specifies the suppress-limit value. When the penalty for a route exceeds the suppress value, the route is suppressed. The default suppress limit is 2000	1-20000
R5	MAXSUPPRESS	Specifies the max-suppress-time. Maximum time that a dampened route is suppressed. The default max-suppress value is 4 times the half-life time (60 minutes)	1-255
R6	UNREACHTIME	Specifies the un-reachability half-life time for penalty, in minutes. The default value is 15 minutes	1-45

[P20380|Heading 3] set metric
[P20381|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P20382|Normal] Use this command to set a metric value for a route.
[P20383|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to disable this function.
[P20384|Body Text] This command sets the metric value for a route, and influences external neighbors about the preferred path into an Autonomous System (AS). The preferred path is the one with a lower metric value. A router compares metrics for paths from neighbors in the same ASs. To compare metrics from neighbors coming from different ASs, use the bgp always-compare-med command.
[P20385|Body Text] To use the set metric command, you must first have a match clause. Match and set commands set the conditions for redistributing routes from one routing protocol to another. The match command specifies the match criteria under which redistribution is allowed for the current route-map. The set command specifies the set redistribution actions to be performed, if the match criteria are met.
[P20386|Body Text] If the packets do not match any of the defined criteria, they are routed through the normal routing process.
[P20387|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P20388|Normal] set metric METRICVAL
[P20389|Body Text] no set metric

[TABLE 754] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value

[P20418|Heading 3] set origin
[P20419|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P20420|Normal] Use this command to set the BGP origin code.
[P20421|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to delete an entry.
[P20422|Body Text] The origin attribute defines the origin of the path information. The three parameters with this command indicate three different values. IGP is interior to the originating AS. This happens if IGP is redistributed into the BGP. EGP is learned through an Exterior Gateway Protocol. Incomplete is unknown or learned through some other means. This happens when static route is redistributed in BGP and the origin of the route is incomplete.
[P20423|Body Text] To use the set origin command, you must first have a match clause. Match and set commands set the conditions for redistributing routes from one routing protocol to another. The match command specifies the match criteria under which redistribution is allowed for the current route-map. The set command specifies the set redistribution actions to be performed, if the match criteria are met.
[P20424|Body Text] If the packets do not match any of the defined criteria, they are routed through the normal routing process.
[P20425|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P20426|Normal] set origin { egp | igp | incomplete }
[P20427|Body Text] no set origin

[TABLE 756] rows=4 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	egp	Specifies a remote EGP system	-
R3	igp	A local IGP system	-
R4	incomplete	Specifies a system of unknown heritage	-

[P20457|Heading 3] set tag
[P20458|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P20459|Normal] Use this command to set a specified tag value.
[P20460|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to return to the default.
[P20461|Body Text] Tag in this command is the route tag which is labeled by another routing protocol (BGP or other IGP when redistributing), because AS-external-LSA has a route-tag field in its LSAs. Also, with using route-map, ZebOS can tag the LSAs with the appropriate tag value. Sometimes, the tag matches with using route-map, and sometimes, the value
[P20462|Body Text] may be used by another application.
[P20463|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P20464|Normal] set tag TAGVALUE
[P20465|Body Text] no set tag

[TABLE 758] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	TAGVALUE	Tag value for destination routing protocol.	0-4294967295

[P20466|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P20467|Normal] Route-map Configuration
[P20468|Heading 4] Default
[P20469|Normal] No set tag is specified by default.
[P20470|Heading 4] Usage
[P20471|Normal] This command is valid for OSPF and RIP only.
[P20472|Heading 4] Examples
[P20473|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# route-map rmap1 permit 3
Switch(config-route-map)# set tag 6

[P20477|Heading 3] set vpnv6 next-hop
[P20478|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P20479|Normal] Use this command to set a VPNv6 next-hop address.
[P20480|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to disable this function
[P20481|Body Text] To use the set vpn6-hext-hop command, you must first have a match clause. Match and set commands set the conditions for redistributing routes from one routing protocol to another. The match command specifies the match criteria under which redistribution is allowed for the current route-map. The set command specifies the set redistribution actions to be performed, if the match criteria are met.
[P20482|Body Text] If the packets do not match any of the defined criteria, they are routed through the normal routing process.
[P20483|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P20484|Normal] set vpnv6 next-hop IPV6_ADDR
[P20485|Body Text] no set vpnv6 next-hop

[TABLE 759] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value

[P20488|Heading 4] Default

[P20490|Heading 4] Usage
[P20491|Normal] This command is valid for BGP only.
[P20492|Heading 4] Examples
[P20493|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal

[P20496|Heading 3] set weight
[P20497|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P20498|Normal] Use this command to set weights for the routing table.
[P20499|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to delete an entry.
[P20500|Body Text] The weight value is used to assist in best path selection. It is assigned locally to a router. When there are several routes with a common destination, the routes with a higher weight value are preferred.
[P20501|Body Text] To use the set weight command, you must first have a match clause. Match and set commands set the conditions for redistributing routes from one routing protocol to another. The match command specifies the match criteria under which redistribution is allowed for the current route-map. The set command specifies the set redistribution actions to be performed, if the match criteria are met
[P20502|Body Text] match as-path 10
[P20503|Body Text] set weight 400
[P20504|Body Text] In the above configuration, all routes that apply to access-list 10 will have the weight set at 400.
[P20505|Body Text] If the packets do not match any of the defined criteria, they are routed through the normal routing process.
[P20506|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P20507|Normal] set weight WEIGHT
[P20508|Body Text] no set weight

[TABLE 760] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	WEIGHT	Specifies the weight value	0-4294967295

[P20510|Normal] Route-map Configuration
[P20511|Heading 4] Default
[P20512|Normal] No set weight is specified by default.
[P20513|Heading 4] Usage
[P20514|Normal] This command is valid for BGP only.
[P20515|Heading 4] Examples
[P20516|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# route-map rmap1 permit 3
Switch(config-route-map)# set weight 60

[P20551|Heading 3] aggregate-address
[P20552|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P20553|Normal] Use this command to configure BGP aggregate entries.
[P20554|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to disable this function.
[P20555|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P20556|Normal] ( no ) aggregate-address IPADDRESS { summary-only | as-set }

[TABLE 763] rows=4 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	IPV6_ADDR	X:X::X:X/M Specifies the aggregate prefix	IPv6 address
R3	summary-only	Filters more specific routes from updates.	-
R4	as-set	Generates AS set path information	-

[P20557|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P20558|Normal] Address Family Configuration
[P20559|Heading 4] Default
[P20560|Normal] Disabled
[P20561|Heading 4] Usage
[P20562|Normal] Aggregates are used to minimize the size of routing tables. Aggregation combines the characteristics of several different routes and advertises a single route.The aggregate-address command creates an aggregate entry in the BGP routing table if any more-specific BGP routes are available in the specified range. Using the summary-only parameter advertises the prefix only, suppressing the more-specific routes to all neighbors.
[P20563|Heading 4] Examples
[P20564|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router bgp 100
Switch(config-router)# aggregate-address 2018::1/64 as-set summary-only
[P20565|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P20566|Normal] N/A
[P20567|Heading 3] bgp always-compare-med
[P20568|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P20569|Normal] Use this command to compare the Multi Exit Discriminator (MED) for paths from neighbors in different autonomous systems.
[P20570|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to disallow the comparison.
[P20571|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P20572|Normal] ( no ) bgp always-compare-med
[P20573|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P20574|Normal] Router Configuration
[P20575|Heading 4] Default
[P20576|Normal] Disabled
[P20577|Heading 4] Usage
[P20578|Normal] Multi Exit Discriminator (MED) is used in best path selection by BGP. MED is compared after BGP attributes weight, local preference, AS-path and origin have been compared and are equal.
[P20579|Body Text] MED comparison is done only among paths from the same autonomous system (AS). Use bgp always-comparemed command to allow comparison of MEDs from different ASs. The MED parameter is used to select the best path. A path with lower MED is preferred.
[P20580|Heading 4] Examples
[P20581|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router bgp 100
Switch(config-router)# bgp always-compare-med
[P20582|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P20583|Normal] bgp bestpath med
[P20584|Body Text] bgp bestpath as-path ignore

[P20588|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to remove this configuration.
[P20589|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P20590|Normal] bgp as-local-count NUM
[P20591|Body Text] no bgp as-local-count

[TABLE 764] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	NUM	The number of the local AS number prepended to the AS path.	2-64

[P20596|Heading 4] Usage
[P20597|Normal] Use this command to configure the number of prepended local-as number.
[P20598|Heading 4] Examples
[P20599|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal

Switch(config-router)# bgp as-local-count 5

[P20607|Normal] ( no ) bgp bestpath as-path ignore
[P20608|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P20609|Normal] Router Configuration
[P20610|Heading 4] Default
[P20611|Normal] Disabled
[P20612|Heading 4] Usage
[P20613|Normal] None

[P20618|Heading 3] bgp bestpath compare-confed-aspath
[P20619|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P20620|Normal] Use this command to allow comparing of the confederation AS path length.
[P20621|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to revert the selection and ignore AS confederation path length in the BGP best path selection.
[P20622|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P20623|Normal] ( no ) bgp bestpath compare-confed-aspath
[P20624|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P20625|Normal] Router Configuration
[P20626|Heading 4] Default
[P20627|Normal] BGP receives routes with identical eBGP paths from eBGP peers and selects the first route received as the best path.
[P20628|Heading 4] Usage
[P20629|Normal] This command specifies that the AS confederation path length must be used, when available, in the BGP best path decision process. It is effective only when bgp bestpath as-path ignore command has not been specified.
[P20630|Heading 4] Examples
[P20631|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config) router bgp 100
Switch(config-router) bgp bestpath compare-confed-aspath
[P20632|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P20633|Normal] bgp bestpath as-path ignore
[P20634|Heading 3] bgp bestpath compare-routerid
[P20635|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P20636|Normal] Use this command to compare router-id for identical eBGP paths.
[P20637|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to disable this function.
[P20638|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P20639|Normal] ( no ) bgp bestpath compare-routerid
[P20640|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P20641|Normal] Router Configuration
[P20642|Heading 4] Default
[P20643|Normal] BGP receives routes with identical eBGP paths from eBGP peers and selects the first route received as the best path.
[P20644|Heading 4] Usage
[P20645|Normal] When comparing similar routes from peers the BGP router does not consider router ID of the routes. By default, it selects the first received route. Use this command to include router ID in the selection process; similar routes are compared and the route with lowest router ID is selected. The router-id is the highest IP address on the router, with preference given to loopback addresses. Router-id can be manually set by using the bgp router-id command.
[P20646|Heading 4] Examples
[P20647|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config) router bgp 100
Switch(config-router) bgp bestpath compare-routerid
[P20648|Heading 4] Related Commands

[P20650|Body Text] show ip bgp neighbors

[P20667|Heading 3] bgp bestpath med
[P20668|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P20669|Normal] Use this command to specify Multi Exit Discriminator (MED) attribute comparison.
[P20670|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to prevent BGP from considering the MED attribute in comparing paths.
[P20671|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P20672|Normal] bgp bestpath med confed [ missing-as-worst ]
[P20673|Body Text] bgp bestpath med missing-as-worst [ confed ]
[P20674|Body Text] no bgp bestpath med confed [ missing-as-worst ]
[P20675|Body Text] no bgp bestpath med missing-as-worst [ confed ]

[TABLE 765] rows=3 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	confed	Compares MED among confederation paths	-
R3	missing-as-worst	Treats missing MED as the least preferred one	-

[P20676|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P20677|Normal] Router Configuration
[P20678|Heading 4] Default
[P20679|Normal] MED value is zero.
[P20680|Heading 4] Usage
[P20681|Normal] Use this command to specify two MED attributes–confed and missing-as-worst. The confed attribute enables MED comparison among paths learned from confederation peers. The MEDs are compared only if there is no external autonomous system (an AS not within the confederation) in the path. If there is an external autonomous system in the path, the MED comparison is not made.
[P20682|Body Text] The missing-as-worst attribute to consider a missing MED attribute in a path as having a value of infinity, making the path without a MED value the least desirable path. If missing-as-worst is disabled, the missing MED is assigned the value of 0, making the path with the missing MED attribute the best path.
[P20683|Heading 4] Examples
[P20684|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config) router bgp 100
Switch(config-router) bgp bestpath med missing-as-worst
[P20685|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P20686|Normal] bgp-always-compare-med, bgp bestpath as-path ignore, bgp deterministic-med
[P20687|Heading 3] bgp bestpath tie-break-on-age
[P20688|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P20689|Normal] Use this command to preferentially choose old routes when other condition is the same in the algorithm for choosing a route.
[P20690|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to compare addtional information in route choosing rather than the age of route.
[P20691|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P20692|Normal] ( no ) bgp bestpath tie-break-on-age
[P20693|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P20694|Normal] Router Configuration
[P20695|Heading 4] Default
[P20696|Normal] In the default case, BGP will preferentially choose an old route when other condition is the same.
[P20697|Heading 4] Usage
[P20698|Normal] When the the information that influence the quality of routing like aspath、local-preference、med is the same，preferentially chose the old route to prevent route flap.
[P20699|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to let BGP compara addtional information like router-id、neighbor’s address，instead of the age of routes.
[P20700|Heading 4] Examples
[P20701|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal 
Switch(config)# router bgp 100
Switch(config-router)# no bgp bestpath tie-break-on-age

[P20711|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P20712|Normal] Router Configuration
[P20713|Heading 4] Default
[P20714|Normal] When a router is configured as a route reflector, client-to-client reflection is enabled by default.
[P20715|Heading 4] Usage
[P20716|Normal] The bgp client-to-client reflection command is used to configure routers as route reflectors. Route reflectors are used when all Interior Border Gateway Protocol (iBGP) speakers are not fully meshed. If the clients are fully meshed the route reflector is not required, use no bgp client-to-client reflection command to disable the client-to-client route reflection.
[P20717|Heading 4] Examples
[P20718|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config) router bgp 100

[P20724|Heading 4] Command Purpose

R3	A.B.C.D	A.B.C.D Route Reflector Cluster-id in IP address format	IPv4 Address
R4	<1-4294967295>	Route Reflector cluster-id as a 32 bit quantity	1-4294967295

[P20730|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P20731|Normal] Router Configuration
[P20732|Heading 4] Default
[P20733|Normal] N/A
[P20734|Heading 4] Usage
[P20735|Normal] A cluster includes route reflectors and its clients. Usually, each cluster is identified by the router ID of its single route reflector but to increase redundancy sometimes a cluster may have more than one route reflector. All router reflectors in such a cluster are then identified by a cluster ID. The bgp cluster-id command is used to configure the 4 byte cluster ID for clusters with more than one route reflectors.
[P20736|Heading 4] Examples
[P20737|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config) router bgp 100
Switch(config-router) bgp cluster-id 1.1.1.1

[P20769|Normal] A confederation allows an AS to be divided into several ASs. The AS is given a confederation identifier. External routers view only the whole confederation as one AS. [P20779|Normal] bgp dampening REACHTIME
[P20780|Body Text] bgp dampening REACHTIME REUSE

[P20784|Body Text] no bgp dampening REACHTIME REUSE

[TABLE 770] rows=7 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	REACHTIME	Specifies the reachability half-life time in minutes. The time for the penalty to decrease to one-half of its current value. The default is 15 minutes.	1-45
R3	REUSE	Specifies the reuse limit value. When the penalty for a suppressed route decays below the reuse value, the routes become unsuppressed. The default reuse limit is 750 SUPPRESS <1-20000> Specifies the suppress limit value. When the penalty for a route exceeds the suppress value, the route is suppressed. The default suppress limit is 2000.	1-20000
R4	SUPPRESS	Specifies suppress-time.A route dampening more than this value will be suppressd. The default value is 2000.	1-20000
R5	MAXSUPPRESS	Specifies the max-suppress-time. Maximum time that a dampened route is suppressed. The default max-suppress value is 4 times the half-life time (60 minutes).	1-255
R6	UNREACHTIME	Specifies the un-reachability half-life time for penalty, in minutes.	1-45
R7	ROUTEMAP	route-map WORD Route-map to specify criteria for dampening.	The length of route-map name should not greater than 20 and the first character should be ‘a’-‘z’, ‘A’-‘Z’ or ‘0’-‘9’.

[P20787|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P20788|Normal] Router Configuration
[P20789|Body Text] Address Family Configuration
[P20790|Heading 4] Default
[P20791|Normal] N/A
[P20792|Heading 4] Usage
[P20793|Normal] Route dampening minimizes the instability caused by route flapping. A penalty is added for every flap in a flapping route. As soon as the total penalty reaches the suppress limit the advertisement of the route is suppressed. This penalty is decayed according to the configured half time value. Once the penalty is lower than the reuse limit, the route advertisement is un-suppressed.
[P20794|Body Text] The dampening information is purged from the router once the penalty becomes less than half of the reuse limit.
[P20795|Heading 4] Examples
[P20796|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router bgp 100
Switch(config-router)# bgp dampening 20 800 2500 80 25
[P20797|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P20798|Normal] N/A
[P20799|Heading 3] bgp default local-preference
[P20800|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P20801|Normal] Use this command to change the default local preference value.
[P20802|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to revert to the default setting.
[P20803|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P20804|Normal] bgp default local-preference PREF_VALUE
[P20805|Body Text] no default local-preference ( PREF_VALUE | )

[TABLE 771] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	PREF_VALUE	Configure default local preference value. The default local preference value is 100.	0-4294967295

[P20806|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P20807|Normal] Router Configuration
[P20808|Heading 4] Default
[P20809|Normal] The default local preference value is 100.
[P20810|Heading 4] Usage
[P20811|Normal] Local preference indicates the preferred path when there are multiple paths to the same destination. The path having a higher preference is preferred. Use bgp default local-preference command to define preference of a particular path. The preference is sent to all routers and access servers in the local autonomous system.
[P20812|Heading 4] Examples
[P20813|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config) router bgp 100
Switch(config-router) bgp default local-preference 2345555

[P20816|Heading 3] bgp deterministic-med
[P20817|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P20818|Normal] Use this command to compare the Multi Exit Discriminator (MED) variable when choosing among routes advertised by different peers in the same autonomous system.
[P20819|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to disallow this setting.
[P20820|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P20821|Normal] bgp deterministic-med
[P20822|Body Text] no bgp deterministic-med
[P20823|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P20824|Normal] Router Configuration
[P20825|Heading 4] Default
[P20826|Normal] Disabled
[P20827|Heading 4] Usage
[P20828|Normal] "Multi Exit Discriminator (MED) is used in best path selection by BGP. MED is compared after BGP attributes weight, local preference, AS-path and origin have been compared and are equal. Enable bgp deterministic med command on all routers in the local AS, for a correct comparison result. After enabling this command, all paths for the same prefix are grouped together and arranged according to their MED value.
[P20829|Body Text] Based on this comparison, the best path is then chosen.
[P20830|Body Text] This command compares MED variable when choosing routes advertised by different peers in the same AS, to compare MED, when choosing routes from neighbors in different ASs use the bgp always-compare-med command."
[P20831|Heading 4] Examples
[P20832|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config) router bgp 100
Switch(config-router) bgp deterministic-med
[P20833|Heading 4] Related Commands

[P20869|Heading 3] bgp log-neighbor-changes
[P20870|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P20871|Normal] Use this command to enable logging of status change messages without turning on debug bgp commands.
[P20872|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to disable this feature.
[P20873|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P20874|Normal] bgp log-neighbor-changes
[P20875|Body Text] no bgp log-neighbor-changes
[P20876|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P20877|Normal] Router Configuration
[P20878|Heading 4] Default
[P20879|Normal] Disabled
[P20880|Heading 4] Usage
[P20881|Normal] System implementation provides other kinds of logging services for neighbor status, for example, debug bgp fsm, debug bgp events, etc. However, these commands create a significant hit in the logging performance.
[P20882|Body Text] The bgp log-neighbor-changes command, logs the following events:
[P20883|Normal] BGP Notification Received
[P20884|Normal] Erroneous BGP Update Received
[P20885|Normal] User reset request
[P20886|Normal] Peer time-out
[P20887|Normal] Peer Closing down the session
[P20888|Normal] Interface flap
[P20889|Normal] Router ID changed
[P20890|Normal] Neighbor deleted
[P20891|Normal] Member added to peer group
[P20892|Normal] Administrative shutdown
[P20893|Normal] Remote AS changed
[P20894|Normal] RR client configuration modification
[P20895|Normal] Soft reconfiguration modification
[P20896|Heading 4] Examples
[P20897|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router bgp 100
Switch(config-router)# bgp log-neighbor-changes

[P21079|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to remove an administrative distance.
[P21080|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P21081|Normal] distance bgp ED ID LD
[P21082|Body Text] no distance bgp

[TABLE 782] rows=4 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	ED	Distance of EBGP routes.	1-255

[P21083|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P21084|Normal] Router Configuration
[P21085|Body Text] Address Family Configuration
[P21086|Heading 4] Default
[P21087|Normal] N/A
[P21088|Heading 4] Usage
[P21089|Normal] Use this command to set the administrative distance for BGP. This distance is a rating of trustworthiness of a router.
[P21090|Body Text] The higher the distance the lower the trust rating.
[P21091|Body Text] The administrative distance can be set for external, internal and local routes. External paths are routes learned from a neighbor out of the AS. The internal routes are routes learned from another router within the same AS. Local routes are for the router that is being redistributed from another process.
[P21092|Body Text] If the administrative distance is changed, it could create inconsistency in the routing table and obstruct routing.
[P21093|Heading 4] Examples
[P21094|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal 
Switch(config)# router bgp 100
Switch(config-router)# address-family ipv6
Switch(config-router-af)# distance bgp 200 150 10

[P21120|Heading 4] Command Mode

[P21122|Heading 4] Default
[P21123|Normal] N/A
[P21124|Heading 4] Usage
[P21125|Normal] Named community list is a filter based on regular expressions. If the regular expression matches the specified string representing the AS path of the route, then the permit or deny condition applies. Use this command to define the BGP access list globally, use the neighbor router configuration command to apply a specific access list.
[P21126|Heading 4] Examples

Switch(config)# ip as-path access-list mylist deny ^65535$

[P21137|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P21138|Normal] Global Configuration
[P21139|Heading 4] Default
[P21140|Normal] N/A
[P21141|Heading 4] Usage
[P21142|Normal] Use the community-lists to specify BGP community attributes. The community attribute is used for implementing policy routing. It is an optional, transitive attribute and facilitates transfer of local policies through different autonomous systems. It includes community values that are 32 bits long.
[P21143|Body Text] There are two kinds of community-lists: the expanded and standard. The standard community-list defines the community attributes in a specified format and not with regular expressions. The expanded community-list defines the communities attributes with regular expressions.
[P21144|Heading 4] Examples
[P21145|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ip community-list 20 permit 7675:80 7675:90
[P21146|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P21147|Normal] ip community-list standard
[P21148|Body Text] ip community-list expanded

[P21175|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P21176|Normal] Global Configuration
[P21177|Heading 4] Default
[P21178|Normal] N/A
[P21179|Heading 4] Usage
[P21180|Normal] Use the community-lists to specify BGP community attributes. The community attribute is used for implementing policy routing. It is an optional, transitive attribute and facilitates transfer of local policies through different autonomous systems. It includes community values that are 32 bits long.
[P21181|Body Text] There are two kinds of community-lists–the expanded and standard. The standard community-list defines the community attributes in a specified format without regular expressions. The expanded community-list defines the communities attributes with regular expressions.
[P21182|Body Text] Use the ip community-list standard command to add a standard community-list entry. The standard community-list is compiled into binary format and is directly compared with the BGP communities attribute in the BGP updates. The comparison is faster than the expanded community-list. Any community value that does not match the standard community value is automatically treated as expanded.
[P21183|Heading 4] Examples
[P21184|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ip community-list standard CLIST permit 7675:80 7675:90 no-export
[P21185|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P21186|Normal] ip community-list
[P21187|Body Text] ip community-list expanded

[P21206|Heading 3] neighbor activate
[P21207|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P21208|Normal] Use this command to enable the exchange of the specified AF routes with a neighboring router.
[P21209|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to disable exchange of information with a neighbor.
[P21210|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P21211|Normal] neighbor NEIGHBORID activate
[P21212|Body Text] no neighbor NEIGHBORID activate

[TABLE 788] rows=4 cols=3

R4	TAG	Name of an existing peer-group. For information on how to create peer groups, refer to the neighbor peer-group and neighbor remote-as commands. When this parameter is used with a command, the command applies on all peers in the specified group.	-

[P21213|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P21214|Normal] Router Configuration
[P21215|Body Text] Address Family Configuration
[P21216|Heading 4] Default
[P21217|Normal] N/A
[P21218|Heading 4] Usage
[P21219|Normal] After the TCP connection is opened with the neighbor, this command is used to enable or disable the exchange of the specified AF information with a neighboring router.
[P21220|Body Text] To enable the exchange of multicast and VPNv4 address prefix types, neighbors are activated using the neighbor activate command in address family mode.
[P21221|Heading 4] Examples
[P21222|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router bgp 10
Switch(config-router)# address-family ipv6
Switch(config-router-af)# neighbor 2018::1 active

[P21225|Heading 3] neighbor advertisement-interval
[P21226|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P21227|Normal] Use this command to set the minimum interval between sending the BGP routing updates.
[P21228|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to set the interval time to default.
[P21229|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P21230|Normal] neighbor NEIGHBORID advertisement-interval TIME
[P21231|Body Text] no neighbor NEIGHBORID advertisement-interval TIME

[TABLE 789] rows=5 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	NEIGHBORID	(X:X::X:X\|TAG)	-
R3	X:X::X:X	Specifies the address of the BGP neighbor in IPv6 format.	-
R4	TAG	Name of an existing peer-group. For information on how to create peer groups, refer to the neighbor peer-group and neighbor remote-as commands. When this parameter is used with a command, the command applies on all peers in the specified group.	-
R5	TIME	Advertise -interval value in seconds	0-600

[P21232|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P21233|Normal] Router Configuration
[P21234|Heading 4] Default
[P21235|Normal] N/A
[P21236|Heading 4] Usage
[P21237|Normal] Use this command to set the minimum interval between the sending of BGP routing updates. To reduce the flapping of routes to internet, a minimum advertisement interval is set, so that the BGP routing updates are sent only per interval seconds. bgp dampening can also be used to control the effects of flapping routes.
[P21238|Heading 4] Examples
[P21239|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router bgp 10
Switch(config-router)# neighbor 2018::1 advertisement-interval 45
[P21240|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P21241|Normal] N/A
[P21242|Heading 3] neighbor allowas-in
[P21243|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P21244|Normal] Use this command to configure PE routers to allow re-advertisement of all prefixes containing duplicate Autonomous System Numbers (ASNs).
[P21245|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to disable the readvertisement of a PE router’s ASN.
[P21246|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P21247|Normal] neighbor NEIGHBOR allowas-in [ NUMBER ]
[P21248|Body Text] no neighbor NEIGHBOR allowas-in

[TABLE 790] rows=5 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	NEIGHBORID	(X:X::X:X\|TAG)	-
R3	X:X::X:X	Specifies the address of the BGP neighbor in IPv6 format.	IPv6 Address
R4	TAG	Name of an existing peer-group. For information on how to create peer groups, refer to the neighbor peer-group and neighbor remote-as commands. When this parameter is used with a command, the command applies on all peers in the specified group.	Up to 20 characters
R5	NUMBER	Number of occurances of AS number.Default value is 1	1-10

[P21249|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P21250|Normal] Address Family Configuration
[P21251|Heading 4] Default
[P21252|Normal] Disabled
[P21253|Heading 4] Usage
[P21254|Normal] In a hub and spoke configuration, a PE router re-advertises all prefixes containing duplicate ASNs. Use the neighbor allowas-in command to configure two VRFs on each PE router to receive and re-advertise prefixes. One of the VRFs receives prefixes with ASNs from all PE routers and then advertises them to neighboring PE routers. The other VRF receives prefixes with ASNs from the CE router and re-advertises them to all PE routers in the hub and spoke configuration.
[P21255|Body Text] Control the number of times an ASN is advertised, by specifying a number from 1 to 10.
[P21256|Heading 4] Examples
[P21257|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config-router)# address-family ipv6
Switch(config-router-af)# neighbor 2018::1 allowas-in 3
[P21258|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P21259|Normal] N/A

[P21272|Normal] Use this command to set the minimum interval between the ready to send of originated BGP routing updates. For the originated bgp routes， they would be sent out when as-origination-interval and advertisement-interval expired at the same time.

[P21301|Heading 4] Command Mode

[P21305|Heading 4] Usage
[P21306|Normal] Outbound Route Filters (ORFs) send and receive capabilities to lessen the number of updates exchanged between neighbors. By filtering updates, this option minimizes generating and processing of updates.
[P21307|Body Text] The local router advertises the ORF capability in send mode and the remote router receives the ORF capability in receive mode applying the filter as outbound policy. The two routers exchange updates to maintain the ORF for each

R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value

[P21404|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P21405|Normal] Address Family Configuration
[P21406|Heading 4] Default
[P21407|Normal] N/A
[P21408|Heading 4] Usage
[P21409|Normal] The neighbor maximum-prefix command allows the configuration of a specified number of prefixes that a BGP router is allowed to receive from a neighbor. When the warning-only option is not used, if any extra prefixes are received, the router ends the peering. A terminated peer, stays down until the clear ip bgp command is used.

Switch(config-router)# address-family ipv6
Switch(config-router-af)# neighbor 2018::1 maximum-prefix 1244 warning-only

[P21476|Normal] Use this command to Neighbors with the same update policies are grouped into peer groups. This facilitates the updates of various policies, such as, distribute and filter lists. [P21500|Heading 3] neighbor prefix-list
[P21501|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P21502|Normal] Use this command to distribute BGP neighbor information as specified in a prefix list.
[P21503|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to remove an entry.
[P21504|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P21505|Normal] neighbor NEIGHBORID prefix-list LISTNAME ( in | out )
[P21506|Body Text] no neighbor NEIGHBORID prefix-list LISTNAME ( in | out )

[TABLE 805] rows=7 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	NEIGHBORID	(X:X::X:X\|TAG)	-
R3	X:X::X:X	Specifies the address of the BGP neighbor in IPv6 format.	IPv6 Address
R4	TAG	Name of an existing peer-group. For information on how to create peer groups, refer to the neighbor peer-group and neighbor remote-as commands. When this parameter is used with a command, the command applies on all peers in the specified group.	Up to 20 characters
R5	LISTNAME	The number of an AS-path access list.	Up to 20 characters
R6	in	Specifies that the access list applies to incoming advertisements.	-
R7	out	Specifies that the access list applies to outgoing advertisements.	-

[P21507|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P21508|Normal] Address Family Configuration
[P21509|Heading 4] Default
[P21510|Normal] N/A
[P21511|Heading 4] Usage
[P21512|Normal] Use this command to specify a prefix list for filtering BGP advertisements. Filtering by prefix list matches the prefixes of routes with those listed in the prefix list. If there is a match, the route is used. An empty prefix list permits all prefixes. If a given prefix does not match any entries of a prefix list, the route is denied access. When multiple entries of a prefix list match a prefix, the entry with the smallest sequence number is considered to be a real match.
[P21513|Body Text] The router begins the search at the top of the prefix list, with the sequence number 1. Once a match or deny occurs, the router does not need to go through the rest of the prefix list. For efficiency the most common matches or denies are listed at the top.
[P21514|Body Text] The neighbor distribute-list command is an alternative to the neighbor prefix-list command and only
[P21515|Body Text] one of them can be used for filtering to the same neighbor in any direction.
[P21516|Heading 4] Examples
[P21517|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ip prefix-list list1 deny 30.0.0.0/24
Switch(config)# router bgp 12
Switch(config-router)# address-family ipv6
Switch(config-router-af)# neighbor 10.10.10.10 prefix-list list1 in
[P21518|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P21519|Normal] ip prefix-list

[P21554|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P21555|Normal] Use this command to configure the router as a BGP route reflector and configure the specified neighbor as its client.
[P21556|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to indicate that the neighbor is not a client.
[P21557|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P21558|Normal] neighbor NEIGHBORID route-reflector-client
[P21559|Body Text] no neighbor NEIGHBORID route-reflector-client

[P21560|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P21561|Normal] Address Family Configuration
[P21562|Heading 4] Default
[P21563|Normal] N/A
[P21564|Heading 4] Usage
[P21565|Normal] Route reflectors are a solution for the explosion of iBGP peering within an autonomous system. By route reflection the number of iBGP peers within an AS is reduced. Use the neighbor route-reflector-client command to configure the local router as the route reflector and specify neighbors as its client.
[P21566|Body Text] An AS can have more than one route reflector. One route reflector treats the other route reflector as another iBGP speaker.
[P21567|Heading 4] Examples
[P21568|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router bgp 10
Switch(config-router)# address-family ipv6
Switch(config-router-af)# neighbor 2018::1 route-reflector-client

[P21618|Normal] Use this command to store updates for inbound soft reconfiguration. Soft-reconfiguration may be used in lieu of BGP route refresh capability. [P21647|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P21648|Normal] Router Configuration
[P21649|Heading 4] Default
[P21650|Normal] N/A
[P21651|Heading 4] Usage
[P21652|Normal] Keepalive messages are sent by a router to inform another router that the BGP connection between the two is still active. The keepalive interval is the period of time between each keepalive message sent by the router. The holdtime interval is the time the router waits to receive a keepalive message and if it does not receive a message for this period it declares the neighbor dead.

Switch(config)# router bgp 12
Switch(config-router)# address-family ipv6

[P21666|Normal] N/A
[P21667|Heading 4] Usage
[P21668|Normal] When the aggregate-address command is used with the summary-only option, the more-specific routes of the aggregate are suppressed to all neighbors. Use the unsuppress-map command to selectively leak more-specific routes to a particular neighbor.
[P21669|Heading 4] Examples
[P21670|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)#router bgp 10
Switch(config-router)address-family ipv6
Switch(config-router-af)neighbor 2018::1 unsuppress-map mymap
[P21671|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P21672|Normal] N/A
[P21673|Heading 3] neighbor update-source
[P21674|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P21675|Normal] Use this command to allow internal BGP sessions to use any operational interface for TCP connections.
[P21676|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to restore the interface assignment to the closest interface.
[P21677|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P21678|Normal] neighbor NEIGHBORID update-source IFNAME
[P21679|Body Text] no neighbor NEIGHBORID update-source

[TABLE 815] rows=5 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	NEIGHBORID	(X:X::X:X\|TAG)	-
R3	X:X::X:X	Specifies the address of the BGP neighbor in IPv6 format.	IPv6 Address
R4	TAG	Name of an existing peer-group. For information on how to create peer groups, refer to the neighbor peer-group and neighbor remote-as commands. When this parameter is used with a command, the command applies on all peers in the specified group.	Up to 20 characters
R5	IFNAME	Specifies the loopback interface.	Support physical/aggregation/loopback/vlan/tunnel ports

[P21680|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P21681|Normal] Router Configuration
[P21682|Heading 4] Default
[P21683|Normal] N/A
[P21684|Heading 4] Usage
[P21685|Normal] Use this command in conjunction with any specified interface on the router. The loopback interface is the interface that is most commonly used with this command. The use of loopback interface eliminates a dependency and BGP does not have to rely on the availability of a particular interface for making TCP connections.
[P21686|Heading 4] Examples
[P21687|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router bgp 10
Switch(config-router)# neighbor 2018::1 update-source eth-0-1
[P21688|Heading 4] Related Commands

[P21690|Heading 3] neighbor weight
[P21691|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P21692|Normal] Use this command to set default weights for routes from this neighbor.
[P21693|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to remove a weight assignment.
[P21694|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P21695|Normal] neighbor NEIGHBORID weight WEIGHT
[P21696|Body Text] no neighbor NEIGHBORID weight

[TABLE 816] rows=5 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	NEIGHBORID	(X:X::X:X\|TAG)	-
R3	X:X::X:X	Specifies the address of the BGP neighbor in IPv6 format.	IPv6 Address
R4	TAG	Name of an existing peer-group. For information on how to create peer groups, refer to the neighbor peer-group and neighbor remote-as commands. When this parameter is used with a command, the command applies on all peers in the specified group.	Up to 20 characters
R5	WEIGHT	Specifies the weight this command assigns to the route.	0-65535

[P21697|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P21698|Normal] Address Family Configuration
[P21699|Heading 4] Default
[P21700|Normal] N/A
[P21701|Heading 4] Usage
[P21702|Normal] Use this command to specify a weight value to all routes learned from a neighbor. The route with the highest weight gets preference when there are other routes on the network.
[P21703|Body Text] Unlike the local-preference attribute, the weight attribute is relevant only to the local router.
[P21704|Body Text] The weights assigned using the set weight command overrides the weights assigned using this command.
[P21705|Heading 4] Examples
[P21706|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router bgp 12
Switch(config-router)address-family ipv6
Switch(config-router-af)# neighbor 2018::1 weight 60
[P21707|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P21708|Normal] N/A
[P21709|Heading 3] neighbor collide-established
[P21710|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P21711|Normal] Use this command to configure a BGP neighbor should be included into collision detection even its stats is established.
[P21712|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to disable this function.
[P21713|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P21714|Normal] neighbor NEIGHBORID collide-established
[P21715|Body Text] no neighbor NEIGHBORID collide-established

[TABLE 817] rows=3 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	NEIGHBORID	(X:X::X:X\|TAG)	-
R3	X:X::X:X	Specifies the address of the BGP neighbor in IPv6 format.	IPv6 Address

[P21716|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P21717|Normal] Router Configuration
[P21718|Heading 4] Default
[P21719|Normal] In the default case, if a neighbor’s state is established, it will not be included into collision detection.
[P21720|Heading 4] Usage
[P21721|Normal] When building connection with BGP neighbors, devices on both sides may start TCP connections in the sasme time. There will be two TCP connections in this case. To avoid reduncancy, collision detection is required to shutdown the connection on the side whose router-id or BGP identifier is smaller.
[P21722|Body Text] In the default case, when a BGP neighbor is already established, it will not be included into collision detection, which may causes redundant connections. Therefore, this command should be used to include established neighbors into collision detection.
[P21723|Heading 4] Examples
[P21724|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal 
Switch(config)# router bgp 100
Switch(config-router)# neighbor 3000::1 collide-establishe
[P21725|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P21726|Normal] N/A
[P21727|Heading 3] neighbor disallow-infinite-holdtime
[P21728|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P21729|Normal] Use this command to prohibit BGP neighbor to use infinite holdtime in OPEN message.
[P21730|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to allow BGP neighbor to use infinite holdtime.
[P21731|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P21732|Normal] neighbor NEIGHBORID disallow-infinite-holdtime
[P21733|Body Text] no neighbor NEIGHBORID disallow-infinite-holdtime

[TABLE 818] rows=3 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	NEIGHBORID	(X:X::X:X\|TAG)	-
R3	X:X::X:X	Specifies the address of the BGP neighbor in IPv6 format.	IPv6 Address

[P21734|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P21735|Normal] Router Configuration
[P21736|Heading 4] Default
[P21737|Normal] In the default case, if a neighbor’s state is established, it will not be included into collision detection.
[P21738|Heading 4] Usage
[P21739|Normal] After building connection with BGP neighbors, devices need to send keepalive message to keep the connetion. The interval of sending keepalive message is the holdtime. When a neighbor negotiated the holdtime to be 0(infinite), the two neighbors on both sides will not need keepalive messages anymore.
[P21740|Body Text] Use this command to prohibit the neighbor to neigotiate the holdtime to infinite.
[P21741|Heading 4] Examples
[P21742|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal 
Switch(config)# router bgp 100
Switch(config-router)# neighbor 3000::1 disallow-infinite-holdtime 
[P21743|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P21744|Normal] N/A
[P21745|Heading 3] neighbor dont-capability-negotiate
[P21746|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P21747|Normal] Use this command to prohibit BGP neighbor to attach capability segement in OPEN message.
[P21748|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to allow BGP neighbor to attach capability segement.
[P21749|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P21750|Normal] neighbor NEIGHBORID dont-capability-negotiate
[P21751|Body Text] no neighbor NEIGHBORID dont-capability-negotiate

[TABLE 819] rows=3 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	NEIGHBORID	(X:X::X:X\|TAG)	-
R3	X:X::X:X	Specifies the address of the BGP neighbor in IPv6 format.	IPv6 Address

[P21752|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P21753|Normal] Router Configuration
[P21754|Heading 4] Default
[P21755|Normal] In the default case, it is allowed for a BGP neighbor to attach the capability segment in OPEN messages.
[P21756|Heading 4] Usage
[P21757|Normal] In the BGP open messages, neighbors can negotiate capabilities through the capability segment in open messages.
[P21758|Body Text] When the switch received an open message containing capability segment after enabled this function, it will send a notification message and shutdown the connetion with the neighbor.
[P21759|Heading 4] Examples
[P21760|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal 
Switch(config)# router bgp 100
Switch(config-router)# neighbor 3000::1 dont-capability-negotiate 
[P21761|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P21762|Normal] N/A
[P21763|Heading 3] neighbor enforce-multihop
[P21764|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P21765|Normal] Use this command to allow EBGP neighbor to build connection through multihop routes.
[P21766|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to prohibit EBGP neighbor to build connection through multihop routes, which means EBGP neighbor must be directly connected.
[P21767|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P21768|Normal] neighbor NEIGHBORID enforce-multihop
[P21769|Body Text] no neighbor NEIGHBORID enforce-multihop

[TABLE 820] rows=3 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	NEIGHBORID	(X:X::X:X\|TAG)	-
R3	X:X::X:X	Specifies the address of the BGP neighbor in IPv6 format.	IPv6 Address

[P21770|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P21771|Normal] Router Configuration
[P21772|Heading 4] Default
[P21773|Normal] In the default case, it is only allowed to build connection with directly connected EBGP neighbor.
[P21774|Heading 4] Usage
[P21775|Normal] Usually EBGP neighbor connection is built through direct connection. And the TTL of its TCP packets is 1. When build neighbor through non-direct connection like loopback interface, due to the limitation of TTL, the connection will fail. Then this command will be used to allow connection with EBGP neighbor through multihop routes.
[P21776|Heading 4] Examples
[P21777|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal 
Switch(config)# router bgp 100
Switch(config-router)# neighbor 3000::1 enforce-multihop

[P21831|Heading 3] network
[P21832|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P21833|Normal] Use this command to specify the networks to be advertised by the BGP routing process. A unicast network address without a mask is accepted if it falls into the natural boundary of its class. A class-boundary mask is derived if the address matches its natural class-boundary.
[P21834|Body Text] Use the no form of this command to remove a network route entry.
[P21835|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P21836|Normal] network X:X::X:X/M
[P21837|Body Text] network X:X::X:X/M route-map WORD
[P21838|Body Text] no network X:X::X:X/M
[P21839|Body Text] no network X:X::X:X/M route-map WORD

[TABLE 824] rows=3 cols=3

R2	X:X::X:X/M	IPv6 prefix <network>, e.g., 2018::	IPv6 address with mask length
R3	WORD	Name of the route map	The length of route-map name should not greater than 20 and the first character should be ‘a’-‘z’, ‘A’-‘Z’ or ‘0’-‘9’.

[P21840|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P21841|Normal] Address Family Configuration
[P21842|Heading 4] Default
[P21843|Normal] N/A
[P21844|Heading 4] Usage
[P21845|Normal] N/A
[P21846|Heading 4] Examples
[P21847|Normal] The following example illustrates a address configured as a network route. The network prefix mask length of 64 will be internally derived, that is, 2018::/64:
[P21848|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)#router bgp 1
Switch(config-router)address-family ipv6
Switch(config-router-af)#network 2018::/64

!
router bgp 1
no synchronization
network 2018::/64
!

[P21851|Heading 3] network synchronization
[P21852|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P21853|Normal] Use this command to ensure the exact same static network prefix, specified through any of the network commands, is local or has IGP reachability (in the NSM RIB) before being introduced into the BGP RIB.
[P21854|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to disable this function.
[P21855|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P21856|Normal] network synchronization
[P21857|Body Text] no network synchronization
[P21858|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P21859|Normal] Router Configuration
[P21860|Body Text] Address Family Configuration
[P21861|Heading 4] Default
[P21862|Normal] Network synchronization is disabled by default.
[P21863|Heading 4] Usage
[P21864|Normal] N/A
[P21865|Heading 4] Examples
[P21866|Normal] The following example enables IGP synchronization of BGP static network routes in the router configuration mode:
[P21867|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router bgp 11
Switch(config-router)# network synchronization
[P21868|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P21869|Normal] N/A
[P21870|Heading 3] synchronization
[P21871|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P21872|Normal] Use this command to enable IGP synchronization of Internal BGP (iBGP) learned routes with the Internal Gateway Protocol (IGP) system in the router configuration mode or in the address-family configuration mode.
[P21873|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to disable this function.
[P21874|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P21875|Normal] synchronization
[P21876|Body Text] no synchronization
[P21877|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P21878|Normal] Router Configuration
[P21879|Body Text] Address Family Configuration
[P21880|Heading 4] Default
[P21881|Normal] IGP synchronization is disabled.
[P21882|Heading 4] Usage
[P21883|Normal] Synchronization is used when a BGP router should not advertise routes learned from iBGP neighbors, unless those routes are also present in an IGP (for example, OSPF). Synchronization may be enabled when all the routers in an autonomous system do not speak BGP, and the autonomous system is a transit for other autonomous systems. The no synchronization command is used when BGP router can advertise routes learned from its iBGP neighbors without waiting for the IGP reachability to be present.
[P21884|Heading 4] Examples
[P21885|Normal] The following example enables IGP synchronization of BGP static network routes in the IPv6-Unicast address family:
[P21886|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router bgp 11
Switch(config)# address-family ipv6
Switch(config-af)# network synchronization

[P22282|Heading 3] ip igmp access-group
[P22283|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P22284|Normal] Use this command to apply an access-list to the igmp interface.
[P22285|Body Text] To remove this setting, use the no form of this command.
[P22286|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P22287|Normal] ip igmp access-group LIST
[P22288|Body Text] no ip igmp access-group

[TABLE 842] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	LIST	The name of the ip access-list to be applied. The format of access-list should be ipv4.	Up to 40 characters

[P22289|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P22290|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P22291|Heading 4] Default
[P22292|Normal] Access-group is not configured on any igmp interface by default.
[P22293|Heading 4] Usage
[P22294|Normal] No matter the source ip or the destination ip in ACE should take effect respectively. If ACE’s action is deny, then the packet should be ignored; otherwise, if it matches one whose action is permit, then it should be processed regularly.
[P22295|Heading 4] Examples
[P22296|Normal] This example shows how to apply the access-list acl1 to the interface vlan1:
[P22297|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface vlan 1
Switch(config-if)# ip igmp access-group acl1
[P22298|Normal] This example shows how to remove the access-list acl1 on the interface:
[P22299|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface vlan 1
Switch(config-if)# no ip igmp access-group

[P22396|Heading 4] Usage
[P22397|Normal] This command is used to set the mroute-proxy port on the interface. Only one mroute-proxy port can be set on the interface. When set it again, the new setting will overwrite the old one.
[P22398|Heading 4] Examples
[P22399|Normal] This example shows how to set the mroute-proxy port to eth-0-1 on this interface:
[P22400|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface vlan 1
Switch(config-if)# ip igmp mroute-proxy eth-0-1
[P22401|Normal] This example shows how to remove the mroute-proxy port on this interface:
[P22402|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface vlan 1
Switch(config-if)# no ip igmp mroute-proxy

[P23295|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P23296|Normal] Use this command to apply an access-list to limit the pim register message received by rp.

[P23301|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P23302|Normal] Global Configuration
[P23303|Heading 4] Default
[P23304|Normal] None
[P23305|Heading 4] Usage
[P23306|Normal] This feature is used to prevent the unauthorized user registered to the switch.
[P23307|Body Text] When enable this feature, the system will send back a register stop message when the unauthorized register message is received.
[P23308|Heading 4] Examples
[P23309|Normal] This example shows how to apply the access-list acl1 to limit the pim register message received by rp:
[P23310|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal

[P23311|Normal] This example shows how to remove the limits:
[P23312|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# no ip pim accept-register

[P23375|Heading 3] ip pim dr-priority
[P23376|Heading 4] Command Purpose

[P23378|Body Text] To reset it to default value, use the no form of this command.
[P23379|Heading 4] Command Syntax

[P23381|Body Text] no ip pim dr-priority

[TABLE 893] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value

[P23382|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P23383|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P23384|Heading 4] Default
[P23385|Normal] 1
[P23386|Heading 4] Usage
[P23387|Normal] When a hello message without DR priority is received, it will be regarded to have the max DR priority and to be elected as DR. When more than one router’s hello messages do not have DR priority, the one which have the highest ip address will be elected as DR.
[P23388|Heading 4] Examples
[P23389|Normal] This example shows how to set the pim router DR priority to 1000:
[P23390|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config-if)# ip pim dr-priority 1000
[P23391|Normal] This example shows how tos reset the pim router DR priority to default value:
[P23392|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config-if)# no ip pim dr-priority

[P23394|Normal] None
[P23395|Heading 3] ip pim exclude-genid
[P23396|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P23397|Normal] Use this command to exclude generation id option from pim hello packets on this interface.
[P23398|Body Text] To reset to the default setting, use the no form of this command.
[P23399|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P23400|Normal] ip pim exclude-genid
[P23401|Body Text] no ip pim exclude-genid
[P23402|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P23403|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P23404|Heading 4] Default
[P23405|Normal] Disable
[P23406|Heading 4] Usage
[P23407|Normal] GenerationID is the ID of a PIM neighbour, it is carried in PIM hello message,the receiver device will record every received GenerationID in the hello packet and check if GenerationID has changed, if GenerationID changed, will consider neighbour state changed and restart state machine.
[P23408|Heading 4] Examples
[P23409|Normal] This example shows how to exclude generation id option from pim hello packets on this interface:
[P23410|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config-if)# ip pim exclude-genid
[P23411|Normal] This example shows how to reset the generation id option to the default setting:
[P23412|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config-if)# no ip pim exclude-genid

[P23502|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P23503|Normal] Global Configuration
[P23504|Heading 4] Default
[P23505|Normal] By default, will not limit PIM register messages, if a limit is set, PIM register messages will be discard when pakcet reached by this limit.
[P23506|Heading 4] Usage
[P23507|Normal] There is no rate limit for pim registers by default.
[P23508|Body Text] When the rate limit is configured, the exceed pim register message will be dropped on the rp.
[P23509|Heading 4] Examples
[P23510|Normal] This example shows how to set the rate limit for pim registers to 100 per second.:
[P23511|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ip pim register-rate-limit 100
[P23512|Normal] This example shows how to cancel the rate limit:
[P23513|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# no ip pim register-rate-limit

[P24073|Heading 4] Command Purpose

[P24075|Body Text] To cancel this setting, use the no form of this command.
[P24076|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P24077|Normal] ip pim nexthop-address NEXTHOP-ADDRESS virtual-address VIRTUAL-ADDRESS

R3	VIRTUAL-ADDRESS	virtual address	IPv4 Address

[P24079|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P24080|Normal] Global Configuration
[P24081|Heading 4] Default
[P24082|Normal] None
[P24083|Heading 4] Usage
[P24084|Normal] When PIM use virtual address to connect neighbour, Use this command to the virtual address of the pim nexthop address.
[P24085|Body Text] The command is used to enable the linkage between PIM-SM and VRRP,when enbale the command,it need to shutdown or no shutdown the port of ip pim bsr.
[P24086|Body Text] When enable the command, it also can be take effect if enable or disable the vrrp.
[P24087|Heading 4] Examples
[P24088|Normal] This example shows how to set a nexthop address with virtual address:
[P24089|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config-if)# ip pim nexthop-address 10.1.1.2 virtual-address 20.1.1.2
[P24090|Normal] This example shows how to unset this setting:
[P24091|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config-if)# no ip pim nexthop-address

[P24406|Heading 2] MLD Commands
[P24407|Heading 3] ipv6 mld access-group
[P24408|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P24409|Normal] Use this command to apply an access-list to the mld interface.
[P24410|Body Text] To remove this setting, use the no form of this command.
[P24411|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P24412|Normal] ipv6 mld access-group LISTNAME
[P24413|Body Text] no ipv6 mld access-group

[TABLE 927] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	LISTNAME	The name of the ipv6 access-list to be applied. The format of access-list should be ipv6.	A string with 1-20 characters

[P24414|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P24415|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P24416|Heading 4] Default
[P24417|Normal] Access-group is not configured on any mld interface by default.
[P24418|Heading 4] Usage
[P24419|Normal] No matter the source ipv6 prefix or the destination ipv6 prefix in ACE should take effect respectively. If ACE’s action is deny, then the packet will be ignored; Otherwise if it matches one whose action is permit, then it will be processed regularly.
[P24420|Heading 4] Examples
[P24421|Normal] This example shows how to apply the access-list acl1 to the interface vlan1:
[P24422|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface vlan 1
Switch(config-if)# ipv6 mld access-group acl1
[P24423|Normal] This example shows how to remove the access-list acl1 on the interface:
[P24424|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface vlan 1
Switch(config-if)# no ipv6 mld access-group
[P24425|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P24426|Normal] show ipv6 mld interface

[P24436|Heading 4] Default
[P24437|Normal] Access-group is not configured on any mld interface by default.
[P24438|Heading 4] Usage
[P24439|Normal] No matter the source ipv6 prefix or the destination ipv6 prefix in ACE should be take effect respectively. If ACE’s action is denied, then the packet should be ignored; Otherwise if it matches one whose action is permit, then it should be processed regularly.

[P25420|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P25421|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P25422|Heading 4] Default
[P25423|Normal] 1
[P25424|Heading 4] Usage
[P25425|Normal] When a hello message without DR priority is received, it will be regarded to have the max DR priority and to be elected as DR. When more than one router’s hello messages do not have DR priority, the one which have the highest ipv6 address will be elected as DR.
[P25426|Heading 4] Examples
[P25427|Normal] This example shows how to set the pim router DR priority to 1000:
[P25428|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# ipv6 pim dr-priority 1000
[P25429|Normal] This example shows how to return the pim router DR priority to default value:
[P25430|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# no ipv6 pim dr-priority

[P25433|Heading 3] ipv6 pim exclude-genid
[P25434|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P25435|Normal] Use this command to exclude generation id option from pim hello packets on this interface.
[P25436|Body Text] To return to the default setting, use the no form of this command.
[P25437|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P25438|Normal] ipv6 pim exclude-genid
[P25439|Body Text] no ipv6 pim exclude-genid
[P25440|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P25441|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P25442|Heading 4] Default
[P25443|Normal] Disable
[P25444|Heading 4] Usage
[P25445|Normal] GenerationID is the ID of a PIM neighbour, it is carried in PIM hello message,the receiver device will record every received GenerationID in the hello packet and check if GenerationID has changed, if GenerationID changed, will consider neighbour state changed and restart state machine.
[P25446|Heading 4] Examples
[P25447|Normal] This example shows how to exclude generation id option from pim hello packets on this interface:
[P25448|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# ipv6 pim exclude-genid
[P25449|Normal] This example shows how to return the generation id option to the default setting:
[P25450|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# no ipv6 pim exclude-genid

[P26141|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P26142|Normal] Global Configuration
[P26143|Heading 4] Default
[P26144|Normal] None
[P26145|Heading 4] Usage
[P26146|Normal] You can define a class map for each class of traffic to be used in QoS policies. If the packet matches any of the criteria configured for this class map with the match command, then this class map is applied to the packet. If no execution strategy is specified (match-any or match-all), then the default value of match-any is applied to the traffic class.

Switch(config)# policy-map type qos pmap_qos

[P26351|Heading 3] policer
[P26352|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P26353|Normal] Use this command to rate-limit traffic matching this traffic class for a specified interface. To cancel rate limit, use the no form of this command.
[P26354|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P26355|Normal] policer { color-blind | color-aware } cir CIR [ cbs CBS ] [ eir EBS ] [ ebs EBS ] [ conform { transmit [ set-traffic-class CLASS-ID ] | drop } | exceed { transmit [ set-traffic-class CLASS-ID ] | drop } | violate { transmit [ set-traffic-class CLASS-ID ] | drop } ] [ statistics ]
[P26356|Body Text] policer pps { color-blind | color-aware } cir CIR [ cbs CBS ] [ eir EBS ] [ ebs EBS ] [ conform { transmit [ set-traffic-class CLASS-ID ] | drop } | exceed { transmit [ set-traffic-class CLASS-ID ] | drop } | violate { transmit [ set-traffic-class CLASS-ID ] | drop } ] [ statistics ]
[P26357|Body Text] no policer

[TABLE 1013] rows=15 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	color-blind	Do not care input packet’s color	-
R3	color-aware	Care input packet’s color	-
R4	pps	PPS mode, default is BPS mode	-
R5	CIR	CIR - Commit Information Rate.	On BPS mode, the range is 0-100,000,000 kbps; On PPS mode, the range is 0-148,809,523 kbps.
R6	CBS	CBS - Commit Burst Size.	On BPS mode, the range is 0-640,000 bytes, default value is 640000; On PPS mode, the range is 0-7,600 packets, default value is 4400.
R7	EIR	EIR - Excess Information Rate. When eir is not set, use RFC 2697. When eir is set, use RFC 4115.	On BPS mode, the range is 0-100,000,000 kbps; On PPS mode, the range is 0-148,809,523 kbps.
R8	EBS	EBS - Excess Burst Size.	On BPS mode, the range is 0-640,000 bytes, default value is 640000; On PPS mode, the range is 0-7,600 packets, default value is 4400.
R9	conform	The action when the traffic not exceed C bucket. The default action is transmit	-
R10	exceed	On single bucket mode, is the action when the traffic exceed C bucket.The default action is drop. On double bucket mode, is the action when the traffic exceed C bucket and not exceed E bucket, the default action is transmit	-
R11	violate	On single bucekt mode, not support this action. On double bucket mode, is the action when the traffic exceed E bucket, the default action is drop.	-
R12	transmit	transmit the packet	-
R13	drop	drop the packet	-
R14	set-traffic-class CLASS-ID	set traffic-class for the packet	range 0-7
R15	statistics	enable policer statistics	-

[P26371|Normal] Use this command to create an aggregate policer instance. The aggregate policer can be shared by multiple classes of traffic. To remove the aggregate policer instance, use the no form of this command.
[P26372|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P26373|Normal] qos aggregate-policer NAME { color-blind | color-aware } cir CIR [ cbs CBS ] [ eir EBS ] [ ebs EBS ] [ conform { transmit [ set-traffic-class CLASS-ID ] | drop } | exceed { transmit [ set-traffic-class CLASS-ID ] | drop } | violate { transmit [ set-traffic-class CLASS-ID ] | drop } ] [ statistics ]
[P26374|Body Text] qos aggregate-policer NAME pps { color-blind | color-aware } cir CIR [ cbs CBS ] [ eir EBS ] [ ebs EBS ] [ conform { transmit [ set-traffic-class CLASS-ID ] | drop } | exceed { transmit [ set-traffic-class CLASS-ID ] | drop } | violate { transmit [ set-traffic-class CLASS-ID ] | drop } ] [ statistics ]
[P26375|Body Text] no qos aggregate-policer NAME

[TABLE 1014] rows=16 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	NAME	Specify an aggregate-policer name	The name can be a maximum of 40 characters. The name is case sensitive and can only contain alphanumeric characters, hyphens, and underscores.
R3	color-blind	Do not care input packet’s color	-
R4	color-aware	Care input packet’s color	-
R5	pps	PPS mode, default is BPS mode	-
R6	CIR	CIR - Commit Information Rate.	On BPS mode, the range is 0-100,000,000 kbps; On PPS mode, the range is 0-148,809,523 kbps.
R7	CBS	CBS - Commit Burst Size.	On BPS mode, the range is 0-640,000 bytes, default value is 640000; On PPS mode, the range is 0-7,600 packets, default value is 4400.
R8	EIR	EIR - Excess Information Rate. When eir is not set, use RFC 2697. When eir is set, use RFC 4115.	On BPS mode, the range is 0-100,000,000 kbps; On PPS mode, the range is 0-148,809,523 kbps.
R9	EBS	EBS - Excess Burst Size.	On BPS mode, the range is 0-640,000 bytes, default value is 640000; On PPS mode, the range is 0-7,600 packets, default value is 4400.
R10	conform	The action when the traffic not exceed C bucket. The default action is transmit	-
R11	exceed	On single bucket mode, is the action when the traffic exceed C bucket.The default action is drop. On double bucket mode, is the action when the traffic exceed C bucket and not exceed E bucket, the default action is transmit	-
R12	violate	On single bucekt mode, not support this action. On double bucket mode, is the action when the traffic exceed E bucket, the default action is drop.	-
R13	transmit	transmit the packet	-
R14	drop	drop the packet	-
R15	set-traffic-class CLASS-ID	set traffic-class for the packet	range 0-7
R16	statistics	enable policer statistics	-

[P26516|Body Text] 1 1/64 ~1.5%

[P26522|Body Text] 7 1 50%
[P26523|Body Text] 8 2 ~66%
[P26524|Body Text] 9 4 ~80%
[P26525|Body Text] 10 8 ~89%

[P27328|Heading 3] qos aggregate-policer
[P27329|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P27330|Normal] Use this command to create an aggregate policer instance. The aggregate policer can be shared by multiple classes of traffic. To remove the aggregate policer instance, use the no form of this command.
[P27331|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P27332|Normal] qos aggregate-policer NAME mode rfc2697 ( color-blind | color-aware | ) cir CIR-RATE ( cbs CBS-SIZE | ) ( ebs EBS-SIZE | ) ( drop-color COLOR | ) ( use-l3-length | ) ) ( stats | )
[P27333|Body Text] qos aggregate-policer NAME mode rfc2698 ( color-blind | color-aware | ) cir CIR-RATE ( cbs CBS-SIZE | ) ( pir PIR-RATE ( pbs PBS-SIZE | ) ) ( drop-color COLOR | ) ( use-l3-length | ) ) ( stats | )
[P27334|Body Text] qos aggregate-policer NAME mode ( rfc4115 | bwp ) ( color-blind | color-aware | ) cir CIR-RATE ( cbs CBS-SIZE | ) ( eir PIR-RATE ( ebs PBS-SIZE | ) ) ( drop-color COLOR | ) ( use-l3-length | ) ) ( stats | )
[P27335|Body Text] no qos aggregate-policer NAME

[TABLE 1069] rows=14 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	NAME	Specify an aggregate-policer name	The name can be a maximum of 40 characters. The name is case sensitive and can only contain alphanumeric characters, hyphens, and underscores.
R3	mode	Use rfc2697, rfc2698, rfc4115 or bwp mode	-
R4	color-blind	Color blind mode policer	-
R5	color-aware	Color aware mode policer	-
R6	cir CIR-RATE	CIR - Commit Information Rate	0 to 10,000,000 kbps
R7	cbs CBS-SIZE	CBS - Commit Burst Size	0 to 128,000 bytes
R8	eir EIR-RATE	EIR-Excess Information Rate	0 to 10,000,000 kbps
R9	ebs EBS-SIZE	EBS - Excess Burst Size with the range of 0 to 128,000 bytes	0 to 128,000 bytes
R10	pir PIR-RATE	PIR - Peak Information Rate	0 to 10,000,000 kbps
R11	pbs PBS-SIZE	PBS - Peak Burst Size	0 to 128,000 bytes
R12	drop-color COLOR	drop color configuration includes yellow and red	yellow/red
R13	use-l3-length	Use l3 length for policing	-
R14	stats	enable policer statistics	-

[P27336|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P27337|Normal] Global Configuration
[P27338|Heading 4] Default
[P27339|Normal] Disabled
[P27340|Heading 4] Usage
[P27341|Normal] This command is used to create aggregate-policer instance. Color-blind or Color-aware, SRTCM or TRTCM can be configured.
[P27342|Body Text] The max number of aggregate policer and flow policer, which is configured in policy-map, is 128 per line-card.
[P27343|Body Text] If policer with statistics is configured, and stats are entered when the policer is created, policer statistics is working.
[P27344|Body Text] The statistics cannot be modified after the policer is created.
[P27345|Heading 4] Examples
[P27346|Normal] This example shows how to create an aggregate-policer named agg_plc for SRTCM mode:
[P27347|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# qos aggregate-policer agg_plc mode rfc2697 color-aware cir 10000 cbs 128000 ebs 128000 drop-color red
[P27348|Normal] Remove aggregate-policer:
[P27349|Terminal Display] Switch(config)# no qos aggregate-policer agg_plc

[P27354|Heading 3] service-policy
[P27355|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P27356|Normal] Use this command to apply a policy-map to member interfaces (member vlan) of the port group (vlan group) to affect the traffic classification rules. To remove the policy-map from the port group (vlan group), use the no form of this command.
[P27357|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P27358|Normal] service-policy ( input | output ) NAME
[P27359|Body Text] no service-policy ( input | output )

[TABLE 1070] rows=4 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	NAME	the policy-map name	The name can be a maximum of 40 characters. The name is case sensitive and can only contain alphanumeric characters, hyphens, and underscores.
R3	input	apply policy-map to the inbound of member interfaces (member vlan)	-
R4	output	apply policy-map to the outbound of member interfaces (member vlan)	-

[P27360|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P27361|Normal] Port-group Configuration
[P27362|Body Text] Vlan-group Configuration
[P27363|Heading 4] Default
[P27364|Normal] None
[P27365|Heading 4] Usage
[P27366|Normal] Use this command to apply a policy map defined by the policy-map command to the input or output of member interfaces (member vlan) of the port group (vlan group).
[P27367|Body Text] If the interface (vlan) has already been applied a policy-map， it cannot be added to the port group (vlan group).
[P27368|Heading 4] Examples
[P27369|Normal] Configure a policy to ingress of member interfaces of the port group :
[P27370|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# port-group port_group_1
Switch(config-port-group)# service-policy input plc_map1
[P27371|Normal] Remove a policy from ingress of member interfaces of the port group :
[P27372|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# port-group port_group_1
Switch(config-port-group)# no service-policy input
