[P27396|Heading 3] trust
[P27397|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P27398|Normal] Use this command to configure the port trust state. To return to the default value, use the no form of this command.
[P27399|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P27400|Normal] trust ( dscp | cos ( stag-cos | ctag-cos | ) | port )
[P27401|Body Text] no trust

[TABLE 1072] rows=6 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	dscp	Trust DSCP indicates all incoming IP packets will be assigned with the priority and color according to the packet DSCP field, and for other packets, the priority and color of that packet will be mapped the same as trust CoS.	-
R3	cos	Select which CoS will be specified for interface. The range of CoS is from 0 to 7.	-
R4	ctag-cos	Trust ctag-cos indicates all incoming packets will be assigned with the priority and color according to the packet inner CoS field if the packet is double-tagged. If that packet is carried with only one VLAN tag or it is untagged, the behavior should be the same as that of trust port.	-
R5	stag-cos	Trust stagc-cos indicates all incoming packets will be assigned with the priority and color according to the packet outer CoS field if the packet is double-tagged. If that packet is carried with only one VLAN tag or it is untagged, the behavior should be the same as that of trust CoS.	-
R6	port	Trust port indicates all incoming packets will be assigned with the priority and color according to the port CoS value.	-

[P27402|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P27403|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P27404|Heading 4] Default
[P27405|Normal] Trust the CoS value in packets.
[P27406|Heading 4] Usage
[P27407|Normal] The port trust state is the criteria for classifying incoming packets from the port. All classified packets will be indentified with a priority and color according to the trust state. The default port trust state is trust cos.
[P27408|Heading 4] Examples
[P27409|Normal] This example shows how to configure the trust state:
[P27410|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal 
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# trust dscp

[P27506|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P27507|Normal] Use this command to set the maximum of secure dynamic MAC addresses on a port. Use the no switchport port-security maximum command to return to the default settings.
[P27508|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P27509|Normal] switchport port-security maximum MAXIMUM
[P27510|Body Text] no switchport port-security maximum

[TABLE 1076] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	MAXIMUM	Maximum number of secure MAC addresses for the interface	0-16384

[P27511|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P27512|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P27513|Heading 4] Default
[P27514|Normal] 1
[P27515|Heading 4] Usage
[P27516|Normal] If the new maximum is smaller than the current secure addresses on the interface, the configuration is rejected.
[P27517|Body Text] Once the secure dynamic MAC address number on the port reached the maximum number, no more address can be learnt on that port.
[P27518|Body Text] The maximum number 0 indicates that no dynamic secure MAC is allowed, only static secure MAC is supported.
[P27519|Heading 4] Examples
[P27520|Normal] This example sets the maximum number of secure dynamic MAC addresses on a port:
[P27521|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# switchport port-security maximum 1024
[P27522|Normal] This example restores the maximum number of secure dynamic MAC addresses on a port to default value:
[P27523|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# no switchport port-security maximum

[P27750|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P27751|Normal] Use this command to create MAC ACL and then enter MAC ACL in global configuration mode. Use no mac access-list command to delete the MAC ACL.
[P27752|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P27753|Normal] mac access-list ACL_NAME
[P27754|Body Text] no mac access-list ACL_NAME

[P27755|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P27756|Normal] Global Configuration
[P27757|Heading 4] Default
[P27758|Normal] None
[P27759|Heading 4] Usage
[P27760|Normal] If the system already has a MAC ACL with the same name, this command will enter the MAC ACL configuration mode. However, if the ACL name is used by other type of ACL, a prompt message will be shown.
[P27761|Body Text] When the name is not used by any ACL, this command is to create the MAC ACL firstly and then enter the MAC ACL configuration mode.
[P27762|Heading 4] Examples
[P27763|Normal] This example shows how to create a MAC ACL named list_mac_1 and then enter the MAC ACL configuration mode:
[P27764|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# mac access-list list_mac_1
Switch(config-mac-acl)#
[P27765|Normal] This example shows how to remove the MAC ACL named list_mac_1:
[P27766|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# no mac access-list list_mac_1

[P27797|Heading 3] deny src-mac
[P27798|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P27799|Normal] Use this command to create a MAC filter for discarding ongoing packets matching the filter rule.
[P27800|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P27801|Normal] ( SEQUENCE_NUM | ) deny src-mac ( any | MAC_ADDR MAC_ADDR_MASK | host MAC_ADDR ) ( dest-mac ( any | MAC_ADDR MAC_ADDR_MASK | host MAC_ADDR ) | ) ( untag-vlan | ( ( vlan VLAN_ID | ) ( cos COS | ) ( inner-vlan INNER_VLAN | ) ( inner-cos INNER_COS | ) ) ( protocol ( arp ( arp-op-code ) | rarp | ETH_TYPE mask ETH_TYPE_MASK ) | packet-length OPERATOR LENGTH | ) ( TIME_RANGE_NAME | )

[TABLE 1092] rows=20 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	SEQUENCE_NUM	The sequence number of the filter in MAC ACL. An auto-generated sequence number will be assigned to the filter if this field is not presented.	1-131071
R3	any	Any host	-
R4	MAC_ADDR MAC_ADDR_MASK	The MAC address and its wildcard bits	MAC and wildcard in HHHH.HHHH.HHHH format
R5	host MAC_ADDR	The host with a specified MAC address	MAC address in HHHH.HHHH.HHHH format
R6	dest-mac	Destination MAC address	-
R7	untag-vlan	Without vlan tag	-
R8	VLAN_ID	VLAN-ID	1-4094
R9	COS	CoS Value	0-7
R10	INNER_VLAN	Inner VLAN-ID	1-4094
R11	INNER_COS	Inner CoS value	0-7
R12	protocol	The protocol type which including ARP, RARP or Ether type	-
R13	arp	ARP protocol	-
R14	arp-op-code	arp-op-code	0-65535
R15	rarp	RARP protocol	-
R16	ETH_TYPE	Ether type	0-0xFFFF
R17	ETH_TYPE_MASK	Ether type mask	0-0xFFFF
R18	TIME_RANGE_NAME	The time-range used by the MAC filter	A string with up to 40 characters
R19	OPERATOR	Packet length,operator including eq (equal to), lt (less than), gt (greater than), and range	eq (equal to), lt (less than), gt (greater than), and range
R20	LENGTH	The length value	64-16382

[P27802|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P27803|Normal] MAC ACL Configuration
[P27804|Heading 4] Default
[P27805|Normal] None
[P27806|Heading 4] Usage
[P27807|Normal] An auto-generated sequence number will be assigned to the filter if the sequence-num field is not presented. The auto-generated sequence number is incremented by 10 on the maximum existing sequence number in the MAC ACL. i.e. when the maximum existing sequence number is 100, the sequence number of subsequent created MAC filter is 110. Eth-type is not supported in egress ACL.
[P27808|Heading 4] Examples
[P27809|Normal] This example shows how to create a filter in MAC ACL to deny the packets with source MAC address 001A.A02C.A1DF:
[P27810|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# mac access-list list_mac_1
Switch(config-mac-acl)# 1 deny src-mac host 001A.A02C.A1DF
[P27811|Normal] This example shows how to create a filter in MAC ACL to deny all the packets:
[P27812|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# mac access-list list_mac_1
Switch(config-mac-acl)# 2 deny src-mac any
[P27813|Normal] This example shows how to create a filter in MAC ACL to deny the packet whose source MAC address is between the ranges specified:
[P27814|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# mac access-list list_mac_1
Switch(config-mac-acl)# 3 deny src-mac 001A.A02C.A1DF 001A.A02C.0000
[P27815|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P27816|Normal] no sequence-num

[P27822|Heading 4] Command Mode

[P27824|Heading 4] Default

[P27827|Normal] An auto-generated sequence number will be assigned to the filter if the sequence-num field is not presented. The auto-generated sequence number is incremented by 10 on the maximum existing sequence number in the MAC ACL. i.e. when the maximum existing sequence number is 105, the sequence number of subsequent created MAC filter is 115. Eth-type is not supported in egress ACL.

Switch(config-mac-acl)# 2 permit src-mac any

[P27900|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P27901|Normal] IP ACL Configuration
[P27902|Heading 4] Default
[P27903|Normal] None
[P27904|Heading 4] Usage
[P27905|Normal] If IP address wildcard bit is provided, the IP address is logical-and in bitwise with the reverse bits of the wildcard bits. For example, 10.10.10.0 0.0.0.255 means the addresses from 10.10.10.0 to 10.10.10.255 are matched.
[P27906|Body Text] An auto-generated sequence number will be assigned to the filter if the sequence-num field is not presented. The auto-generated sequence number is incremented by 10 on the maximum existing sequence number in the IP ACL. i.e. when the maximum existing sequence number is 100, the sequence number of subsequent created IP filter is 110.
[P27907|Heading 4] Examples
[P27908|Normal] This example shows how to create a filter in IP ACL to deny any IP packets:
[P27909|Body Text] This example shows how to create a filter in IP ACL to deny the fragment packets with the source IP addresss 1.1.1.1:
[P27910|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ip access-list list_ipv4_1
Switch(config-ip-acl)# 2 deny any host 1.1.1.1 any fragments
[P27911|Normal] This example shows how to create a filter in IP ACL to deny any routed packets:
[P27912|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ip access-list list_ipv4_1
Switch(config-ip-acl)# 3 deny any any any routed-packet

[P27920|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P27921|Normal] IP ACL Configuration
[P27922|Heading 4] Default
[P27923|Normal] None
[P27924|Heading 4] Usage
[P27925|Normal] The fragments will be invalid when the layer 4 information is specified (i.e. src-port).
[P27926|Heading 4] Examples
[P27927|Normal] This example shows how to create a filter in IP ACL to deny any TCP packets:
[P27928|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ip access-list list_ipv4_1
Switch(config-ip-acl)# 1 deny tcp any any
[P27929|Normal] This example shows how to create a filter in IP ACL to deny the TCP packets with the source IP address 1.1.1.1, source port 0-100:
[P27930|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ip access-list list_ipv4_1
Switch(config-ip-acl)# 2 deny tcp host 1.1.1.1 src-port range 0 100 any
[P27931|Normal] This example shows how to create a filter in IP ACL to deny any TCP packets in established TCP streams:
[P27932|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ip access-list list_ipv4_1
Switch(config-ip-acl)# 3 deny tcp any any established
[P27933|Normal] This example shows how to create a filer in IP ACL to deny the TCP ACK packets with the source IP address 1.1.1.1:
[P27934|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ip access-list list_ipv4_1
Switch(config-ip-acl)# 4 deny tcp 10.10.10.0 0.0.0.0 any match-any ack

[P28034|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P28035|Normal] IP ACL Configuration
[P28036|Heading 4] Default
[P28037|Normal] None
[P28038|Heading 4] Usage
[P28039|Normal] If IP address wildcard bits are provided, the IP address is logical-and in bitwise with the reverse bits of the wildcard bits. For example, 10.10.10.0 0.0.0.255 means the addresses from 10.10.10.0 to 10.10.10.255 are matched.
[P28040|Body Text] An auto-generated sequence number will be assigned to the filter if the sequence-num field is not presented. The auto-generated sequence number is incremented by 10 on the maximum existing sequence number in the IP ACL. i.e. when the maximum existing sequence number is 105, the sequence number of subsequent created IP filter is 115.
[P28041|Heading 4] Examples
[P28042|Normal] This example shows how to create a filter in IP ACL to permit any IP packets:
[P28043|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ip access-list list_ipv4_1
Switch(config-ip-acl)# 2 deny gre host 1.1.1.1 any vsid 10 mask 0xffffff

[P28051|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P28052|Normal] IP ACL Configuration
[P28053|Heading 4] Default
[P28054|Normal] None
[P28055|Heading 4] Usage
[P28056|Normal] The fragments will be invalid when the layer 4 information is specified (i.e. src-port).
[P28057|Heading 4] Examples
[P28058|Normal] This example shows how to create a filter in IP ACL to permit any TCP packets:
[P28059|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ip access-list list_ipv4_1
Switch(config-ip-acl)#  10 permit any any any
[P28060|Normal] This example shows how to create a filter in IP ACL to permit the TCP packets with the source IP address 1.1.1.1, and source port ranges from 0 to 100:
[P28061|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config-ex-ip-acl)# 20 permit tcp host 1.1.1.1 any non-first-fragments
[P28062|Normal] This example shows how to create a filter in IP ACL to permit any TCP packets in established TCP streams:
[P28063|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ip access-list list_ipv4_1
Switch(config-ip-acl)# 30 permit any any any routed-packet
[P28064|Normal] This example shows how to create a filter in IP ACL to permit the TCP ACK packets with the source IP address 10.10.10.0:
[P28065|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ip access-list list_ipv4_1
Switch(config-ip-acl)# 4 permit tcp 10.10.10.0 0.0.0.0 any match-any ack

[P28080|Normal] This example shows how to create a filter in IP ACL to deny any UDP packets:

[P28187|Normal] If the system already has a UDF ACL with the same name, this command will enter the UDF ACL configuration mode. However, if the ACL name is used by other type of ACL, a prompt message will be shown.
[P28188|Body Text] When the name is not used by any ACL, this command is to create the UDF ACL firstly and then enter the UDF ACL configuration mode.
[P28189|Heading 4] Examples
[P28190|Normal] This example shows how to create a UDF ACL named list_udf_1 and then enter the UDF ACL configuration mode:
[P28191|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# user-define access-list list_udf_1
Switch(config-udf-acl)#
[P28192|Normal] This example shows how to remove the UDF ACL named list_udf_1:
[P28193|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# no user-define access-list list_udf_1

[P28305|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P28306|Normal] Extend IP ACL Configuration
[P28307|Heading 4] Default
[P28308|Normal] None
[P28309|Heading 4] Usage
[P28310|Normal] An auto-generated sequence number will be assigned to the filter if the sequence-num field is not presented. The auto-generated sequence number is incremented by 10 on the maximum existing sequence number in the extend IP ACL. i.e. when the maximum existing sequence number is 100, the sequence number of subsequent created MAC filter is 110.
[P28311|Heading 4] Examples
[P28312|Normal] This example shows how to create a filter in extend IP ACL to deny the packets with source MAC address 001A.A02C.A1DF:
[P28313|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ip access-list list_ipv4_1 extend
Switch(config-ex-ip-acl)# 1 deny src-mac host 001A.A02C.A1DF
[P28314|Normal] This example shows how to create a filter in extend IP ACL to deny all the packets:
[P28315|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ip access-list list_ipv4_1 extend
Switch(config-ex-ip-acl)# 2 deny src-mac any
[P28316|Normal] This example shows how to create a filter in extend IP ACL to deny the packet whose source MAC address is between the ranges specified:
[P28317|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ip access-list list_ipv4_1 extend
Switch(config-ex-ip-acl)# 3 deny src-mac 001A.A02C.A1DF 001A.A02C.0000

[P28345|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P28346|Normal] Extend IP ACL Configuration
[P28347|Heading 4] Default
[P28348|Normal] None
[P28349|Heading 4] Usage
[P28350|Normal] If an IP address wildcard bit is provided, the IP address is logically-anded in bitwise with the reverse bits of the wildcard bits. For example, 10.10.10.0 0.0.0.255 means the addresses from 10.10.10.0 to 10.10.10.255 are matched.
[P28351|Body Text] An auto-generated sequence number will be assigned to the filter if the sequence-num field is not presented. The auto-generated sequence number is incremented by 10 on the maximum existing sequence number in the extend IP ACL. i.e. when the maximum existing sequence number is 100, the sequence number of subsequent created IP filter is 110.
[P28352|Heading 4] Examples
[P28353|Normal] This example shows how to create a filter in extend IP ACL to deny any IP packets:
[P28354|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ip access-list list_ipv4_1 extend
Switch(config-ex-ip-acll)# 1 deny any any any
[P28355|Normal] This example shows how to create a filter in extend IP ACL to deny the fragment packets with the source IP addresss 1.1.1.1:
[P28356|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ip access-list list_ipv4_1 extend
Switch(config-ex-ip-acll)# 2 deny any host 1.1.1.1 any fragments
[P28357|Normal] This example shows how to create a filter in extend IP ACL to deny any routed packets:
[P28358|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ip access-list list_ipv4_1 extend
Switch(config-ex-ip-acll)# 3 deny any any any routed-packet

[P28366|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P28367|Normal] Extend IP ACL Configuration
[P28368|Heading 4] Default
[P28369|Normal] None
[P28370|Heading 4] Usage
[P28371|Normal] The fragments will be invalid when the layer 4 information is specified (i.e. src-port).
[P28372|Heading 4] Examples
[P28373|Normal] This example shows how to create a filter in extend IP ACL to deny any TCP packets:
[P28374|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ip access-list list_ipv4_1 extend
Switch(config-ex-ip-acl)# 1 deny tcp any any
[P28375|Normal] This example shows how to create a filter in extend IP ACL to deny the TCP packets with the source IP address 1.1.1.1, source port 0-100:
[P28376|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ip access-list list_ipv4_1 extend
Switch(config-ex-ip-acl)# 2 deny tcp host 1.1.1.1 src-port range 0 100 any
[P28377|Normal] This example shows how to create a filter in extend IP ACL to deny any TCP packets in established TCP streams:
[P28378|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ip access-list list_ipv4_1 extend
Switch(config-ex-ip-acl)# 3 deny tcp any any established
[P28379|Normal] This example shows how to create a filer in extend IP ACL to deny the TCP ACK packets with the source IP address 10.10.10.10:
[P28380|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ip access-list list_ipv4_1 extend
Switch(config-ex-ip-acl)# 4 deny tcp 10.10.10.0 0.0.0.0 any match-any ack

[P28478|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P28479|Normal] Extend IP ACL Configuration
[P28480|Heading 4] Default
[P28481|Normal] None
[P28482|Heading 4] Usage
[P28483|Normal] If an IP address wildcard bit is provided, the IP address is logically-anded in bitwise with the reverse bits of the wildcard bits. For example, 10.10.10.0 0.0.0.255 means the addresses from 10.10.10.0 to 10.10.10.255 are matched.
[P28484|Body Text] An auto-generated sequence number will be assigned to the filter if the sequence-num field is not presented. The auto-generated sequence number is incremented by 10 on the maximum existing sequence number in the extend IP ACL. i.e. when the maximum existing sequence number is 105, the sequence number of subsequent created IP filter is 115.
[P28485|Heading 4] Examples
[P28486|Normal] This example shows how to create a filter in extend IP ACL to deny any NVGRE packets:
[P28487|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ip access-list list_ipv4_1 extend
Switch(config-ex-ip-acl)# 1 deny nvgre any any vsid 0 mask 0
[P28488|Normal] This example shows how to create a filter in extend IP ACL to deny the NVGRE packets with the source IP address 1.1.1.1, any destination IP address and the nvgre vsid is 10:
[P28489|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ip access-list list_ipv4_1 extend
Switch(config-ex-ip-acl)# 2 deny gre host 1.1.1.1 any vsid 10 mask 0xffffff
[P28490|Normal] This example shows how to create a filter in extend IP ACL to permit any routed packets:
[P28491|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ip access-list list_ipv4_1 extend
Switch(config-ex-ip-acl)# 30 permit any any any routed-packet

[P28521|Heading 4] Command Mode

[P28523|Heading 4] Default
[P28524|Normal] None
[P28525|Heading 4] Usage
[P28526|Normal] The fragments will be invalid when the layer 4 information is specified (i.e. src-port).

[P28528|Normal] This example shows how to create a filter in extend IP ACL to deny any UDP packets:
[P28529|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal

Switch(config-ex-ip-acll)# 1 permit udp any any

[P28531|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ip access-list list_ipv4_1 extend
Switch(config-ex-ip-acll)# 2 permit udp host 1.1.1.1 src-port eq 10 any dst-port lt 2000

[P28649|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P28650|Normal] Global Configuration
[P28651|Heading 4] Default
[P28652|Normal] None
[P28653|Heading 4] Usage
[P28654|Normal] If the system already has an IPv6 ACL with the same name, this command will enter the IPv6 ACL configuration mode. However, if the ACL name is used by other type of ACL, a prompt message will be shown.
[P28655|Body Text] When the name is not used by any ACL, this command is to create the IPv6 ACL firstly and then enter the IPv6 ACL configuration mode.
[P28656|Heading 4] Examples
[P28657|Normal] This example shows how to create an IPv6 ACL named list_ipv6_1 and then enter the IPv6 ACL configuration mode:
[P28658|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ipv6 access-list list_ipv6_1
Switch(config-ipv6-acl)#
[P28659|Normal] This example shows how to remove the IPv6 ACL named list_ipv6_1:
[P28660|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# no ipv6 access-list list_ipv6_1

[P28711|Heading 4] Command Mode

[P28713|Heading 4] Default
[P28714|Normal] None
[P28715|Heading 4] Usage
[P28716|Normal] An auto-generated sequence number will be assigned to the filter if the sequence-num field is not presented. The auto-generated sequence number is incremented by 10 on the maximum existing sequence number in the IPv6 ACL. For example, when the maximum existing sequence number is 100, the sequence number of subsequent created IPv6 filter is 110.
[P28717|Heading 4] Examples
[P28718|Normal] This example shows how to create a filter in IPv6 ACL to deny any IPv6 packets:
[P28719|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ipv6 access-list list_ipv6_1
Switch(config-ipv6-acl)# 1 deny any any any
[P28720|Normal] This example shows how to create a filter in IPv6 ACL to deny any routed packets:
[P28721|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ipv6 access-list list_ipv6_1
Switch(config-ipv6-acl)# 2 deny any any any routed-packet
[P28722|Heading 4] Related Commands

[P28854|Normal] None

[P28856|Normal] This example shows how to create a filter in IPv6 ACL to permit any UDP packets:

Switch(config-ipv6-acl)# 1 permit udp any any
[P28858|Normal] This example shows how to create a filter in IPv6 ACL to permit the UDP packets with the source IPv6 address 2001::2020, source port 8080:

Switch(config)# ipv6 access-list list_ipv6_1
Switch(config-ipv6-acl)# 2 permit udp host 2001::2020 src-port eq 8080 any

[P28946|Normal] This example shows how to remove the port group named list_mac_1:

[P29696|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P29697|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P29698|Heading 4] Default
[P29699|Normal] The default value of dot1x max-reauth-req is 2 times.
[P29700|Heading 4] Usage
[P29701|Normal] You should change the default value of this command only to adjust for unusual circumstances such as unreliable links or specific behavioral problems with certain clients and authentication servers.

[P29707|Heading 3] dot1x port-control
[P29708|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P29709|Normal] Use the dot1x port-control interface configuration command on the switch to enable manual control of the authorization state of the port. Use the no form of this command to return to the default setting.
[P29710|Body Text] Support config dot1x in routed port, while can’t config it in a logical port such as agg, and so on.
[P29711|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P29712|Normal] dot1x port-control ( auto | force-authorized | force-unauthorized | dir ( both | in ) )
[P29713|Body Text] no dot1x port-control

[TABLE 1190] rows=7 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	auto	Enable IEEE 802.1x authentication on the port and cause the port to change to the authorized or unauthorized state based on the IEEE 802.1x authentication exchange between the switch and the client	-
R3	force-authorized	Disable IEEE 802.1x authentication on the port and cause the port to transition to the authorized state without an authentication exchange. The port sends and receives normal traffic without IEEE 802.1x-based authentication of the client	-
R4	force-unauthorized	Deny all access through this port by forcing the port to change to the unauthorized state, ignoring all attempts by the client to authenticate. The switch cannot provide authentication services to the client through the port	-
R5	dir	Specify the dot1x control direction	-
R6	both	Discard received and transmitted packets	-
R7	in	Discard received packets only	-

[P29714|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P29715|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P29716|Heading 4] Default
[P29717|Normal] Dot1x port control is disabled by default.
[P29718|Body Text] The default value of the control direction is “in”.
[P29719|Heading 4] Usage
[P29720|Normal] You must globally enable IEEE 802.1x authentication on the switch by using the dot1x system-auth-control global configuration command before enabling IEEE 802.1x authentication on a specific port.
[P29721|Heading 4] Examples
[P29722|Normal] The following is sample output from the dot1x port-control command:
[P29723|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# dot1x port-control auto
[P29724|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P29725|Normal] show dot1x

[P29749|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P29750|Normal] Interface Configuration

[P29753|Heading 4] Usage

[P29815|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P29816|Normal] Use the dot1x re-authenticate privileged EXEC command on the switch stack to manually initiate a re-authentication of the specified IEEE 802.1x-enabled port.
[P29817|Heading 4] Command Syntax

[P29819|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P29820|Normal] Privileged EXEC
[P29821|Heading 4] Default
[P29822|Normal] None
[P29823|Heading 4] Usage
[P29824|Normal] You can use this command to re-authenticate a client without waiting for the configured number of seconds between re-authentication attempts (re-authperiod) and automatic re-authentication.

[P29830|Heading 3] dot1x timeout
[P29831|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P29832|Normal] Use the dot1x timeout interface configuration command on the switch stack or on a standalone switch to set IEEE 802.1x timers. Use the no form of this command to return to the default setting.
[P29833|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P29834|Normal] dot1x timeout ( re-authperiod SECONDS | server-timeout SECONDS | supp-timeout SECONDS | tx-period SECONDS )
[P29835|Body Text] no dot1x timeout ( reauth-period | server-timeout | supp-timeout | tx-period )

[TABLE 1195] rows=5 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	re-authperiod SECONDS	Set the number of seconds between reauthentication attempts.	60-65535 seconds
R3	server-timeout SECONDS	Number of seconds that the switch waits for the retransmission of packets by the switch to the authentication server.	1-65535 seconds
R4	supp-timeout SECONDS	Number of seconds that the switch waits for the retransmission of packets by the switch to the IEEE 802.1x client.	1-65535 seconds
R5	tx-period SECONDS	Number of seconds that the switch waits for a response to an EAP-request/identity frame from the client before retransmitting the request.	1-65535 seconds

[P29836|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P29837|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P29838|Heading 4] Default
[P29839|Normal] None
[P29840|Heading 4] Usage
[P29841|Normal] You should change the default value of this command only to adjust for unusual circumstances such as unreliable links or specific behavioral problems with certain clients and authentication servers.
[P29842|Body Text] The dot1x timeout re-authperiod interface configuration command affects the behavior of the switch only if you have enabled periodic re-authentication by using the dot1x reauthentication interface configuration command.
[P29843|Body Text] The default value of re-authperiod is 3600 seconds.
[P29844|Body Text] The default value of tx-period is 30 seconds.
[P29845|Body Text] The default value of supp-timeout is 30 seconds.
[P29846|Body Text] The default value of server-timeout is 30 seconds.
[P29847|Heading 4] Examples
[P29848|Normal] The following is sample output from the dot1x timeout command:
[P29849|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# dot1x reauthentication
Switch(config-if)# dot1x timeout reauth-period 4000
[P29850|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P29851|Normal] dot1x reauthentication
[P29852|Body Text] show dot1x
[P29853|Heading 3] dot1x guest-vlan
[P29854|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P29855|Normal] Use the dot1x guest-vlan interface configuration command to specify an active VLAN as an 802.1x guest VLAN. Use the no form of this command to return to the default setting.
[P29856|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P29857|Normal] dot1x guest-vlan VLAN_ID
[P29858|Body Text] no dot1x guest-vlan

[TABLE 1196] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	VLAN_ID	Specify an active VLAN as an 802.1x guest VLAN.	2-4094

[P29859|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P29860|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P29861|Heading 4] Default
[P29862|Normal] No guest VLAN is configured.
[P29863|Heading 4] Usage
[P29864|Normal] When you configure a guest VLAN, clients that are not 802.1x-capable are put into the guest VLAN when the server does not receive a response to its Extensible Authentication Protocol over LAN (EAPOL) request/identity frame. Clients that are 802.1x-capable but fail authentication are not granted access to the network.
[P29865|Body Text] The guest VLAN feature is not supported on internal VLANs (routed ports) or trunk ports; it is supported only on access ports
[P29866|Heading 4] Examples
[P29867|Normal] This example shows how to specify VLAN 5 as an 802.1x guest VLAN:
[P29868|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)#vlan database
Switch(config-vlan)#vlan 5
Switch(config-vlan)#exit
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)#switchport mode access
Switch(config-if)#dot1x port-control auto
Switch(config-if)#dot1x guest-vlan 5
[P29869|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P29870|Normal] show dot1x
[P29871|Body Text]

[P29912|Heading 4] Command Purpose

[P29915|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P29916|Normal] dot1x port-mode ( port | mac )

[P29918|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P29919|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P29920|Heading 4] Default
[P29921|Normal] By default the mode is port based.
[P29922|Heading 4] Usage
[P29923|Normal] Use the “dot1x port-mode” command to set control mode of the interface.
[P29924|Body Text] Use the no form of this command to restore the default value.
[P29925|Body Text] dot1x port-control must be enabled before set the control mode.
[P29926|Body Text] The control mode cannot be changed if there are users on line.
[P29927|Heading 4] Examples
[P29928|Normal] The following is a sample to use the dot1x port-mode command:
[P29929|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal

[P29931|Normal] dot1x port-control
[P29932|Heading 3] dot1x max-user
[P29933|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P29934|Normal] Use the “dot1x max-user” command to set max user of the interface.
[P29935|Body Text] Use the no form of this command to restore the default value.
[P29936|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P29937|Normal] dot1x max-user COUNT
[P29938|Body Text] no dot1x max-user

[TABLE 1200] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	COUNT	Max user number of the port	1-255

[P29939|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P29940|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P29941|Heading 4] Default
[P29942|Normal] By default the user number is uncontrolled on port. The max number is according to the system hardware profile.
[P29943|Heading 4] Usage
[P29944|Normal] Use the “dot1x max-user” command to set max user of the interface.
[P29945|Body Text] Use the no form of this command to restore the default value.
[P29946|Body Text] dot1x port-control must be enabled before set the max value.
[P29947|Body Text] If there are users online, the set value should be larger than or at least be same as the users count.
[P29948|Body Text] The set value cannot be larger than the hardware resource count.
[P29949|Body Text] This count should limit the number of dot1x mac based user in state “accept” , “reject” and “reauth”, which should use hardware table for forwarding or discarding. The total number of users include “waiting” states should be 2 times as this configuration.
[P29950|Heading 4] Examples
[P29951|Normal] The following is a sample to use the dot1x max-user command:
[P29952|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# dot1x max-user 10

[P29954|Normal] dot1x port-control

[P30053|Heading 4] Command Mode

[P30056|Normal] Disable
[P30057|Heading 4] Usage

[P30061|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal

[P30302|Heading 3] ip arp inspection validate
[P30303|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P30304|Normal] Use this command to enable additional validation on the destination MAC address, the sender and target IP addresses, and the source MAC address.
[P30305|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P30306|Normal] [ no ] ip arp inspection validate ( dst-mac | ip | src-mac )

[TABLE 1217] rows=4 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	dst-mac	Validate destination MAC address	-
R3	ip	Validate IP addresses	-
R4	src-mac	Validate source MAC address	-

[P30307|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P30308|Normal] Global Configuration
[P30309|Heading 4] Default
[P30310|Normal] No default is defined.
[P30311|Heading 4] Usage
[P30312|Normal] For src-mac, check the source MAC address in the Ethernet header against the sender MAC address in the ARP body. This check is performed on both ARP requests and responses. When enabled, packets with different MAC addresses are classified as invalid and are dropped.
[P30313|Body Text] For dst-mac, check the destination MAC address in the Ethernet header against the target MAC address in ARP body. This check is performed for ARP responses. When enabled, packets with different MAC addresses are classified as invalid and are dropped.
[P30314|Body Text] For ip, check the ARP body for invalid and unexpected IP addresses. Addresses include 0.0.0.0, 255.255.255.255, and all IP multicast addresses. Sender IP addresses are checked in all ARP requests and responses, and target IP addresses are checked only in ARP responses.
[P30315|Heading 4] Examples
[P30316|Normal] This example shows how to enable additional validation on the destination MAC address.:
[P30317|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ip arp inspection validate dst-mac

[P30511|Normal] For any DHCP snooping configuration to take effect, you must globally enable DHCP snooping. DHCP snooping is not active until you enable snooping on a VLAN by using the dhcp snooping vlan vlan-id global configuration command.

[P30522|Heading 4] Command Syntax

[P30524|Body Text] no dhcp snooping bindings ( ipv4 IP_ADDR | mac MAC_ADDR | vlan VLAN_ID | interface IFNAME | )

R5	IFNAME	Specify an interface on which to add or delete a binding entry	Support physical and AGG interfaces
R6	expiry SECONDS	Specify the interval (in seconds) after which the binding entry is no longer valid.	0 - 86400

[P30525|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P30526|Normal] Global Configuration
[P30527|Heading 4] Default
[P30528|Normal] No default database is defined.
[P30529|Heading 4] Usage
[P30530|Normal] Use this command when you are testing or debugging the switch.
[P30531|Body Text] In the DHCP snooping binding database, each database entry, also referred to a binding, has an IP address, an associated MAC address, the lease time, the interface to which the binding applies, and the VLAN to which the interface belongs.
[P30532|Body Text] Use the show dhcp snooping binding privileged EXEC command to display the configured bindings.
[P30533|Heading 4] Examples
[P30534|Normal] This example shows how to generate a DHCP binding configuration with an expiration time of 1000 seconds on a port in VLAN 1:
[P30535|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# dhcp snooping binding mac 0001.000c.01ef vlan 1 ipv4 10.10.1.1 interface eth-0-1 expiry 1000

[P30574|Heading 3] dhcp snooping information option
[P30575|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P30576|Normal] Use the dhcp snooping information option global configuration command on the switch to enable DHCP option-82 data insertion. Use the no form of this command to disable DHCP option-82 data insertion.
[P30577|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P30578|Normal] dhcp snooping information option
[P30579|Body Text] no dhcp snooping information option
[P30580|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P30581|Normal] Global Configuration
[P30582|Heading 4] Default
[P30583|Normal] DHCP option-82 data is not inserted.
[P30584|Heading 4] Usage
[P30585|Normal] You must globally enable DHCP snooping by using the dhcp snooping global configuration command for any DHCP snooping configuration to take effect.
[P30586|Body Text] When the option-82 feature is enabled and a switch receives a DHCP request from a host, it adds the option-82 information in the packet. The option-82 information contains the switch MAC address (the remote ID suboption) and the port identifier, vlan-mod-port, from which the packet is received (circuit ID suboption). The switch forwards the DHCP request that includes the option-82 field to the DHCP server.
[P30587|Body Text] When the DHCP server receives the packet, it can use the remote ID, the circuit ID, or both to assign IP addresses and implement policies, such as restricting the number of IP addresses that can be assigned to a single remote ID or a circuit ID. Then the DHCP server echoes the option-82 field in the DHCP reply.
[P30588|Body Text] The DHCP server unicasts send the reply to the switch if the request has been relayed to the server by the switch. When the client and server are on the same subnet, the server broadcasts the reply. The switch inspects the remote ID and possibly the circuit ID fields to verify that it originally inserted the option-82 data. The switch removes the option-82 field and forwards the packet to the switch port that connects to the DHCP host that sent the DHCP request.
[P30589|Heading 4] Examples
[P30590|Normal] This example shows how to enable DHCP option-82 data insertion:
[P30591|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# dhcp snooping information option
[P30592|Normal] You can verify your settings by entering the show dhcp snooping config privileged EXEC command.:
[P30593|Terminal Display] Switch# show dhcp snooping config
dhcp snooping service: enabled
dhcp snooping switch: enabled
Verification of hwaddr field: enabled
Insertion of relay agent information (option 82): enabled
Relay agent information (option 82) on untrusted port: not allowed
dhcp snooping vlan 1
[P30594|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P30595|Normal] show dhcp snooping config
[P30596|Body Text] show dhcp snooping binding
[P30597|Heading 3] dhcp snooping information option allow-untrusted
[P30598|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P30599|Normal] Use the dhcp snooping information option allow-untrusted global configuration command on an aggregation switch to configure it to accept DHCP packets with option-82 information that are received on untrusted ports that might be connected to an edge switch. Use the no form of this command to return to the default setting.
[P30600|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P30601|Normal] dhcp snooping information option allow-untrusted
[P30602|Body Text] no dhcp snooping information option allow-untrusted
[P30603|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P30604|Normal] Global Configuration
[P30605|Heading 4] Default
[P30606|Normal] The switch drops DHCP packets with option-82 information that are received on untrusted ports that might be connected to an edge switch.
[P30607|Heading 4] Usage
[P30608|Normal] You might want an edge switch to which a host is connected to insert DHCP option-82 information at the edge of your network. You might also want to enable DHCP security features, such as DHCP snooping, IP source guard, or dynamic Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) inspection, on an aggregation switch. However, if DHCP snooping is enabled on the aggregation switch, the switch drops packets with option-82 information that are received on an untrusted port and does not learn DHCP snooping bindings for connected devices on a trusted interface.
[P30609|Body Text] If the edge switch to which a host is connected inserts option-82 information and you want to use DHCP snooping on an aggregation switch, enter the dhcp snooping information option allow-untrusted command on the aggregation switch. The aggregation switch can learn the bindings for a host even though the aggregation switch receives DHCP snooping packets on an untrusted port. You can also enable DHCP security features on the aggregation switch. The port on the edge switch to which the aggregation switch is connected must be configured as a trusted port.
[P30610|Heading 4] Examples
[P30611|Normal] This example shows how to configure an access switch to not check the option-82 information in untrusted packets from an edge switch and to accept the packets:
[P30612|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# dhcp snooping information option allow-untrusted
[P30613|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P30614|Normal] show dhcp snooping config
[P30615|Heading 3] dhcp snooping information option allow-untrusted (interface)
[P30616|Heading 4] Command Purpose

Use the no form of this command to return to the default setting.
[P30618|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P30619|Normal] dhcp snooping information option allow-untrusted
[P30620|Body Text] no dhcp snooping information option allow-untrusted
[P30621|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P30622|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P30623|Heading 4] Default
[P30624|Normal] Allow-untrusted is not configured on interface.DHCP packets with Option-82 will be processed according to global configuration.
[P30625|Heading 4] Usage
[P30626|Normal] You might want an edge switch to which a host is connected to insert DHCP option-82 information at the edge of your network. You might also want to enable DHCP security features, such as DHCP snooping, IP source guard, or dynamic Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) inspection, on an aggregation switch. However, if DHCP snooping is enabled on the aggregation switch, the switch drops packets with option-82 information that are received on an untrusted port and does not learn DHCP snooping bindings for connected devices on a trusted interface.
[P30627|Body Text] If the edge switch to which a host is connected inserts option-82 information and you want to use DHCP snooping on an aggregation switch, enter the dhcp snooping information option allow-untrusted command on the aggregation switch. The aggregation switch can learn the bindings for a host even though the aggregation switch receives DHCP snooping packets on an untrusted port. You can also enable DHCP security features on the aggregation switch. The port on the edge switch to which the aggregation switch is connected must be configured as a trusted port.
[P30628|Heading 4] Examples
[P30629|Normal] This example shows how to configure an interface to not check the option-82 information in untrusted packets from an edge switch and to accept the packets:
[P30630|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1 
Switch(config-if)# dhcp snooping information option allow-untrusted

[P30668|Heading 4] Command Purpose

[P30673|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P30674|Normal] Global Configuration
[P30675|Heading 4] Default
[P30676|Normal] The switch verifies the source MAC address in a DHCP packet that is received on untrusted ports matches the client hardware address in the packet.
[P30677|Heading 4] Usage
[P30678|Normal] In a service-provider network, when a switch receives a packet from a DHCP client on an untrusted port, it automatically verifies that the source MAC address and the DHCP client hardware address match. If the addresses match, the switch forwards the packet. If the addresses do not match, the switch drops the packet.
[P30679|Heading 4] Examples
[P30680|Normal] This example shows how to disable the MAC address verification:
[P30681|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# no dhcp snooping verify mac-address
[P30682|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P30683|Normal] show dhcp snooping config
[P30684|Heading 3] dhcp snooping vlan
[P30685|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P30686|Normal] Use the dhcp snooping vlan global configuration command on the switch to enable DHCP snooping on a VLAN. Use the no form of this command to return to the default setting.
[P30687|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P30688|Normal] dhcp snooping vlan VLAN-RANGE
[P30689|Body Text] no dhcp snooping vlan VLAN-RANGE

[TABLE 1229] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	VLAN-RANGE	Specify a VLAN ID or a range of VLANs on which to enable DHCP snooping.	1-4094

[P30690|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P30691|Normal] Global Configuration
[P30692|Heading 4] Default
[P30693|Normal] DHCP snooping is disabled on all VLANs.
[P30694|Heading 4] Usage
[P30695|Normal] You can enter a single VLAN ID identified by VLAN ID number, a series of VLAN IDs separated by commas, a range of VLAN IDs separated by hyphens, or a range of VLAN IDs separated by entering the starting and ending VLAN IDs separated by a space.
[P30696|Body Text] You must first globally enable DHCP snooping before enabling DHCP snooping on a VLAN.
[P30697|Heading 4] Examples
[P30698|Normal] This example shows how to enable DHCP snooping on VLAN 10:
[P30699|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# dhcp snooping vlan 10

[P30860|Body Text] no dhcp snooping database ftp

[P31005|Heading 2] IP Source Guard Commands
[P31006|Heading 3] ip source binding
[P31007|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P31008|Normal] Use the ip source binding global configuration command on the switch to configure static IP source bindings on the switch. Use the no form of this command to delete static bindings.
[P31009|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P31010|Normal] ip source binding mac MAC_ADDR vlan VLAN_ID ip IP_ADDR interface IFNAME
[P31011|Body Text] no ip source binding mac MAC_ADDR vlan VLAN_ID ip IP_ADDR interface IFNAME

[TABLE 1245] rows=5 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	MAC_ADDR	Specify a MAC address	MAC Address
R3	VLAN_ID	Specify a VLAN number	1-4094
R4	IP_ADDR	Specify an IPv4 address	IPv4 Address
R5	IFNAME	Specify an interface on which to add or delete a binding entry	Support physical and aggregation interfaces

[P31012|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P31013|Normal] Global Configuration
[P31014|Heading 4] Default
[P31015|Normal] None
[P31016|Heading 4] Usage
[P31017|Normal] A static IP source binding entry has an IP address, its associated MAC address, and its associated VLAN number.
[P31018|Body Text] The same MAC and IP can only be bound in one binding entry. Duplication of MAC or IP in binding entries is not allowed.
[P31019|Body Text] No IP source bindings are configured by default.
[P31020|Heading 4] Examples
[P31021|Normal] The following is sample output from the ip source binding command:
[P31022|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ip source binding mac 0001.1234.1234 vlan 1 ip 172.20.50.5 interface eth-0-1
[P31023|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P31024|Normal] show ip source binding
[P31025|Body Text] no ip source binding

[P31031|Body Text] no ip source binding mac MAC_ADDR vlan VLAN_ID ipv6 IPV6_ADDR interface IFNAME

[P31087|Heading 4] Command Purpose

[P31089|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P31090|Normal] ip verify source ( ip | ip-mac | ip-vlan | ip-mac-vlan )
[P31091|Body Text] no ip verify source

R2	ip	Check only IP address	-
R3	ip-mac	Check IP address and MAC address	-
R4	ip-vlan	Check IP address and VLAN	-
R5	ip-mac-vlan	Check IP address, MAC address, and VLAN	-

[P31092|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P31093|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P31094|Heading 4] Default
[P31095|Normal] None
[P31096|Heading 4] Usage
[P31097|Normal] When IP source guard is enabled on an access port, the ip-mac-vlan keyword is equivalent to the ip-mac keyword.
[P31098|Body Text] By default, IP source guard is disabled on interfaces.
[P31099|Heading 4] Examples
[P31100|Normal] The following example shows how to enable IP source guard on an interface:
[P31101|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1 
Switch(config-if)# ip verify source ip-mac

[P31470|Heading 2] RADIUS Authentication Commands
[P31471|Heading 3] radius-server deadtime
[P31472|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P31473|Normal] To improve RADIUS response times when some servers might be unavailable and cause the unavailable servers to be skipped immediately, use the radius-server deadtime command in global configuration mode. To set dead-time to default value, use the no form of this command.
[P31474|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P31475|Normal] radius-server deadtime MINUTES
[P31476|Body Text] no radius-server deadtime

[TABLE 1265] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	MINUTES	Length of time, in minutes, for which a RADIUS server is skipped over by transaction requests	1-20 minutes

[P31477|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P31478|Normal] Global Configuration
[P31479|Heading 4] Default
[P31480|Normal] 5 minutes
[P31481|Heading 4] Usage
[P31482|Normal] Use this command to cause the switch to mark as “dead” any RADIUS servers that fail to respond to authentication requests, thus avoiding the wait for the request to time out before trying the next configured server. A RADIUS server marked as “dead” is skipped by additional requests for the duration of minutes, unless there are no servers not marked “dead”.
[P31483|Body Text] The default value of the radius deadtime is 5 minutes.
[P31484|Heading 4] Examples
[P31485|Normal] The following is sample output from the radius deadtime command:
[P31486|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# radius deadtime 10
[P31487|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P31488|Normal] radius-server host
[P31489|Heading 3] radius-server host
[P31490|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P31491|Normal] To specify a RADIUS server host, use the radius-server host command in global configuration mode. To delete the specified RADIUS host, use the no form of this command.
[P31492|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P31493|Normal] radius-server host HOST_IP_ADDR ( source-interface IFNAME | source-ip SRC_IP_ADDR | )
[P31494|Body Text] radius-server host HOST_IP_ADDR { key ( 8 | secret | ) STRING | retransmit RETRIES | timeout SEC | mgmt-if IPV4_ADDR | auth-port AUTH_PORT | acct-port ACCT_PORT } ( source-interface IFNAME | source-ip SRC_IP_ADDR | )
[P31495|Body Text] radius-server host mgmt-if IPV4_ADDR
[P31496|Body Text] radius-server host mgmt-if IPV4_ADDR { key ( 8 | secret | ) STRING | retransmit RETRIES | timeout SEC | mgmt-if IPV4_ADDRauth-port AUTH_PORT }
[P31497|Body Text] no radius-server host ( mgmt-if | ) IPV4_ADDR ( mgmt-if IPV4_ADDRauth-port AUTH_PORT | )

[TABLE 1266] rows=11 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	mgmt-if	Management port	-
R3	IPV4_ADDR	IPv4 address of the RADIUS server host	IPv4 Address
R4	IPV6_ADDR	IPv6 address of the RADIUS server host	-
R5	AUTH_PORT	(Optional) Port number for authentication requests; the host is not used for authentication if set to 0. If unspecified, the port number defaults to 1812	1-65535
R6	ACCT_PORT	(Optional) Port number for accounting requests; the host is not used for accounting if set to 0. If unspecified, the port number defaults to 1813	1-65535
R7	SECONDS	(Optional) Specifies the timeout value.If no timeout value is specified, the global value is used. The default value should be 5	1-1000 seconds
R8	RETRIES	(Optional) Specifies the retransmit value. If no retransmit value is specified, the global value is used. The default value should be 3	1-100
R9	STRING	(Optional) Specifies the authentication and encryption key for all RADIUS communications between the switch and the RADIUS server. This key must match the encryption used on the RADIUS daemon	Up to 256 characters
R10	IFNAME	Name of source interface	Support physical/aggregation/loopback/vlan/tunnel ports
R11	SRC_IP_ADDR	Source IP address	IPv4 Address

[P31498|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P31499|Normal] Global Configuration
[P31500|Heading 4] Default
[P31501|Normal] None
[P31502|Heading 4] Usage
[P31503|Normal] You can use multiple radius-server host commands to specify multiple hosts. The software searches for hosts in the order in which you specify them.
[P31504|Body Text] If no host-specific timeout, retransmit, or key values are specified, the global values apply to each host.
[P31505|Body Text] If the source interface or source IP address is specified, the packet transmit will use the related IP address as source address.
[P31506|Heading 4] Examples
[P31507|Normal] The following is sample output from the radius-server host command:
[P31508|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# radius-server host 10.10.1.1 key abcde
[P31509|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P31510|Normal] radius-server key
[P31511|Body Text] radius-server timeout
[P31512|Heading 3] radius-server retransmit
[P31513|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P31514|Normal] To specify the number of times the switch searches the list of RADIUS server hosts before giving up, use the radius-server retransmit command in global configuration mode. To disable retransmission, use the no form of this command.
[P31515|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P31516|Normal] radius-server retransmit RETRIES
[P31517|Body Text] no radius-server retransmit

[TABLE 1267] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	RETRIES	Maximum number of retransmission attempts.The default is 3	1-100

[P31518|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P31519|Normal] Global Configuration
[P31520|Heading 4] Default
[P31521|Normal] 3 attempts
[P31522|Heading 4] Usage
[P31523|Normal] The switch tries all servers, allowing each one to time out before increasing the retransmit count.
[P31524|Body Text] If the RADIUS server is only a few hops from the switch, we recommend that you configure the RADIUS server retransmit rate to 5.
[P31525|Body Text] The default value of radius retransmit is 3 attempts.
[P31526|Heading 4] Examples
[P31527|Normal] The following is sample output from the radius retransmit command:
[P31528|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# radius retransmit 5
[P31529|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P31530|Normal] radius-server host
[P31531|Body Text] radius-server key

[P31534|Normal] To set the interval for which a switch waits for a server host to reply, use the radius-server timeout command in global configuration mode. To restore the default, use the no form of this command.
[P31535|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P31536|Normal] radius-server timeout SECONDS
[P31537|Body Text] no radius-server timeout

R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value

[P31538|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P31539|Normal] Global Configuration
[P31540|Heading 4] Default
[P31541|Normal] None
[P31542|Heading 4] Usage
[P31543|Normal] Use this command to set the number of seconds a switch waits for a server host to reply before timing out.
[P31544|Body Text] If the RADIUS server is only a few hops from the switch, we recommend that you configure the RADIUS server timeout to 15 seconds.
[P31545|Body Text] The default value of radius timeout is 5 seconds.
[P31546|Heading 4] Examples
[P31547|Normal] The following is sample output from the radius timeout command:
[P31548|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# radius retransmit 15

[P31661|Heading 4] Command Mode

[P31665|Heading 4] Usage

[P31673|Heading 2] Port Isolate Commands
[P31674|Heading 3] port-isolate group
[P31675|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P31676|Normal] Use the port-isolate group interface configuration command on the switch to set the isolate group of a interface.
[P31677|Body Text] Use the no form of this command to return to the default setting.
[P31678|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P31679|Normal] port-isolate group GROUP
[P31680|Body Text] no port-isolate group

[TABLE 1273] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	GROUP	Port isolate group id	1-30

[P31681|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P31682|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P31683|Heading 4] Default
[P31684|Normal] None
[P31685|Heading 4] Usage
[P31686|Normal] The ports in the same isolate-group can not communicate with each other.
[P31687|Body Text] The ports in different isolate-groups should not be affected by this feature.
[P31688|Body Text] The isolate-groups can only be configured on physical port and Link Aggregation.
[P31689|Heading 4] Examples
[P31690|Normal] The following is sample output from the port-isolate group command:
[P31691|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1 
Switch(config-if)# port-isolate group 4
[P31692|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P31693|Normal] port-isolate mode
[P31694|Heading 3] port-isolate mode
[P31695|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P31696|Normal] Use the port-isolate mode global configuration command on the switch to set isolate mode.
[P31697|Body Text] Use the no form of this command to return to the default setting.
[P31698|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P31699|Normal] port-isolate mode ( all | l2 )
[P31700|Body Text] no port-isolate mode

[TABLE 1274] rows=3 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	all	Isolate bridged packets and routed packets	-
R3	l2	Isolate bridged packets	-

[P31701|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P31702|Normal] Global Configuration
[P31703|Heading 4] Default
[P31704|Normal] None
[P31705|Heading 4] Usage
[P31706|Normal] If configure “port-isolate mode l2”, all routed packets should not obey the port isolate rules.
[P31707|Body Text] If configure “port-isolate mode all”, all packets should obey the port isolate rules.
[P31708|Body Text] The default setting is “l2”
[P31709|Heading 4] Examples
[P31710|Normal] The following is sample output from the port-isolate mode command:
[P31711|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# port-isolate mode all

[P31751|Heading 2] Private Vlan Commands
[P31752|Heading 3] switchport mode private-vlan
[P31753|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P31754|Normal] To configure the switch port’s mode as private vlan, use the “switchport mode private-vlan” command in interface mode.
[P31755|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P31756|Normal] switchport mode private-vlan ( host | promiscuous )

[TABLE 1277] rows=3 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	host	Set the port as private vlan, host port	-
R3	promiscuous	Set the port as private vlan, promiscuous port	-

[P31757|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P31758|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P31759|Heading 4] Default
[P31760|Normal] By default the switch port’s mode is access vlan.
[P31761|Heading 4] Usage
[P31762|Normal] To configure the switch port’s mode as private vlan, use the “switchport mode private-vlan” command in interface mode.
[P31763|Body Text] This can only be configured on a switchport.
[P31764|Heading 4] Examples
[P31765|Normal] The following example shows how to configure the switch port mode:
[P31766|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# switchport mode private-vlan host 
Switch(config-if)# switchport mode private-vlan promiscuous
[P31767|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P31768|Normal] switchport private-vlan
[P31769|Heading 3] switchport private-vlan
[P31770|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P31771|Normal] To configure the primary and secondary vlan of a private vlan, use the “switchport private-vlan” command in interface mode.
[P31772|Body Text] Use the “no” form of this command to restore the default value.
[P31773|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P31774|Normal] switchport private-vlan VLAN_ID ( isolate | community-vlan VLAN_ID | )

[TABLE 1278] rows=4 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	private-vlan VLAN_ID	Set private primary vlan	1-4094
R3	isolate	Set as isolate mode	-
R4	community-vlan VLAN_ID	Set communtiy vlan	1-4094

[P31775|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P31776|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P31777|Heading 4] Default
[P31778|Normal] By default, the primary vlan is 1.
[P31779|Body Text] If the switchport mode is private-vlan host, the default mode is isolate; Or else the switchport mode is promiscuous
[P31780|Heading 4] Usage
[P31781|Normal] To configure the primary and secondary vlan of a private vlan, use the “switchport private-vlan” command in interface mode.
[P31782|Body Text] This can only be configured on a switchport.
[P31783|Heading 4] Examples
[P31784|Normal] The following example shows how to configure the private vlan:
[P31785|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# switchport mode private-vlan host 
Switch(config-if)# switchport private-vlan 1 isolate 
Switch(config-if)# quit
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-2
Switch(config-if)# switchport mode private-vlan host 
Switch(config-if)# switchport private-vlan 1 community-vlan 2
Switch(config-if)# quit
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-3
Switch(config-if)# switchport mode private-vlan promiscuous 
Switch(config-if)# switchport private-vlan 1
[P31786|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P31787|Normal] switchport mode private-vlan

R3	IFNAME	Show by interface	Support physical/aggregation ports

[P31805|Heading 2] DDOS Commands
[P31806|Heading 3] ip icmp intercept
[P31807|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P31808|Normal] To configure the system to resist ICMP flood attack, use the ip icmp intercept command in global configuration mode. To disable this capability, use the no form of this command.
[P31809|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P31810|Normal] ip icmp intercept ( maxcount NUMBER | )
[P31811|Body Text] no ip icmp intercept

[TABLE 1280] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	NUMBER	Specify max counter of received packets per second	0-1000

[P31812|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P31813|Normal] Global Configuration
[P31814|Heading 4] Default
[P31815|Normal] By default, ip icmp intercept is unset.
[P31816|Body Text] If the maxcount is not specified , the default count is 500.
[P31817|Heading 4] Usage
[P31818|Normal] Use this command if you want to set the system to limit the ICMP packet rate.
[P31819|Heading 4] Examples
[P31820|Normal] The following example shows how to configure the ip icmp intercept:
[P31821|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ip icmp intercept maxcount 100
[P31822|Normal] The following example unset the ip icmp intercept:
[P31823|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# no ip icmp intercept
[P31824|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P31825|Normal] show ip-intercept config

[P32122|Heading 3] port-block
[P32123|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P32124|Normal] To configure port block, use the port-block command in interface configuration mode. To delete this configuration, use the no form of this command.
[P32125|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P32126|Normal] port-block ( known-unicast | known-multicast | unknown-unicast | unknown-multicast | broadcast )
[P32127|Body Text] no port-block ( known-unicast | known-multicast | unknown-unicast | unknown-multicast | broadcast )

[TABLE 1290] rows=6 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	known-unicast	Specify that known unicast traffic should be blocked	-
R3	known-multicast	Specify that known multicast traffic should be blocked	-
R4	unknown-unicast	Specify that unknown unicast traffic should be blocked	-
R5	unknown-multicast	Specify that unknown multicast traffic should be blocked	-
R6	broadcast	Specify that broadcast traffic should be blocked	-

[P32128|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P32129|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P32130|Heading 4] Default
[P32131|Normal] Unknown or known multicast and unicast traffic is not blocked.
[P32132|Body Text] Broadcast traffic is not blocked.
[P32133|Heading 4] Usage
[P32134|Normal] By default, all traffic with unknown MAC addresses is sent to all ports. You can block unknown multicast or unicast traffic on protected or non protected ports. If unknown multicast or unicast traffic is not blocked on a protected port, there could be security issues.
[P32135|Body Text] With multicast traffic, the port blocking feature blocks only pure Layer 2 packets. Multicast packets that contain IPv4 or IPv6 information in the header are not blocked.
[P32136|Heading 4] Examples
[P32137|Normal] This example shows how to block unknown multicast traffic on an interface:
[P32138|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# port-block known-unicast

[P32266|Heading 3] dhcpv6 snooping
[P32267|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P32268|Normal] Use the dhcpv6 snooping global configuration command on the switch to globally enable DHCPv6 snooping.
[P32269|Body Text] Use the no form of this command to return to the default setting.
[P32270|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P32271|Normal] dhcpv6 snooping
[P32272|Body Text] no dhcpv6 snooping
[P32273|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P32274|Normal] Global Configuration
[P32275|Heading 4] Default
[P32276|Normal] DHCPv6 snooping is disabled.
[P32277|Heading 4] Usage
[P32278|Normal] For any DHCPv6 snooping configuration to take effect, you must globally enable DHCPv6 snooping. DHCPv6 snooping is not active until you enable snooping on a VLAN by using the dhcpv6 snooping vlan global configuration command.
[P32279|Body Text] You can verify your settings by entering the show dhcpv6 snooping config privileged EXEC command
[P32280|Heading 4] Examples
[P32281|Normal] This example shows how to enable DHCPv6 snooping:
[P32282|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# dhcpv6 snooping
[P32283|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P32284|Normal] dhcpv6 snooping vlan
[P32285|Body Text] show dhcpv6 snooping config
[P32286|Heading 3] dhcpv6 snooping binding
[P32287|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P32288|Normal] Use the dhcpv6 snooping binding global configuration command on the switch to configure the DHCPv6 snooping binding database and to add binding entries to the database.
[P32289|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P32290|Normal] dhcpv6 snooping binding mac MAC-ADDRESS vlan VLAN-ID ipv6 IP-ADDRESS interface IFNAME expiry SECONDS
[P32291|Body Text] no dhcpv6 snooping bindings ( ipv6 IP-ADDRESS | mac MAC-ADDRESS | vlan VLAN-ID | interface IFNAME | )

[TABLE 1296] rows=6 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	mac MAC-ADDRESS	Specify a MAC address	MAC address
R3	vlan VLAN-ID	Specify a VLAN number.	1-4094
R4	ipv6 IP-ADDRESS	Specify an IPv6 address	IPv6 Address
R5	interface IFNAME	Specify an interface on which to add or delete a binding entry	Support physical/aggregation ports
R6	expiry SECONDS	Specify the interval (in seconds) after which the binding entry is no longer valid. The range is 0 to 86400	0-86400 seconds

[P32292|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P32293|Normal] Global Configuration
[P32294|Heading 4] Default
[P32295|Normal] No default database is defined.
[P32296|Heading 4] Usage
[P32297|Normal] Use this command when you are testing or debugging the switch.
[P32298|Body Text] In the DHCPv6 snooping binding database, each database entry, also referred to a binding, has an IP address, an associated MAC address, the lease time, the interface to which the binding applies, and the VLAN to which the interface belongs.
[P32299|Body Text] Use the show dhcpv6 snooping binding privileged EXEC command to display the configured bindings.
[P32300|Heading 4] Examples
[P32301|Normal] This example shows how to generate a DHCPv6 binding with an expiration time of 1000 seconds on a port in VLAN 1:
[P32302|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# dhcpv6 snooping binding mac 0001.000c.01ef vlan 1 ipv6 2001:1::1 interface eth-0-1 expiry 1000

[P32311|Heading 4] Command Mode

[P32315|Heading 4] Usage
[P32316|Normal] You can enter a single VLAN ID identified by VLAN ID number, a series of VLAN IDs separated by commas, a range of VLAN IDs separated by hyphens, or a range of VLAN IDs separated by entering the starting and ending VLAN IDs separated by a space.Existed dhcpv6 snooping dynamic recording tables of a VLAN will be deleted when no-binding is enabled on this VLAN.

[P32340|Heading 4] Command Purpose

R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	vlan VLAN-ID	Set interface-id format for packets with the VLAN	1-4094
R3	vlan-id	Insert svlan of received packet to interface-id	-
R4	ifname	Insert the name of the interface received packet from client to interface-id	-
R5	hostname	Insert host name of the switch to interface-id	-

R7	string STRING	Insert user-defined string in interface-id	-

[P32345|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P32346|Normal] Global Configuration
[P32347|Heading 4] Default
[P32348|Normal] Default format is vlan:ifname:hostname:mac:
[P32349|Heading 4] Usage
[P32350|Normal] The format of interface-id can be a combination of vlan, interface name, hostname mac and user-defined string. This command specifies the existing keywords in the combination.
[P32351|Body Text] If format is configured to specified vlan, only DHCPv6 packets with the vlan are configured with this format; If not, all DHCPv6 request packets will be configured with specified format.
[P32352|Body Text] If option18 format is set on a port, it has high priority for DHCPv6 packets received from this port when insert interface-id option.
[P32353|Heading 4] Examples
[P32354|Normal] The following example shows how to specify the format of interface-id:
[P32355|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal

[P32807|Heading 3] ethernet oam min-rate
[P32808|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P32809|Normal] Use this command to set the OAMPDU timer. Use the no form of the command to reset to default value.
[P32810|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P32811|Normal] ethernet oam min-rate SECONDS
[P32812|Body Text] no ethernet oam min-rate

[TABLE 1311] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	SECONDS	The number of seconds chosen for this timer.	1-10 seconds

[P32813|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P32814|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P32815|Heading 4] Default
[P32816|Normal] The default value of the OAMPDU timer is 1 second
[P32817|Heading 4] Usage
[P32818|Normal] Set the timer to emit at least one OAMPDU per second and ensure that the sublayer adheres to the maximum number of OAMPDUs per second. The minimum is 1 OAMPDU per second and the maximum is 10 OAMPDU per second
[P32819|Heading 4] Examples
[P32820|Normal] The following example shows how to set the OAMPDU timer to 1:
[P32821|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# ethernet oam min-rate 1
[P32822|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P32823|Normal] show ethernet oam status

[P32825|Heading 4] Command Purpose

[P32828|Normal] ethernet oam max-rate PDUS
[P32829|Body Text] no ethernet oam max-rate

[TABLE 1312] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value

[P32830|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P32831|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P32832|Heading 4] Default
[P32833|Normal] The default value of the max-rate is 10 PDUs per second.
[P32834|Heading 4] Usage
[P32835|Normal] This command is to ensure that the sublayer adheres to the maximum number of OAMPDUs per second. The minimum is 1 OAMPDU per second and the maximum is 10 OAMPDUs per second.
[P32836|Heading 4] Examples
[P32837|Normal] The following example shows how to set the OAMPDU maximum number to 10 per second:
[P32838|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal

[P32875|Heading 3] ethernet oam link-monitor frame
[P32876|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P32877|Normal] Use this command to configure the low and high threshold and the window for the frame event. If the low threshold is exceeded, an error frame link event is generated. If the high threshold is exceeded, the action defined using the command ethernet oam link-monitor high threshold action is taken.
[P32878|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P32879|Normal] ethernet oam link-monitor frame threshold high ( HIGH_THRES | none ) low LOW_THRES window WINDOW
[P32880|Body Text] no ethernet oam link-monitor frame threshold

[TABLE 1313] rows=5 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	HIGH_THRES	Value of the high threshold for error frames.	1-65535
R3	none	No high threshold value is set	-
R4	low LOW_THRES	Value of the low threshold for error frames.	0-65535
R5	window WINDOW	Size of frame event window, expressed in milliseconds	10-600

[P32881|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P32882|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P32883|Heading 4] Default
[P32884|Normal] The default value for high threshold is none, meaning that no high threshold is configured.
[P32885|Body Text] The default value of low threshold is 1.
[P32886|Body Text] The default value for the frame event window is 100.
[P32887|Heading 4] Usage
[P32888|Normal] None
[P32889|Heading 4] Examples
[P32890|Normal] The following example shows how to configure the low and high threshold and the window for the frame event:
[P32891|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# ethernet oam link-monitor frame threshold high 5 low 2 window 200
[P32892|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P32893|Normal] show ethernet oam status
[P32894|Heading 3] ethernet oam link-monitor frame-seconds threshold
[P32895|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P32896|Normal] Use this command to configure the low and high threshold and the window for the frame-seconds event. If the low threshold is exceeded, an error-frame-seconds link event is generated. If the high threshold is exceeded then action defined through the command ethernet oam link-monitor high threshold action will be taken.
[P32897|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P32898|Normal] ethernet oam link-monitor frame-seconds threshold high ( HIGH_THRES | none ) low LOW_THRES window WINDOW
[P32899|Body Text] no ethernet oam link-monitor frame-seconds threshold high

[TABLE 1314] rows=5 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	HIGH_THRES	High threshold for the number of error frame-seconds in the range of 1~900	1-900
R3	none	No high threshold value is set	-
R4	low LOW_THRES	Low threshold for the number of error frame-seconds 1~900	1-900
R5	window WINDOW	Window for frame-seconds events, in milliseconds, in multiples of 100	100-9000

[P32900|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P32901|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P32902|Heading 4] Default
[P32903|Normal] The default value for high threshold is none, meaning that no high threshold is configure. The default value for the low threshold is 1. The default value of frame event window is 1000.
[P32904|Heading 4] Usage
[P32905|Normal] None
[P32906|Heading 4] Examples
[P32907|Normal] The following example shows how to configure the threshold and window for the frame-seconds event:
[P32908|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# ethernet oam link-monitor frame-seconds threshold high 5 low 2 window 200
[P32909|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P32910|Normal] show ethernet oam status

[P32913|Normal] Use this command to define action when high threshold is detected. Use no form of the command to reset the action.

[P32916|Body Text] no ethernet oam link-monitor high threshold action error-disable-interface

[P32928|Heading 3] ethernet oam remote-loopback
[P32929|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P32930|Normal] Use this command to configure remote loopback on an interface. This command can be used to enable or disable remote loopback and also configure the remote loopback timeout, which is the number of seconds the DTE will wait for the remote DTE to respond to the ethernet oam remote-loopback enable command. Use the no form of this command to remove remote-loopback support from the interface.
[P32931|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P32932|Normal] ethernet oam remote-loopback { supported | timeout SECS }
[P32933|Body Text] no ethernet oam remote-loopback { supported | timeout }

[TABLE 1315] rows=3 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	supported	Remote loopback can be initiated in the DTE	-
R3	timeout SECS	The remote loopback timeout value in the range of 1~10	1-10 seconds

[P32934|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P32935|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P32936|Heading 4] Default
[P32937|Normal] The default state for the remote loopback is not supported. If a timeout is not configured, the local DTE remains in remote loopback state until the remote DTE responds or the user stops remote loopback administratively.
[P32938|Body Text] One switch supports 4 interfaces in “local Loopback” status at the same time.
[P32939|Heading 4] Usage
[P32940|Normal] None
[P32941|Heading 4] Examples
[P32942|Normal] The following example shows how to support remote-loopback on interface eth-0-1:
[P32943|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# ethernet oam remote-loopback supported
