[P33094|Heading 3] ethernet cfm domain level
[P33095|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P33096|Normal] Use this command to create an MD within which you can manage Ethernet traffic or enter cfm domain mode. Ensure you specify the level for each MD. The levels separate MDs from each other and provide different areas of functionality.
[P33097|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P33098|Normal] ethernet cfm domain DOMAIN_NAME level LEVEL ( format ( no-md-name | string STRING | dns DNS_NAME | mac-address MAC_ADDRESS ) | )
[P33099|Body Text] no ethernet cfm domain DOMAIN_NAME ( level LEVEL | )

[TABLE 1324] rows=7 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	DOMAIN_NAME	Maintenance domain name	The first character should be a-z or A-Z, character only can be 0-9A-Za-z.-_ and the max len is 43
R3	LEVEL	MD level	0-7
R4	no-md-name	There is no md name when create maid of cfm packet	-
R5	string STRING	Maintenance domain ASCII name, used to create maid of cfm packet	The first character should be a-z or A-Z, character only can be 0-9A-Za-z.-_ and the max len is 43
R6	dns DNS_NAME	Maintenance domain DNS name, used to create maid of cfm packet	The first character should be a-z or A-Z, character only can be 0-9A-Za-z.-_ and the max len is 43
R7	mac-address MAC_ADDRESS	Maintenance domain MAC-address with two octets name, used to create maid of cfm packet	MAC-address and 2-octet integer (H.H.H:U(0-65535), example:0001.0001.0001:1)

[P33100|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P33101|Normal] Global Configuration
[P33102|Heading 4] Default
[P33103|Normal] None
[P33104|Heading 4] Usage
[P33105|Normal] The valid range of MD is 0-7, the larger number indicates bigger maintenance domain.
[P33106|Body Text] For Y.1731 mode, domain format should be no-md-name
[P33107|Heading 4] Examples
[P33108|Normal] The following example shows how to create and destroy domain:
[P33109|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ethernet cfm domain test level 5
Switch(config-ether-cfm)# exit
Switch(config)# no ethernet cfm domain test

[TABLE 1325] rows=5 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	CSI_ID	Maintenance association name	The first character should be a-z or A-Z, character only can be 0-9A-Za-z.-_ and the max len is 43. MD(Maintenance domain) name and MA(Maintenance association) name totally up to 44 characters.
R3	vlan VLAN_ID	Vlan id	1-4094
R4	string STRING	Maintenance association ASCII name, used to create maid of cfm packet	The first character should be a-z or A-Z, character only can be 0-9A-Za-z.-_ and the max len is 43
R5	icc-based ICC_NAME	Maintenance association icc-based name, used to create maid of cfm packet	The first character should be a-z or A-Z, character only can be 0-9A-Za-z.-_ and the max len is 13

[P33129|Heading 3] ethernet cfm mep
[P33130|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P33131|Normal] Use this command to define an MEP within an MA. Each MEP and remote MEP must have a unique ID within an MA. If two or more MEPs share the same ID, CFM raises an event indicating a duplicate MEP exists in the MA.
[P33132|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P33133|Normal] ethernet cfm mep ( down | up ) mpid MEPID domain DOMAIN_NAME ( vlan VLAN_ID | ) interval ( 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 )
[P33134|Body Text] no ethernet cfm mep ( down | up ) mpid MEPID domain DOMAIN_NAME ( vlan VLAN_ID | )

[TABLE 1326] rows=13 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	down	Down mep	-
R3	up	Up mep	-
R4	MEPID	Local mep id	1-8191
R5	DOMAIN_NAME	Maintenance domain name	String with up to 43 characters
R6	vlan VLAN_ID	Vlan id, the range is 1 to 4094	1-4094
R7	1	CCM Interval 3.3 millisecond	-
R8	2	CCM Interval 10 millisecond	-
R9	3	CCM Interval 100 millisecond	-
R10	4	CCM Interval 1 second	-
R11	5	CCM Interval 10 second	-
R12	6	CCM Interval 1 minute	-
R13	7	CCM Interval 10 minutes	-

R8	vlan VLAN_ID	Vlan id	1-4094

[P34113|Heading 4] Usage
[P34114|Normal] The reason with the highest priority class will get preference treatment when dealing with scheduling. ssh/telnet/mlag is useful when enable cpu-traffic-optimize.
[P34115|Heading 4] Examples

[P34118|Normal] This example shows how to restore the default priority class for BPDU:
[P34119|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# no cpu-traffic-limit reason bpdu class

[P34607|Heading 2] ERPS Commands
[P34608|Heading 3] erps
[P34609|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P34610|Normal] Use this command to create erps domain instance.
[P34611|Body Text] Use the no form of this command to remove the erps domain instance
[P34612|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P34613|Normal] erps DOMAINID ( ERPS_NAME | )
[P34614|Body Text] no erps DOMAINID

[TABLE 1388] rows=3 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	DOMAINID	ERPS domain ID.	1-255
R3	ERPS_NAME	ERPS domain name	String with up to 15 characters

[P34615|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P34616|Normal] Global Configuration
[P34617|Heading 4] Default
[P34618|Normal] None
[P34619|Heading 4] Usage
[P34620|Normal] This command is used to create or delete an erps domain. The command should the use first when config erps.
[P34621|Body Text] ERPS_NAME is optional. If no name is provided by command, system will generate the domain name automatically. The name format follows “ERPS001”, where 001 can be instead of any domain ID between 1-255 provided through the command.
[P34622|Heading 4] Examples
[P34623|Normal] This example shows how to create an erps domain with ID 11 and name test11:
[P34624|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# erps 11 test11
[P34625|Heading 4] Related Commands

[P34629|Normal] Use this command to specify erps domain’s control vlan.
[P34630|Body Text] Use the no form of this command to remove the control vlan.
[P34631|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P34632|Normal] erps DOMAINID ( primary | sub ) control vlan VLANID
[P34633|Body Text] no erps DOMAINID ( primary | sub ) control vlan

[P34634|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P34635|Normal] Global Configuration
[P34636|Heading 4] Default
[P34637|Normal] None
[P34638|Heading 4] Usage
[P34639|Normal] The erps protocol packet is transferred in the control vlan.
[P34640|Body Text] It is best to add the control vlan into the instance which is bound by the domain.
[P34641|Heading 4] Examples
[P34642|Normal] This example shows how to set vlan 15 as primary control vlan for erps domain 11:
[P34643|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# vlan database
Switch(config-vlan)# vlan 15
Switch(config-vlan)# exit
Switch(config)# erps 11 primary control vlan 15

R4	IFPHYSICAL	Ethernet interface name	-
R5	IFAGG	Link aggregation interface name	-

[P34818|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P34819|Normal] Global Configuration
[P34820|Heading 4] Default
[P34821|Normal] None
[P34822|Heading 4] Usage
[P34823|Normal] Of the two ports via which the edge node (assistant-edge node) accesses the subring, one is a common port and the other is an edge port. The common port is the port for the edge node (assistant-edge node) to access the primary ring and the subring, while the edge port is the port for the edge node to access the subring only.
[P34824|Body Text] This command is only available for edge/assistant-edge node.
[P34825|Heading 4] Examples
[P34826|Normal] This example shows how to set interface eth-0-9 as edge interface for ERPS domain 11 ring 1:
[P34827|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-9
Switch(config-if)# switchport mode trunk 
Switch(config-if)# switchport trunk allowed vlan add 15
Switch(config-if)# exit
Switch(config)# erps 11 ring 1 edge interface eth-0-9

[P35031|Heading 3] smart-link relay enable
[P35032|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P35033|Normal] Use this command to enable the switch to relay the smart-link flush packet. To disable relaying the packets, use no form of this command.
[P35034|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P35035|Normal] smart-link relay enable
[P35036|Body Text] no smart-link relay enable
[P35037|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P35038|Normal] Global Configuration
[P35039|Heading 4] Default
[P35040|Normal] Relaying the smart-link flush packet is enabled.
[P35041|Heading 4] Usage
[P35042|Normal] By default, the smart-link flush packet could be flooded. Use the command, “no smart-link relay enable”, to disable the packet flooding to other switches.
[P35043|Heading 4] Examples
[P35044|Normal] The example shows how to enable smart-link relay:
[P35045|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# smart-link relay enable
[P35046|Normal] The example shows how to disable smart-link relay:
[P35047|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# no smart-link relay enable

[P35049|Normal] None
[P35050|Heading 3] interface
[P35051|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P35052|Normal] Use this command to set master or slave member interface of the smart-link group. To unset the member, uses the no form of this command.
[P35053|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P35054|Normal] interface ( IFPHYSICAL | IFAGG ) ( master | slave )
[P35055|Body Text] no interface ( master | slave | all )

[TABLE 1410] rows=5 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	IFPHYSICAL	The name of physical interface	-
R3	IFAGG	The name of link-agg interface, like agg1	-
R4	master	The interface act as master role	-
R5	slave	The interface act as slave role	-

[P35056|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P35057|Normal] Smart-link Configuration
[P35058|Heading 4] Default
[P35059|Normal] There is no any interface member in the smart-link group by default.
[P35060|Heading 4] Usage
[P35061|Normal] Every smart-link group has two member interfaces, master and slave. The interfaces should be physical (i.e. eth-0-1) or aggregator (i.e. agg1) switch interface.
[P35062|Body Text] STP must be disabled in the smart-link interfaces first.
[P35063|Heading 4] Examples
[P35064|Normal] This example shows how to set interfaces eth-0-9 and eth-0-13 as the member interfaces of smart-link group 1:
[P35065|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-9
Switch(config-if)# spanning-tree port disable 
Switch(config-if)# exit
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-13
Switch(config-if)# spanning-tree port disable 
Switch(config-if)# exit
Switch(config)# smart-link group 1
Switch(config-smlk-group)# interface eth-0-9 master 
Switch(config-smlk-group)# interface eth-0-13 slave 
Switch(config-smlk-group)# end
[P35066|Normal] Display the smart link group just created:
[P35067|Terminal Display] Switch# show smart-link group 1
Smart-link group 1 information:

 MASTER eth-0-9     0          N/A             0          N/A                  
 SLAVE  eth-0-13    0           N/A            0          N/A

[P35077|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P35078|Normal] Smart-link Configuration
[P35079|Heading 4] Default
[P35080|Normal] There is no protected MSTP instance in the smart-link group by default.
[P35081|Heading 4] Usage
[P35082|Normal] The smart-link groups only protect these VLANs in the protected MSTP instances. The smart-link group can’t be enabled if no protected instance is configured. To protect those VLANs which are not bound with MSTP instance, use the command “protected mstp instance 0”.
[P35083|Body Text] NOTE: If the MTSP instance is removed, it will be removed from smart-link group at the same time.
[P35084|Heading 4] Examples
[P35085|Normal] This example shows how to set MSTP instance 0, 10 and 100 to the smart-link group 1:
[P35086|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# smart-link group 1
Switch(config-smlk-group)# protected mstp instance 0
Switch(config-smlk-group)# protected mstp instance 10
Switch(config-smlk-group)# protected mstp instance 100
Switch(config-smlk-group)# end

[P35107|Heading 3] restore time
[P35108|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P35109|Normal] Use this command to set restore time of the smart-link group.
[P35110|Body Text] Use the no form of this command to restore the default value.
[P35111|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P35112|Normal] restore time RESTORE-TIME
[P35113|Body Text] no restore time

R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value

[P35114|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P35115|Normal] Smart-link Configuration
[P35116|Heading 4] Default
[P35117|Normal] The default restore time is 60 seconds.
[P35118|Heading 4] Usage
[P35119|Normal] When the master interface is resumed, the links will not be immediately restored to the master interface, but will be delayed a while. The delay time is called restore time.
[P35120|Heading 4] Examples
[P35121|Normal] This example shows how to set restore time as 30 seconds in the smart-link group 1:
[P35122|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# smart-link group 1
Switch(config-smlk-group)# restore time 30
[P35123|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P35124|Normal] show smart-link group
[P35125|Heading 3] restore enable
[P35126|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P35127|Normal] Use this command to enable/disable restoring feature of the smart-link group.
[P35128|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P35129|Normal] restore enable
[P35130|Body Text] no restore enable
[P35131|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P35132|Normal] Smart-link Configuration
[P35133|Heading 4] Default
[P35134|Normal] The restoring feature of the smart-link group is disabled by default.
[P35135|Heading 4] Usage
[P35136|Normal] When master interface fails, the link will be switched to the slave interface. Then, if master interface is resumed, the link will not be switched back to keep the flow stable by default. If restoring feature is enabled, the link will be switched back.
[P35137|Body Text] NOTE: If load-balancing instance is configured, this feature is recommended strongly.
[P35138|Heading 4] Examples
[P35139|Normal] This example shows how to enable the restoring feature in the smart-link group 1:
[P35140|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# smart-link group 1
Switch(config-smlk-group)# restore enable
[P35141|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P35142|Normal] show smart-link group
[P35143|Heading 3] flush send
[P35144|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P35145|Normal] Use this command to set/unset the flush packet sender in the smart-link group.
[P35146|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P35147|Normal] flush send control-vlan VLAN-ID ( password simple PASSWORD | )
[P35148|Body Text] no flush send

[TABLE 1414] rows=3 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	VLAN-ID	Flush packet will be sent through this VLAN.	1-4094
R3	PASSWORD	The simple password of the flush packet	String with up to 15 characters

[P35149|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P35150|Normal] Smart-link Configuration
[P35151|Heading 4] Default
[P35152|Normal] There is no flush sender in the smart-link group by default.
[P35153|Heading 4] Usage
[P35154|Normal] Mac address-table should be updated when a master (forwarding) link goes down and the slave link begins forwarding traffic. Flush packet is used for this purpose.
[P35155|Body Text] NOTE: If the control-vlan is not existed in the switch, sending flush packet will fail.
[P35156|Heading 4] Examples
[P35157|Normal] This example shows how to configure flush sender of the smart-link group 1, control-vlan is 4 and password is “test”:
[P35158|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# smart-link group 1
Switch(config-smlk-group)# flush send control-vlan 4 password simple test

[P35350|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P35351|Normal] Multi-link Group Configuration
[P35352|Heading 4] Default
[P35353|Normal] There is no any interface member in the multi-link group by default.
[P35354|Heading 4] Usage
[P35355|Normal] Every multi-link group has more than two member interfaces. The interfaces should be physical (i.e. eth-0-1) or aggregator (i.e. agg1) switch interface.

[P35357|Heading 4] Examples
[P35358|Normal] This example shows how to set interfaces eth-0-9 and eth-0-13 as the interfaces of multi-link group 1:
[P35359|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-9
Switch(config-if)# spanning-tree port disable
Switch(config-if)# exit
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-13
Switch(config-if)# spanning-tree port disable
Switch(config-if)# exit
Switch(config)# multi-link group 1
Switch(config-multilk-group)# interface eth-0-9 master
Switch(config-multilk-group)# interface eth-0-13 slave
Switch(config-multilk-group)# end

[P35362|Heading 3] protected mstp instance
[P35363|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P35364|Normal] Use this command to set/unset protected MSTP instance to the multi-link group.
[P35365|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P35366|Normal] protected mstp instance INSTANCE-ID
[P35367|Body Text] no protected mstp instance ( all | INSTANCE-ID )

[TABLE 1422] rows=3 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	INSTANCE-ID	MSTP instance ID. The range is 0-4094	0-4094
R3	all	All the instance have been exist	-

[P35368|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P35369|Normal] Multi-link Group Configuration
[P35370|Heading 4] Default
[P35371|Normal] There is no protected MSTP instance in the multi-link group by default.
[P35372|Heading 4] Usage
[P35373|Normal] The multi-link groups only protect these VLANs in the protected MSTP instances. The multi-link group can’t be enabled if no protected instance is configured. To protect those VLANs which are not bound with MSTP instance, use the command “protected mstp instance 0”.
[P35374|Body Text] NOTE: If the MTSP instance is removed, it will be removed from multi-link group at the same time.
[P35375|Heading 4] Examples
[P35376|Normal] This example shows how to set MSTP instance 0, 10 and 100 to the multi-link group 1:
[P35377|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# multi-link group 1
Switch(config-multilk-group)# protected mstp instance 0
Switch(config-multilk-group)# protected mstp instance 10
Switch(config-multilk-group)# protected mstp instance 100
Switch(config-multilk-group)# end

[P35380|Heading 3] load-balance instance
[P35381|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P35382|Normal] Use this command to set/unset load-balancing to the multi-link group.
[P35383|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P35384|Normal] load-balance instance INSTANCE-ID priority <2-4>
[P35385|Body Text] no load-balance instance ( all | INSTANCE-ID )

[TABLE 1423] rows=4 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	INSTANCE-ID	MSTP instance ID. The range is 0-4094	0-4094
R3	<2-4>	Set load-balancing port with same priority	-
R4	all	All the instance have been exist	-

[P35386|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P35387|Normal] Multi-link Group Configuration
[P35388|Heading 4] Default
[P35389|Normal] There is no load-balancing instance in the multi-link group by default.
[P35390|Heading 4] Usage
[P35391|Normal] Load-balancing instances will be active in the slave interface. If user want to configure load-balancing instances, should before the smart-group is enabled.
[P35392|Heading 4] Examples
[P35393|Normal] This example shows how to set protected instance 10 as the load-balancing instance:
[P35394|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# multi-link group 1
Switch(config-multilk-group)# load-balance instance 10 priority 2
[P35395|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P35396|Normal] show multi-link group
[P35397|Heading 3] restore time
[P35398|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P35399|Normal] Use this command to set restore time of the multi-link group.
[P35400|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P35401|Normal] restore time RESTORE-TIME
[P35402|Body Text] no restore time

[TABLE 1424] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	RESTORE-TIME	The restore time of the multi-link group	30-1200 seconds

[P35403|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P35404|Normal] Multi-link Group Configuration
[P35405|Heading 4] Default
[P35406|Normal] The default restore time is 60 seconds.
[P35407|Heading 4] Usage
[P35408|Normal] When the master interface is resumed, the links will not be immediately restored to the master interface, but will be delayed a while. The delay time is called restore time.
[P35409|Heading 4] Examples
[P35410|Normal] This example shows how to set restore time as 30 seconds in the multi-link group 1:
[P35411|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# multi-link group 1
Switch(config-multilk-group)# restore time 30
[P35412|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P35413|Normal] show multi-link group
[P35414|Heading 3] restore enable
[P35415|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P35416|Normal] Use this command to enable/disable restoring feature of the multi-link group.
[P35417|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P35418|Normal] restore enable
[P35419|Body Text] no restore enable
[P35420|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P35421|Normal] Multi-link Group Configuration
[P35422|Heading 4] Default
[P35423|Normal] The restoring feature of the multi-link group is disabled by default.
[P35424|Heading 4] Usage
[P35425|Normal] When master interface fails, the link will be switched to the slave interface. Then, if master interface is resumed, the link will not be switched back to keep the flow stable by default. If restoring feature is enabled, the link will be switched back.
[P35426|Body Text] NOTE: If load-balancing instance is configured, this feature is recommended strongly.
[P35427|Heading 4] Examples
[P35428|Normal] This example shows how to enable the restoring feature in the multi-link group 1:
[P35429|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# multi-link group 1
Switch(config-multilk-group)# restore enable
[P35430|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P35431|Normal] show multi-link group
[P35432|Heading 3] flush send
[P35433|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P35434|Normal] Use this command to set/unset the flush packet sender in the multi-link group.
[P35435|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P35436|Normal] flush send control-vlan VLAN-ID password simple PASSWORD
[P35437|Body Text] no flush send

[TABLE 1425] rows=3 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	VLAN-ID	Flush packet will be sent through this VLAN.	1-4094
R3	PASSWORD	The simple password of the flush packet	String with up to 15 characters

[P35438|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P35439|Normal] Multi-link Group Configuration
[P35440|Heading 4] Default
[P35441|Normal] There is no flush sender in the multi-link group by default.
[P35442|Heading 4] Usage
[P35443|Normal] Mac address-table should be updated when a master (forwarding) link goes down and the slave link begins forwarding traffic. Flush packet is used for this purpose.
[P35444|Body Text] NOTE: If the control-vlan is not existed in the switch, sending flush packet will fail.
[P35445|Heading 4] Examples
[P35446|Normal] This example shows how to configure flush sender of the multi-link group 1, control-vlan is 4 and password is “test”:
[P35447|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# multi-link group 1
Switch(config-multilk-group)# flush send control-vlan 4 password simple test

[P35800|Heading 2] VRRP Commands
[P35801|Heading 3] advertisement-interval
[P35802|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P35803|Normal] To configure the interval between successive advertisements sent by the master virtual router in a Virtual Router Redundancy Protocol (VRRP) group, use the advertisement-interval command in router configuration mode. To restore the default value, use the no form of this command.
[P35804|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P35805|Normal] advertisement-interval interval
[P35806|Body Text] no advertisement-interval

[TABLE 1441] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	INTERVAL	Time interval between successive advertisements sent by the master virtual router. The unit of the interval is in seconds.	1-255 seconds

[P35807|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P35808|Normal] Router Configuration
[P35809|Heading 4] Default
[P35810|Normal] Default is 1 second.
[P35811|Heading 4] Usage
[P35812|Normal] The advertisements sent by the master virtual router communicate the state and priority of the current master virtual router.
[P35813|Body Text] The advertisement-interval command configures the time between successive advertisement packets and the time before other routers declare the master router to be down. Routers or access servers on which timer value are not configured can learn timer values from the master router. The timers configured on the master router always override any other timer settings. All routers in a VRRP group must use the same timer value. If the same timer value is not set, the routers in the VRRP group will not communicate with each other and any misconfigured router will change its state to master.
[P35814|Heading 4] Examples
[P35815|Normal] The following example shows how to configure the master virtual router to send advertisements every 4 seconds:
[P35816|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router vrrp 1
Switch(config-router)# advertisement-interval 4
[P35817|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P35818|Normal] advertisement-interval msec
[P35819|Heading 3] advertisement-interval msec
[P35820|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P35821|Normal] To configure the advertisement interval with milli-second mode between successive advertisements sent by the master virtual router in a VRRP group, use the advertisement-interval msec command in router configuration mode.
[P35822|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P35823|Normal] advertisement-interval msec interval

[TABLE 1442] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	INTERVAL	Time interval between successive advertisements sent by the master virtual router. The unit of the interval is in 100 milli-seconds.	100-900 milli-seconds.

[P35824|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P35825|Normal] Router Configuration
[P35826|Heading 4] Default
[P35827|Normal] None
[P35828|Heading 4] Usage
[P35829|Normal] The advertisements be sent by the master virtual router communicate the state and priority of the current master virtual router.
[P35830|Body Text] The advertisement-interval msec command configures the time between successive advertisement packets and the time before other routers declare the master router to be down. Routers or access servers on which timer values are not configured can learn timer values from the master router. The timers configured on the master router always override any other timer settings. All routers in a VRRP group must use the same timer value. If the same timer value is not set, the routers in the VRRP group will not communicate with each other and any misconfigured router will change its state to master.
[P35831|Heading 4] Examples
[P35832|Normal] The following example shows how to configure the master virtual router to send advertisements every 100 milli-seconds:
[P35833|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router vrrp 1
Switch(config-router)# advertisement-interval msec 100

[P35888|Heading 3] preempt-mode
[P35889|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P35890|Normal] To configure the router to take over as master virtual router for a Virtual Router Redundancy Protocol (VRRP) group if it has higher priority than the current master virtual router, use the preempt-mode enable command in router mode. To disable this function, use the preempt-mode disable command.
[P35891|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P35892|Normal] preempt-mode ( true | false )

[TABLE 1446] rows=3 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	True	Preemption enabled	-
R3	False	Preemption disabled	-

[P35893|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P35894|Normal] Router Configuration
[P35895|Heading 4] Default
[P35896|Normal] Default is true.
[P35897|Heading 4] Usage
[P35898|Normal] By default, the router configured preempt-mode true will take over as master virtual router for the group if it has a higher priority than the current master virtual router.
[P35899|Heading 4] Examples
[P35900|Normal] The following example shows how to configure the router to preempt the current master virtual router when its priority of 200 is higher than that of the current master virtual router:
[P35901|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router vrrp 1
Switch(config-router)# preempt-mode true
Switch(config-router)# priority 200
[P35902|Heading 4] Related Commands

[P35904|Heading 3] preempt delay
[P35905|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P35906|Normal] To configure the master down interval when preempt takes effect.
[P35907|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P35908|Normal] preempt delay time

[TABLE 1447] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	TIME	Preempt delay time	0-3600 seconds

[P35909|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P35910|Normal] Router Configuration
[P35911|Heading 4] Default
[P35912|Normal] Default is 0 second.
[P35913|Heading 4] Usage
[P35914|Normal] The original master down interval =(3advt_interval) + skew_time. when preempt delay time is configured, then master down interval =(3advt_interval) + skew_time + preempt_delay. By default, preempt delay is 0 second.
[P35915|Heading 4] Examples
[P35916|Normal] The following example shows how to configure the router to preempt the current master virtual router when its priority of 200 is higher than that of the current master virtual router, but delay 30 seconds to preempt:
[P35917|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router vrrp 1
Switch(config-router)# preempt-mode true
Switch(config-router)# priority 200
Switch(config-router)# preempt delay 30

[P36010|Heading 3] virtual-ip
[P36011|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P36012|Normal] To enable the Virtual Router Redundancy Protocol (VRRP) on an interface and identify the IP address of the virtual router, use the virtual-ip command in router configuration mode. To disable VRRP on the interface and remove the IP address of the virtual router, use the no form of this command.
[P36013|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P36014|Normal] virtual-ip IP-ADDRESS
[P36015|Body Text] no virtual-ip

[TABLE 1452] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	IP-ADDRESS	IP address of the virtual router	IPv4 Address

[P36016|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P36017|Normal] Router Configuration
[P36018|Heading 4] Default
[P36019|Normal] None
[P36020|Heading 4] Usage
[P36021|Normal] For VRRP to elect a designated router, at least one router on the cable must have been configured with the primary address of the virtual router.
[P36022|Body Text] VRRP does not support address learning. All addresses must be configured.
[P36023|Body Text] All routers in the VRRP group must be configured with the same primary address for the virtual router. If different primary addresses are configured, the routers in the VRRP group will not communicate with each other and any mis-configured routers in the group will change their state to master.
[P36024|Body Text] The virtual IP address must be in the same subnet with VRRP interface, and if virtual IP is equal to the interface IP address, it is called IP address owner.
[P36025|Heading 4] Examples
[P36026|Normal] The following example shows how to enable VRRP on eth-0-1. The VRRP group is 1. IP address 10.0.1.20 is the address of the virtual router:
[P36027|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)#interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)#no switchport
Switch(config-if)#ip address 10.0.1.1/24
Switch(config)#router vrrp 1
Switch(config-router)#interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-router)#virtual-ip 10.0.1.20
Switch(config-router)#enable
[P36028|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P36029|Normal] router vrrp
[P36030|Heading 3] virtual-ipv6
[P36031|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P36032|Normal] To configure an identify the IPv6 address of the virtual router, use the virtual-ipv6 command in router configuration mode. To remove the IPv6 address of the virtual router, use the no form of this command.
[P36033|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P36034|Normal] virtual-ip IPv6-ADDRESS ( link-local | )
[P36035|Body Text] no virtual-ip IPv6-ADDRESS ( link-local | )

[TABLE 1453] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	IPv6-ADDRESS	IPv6 address of the virtual router	IPv6 Address

[P36036|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P36037|Normal] Router Configuration
[P36038|Heading 4] Default
[P36039|Normal] None
[P36040|Heading 4] Usage
[P36041|Normal] All routers in the VRRP group must be configured with the same virtual ipv6 address for the virtual router.
[P36042|Body Text] The virtual IPv6 address must be in the same subnet with VRRP interface, and if virtual IPv6 address is equal to the interface IPv6 address, it is called IP address owner, and priority will be set to 255. Link-local virtual IPv6 address must configure before global unicast virtual IPv6 address.
[P36043|Heading 4] Examples
[P36044|Normal] The following example shows how to configure virtual IPv6 address :
[P36045|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)#interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)#no switchport
Switch(config-if)#ipv6 address 2000::1/64
Switch(config)#router ipv6 vrrp 1
Switch(config-router)#interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-router)#virtual-ipv6 fe80::1 link-local
Switch(config-router)#virtual-ipv6 2000::1
Switch(config-router)#enable
[P36046|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P36047|Normal] router ipv6 vrrp

[P36098|Heading 3] delay up
[P36099|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P36100|Normal] Use this command to specify the delay time before communication state of track object changes to up.
[P36101|Body Text] Use the no form of this command to restore the default value.

[P36103|Normal] delay up SECONDS
[P36104|Body Text] no delay up

[P36105|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P36106|Normal] Track Configuration
[P36107|Heading 4] Default
[P36108|Normal] By default the delay time is 0.
[P36109|Heading 4] Usage

[P36113|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal

[P36143|Heading 4] Default
[P36144|Normal] The default value is 60 seconds.
[P36145|Heading 4] Usage
[P36146|Normal] The frequency value should follow this rule：

[P36599|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P36600|Normal] Global Configuration
[P36601|Heading 4] Default
[P36602|Normal] None
[P36603|Heading 4] Usage
[P36604|Normal] This virtual mac is used for interface configured virtual IP address. The address is receive-only; the switch never sends packets with this address as the source. And it only exists in ARP replay for virtual IP.
[P36605|Heading 4] Examples
[P36606|Normal] The following example is the result of this command:
[P36607|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ip virtual-router mac 1.1.1
[P36608|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P36609|Normal] ip virtual-router address
[P36610|Heading 3] ip virtual-router address
[P36611|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P36612|Normal] Use this command to configure a virtual IP address for interface.
[P36613|Body Text] Use the no form of this command to remove the virtual-router IP.
[P36614|Heading 4] Command Syntax

[P36616|Body Text] no ip virtual-router address

R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	A.B.C.D	Virtual IP address without mask	IPv4 Address
R3	A.B.C.D/M	Virtual IP address with mask	IPv4 Address and mask length

[P36617|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P36618|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P36619|Heading 4] Default
[P36620|Normal] None
[P36621|Heading 4] Usage
[P36622|Normal] The ip virtual-router address command assigns a virtual IP address to the interface . The virtual IP address without mask should be in the subnet of the primary IP address assigned to the interface and the virtual IP address with mask should not be in the subnet of the primary IP address assigned to the interface. The virtual IP address without mask and the virtual IP address with mask must be selected only one to be configured. if virtual mac is not configured, there is no reply to ARP request packet for the virtual IP address.
[P36623|Heading 4] Examples
[P36624|Normal] The following example is the result of this command:
[P36625|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# ip virtual-router address 1.1.1.1

[P36628|Heading 2] IP BFD Commands
[P36629|Heading 3] bfd interval
[P36630|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P36631|Normal] Use this command to specify the desired transmit interval, receive interval and detect multiplier of IP BFD on the interface.
[P36632|Body Text] Use the “no” form of this command to restore the default value.
[P36633|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P36634|Normal] bfd interval { tx MINTX | rx MINRX | multiplier MULTIPLIER }
[P36635|Body Text] no bfd interval

[TABLE 1487] rows=4 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	MINTX	Set BFD minimum trasmit interval	3-1000 millisecond
R3	MINRX	Set BFD minimum receive interval	3-1000 millisecond
R4	MULTIPLIER	Set the value of Hello Multiplier	2-15

[P36636|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P36637|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P36638|Heading 4] Default
[P36639|Normal] The default value for minimum tx interval and rx interval is 20ms.
[P36640|Body Text] The default value for detect multiple is 3.
[P36641|Heading 4] Usage
[P36642|Normal] Use this command to specify the transmit interval, receive interval and detect multiple of IP BFD on the interface.
[P36643|Body Text] This configuration should affect all the IP BFD sessions on this interface. The actual transmit interval and receive interval need to negotiate with another end of the session.
[P36644|Heading 4] Examples
[P36645|Normal] In the following example, the desired transmit interval is set as 3 ms, the desired receive interval is set as 3 ms, the detect multiplier is set as 3 times:
[P36646|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# bfd interval mintx 3 minrx 3 multiplier 3
[P36647|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P36648|Normal] None
[P36649|Heading 3] bfd NAME peer-ip A.B.C.D interface
[P36650|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P36651|Normal] Use this command to configure one Single-hop IP BFD session.
[P36652|Body Text] Use the “no” form of this command to remove the session
[P36653|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P36654|Normal] bfd NAME peer-ip A.B.C.D ( vrf NAME | ) interface ( IFPHYSICAL | IFVLAN | IFAGG ) ( source-ip A.B.C.D | ) ( auto | local LDISR remote RDISR )
[P36655|Body Text] no bfd NAME

[TABLE 1488] rows=8 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	peer-ip A.B.C.D	BFD destination ip address	IPv4 Address
R3	vrf NAME	specify a vrf for bfd	-
R4	interface	specify an interface for single hop bfd	-
R5	Source-ip A.B.C.D	specify source ip address	IPv4 Address
R6	auto	Allocating local discriminator by system	-
R7	LDISR	specify local discriminator by users	257-8191
R8	RDISR	specify local discriminator by users	1-4294967295

[P36656|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P36657|Normal] Global Configuration
[P36658|Heading 4] Default
[P36659|Normal] By default there is no IP Single BFD session to be created.
[P36660|Heading 4] Usage
[P36661|Normal] Use this command to specify the IP BFD for static route. BFD session is created, the bfd configurations need meet the following conditions:
[P36662|Normal] The destination ip address should be subnet with the ip address of the binded interface.
[P36663|Normal] The specified vrf should be same as that of the binded interface. If users don’t specify the vrf, the bfd vrf would be default.
[P36664|Normal] The source ip address should be same as that of the binded interface. If users don’t specify the source ip address, the source ip would be got from the binded interface, which is subnet with the destination ip address. If there are many ip addresses of the binded interface subnet the the destination ip address, the primary ip address would be selected firstly, and the smaller values of the ip adderss would be chosen secondly.
[P36665|Normal] If users specify the local and remote discriminator, bfd uses them. Otherwise, the bfd local discriminator would be allocated by system.
[P36666|Heading 4] Examples
[P36667|Normal] In the following example, the single-hop IP bfd session “test” is created:
[P36668|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# bfd test peer-ip 9.9.9.2 interface eth-0-9 local 10 remote 20
[P36669|Heading 4] Related Commands

[P36830|Heading 4] Related Commands

[P36832|Heading 3] sbfd NAME
[P36833|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P36834|Normal] Use this command to configure one Seamless BFD session.
[P36835|Body Text] Use the “no” form of this command to remove this configurations.
[P36836|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P36837|Normal] sbfd NAME peer-ip A.B.C.D interface ( IFPHYSICAL | IFVLAN | IFAGG ) ( source-ip A.B.C.D | )
[P36838|Body Text] no bfd NAME

[TABLE 1495] rows=5 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	NAME	sbfd session name	String with up to 16 characters
R3	peer-ip A.B.C.D	BFD destination ip address	IP Address
R4	interface	specify an interface for single hop bfd	Physical/vlan/agg interface
R5	Source-ip A.B.C.D	specify source ip address	IP Address

[P36839|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P36840|Normal] Global Configuration
[P36841|Heading 4] Default
[P36842|Normal] By default there is no SBFD session to be created.
[P36843|Heading 4] Usage
[P36844|Normal] Use this command to specify the SBFD for static route. SBFD session is created, the bfd configurations need meet the following conditions:
[P36845|Normal] The destination ip address should be subnet with the ip address of the binded interface.
[P36846|Normal] The specified vrf should be same as that of the binded interface. If users don’t specify the vrf, the bfd vrf would be default.
[P36847|Normal] The source ip address should be same as that of the binded interface. If users don’t specify the source ip address, the source ip would be got from the binded interface, which is subnet with the destination ip address. If there are many ip addresses of the binded interface subnet the the destination ip address, the primary ip address would be selected firstly, and the smaller values of the ip adderss would be chosen secondly.
[P36848|Normal] If users specify the local and remote discriminator, bfd uses them. Otherwise, the bfd local discriminator would be allocated by system.
[P36849|Heading 4] Examples
[P36850|Normal] In the following example, user configures to create the sbfd session ‘test’:
[P36851|Terminal Display] Switch (config)# sbfd test peer-ip 9.9.9.2 interface eth-0-9

[P36958|Heading 1] Device Management Commands
[P36959|Heading 2] STM Commands
[P36960|Heading 3] stm prefer
[P36961|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P36962|Normal] Use the stm prefer Global Configuration command to configure the profile used in Switch Table Management (STM) resource allocation. You can use profile to allocate system memory to best support the features being used in your application. Use profile to approximate the maximum number of unicast MAC addresses, quality of service (QoS) access control entries (ACEs) and unicast routes. Use the no form of this command to return to the default profile.
[P36963|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P36964|Normal] stm prefer ( default | layer3 | ipv6 | mpls | extended-buffer )
[P36965|Body Text] no stm prefer

[TABLE 1498] rows=6 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	default	Provide balance to all features	-
R3	layer3	Provide maximum Host Route/Indirect Route entries. You would typically use this profile for a router or aggregator in the middle of a network	-
R4	ipv6	Unicast bias, supporting more IPv6 Ucast Routes. This profile is only existed when IPv6 feature is supported.	-
R5	mpls	The mpls template supports the maximum number of MPLS/MAC entries.	-
R6	extended-buffer	Extended-buffer bias, with more packet buffer.	-

[P36966|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P36967|Normal] Global Configuration
[P36968|Heading 4] Default
[P36969|Normal] System use the default profile when first boot up, this profile balance all the features.
[P36970|Heading 4] Usage
[P36971|Normal] Users must reload the switch for the configuration to take effect.
[P36972|Heading 4] Examples
[P36973|Normal] This example shows how to configure the ipv4 profile on the switch. You can verify your settings by entering the show stm prefer in privileged EXEC mode:
[P36974|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# stm prefer layer3
Switch(config)# exit
Switch# reload

[P36979|Normal] Use the show stm prefer privileged EXEC command to display information about the profiles that can be used to maximize system resources for a particular feature, or use the command without a keyword to display the profile in use.

R4	ipv6	Unicast bias, supporting more IPv6 Ucast Routes. This profile is only existed when IPv6 feature is supported.	-
R5	mpls	The mpls template supports the maximum number of MPLS/MAC entries.	-
R6	extended-buffer	Extended-buffer bias, with more packet buffer.	-

[P37011|Heading 3] logging alarm-trap
[P37012|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P37013|Normal] To limit messages logged to the syslog servers based on severity, use the logging alarm-trap command in Global Configuration mode. To restore the default level, use the no form of this command.
[P37014|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P37015|Normal] logging alarm-trap ( enable | disable | level ( high | lower | middle | minor ) )
[P37016|Body Text] no logging alarm-trap level

[TABLE 1500] rows=7 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	enable	Enable logging traps	-
R3	disable	Disable logging traps	-
R4	level high	The high alarm level	-
R5	level lower	The lower alarm level.	-
R6	level middle	The middle alarm level	-
R7	level minor	The minor alarm level	-

[P37017|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P37018|Normal] Global Configuration
[P37019|Heading 4] Default
[P37020|Normal] Logging trap is disabled.
[P37021|Heading 4] Usage
[P37022|Normal] A trap is an unsolicited message sent to a remote network management host. Logging traps should not be confused with SNMP traps.
[P37023|Heading 4] Examples
[P37024|Normal] The following shows how to limit messages logged to the log servers based on severity:
[P37025|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# logging alarm-trap enable
Switch(config)# logging alarm-trap level high

[P37045|Heading 4] Command Purpose

[P37047|Heading 4] Command Syntax

R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	0 \| emergency	System is unusable	-
R3	1 \| alert	Immediate action needed	-
R4	2 \| critical	Critical conditions	-
R5	3 \| error	Error conditions	-
R6	4 \| warning	Warning conditions	-
R7	5 \| notice	Normal but significant conditions	-
R8	6 \| information	Informational messages	-
R9	7 \| debug	Debugging messages	-
R10	SEVERITY_LEVEL	Severity level	0-7

[P37050|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P37051|Normal] Global Configuration
[P37052|Heading 4] Default
[P37053|Normal] Logging file level is inofrmation.
[P37054|Heading 4] Usage
[P37055|Normal] Specifying a severity-level causes messages only at that level and numerically lower levels to files.

[P37057|Normal] In the following example, the user specifies that only messages of the levels error, critical, alerts, and emergency be logged to files:

[P37095|Heading 3] logging merge
[P37096|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P37097|Normal] To enable the logging mergence, use the logging merge command in Global Configuration mode. To restore to default value, use the no form of this command.
[P37098|Heading 4] Command Syntax

R5	timeout SECONDS	Set timeout. The range is 1 to 300 seconds, default value is 10 seconds	1-300

[P37101|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P37102|Normal] Global Configuration
[P37103|Heading 4] Default
[P37104|Normal] Logging mergence is enabled.
[P37105|Heading 4] Usage
[P37106|Normal] The logging merge command merges all the same logs into one during a specified time range. During this time, the switch buffered these same logs. You can use the timeout keyword to set the time range, and use the fifo-size to set the buffer size.
[P37107|Heading 4] Examples
[P37108|Normal] The following shows how to enable logging merge function:
[P37109|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# logging merge enable

[P37111|Normal] logging merge timeout 30

[P37182|Normal] logging server address ( mgmt-if | vrf NAME | ) ( IPV4_ADDR | IPV6_ADDR ) ( dest-port PORT_NUM | ) ( transport ( tcp | udp ) | ) ( source-interface IFNAME | source-ip SRC_IP_ADDR | )

R5	IPV6_ADDR	IPv6 address of the server that will receive the system logging messages	IPv6 Address

[P37184|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P37185|Normal] Global Configuration
[P37186|Heading 4] Default
[P37187|Normal] System logging messages are not sent to any remote server.
[P37188|Body Text] Default transport type is UDP, default port is 514
[P37189|Heading 4] Usage
[P37190|Normal] The logging server address command identifies a remote server (usually a device serving as a syslog server) to receive logging messages. By issuing this command more than once, you can build a list of servers that receive logging messages.
[P37191|Body Text] If the source interface or source IP address is specified, the packet transmit will use the related IP address as source address.
[P37192|Heading 4] Examples
[P37193|Normal] In the following example, messages are logged to a server at 209.165.202.169:
[P37194|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# logging server address 209.165.202.169

[P37405|Normal] If the parameter for direction (both|tx|rx) is not specified, the default value is both.
[P37406|Body Text] Before configure the monitor session source vlan, User should create vlan by command “vlan database”, and create vlan interface by command “interface vlan” first.
[P37407|Heading 4] Examples
[P37408|Normal] This example shows how to create vlan and vlan interface:
[P37409|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# vlan database
Switch(config-vlan)# vlan 2
Switch(config-vlan)# exit
Switch(config)#interface vlan2
Switch(config-if)#exit
[P37410|Normal] This example shows how to set the mirror source to vlan2 in session 1:
[P37411|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# monitor session 1 source vlan 2 both
[P37412|Normal] This example shows how to set the mirror source to vlan2 in session 1 to monitor received traffic only:
[P37413|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# monitor session 1 source vlan 2 rx
[P37414|Normal] This example shows how to set the mirror source to vlan2 in session 1 to monitor transmitted traffic only:
[P37415|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# monitor session 1 source vlan 2 tx
[P37416|Normal] This example shows how to remove this setting:
[P37417|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)#no monitor session 1 source vlan 2 both
[P37418|Normal] This example shows how to delete vlan and vlan interface:
[P37419|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)#no interface vlan2
Switch(config)# vlan database
Switch(config-vlan)# no vlan 2
Switch(config-vlan)# exit

R5	rx	monitor received traffic only on that interface	-
R6	tx	monitor transmitted traffic only on that interface	-

[P37433|Heading 4] Command Mode

[P37445|Normal] This example shows how to set the mirror source to cpu in session 1 to monitor transmitted traffic only:

[P37459|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P37460|Normal] Global Configuration
[P37461|Heading 4] Default
[P37462|Normal] None
[P37463|Heading 4] Usage
[P37464|Normal] The destination tunnel and its mode should be created before configuring ERSPAN monitor destination.
[P37465|Body Text] The ERSPAN destination interface can only be a tunnel interface.
[P37466|Body Text] About tunnel configuration, please refer to ”IPv6_Service_CLI_en.doc”
[P37467|Heading 4] Examples
[P37468|Normal] This example shows how to create the tunnel::

[P37470|Normal] This example shows how to set the ERSPAN mirror destination to tunnel1 in session 1::
[P37471|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# monitor session 1 destination interface tunnel1
[P37472|Normal] This example shows how to remove this setting::
[P37473|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# no monitor session 1 destination
[P37474|Normal] This example shows how to delete the tunnel::
[P37475|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch (config)# no interface tunnel1
Switch (config-vlan)# exit

[P37488|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P37489|Normal] Global Configuration
[P37490|Heading 4] Default
[P37491|Normal] None
[P37492|Heading 4] Usage
[P37493|Normal] The destination vlan should be created in vlan database.
[P37494|Body Text] The destination interface can be either physical port or Aggregator interface.
[P37495|Body Text] To prevent another copy of packets flood out from the destination outgoing port, user can remove the port from default vlan by command “switchport trunk allowed vlan remove 1”.
[P37496|Heading 4] Examples

[P37498|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal

[P37500|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal

[P37501|Normal] This example shows how to remove this setting:
[P37502|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# no monitor session 1 destination remote vlan
[P37503|Normal] This example shows how to delete the vlan:
[P37504|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# vlan database
Switch(config-vlan)# no vlan 2
Switch(config-vlan)# exit

[P37510|Heading 3] monitor mac escape
[P37511|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P37512|Normal] Use this command to set remote mirror Mac escape feature. When these escape entries are set, the packets with specified MAC-DA will not be mirrored to the remote destination vlan when using Rspan(unsupport ERSPAN) .
[P37513|Body Text] To remove this setting, use the no form of this command.
[P37514|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P37515|Normal] monitor mac escape MAC MASK
[P37516|Body Text] no monitor mac escape ( MAC MASK | )

[TABLE 1523] rows=3 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	MAC	mac address	mac address in HHHH. HHHH. HHHH format
R3	MASK	mac address mask	mac address mask in HHHH. HHHH. HHHH format

[P37517|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P37518|Normal] Global Configuration
[P37519|Heading 4] Default
[P37520|Normal] None
[P37521|Heading 4] Usage
[P37522|Normal] Mac escape is used for remote mirror. It will not affect the result of local mirror.
[P37523|Body Text] If a Mac escape entry is set, the packet with this Mac destination can not be mirrored in remote mirror.
[P37524|Body Text] Command “no monitor mac escape ” should delete the specified entry.
[P37525|Body Text] Command “no monitor mac escape” should delete all entries.
[P37526|Heading 4] Examples
[P37527|Normal] This example shows how to set the mirror mac escape:
[P37528|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# monitor mac escape 00cc.1122.3344 ffff.ffff.0000
[P37529|Normal] This example shows how to remove this setting:
[P37530|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# no monitor mac escape 00cc.1122.3344 ffff.ffff.0000

[P38041|Heading 1] Network Management Commands
[P38042|Heading 2] Network Diagnosis Commands
[P38043|Heading 3] ping
[P38044|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P38045|Normal] The switch supports IP ping, which you can use to test connectivity to remote hosts. Ping sends an echo request packet to an address and waits for a reply. Ping returns one of these responses:
[P38046|Body Text] Normal response- The normal response (hostname is alive) occurs in 1 to 10 seconds, depending on network traffic.
[P38047|Body Text] Destination does not respond- If the host does not respond, a no-answer message is returned.
[P38048|Body Text] Unknown host- If the host does not exist, an unknown host message is returned.
[P38049|Body Text] Destination unreachable- If the default gateway cannot reach the specified network, a destination-unreachable message is returned.
[P38050|Body Text] Network or host unreachable- If there is no entry in the route table for the host or network, a network or host unreachable message is return.
[P38051|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P38052|Normal] ping ( ip | mgmt-if ) WORD
[P38053|Body Text] ping ( vrf WORD | ) [ -a WORD | -si IFNAME | -m INTERVAL | -c COUNT | -s DATASIZE | -f | -tos TOS | -h TTL | -t TIMEOUT ] WORD
[P38054|Body Text] ping ( mgmt-if | vrf WORD | ) ipv6 [ -a WORD | -m INTERVAL | -c COUNT | -s DATASIZE | -tc TC | -h HL | -t TIMEOUT ] WORD ( interface IFNAME | )

[TABLE 1544] rows=19 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	-a WORD	Select source IP address, the default is the IP address of the output interface	-
R3	-si IFNAME	Set the specified interface as the source interface of ping packet	Support physical/aggregation/loopback/tunnel/vlan ports
R4	ip	Public network IPv4 echo	-
R5	vrf WORD	VPN Routing/Forwarding instance	Up to 31 characters
R6	mgmt-if	Management interface	-
R7	WORD	Ping destination IPv4 or IPv6 address or hostname	-
R8	ipv6	Public network IPv6 echo	-
R9	interface	Outgoing interface for LinkLocal address/host	-
R10	IFNAME	Interface’s name	Support physical/aggregation/loopback/tunnel/vlan ports
R11	-m INTERVAL	specify interval for sending ping packets	10-10000 millisecond
R12	-c COUNT	specify the number of ping packets	1-4294967295
R13	-s DATASIZE	specify the data size of ping packet	20-9600 bytes
R14	-f	specify the Don’t Fragment flag in packet	-
R15	-tos TOS	Specify the packet tos value	0-255
R16	-h TTL	specify the TTL value in ping packet	1-255
R17	-tc TC	specify the Traffic Class value in ipv6 ping packet	0-255
R18	-h HL	specify the Hop Limit value in ipv6 ping packet	1-255
R19	-t TIMEOUT	specify the timeout value to wait for replay packet	0-100 second,0 stands for continuous waiting

[P38064|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P38065|Normal] traceroute
[P38066|Heading 3] traceroute
[P38067|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P38068|Normal] You can use IP traceroute to identify the path that packets take through the network on a hop-by-hop basis. The command output displays all network layer (Layer 3) devices, such as routers, that the traffic passes through on the way to the destination.
[P38069|Body Text] Your switches can participate as the source or destination of the traceroute privileged EXEC command and might or might not appear as a hop in the traceroute command output. If the switch is the destination of the traceroute, it is displayed as the final destination in the traceroute output. Intermediate switches do not show up in the traceroute output if they are only bridging the packet from one port to another within the same VLAN. However, if the intermediate switch is a multilayer switch that is routing a particular packet, this switch shows up as a hop in the traceroute output.
[P38070|Body Text] The traceroute privileged EXEC command uses the Time To Live (TTL) field in the IP header to cause routers and servers to generate specific return messages. Traceroute starts by sending a User Datagram Protocol (UDP) datagram to the destination host with the TTL field set to 1. If a router finds a TTL value of 1 or 0, it drops the datagram and sends back an Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP) time-to-live-exceeded message to the sender. Traceroute determines the address of the first hop by examining the source address field of the ICMP time-to-live-exceeded message.
[P38071|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P38072|Normal] traceroute ( ip | vrf WORD | mgmt-if | ) WORD
[P38073|Body Text] traceroute ( vrf WORD | ) ipv6 WORD

[TABLE 1545] rows=8 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	-a	Select source IP address, the default is the IP address of the output interface	-
R3	-si	Set the specified interface as the source interface of traceroute packet	-
R4	ip	Public network IPv4 echo	-
R5	ipv6	Public network IPv6 echo	-
R6	vrf WORD	VPN Routing/Forwarding instance	-
R7	mgmt-if	Management interface	-
R8	WORD	Destination IP address or hostname	-

[P38134|Heading 2] NTP Commands
[P38135|Heading 3] ntp ace
[P38136|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P38137|Normal] To create the Access Control Entries (ACE) of a NTP server/peer, use the ntp ace command in global configuration mode. To remove the ace, use the no form of this command.
[P38138|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P38139|Normal] ntp ace ( IP_ADDR | HOSTNAME ) ( mask MASK_LENGTH | ) ( version | kod | ignore | noquery | nomodify | notrap | noserve | nopeer | notrust | limited | none )
[P38140|Body Text] no ntp ace ( IP_ADDR | HOSTNAME ) ( mask MASK | ) ( version | kod | ignore | noquery | nomodify | notrap | noserve | nopeer | notrust | limited | none )

[TABLE 1549] rows=16 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	IP_ADDR	IP address of the time server or peer	IPv4 Address， exclude 127.0.0.1 & 0.0.0.0
R3	HOSTNAME	Name of the time server or peer	Up to 256 characters
R4	MASK_LENGTH	Specify network mask length of the address	1-32
R5	MASK	Specify network mask of the address	In IPv4 Address format
R6	version	Ignore these hosts if not the current NTP version	-
R7	kod	If access is denied, send a kiss-of-death packet	-
R8	ignore	Ignore all packets from host that match this entry	-
R9	noquery	Ignore all NTP mode 6 and 7 packets from the source, time service is not affected	-
R10	nomodify	Ignore all NTP mode 6 and 7 packets which attempt to modify the state of the server	-
R11	notrap	Decline to provide mode 6 control message trap service to matching hosts	-
R12	noserve	Ignore NTP packets whose mode is other than 6 or 7	-
R13	nopeer	Provide stateless time service to polling hosts, but do not allocate peer memory resources	-
R14	notrust	Treat these hosts normally in other respects, but never use them as synchronization sources	-
R15	limited	These hosts are subject to limitation of number of clients from the same net	-
R16	none	No limit	-

[P38141|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P38142|Normal] Global Configuration
[P38143|Heading 4] Default
[P38144|Normal] None
[P38145|Heading 4] Usage
[P38146|Normal] Use this command if you want to allow the system to synchronize with the specified server. The server will not synchronize to this machine.
[P38147|Heading 4] Examples
[P38148|Normal] The following example shows how to create an ACE for 1.1.1.1:
[P38149|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ntp ace 1.1.1.1 version
[P38150|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P38151|Normal] show ntp
[P38152|Heading 3] ntp authentication
[P38153|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P38154|Normal] To enable NTP authentication, use the ntp authentication enable command. To disable the NTP authentication, use the ntp authentication disable command.
[P38155|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P38156|Normal] ntp authentication ( enable | disable )

[TABLE 1550] rows=3 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	enable	Enable NTP authentication	-
R3	disable	Disable NTP authentication	-

[P38157|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P38158|Normal] Global Configuration
[P38159|Heading 4] Default
[P38160|Normal] None
[P38161|Heading 4] Usage
[P38162|Normal] When NTP authentication is enabled, the switch will synchronize the time with NTP servers with trusted key only. For more information about trusted key, please see the ntp trustedkey command.
[P38163|Heading 4] Examples
[P38164|Normal] The following example shows how to enables NTP authentication:
[P38165|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ntp authentication enable
[P38166|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P38167|Normal] show ntp
[P38168|Heading 3] ntp disable
[P38169|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P38170|Normal] To configure Disable NTP packets from being received on the interface, use the ntp disable command in interface configuration mode. To disable this capability, use the no form of this command.
[P38171|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P38172|Normal] ntp disable
[P38173|Body Text] no ntp disable
[P38174|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P38175|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P38176|Heading 4] Default
[P38177|Normal] By default, all interfaces receive NTP packets.
[P38178|Heading 4] Usage
[P38179|Normal] Only physical interface, vlan interface and loopback interface support this command.
[P38180|Heading 4] Examples
[P38181|Normal] In the following example, the system is configured not to receive NTP packet in interface eth-0-1:
[P38182|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# ntp disable

[P38218|Heading 3] ntp max-distance
[P38219|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P38220|Normal] Use ntp max-distance command to config ntp max sync distance threshold. This command used in ntp client, and ntp calculate the sync distance to each ntp server and compare it with the ntp max sync distance which configured by ntp max-distance command. If the distance calculate by ntp over the distance configured by ntp max-distance, client will not sync with this ntp server.
[P38221|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P38222|Normal] ntp max-distance DISTANCE
[P38223|Body Text] no ntp max-distance DISTANCE

[TABLE 1552] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	DISTANCE	Specify the ntp max sync distance threshold in seconds, default 10s.	1-16

Enter configuration commands, one per line.  End with CNTL/Z.

[P38233|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P38234|Normal] None
[P38235|Heading 3] ntp peer
[P38236|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P38237|Normal] To configure the software clock to synchronize a peer or to be synchronized by a peer, use the ntp peer command in global configuration mode. To disable this capability, use the no form of this command.
[P38238|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P38239|Normal] ntp peer( HOSTNAME | IP_ADDR ) { key KEY_ID | prefer | version VER } { source-interface IFNAME | source-ip SRC_ADDR }
[P38240|Body Text] no ntp peer( HOSTNAME | IP_ADDR )

[TABLE 1553] rows=8 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	HOSTNAME	Name of the time server or peer	Up to 256 characters
R3	IP_ADDR	IP address of the time server or peer	IPv4 Address
R4	KEY_ID	Authentication key to use when sending packets to this peer	1-64000
R5	prefer	Makes this peer the preferred peer that provides synchronization	-
R6	VER	Defines the Network Time Protocol (NTP) version number	1-3
R7	IFNAME	Name of source interface	Support physical/aggregation/loopback/tunnel/vlan ports
R8	SRC_ADDR	Source IP address	IPv4 Address

[P38241|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P38242|Normal] Global Configuration
[P38243|Heading 4] Default
[P38244|Normal] None
[P38245|Heading 4] Usage
[P38246|Normal] When a peer is configured, the default NTP version number is 3, no authentication key is used, and the source IP address is taken from the outgoing interface.
[P38247|Body Text] Use this command to allow a device to synchronize with a peer, or vice versa. Using the prefer keyword reduces switching between peers.
[P38248|Body Text] If the source interface or source IP address is specified, the packet transmit will use the related IP address as source address.
[P38249|Heading 4] Examples
[P38250|Normal] The following example shows how to configure a switch to allow its software clock to be synchronized with the clock of the peer (or vice versa) at IP address 192.168.22.33 using NTP version 2.:
[P38251|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ntp peer 192.168.22.33 version 2
[P38252|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P38253|Normal] show ntp

[P38277|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P38278|Normal] Global Configuration
[P38279|Heading 4] Default
[P38280|Normal] The server will not synchronize to this machine.
[P38281|Heading 4] Usage
[P38282|Normal] Use this command if you want to allow the system to synchronize with the specified server.
[P38283|Body Text] If the source interface or source IP address is specified, the packet transmit will use the related IP address as source address.
[P38284|Heading 4] Examples
[P38285|Normal] The following example shows how to configure a switch to allow its software clock to be synchronized with the clock by the device at IP address 172.16.22.44 using NTP version 2:
[P38286|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ntp server 172.16.22.44 version 2
[P38287|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P38288|Normal] show ntp
[P38289|Heading 3] ntp trustedkey
[P38290|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P38291|Normal] To authenticate the identity of a system to which Network Time Protocol (NTP) will synchronize, use the ntp trustedkey command in global configuration mode. To disable authentication of the identity of the system, use the no form of this command.
[P38292|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P38293|Normal] ntp trustedkey KEY_ID
[P38294|Body Text] no ntp trustedkey KEY_ID

[TABLE 1556] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	KEY_ID	Authentication key to use when sending packets to this peer	1-64000

[P38295|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P38296|Normal] Global Configuration
[P38297|Heading 4] Default
[P38298|Normal] None
[P38299|Heading 4] Usage
[P38300|Normal] If authentication is enabled, use this command to define one or more key numbers (corresponding to the keys defined with the ntp key command) that a peer NTP system must provide in its NTP packets, in order for this system to synchronize to it. This function provides protection against accidentally synchronizing the system to a system that is not trusted, because the other system must know the correct authentication key.
[P38301|Heading 4] Examples
[P38302|Normal] The following example shows how to configure the system to synchronize only to systems providing authentication key 42 in its NTP packets:

[P38420|Heading 3] ntp mgmt-if
[P38421|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P38422|Normal] To enable NTP management interface, use the ntp mgmt-if command. To enable management interface only, use the only parameter. To enable both in-band and management interface, use the enable parameter. To disable NTP management interface, use the no ntp mgmt-if command.
[P38423|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P38424|Normal] ntp mgmt-if ( enable | only )
[P38425|Body Text] no ntp mgmt-if

[TABLE 1557] rows=3 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	only	Only use management interface	-
R3	enable	Both use management interface and in-band interface	-

[P38426|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P38427|Normal] Global Configuration
[P38428|Heading 4] Default
[P38429|Normal] Disable management interface by default and only use in-band interface
[P38430|Heading 4] Usage
[P38431|Normal] Use this command to enable management interface, then the ntp client will connect to the server or peer.
[P38432|Heading 4] Examples
[P38433|Normal] The following example shows only use management interface:
[P38434|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ntp mgmt-if only

[P38732|Normal] Use this command to configure a physical interface as phy level loopback mode. Use the no loopback command to cancel this configuration.
[P38733|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P38734|Normal] loopback phy ( internal IFPHYSICAL | external )

[TABLE 1569] rows=3 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	internal IFPHYSICAL	Packets transmitted to the interface should be looped back to a specified physical interface without any modification. The destination physical interface	-
R3	external	Packets received from the interface should be looped back to the interface itself without any modification	-

[P38735|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P38736|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P38737|Heading 4] Default
[P38738|Normal] None
[P38739|Heading 4] Usage
[P38740|Normal] Only one type of loopback can be applied on a physical interface. A new configuration should replace the old configuration.
[P38741|Heading 4] Examples
[P38742|Normal] In the following example, the physical interface is set to phy level loopback mode:
[P38743|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# loopback phy internal eth-0-2
[P38744|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P38745|Normal] no loopback

[TABLE 1570] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	mac-address swap	If this flied is entered, the packet’s SMAC incoming from port level loopback interface will be swapped with its DMAC, and the FCS will be updated	-

[P38751|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P38752|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P38753|Heading 4] Default
[P38754|Normal] None
[P38755|Heading 4] Usage
[P38756|Normal] Only one type of loopback can be applied on a physical interface. A new configuration should replace the old configuration.
[P38757|Heading 4] Examples

Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1

[P38768|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P38769|Heading 4] Default

[P38796|Heading 3] l2 ping
[P38797|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P38798|Normal] Use this command to ping specified DMAC from specified physical interface, using protocol packet with ethertype 0x9009.
[P38799|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P38800|Normal] l2 ping HHHH.HHHH.HHHH interface IFPHYSICAL ( { vlan VLAN_ID | interval INTERVAL | timeout TIMEOUT | count COUNT | size SIZE } | )

[TABLE 1571] rows=8 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	HHHH.HHHH.HHHH	The DMAC to ping	MAC Address in HHHH.HHHH.HHHH format
R3	interface IFPHYSICAL	The interface to ping from	Support physical ports
R4	VLAN_ID	The vlan id of the protocol ping packet	1-4094
R5	INTERVAL	The interval time between two ping action, second	1-65535
R6	TIMEOUT	The time wait for a ping action, second	1-65535
R7	COUNT	Total ping times	1-65535
R8	SIZE	The size of the protocol ping packet	64-1518

[P38801|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P38802|Normal] Privileged EXEC
[P38803|Heading 4] Default
[P38804|Normal] The ping protocol packet is without vlan tag by default.
[P38805|Body Text] The default interval ping time is 200 milliseconds.
[P38806|Body Text] The default count is 5.
[P38807|Body Text] The default size of the ping protocol packet is 64.
[P38808|Heading 4] Usage
[P38809|Normal] The ping action can be canceled by “Ctrl + C”.
[P38810|Heading 4] Examples
[P38811|Normal] The following example shows how to ping a specified destination mac.:
[P38812|Terminal Display] Switch# l2 ping 0000.0000.0001 interface eth-0-1 vlan 101 interval 200 timeout 1000 count 10 size 1500

[P38984|Heading 3] rmon alarm
[P38985|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P38986|Normal] Use this command to set an alarm on a MIB object.
[P38987|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P38988|Normal] rmon alarm INDEX OID interval INTERVAL ( delta | absolute ) rising-threshold RTHRE ( event numbs | ) falling-threshold FTHRE ( event NUMBER | ) ( owner OWNER | )
[P38989|Body Text] no rmon alarm Index

[TABLE 1576] rows=11 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	INDEX	Alarm index.	1-65535
R3	OID	Variable for setting alarm(etherStatsEntry.m.n)	MIB OID
R4	INTERVAL	Specify the time in seconds the alarm monitors the MIB object(seconds).	1-65535
R5	delta	Specify the delta keyword to test the change between samples of a MIB variable	-
R6	absolute	Specify the absolute keyword to test each MIB variable directly	-
R7	rising-threshold RTHRE	Alarm rising threshold.	-2147483648 - 2147483646
R8	event numbs	Specify the event number to trigger when the falling threshold	1-65535
R9	falling-threshold FTHRE	Alarm falling threshold.	-2147483648-2147483646
R10	event NUMBER	Specify the event number to trigger when the falling threshold	1-65535
R11	owner OWNER	exceeds its limit.	Up to 15 characters

[P38990|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P38991|Normal] Global Configuration
[P38992|Heading 4] Default
[P38993|Normal] None
[P38994|Heading 4] Usage
[P38995|Normal] We need to create events for rising threshold and falling threshold first before we create an alarm for a mib.
[P38996|Body Text] Also the statistics need to be created on an interface, because we only support to set alarm monitor on etherStatsEntry.
[P38997|Heading 4] Examples
[P38998|Normal] This example shows how to set an alarm:
[P38999|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# rmon alarm 1 etherStatsEntry.3.1 interval 10 delta rising-threshold 1000 event 1 falling-threshold 5 event 1 owner test

R5	auth	Specifies authentication of a packet without encrypting it	-
R6	noauth	Specifies no authentication of a packet	-
R7	priv	Specifies authentication of a packet with encryption	-
R8	context CONTEXT	(Optional) Specifies the SNMP context to associate with this SNMP group and its views.	Up to 31 characters
R9	prefix	The context only match the prefix	-
R10	exact	The context should match the whole part	-
R11	READ	Optional) Specifies a read view for the SNMP group. This view enables you to view only the contents of the agent	Up to 31 characters
R12	WRITE	(Optional) Specifies a write view for the SNMP group. This view enables you to enter data and configure the contents of the agent.	Up to 31 characters
R13	NOTIFY	(Optional) Specifies a notify view for the SNMP group. This view enables you to specify a notify, inform, or trap	Up to 31 characters

[P39117|Heading 3] snmp-server community
[P39118|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P39119|Normal] To set up the community access string to permit access to the Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP), use the snmp-server community command in global configuration mode. To remove the specified community string, use the no form of this command.
[P39120|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P39121|Normal] snmp-server community ( 8 | ) STRING ( read-only | read-write ) ( view NAME | )
[P39122|Body Text] no snmp-server community string

[TABLE 1582] rows=6 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	STRING	Community string that consists of 1 to 127 alphanumeric characters and functions much like a password, permitting access to SNMP. Blank spaces are not permitted in the community string ,support digit char and special char as ~!@#$%^&*()_+`-= ,./;[]<:{}	A string with 1-127 characters
R3	read-only	Specifies read-only access. Authorized management stations can retrieve only MIB objects	-
R4	read-write	Specifies read-write access. Authorized management stations can both retrieve and modify MIB objects	-
R5	view NAME	Specifies a previously defined view. The view defines the objects available to the SNMP community	Up to 31 characters
R6	8	Specifies a HIDDEN community will follow	-

[P39123|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P39124|Normal] Global Configuration
[P39125|Heading 4] Default

[P39131|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal

[P39290|Heading 4] Command Purpose

[P39295|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P39296|Normal] Global Configuration
[P39297|Heading 4] Default
[P39298|Normal] No notifications controlled by this command are sent
[P39299|Heading 4] Usage
[P39300|Normal] The snmp-server trap enable command is used in conjunction with the snmp-server trap target-address command. Use the snmp-server trap target-address command to specify which host or hosts receive SNMP notifications. To send notifications, you must configure at least one snmp-server trap target-address command.

[P39410|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P39411|Normal] To create or update a view entry, use the snmp-server view command in global configuration mode. To remove the specified Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) server view entry, use the no form of this command.
[P39412|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P39413|Normal] snmp-server view NAME ( included | excluded ) sub-tree
[P39414|Body Text] no snmp-server view NAME ( included | excluded ) sub-tree

[TABLE 1598] rows=5 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	NAME	Label for the view record that you are updating or creating. The name is used to reference the record	Up to 31 characters
R3	included	Configures the OID (and subtree OIDs) specified in sub-tree argument to be included in the SNMP view	-
R4	excluded	Configures the OID (and subtree OIDs) specified in sub-tree argument to be explicitly excluded from the SNMP view	-
R5	sub-tree	Object identifier of the ASN.1 subtree to be included or excluded from the view	-

[P39415|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P39416|Normal] Global Configuration
[P39417|Heading 4] Default
[P39418|Normal] No view entry exists
[P39419|Heading 4] Usage
[P39420|Normal] Other SNMP commands require an SMP view as an argument. You use this command to create a view to be used as arguments for other commands.
