[P39422|Normal] The following is sample output from the snmp-server view command:
[P39423|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# snmp-server view abc excluded 1.3.6.2

[P39736|Heading 3] sflow counter-sampling enable
[P39737|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P39738|Normal] Use this command to enable or disable counter sampling on specified port.
[P39739|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P39740|Normal] sflow counter-sampling enable
[P39741|Body Text] no sflow counter-sampling enable
[P39742|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P39743|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P39744|Heading 4] Default
[P39745|Normal] Disabled
[P39746|Heading 4] Usage
[P39747|Normal] Use this command to enable counter sampling on specified port. Use the no parameter with this command to disable counter sampling. By default, sFlow counter sampling is disabled in all ports.
[P39748|Body Text] This command can only be configured on a port which is not a link-agg group member. The port can be either a physical port or a link-agg port.
[P39749|Heading 4] Examples
[P39750|Normal] This example shows how to enable sFlow counter sampling on interface eth-0-1:
[P39751|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# sflow counter-sampling enable
[P39752|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P39753|Normal] show sflow
[P39754|Heading 3] sflow flow-sampling rate
[P39755|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P39756|Normal] Use this command to configure flow sampling rate.
[P39757|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P39758|Normal] sflow flow-sampling rate RATE
[P39759|Body Text] no sflow flow-sampling rate

[TABLE 1610] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	RATE	Sample rate value	must be a power of 2, the range is 32-1048576

[P39760|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P39761|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P39762|Heading 4] Default
[P39763|Normal] 8192
[P39764|Heading 4] Usage
[P39765|Normal] Use this command to set sFlow packet sampling rate. Use no parameter with this command to set default sampling rate. Default sampling rate value is 8192.
[P39766|Body Text] sFlow uses CPU resources to collect samples and send samples to the collector. If a low sampling rate is set, CPU utilization can become high. To protect CPU from overwhelming, exceeded flow samples would be dropped. If a sampling rate less than default value is configured, a prompt will be given to info the potential of involving a high CPU utilization.
[P39767|Body Text] This command can only be configured on a port which is not a link-agg group member. The port can be either a physical port or a link-agg port.
[P39768|Heading 4] Examples
[P39769|Normal] This example shows how to set the sFlow sampling rate to 2048 on eth-0-1:
[P39770|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# sflow flow-sampling rate 2048
% Warning: sFlow sampling requires high CPU usage, especially with a low rate.
  It is suggested not configure a rate less than default value 8192.
[P39771|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P39772|Normal] show sflow
[P39773|Heading 3] sflow flow-sampling enable
[P39774|Heading 4] Command Purpose

[P39776|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P39777|Normal] sflow flow-sampling enable ( input | output | both )
[P39778|Body Text] no sflow flow-sampling enable ( input | output | both )
[P39779|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P39780|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P39781|Heading 4] Default
[P39782|Normal] Disabled
[P39783|Heading 4] Usage
[P39784|Normal] Use this command to enable ingress direction of packet sampling on individual port. Use the no parameter with this command to disable packet sampling. By default, sFlow packet sampling is disabled in all ports.
[P39785|Body Text] This command can only be configured on a port which is not a link-agg group member. The port can be either a physical port or a link-agg port.
[P39786|Heading 4] Examples
[P39787|Normal] This example shows how to enable input packet sampling on route port eth-0-1:
[P39788|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1
Switch(config-if)# sflow flow-sampling enable input
[P39789|Heading 4] Related Commands

[P40190|Heading 3] ipfix recorder
[P40191|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P40192|Normal] Use this command to create a ipfix recorder and enter recorder configure mode. To remove the ipfix recorder, use the no form of this command.
[P40193|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P40194|Normal] ipfix recorder NAME
[P40195|Body Text] no ipfix recorder NAME

[TABLE 1631] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	NAME	ipfix recorder name	Up to 32 characters

[P40196|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P40197|Normal] Global Configuration
[P40198|Heading 4] Default
[P40199|Normal] None
[P40200|Heading 4] Usage
[P40201|Normal] If ipfix recorder has existed，it will enter IPFIX recorder Configuration；if ipfix recorder is new，it will create a recorder and enter IPFIX recorder Configuration；this command should work with the commands of match and collect.
[P40202|Heading 4] Examples
[P40203|Normal] This example shows how to create ipfix recorder recorder1in global configuration and enter IPFIX recorder Configuration:
[P40204|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# ipfix recorder recorder1
Switch(Config-ipfix-reocrder)# 
Delete ipfix recorder recorder1:
Switch(config)# no ipfix recorder recorder1 

Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# no ipfix recorder recorder1

[P41009|Heading 2] Hardware Monitor Commands
[P41010|Heading 3] hardware monitor watermark
[P41011|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P41012|Normal] Use this command to change the recording period of the watermark function. Use the no form of the command to restore the recording period to the default value (30).
[P41013|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P41014|Normal] hardware monitor watermark interval <1-60>
[P41015|Body Text] no hardware monitor watermark interval

[TABLE 1672] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	<1-60>	The recording period of watermark functin. Unit: minute(s)	1-60

[P41016|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P41017|Normal] Global Configuration
[P41018|Heading 4] Default
[P41019|Normal] The default value of recording period is 30 minutes.
[P41020|Heading 4] Usage
[P41021|Normal] Watermark function is used to record the biggest buffer usage and biggest time delay of a certain port within a period; this record is periodically.
[P41022|Heading 4] Examples
[P41023|Normal] The following example shows how to set the recording period of the watermark function to 2 minutes:
[P41024|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Enter configuration commands, one per line.  End with CNTL/Z.
Switch(config)# hardware monitor watermark interval 2
[P41025|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P41026|Normal] show hardware monitor watermark interface IFPHYSICAL
[P41027|Heading 3] show hardware monitor watermark interface
[P41028|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P41029|Normal] Use this command to display the maximum buffer cell usage and maximum delay of a port counted by the watermark function in a recording period. Use the clear form of the command to clear statistics on a port.
[P41030|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P41031|Normal] show hardware monitor watermark interface IFPHYSICAL
[P41032|Body Text] clear hardware monitor watermark interface IFPHYSICAL

[TABLE 1673] rows=2 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	IFPHYSICAL	physical port number	depending on the specific version model

[P41035|Heading 4] Default
[P41036|Normal] None
[P41037|Heading 4] Usage
[P41038|Normal] None
[P41039|Heading 4] Examples

[P41041|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Enter configuration commands, one per line.  End with CNTL/Z.
Switch(config)# hardware monitor watermark interval 1
Switch(config)# end
Switch# show hardware monitor watermark interface eth-0-5

              Time        Latency  Buffer(total)
---------------------------------------------------------------------
   Jan 28 07:12:25       16040000          58373
   Jan 28 07:11:25       16032288          58373

[P41044|Heading 3] hardware monitor notify server
[P41045|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P41046|Normal] Use this command to configure the IP address and UDP port number of the notification server. Use the no form of the command to delete the configuration.
[P41047|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P41048|Normal] hardware monitor notify server A.B.C.D ( port <1-65535> | )
[P41049|Body Text] no hardware monitor notify server

R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value

R3	<1-65535>	UDP port number.	1-65535

[P41050|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P41051|Normal] Global Configuration
[P41052|Heading 4] Default
[P41053|Normal] The default port number is 20008.
[P41054|Heading 4] Usage
[P41055|Normal] After you run this command, the switch sends Buffer Stats Notify、Latency Stats Notify、Buffer Micro-burst Notify or Latency Event Notify packets the server periodically or immediately.
[P41056|Heading 4] Examples
[P41057|Normal] The following example show how to set the IP address of the notification server to 192.108.10.2 and UDP port number to 35000:
[P41058|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Enter configuration commands, one per line.  End with CNTL/Z.
Switch(config)# hardware monitor notify server 192.108.10.2 port 35000

[P41085|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P41086|Heading 4] Default
[P41087|Normal] N/A
[P41088|Heading 4] Usage
[P41089|Normal] After this function is enabled, the switch periodically sends a Buffer Status Notify message to the notification server. When a congestion event occurs, the switch immediately sends a Buffer Micro-Burst Notify message to the notification server.

[P41091|Normal] The following example shows how to enable Buffer Statistics Notification and congestion event notification for port eth-0-9:
[P41092|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Enter configuration commands, one per line.  End with CNTL/Z.
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-9
Switch(config-if)# hardware buffer-monitor notify

[P41241|Normal] N/A
[P41242|Heading 4] Usage
[P41243|Normal] N/A
[P41244|Heading 4] Examples
[P41245|Normal] The following example shows how to enable the delay monitoring function for port eth-0-9:
[P41246|Terminal Display] DUT1# configure terminal
Enter configuration commands, one per line.  End with CNTL/Z.
DUT1(config)# interface eth-0-9
DUT1(config-if)# hardware latency-monitor enable
[P41247|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P41248|Normal] None
[P41249|Heading 3] hardware latency-monitor threshold event
[P41250|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P41251|Normal] Use this command to set the threshold for reporting the triggering delay event on a port. Use the no form of this command to restore the threshold to the default value.
[P41252|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P41253|Normal] hardware latency-monitor threshold event low <64-2147483647> high <64-2147483647>
[P41254|Body Text] no hardware latency-monitor threshold event

[TABLE 1686] rows=3 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	<64-2147483647>	Low threshold for triggering delayed event reporting. Unit: ns	64-2147483647
R3	<64-2147483647>	High threshold for triggering delayed event reporting. Unit: ns	64-2147483647

[P41255|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P41256|Normal] Global Configuration
[P41257|Heading 4] Default
[P41258|Normal] The default value of low threshold: 768
[P41259|Body Text] The defaulr value of high threshold: 3072
[P41260|Heading 4] Usage
[P41261|Normal] The value of the high or low threshold must be an integer multiple of 64. If the dalay time of a packet is higher than the upper threshold, the switch reports a delay start event. If the delay event of the packet is higher than the high threshold and lower than the low threshold, the switch reports a delay end event. Before running this command, you need to enable the delay monitoring function of the port.
[P41262|Heading 4] Examples
[P41263|Normal] The following example shows how to set the global low threshold for reporting congestion events and the global high threshold to 64000ns:
[P41264|Terminal Display] DUT1# configure terminal
Enter configuration commands, one per line.  End with CNTL/Z.
DUT1(config)# hardware latency-monitor threshold event low 640 high 64000
[P41265|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P41266|Normal] None
[P41267|Heading 3] hardware latency-monitor range
[P41268|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P41269|Normal] Use this command to configure eight delay intervals. Use the no form of the command to restore the dalay interval to the default value.
[P41270|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P41271|Normal] hardware latency-monitor range <1-4261412864> <1-4261412864> <1-4261412864> <1-4261412864> <1-4261412864> <1-4261412864> <1-4261412864>
[P41272|Body Text] no hardware latency-monitor range

[TABLE 1687] rows=8 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	<1-4261412864>	the value of latency range 1	1-4261412864. Unit: ns. It must be integer multiple of 64.
R3	<1-4261412864>	the value of latency range 2	1-4261412864. Unit: ns. It must be integer multiple of 64 and greater than interval 1
R4	<1-4261412864>	the value of latency range 3	1-4261412864. Unit: ns. It must be integer multiple of 64 and greater than interval 2
R5	<1-4261412864>	the value of latency range 4	1-4261412864. Unit: ns. It must be integer multiple of 64 and greater than interval 3
R6	<1-4261412864>	the value of latency range 5	1-4261412864. Unit: ns. It must be integer multiple of 64 and greater than interval 4
R7	<1-4261412864>	the value of latency range 6	1-4261412864. Unit: ns. It must be integer multiple of 64 and greater than interval 5
R8	<1-4261412864>	the value of latency range 7	1-4261412864. Unit: ns. It must be integer multiple of 64 and greater than interval 6

[P41273|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P41274|Normal] Global Configuration
[P41275|Heading 4] Default
[P41276|Normal] the default value of latency range 1: 1-448
[P41277|Body Text] the default value of latency range 2: 448-768
[P41278|Body Text] the default value of latency range 3: 768-1152
[P41279|Body Text] the default value of latency range 4: 1152-1536
[P41280|Body Text] the default value of latency range 5: 1536-2048
[P41281|Body Text] the default value of latency range 6: 2048-3072
[P41282|Body Text] the default value of latency range 7: 3072-5120
[P41283|Body Text] the default value of latency range 8: 5120-infinity
[P41284|Heading 4] Usage
[P41285|Normal] None
[P41286|Heading 4] Examples
[P41287|Normal] The following example shows how to set the eight delay ranges to 1-640，640-3200，3200-6400，6400-12800，12800-25600，25600-128000，128000-256000，256000-infinity:
[P41288|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Enter configuration commands, one per line.  End with CNTL/Z.
Switch(config)# hardware latency-monitor range 640 3200 6400 12800 25600 128000 256000

[P41309|Heading 4] Command Purpose

[P41314|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P41315|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P41316|Heading 4] Default
[P41317|Normal] The default value of the discard threshold is 8. That is, packets whose forwarding delay reaches the eighth delay range are discard.
[P41318|Heading 4] Usage
[P41319|Normal] Before using this command, you need to enable the function of discarding packets with high forwarding delay on the port.

[P41322|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal

Switch(config-if)# hardware latency-monitor threshold drop 6

R3	PREFIX	IP route prefix for the destination	IPv4 address
R4	MASK	Prefix mask for the destination	Mask in IPv4 address format
R5	PREFIX-LENGTH	Prefix length for the destination	1-32
R6	NH-ADDRESS	IP address of the next hop that can be used to reach that network	IPv4 address
R7	IFNAME	Interface name of the next hop that can be used to reach that network	Only support tunnel and null interface
R8	REMOTE-VTEP	Overlay tunnel of the next hop that can be used to reach that network.	remote-vtep index
R9	DISTANCE	(Optional) An administrative distance. The default administrative distance for a static route is 1	1-255
R10	BFD-NAME	Specify the name of bfd	A string up to 16 characters

[P42175|Normal] This command is used to specify overlay vtep peer address and type on remote device, administrator must know all the peer addresses and types on the network and make sure that they can route between each other.
[P42176|Heading 4] Examples

Switch(config-overlay)# remote-vtep 20 ip-address 2.2.2.2 type vxlan src-ip 1.1.1.1

[P42179|Normal] The following example removes remote vtep:
[P42180|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# overlay
Switch(config-overlay)# no remote-vtep 20

[P42331|Normal] ip route ( vrf VRF_NAME | ) ( ADDRESS WILDCARD-MASK | ADDRESS/PREFIX-LENGTH ) remote-vtep INDEX vni VNI ( | inner-macda mac-addr ) ( description LINE | )
[P42332|Body Text] no ip route ( vrf VRF_NAME | ) ( ADDRESS WILDCARD-MASK | ADDRESS/PREFIX-LENGTH ) remote-vtep INDEX vni VNI ( | inner-macda mac-addr ) ( description | )

R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value

R5	PREFIX-LENGTH	Prefix length of the address	1-32
R6	INDEX	The index of remote vtep	1-65535

[P42333|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P42334|Normal] Global Configuration
[P42335|Heading 4] Default
[P42336|Normal] None
[P42337|Heading 4] Usage
[P42338|Normal] If the inner mac destination address is not specified, it will use the remote vtep’s virtual mac address as the inner mac destination address.
[P42339|Heading 4] Examples
[P42340|Normal] This example shows how to add an overlay route:
[P42341|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal

[P42342|Normal] This example shows how to delete an an overlay route:
[P42343|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# no ip route vrf tenant1 3.3.3.3/32 nvgre-peer 5.5.5.5 vni 50000 inner-macda a.a.a
Switch(config)# no ip route vrf tenant1 4.4.4.4/32 nvgre-peer 5.5.5.5 vni 50000

[P42466|Heading 4] Command Purpose

[P42469|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P42470|Normal] address-family l2vpn evpn
[P42471|Body Text] no address-family l2vpn evpn
[P42472|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P42473|Normal] Router Configuration
[P42474|Heading 4] Default
[P42475|Normal] None
[P42476|Heading 4] Usage
[P42477|Normal] Use the address family command to enter the address family mode allowing configuration of address-family specific parameters. To leave the address family mode and return to the Configure mode use the exit-address-family command.
[P42478|Body Text] EVPN feature should be enabled before enter this address family configure mode.
[P42479|Heading 4] Examples
[P42480|Normal] The following example shows how to EVPN address family configure mode:
[P42481|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# router bgp 1
Switch(config-router)# address-family l2vpn evpn
Switch(config-router-af)#

[P42613|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P42614|Normal] neighbor ( IP_ADDR | WORD ) ( both | extended | standard )
[P42615|Body Text] no neighbor ( IP_ADDR | WORD ) ( both | extended | standard )

[TABLE 1755] rows=6 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	IP_ADDR	Specifies the address of the BGP neighbor in IPv4 format	IPv4 Address
R3	WORD	Name of an existing peer-group	Up to 20 characters
R4	both	Sends Standard and Extended Community attributes	-
R5	extended	Sends Extended Community attributes	-
R6	standard	Sends Standard Community attributes	-

[P42616|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P42617|Normal] Address Family Configuration
[P42618|Heading 4] Default
[P42619|Normal] None
[P42620|Heading 4] Usage
[P42621|Normal] None
[P42622|Heading 4] Examples
[P42623|Normal] The following example shows how to set send-community attribute:
[P42624|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)#router bgp 100
Switch(config-router)#address-family l2vpn evpn
Switch(config-router-af)# neighbor 1.1.1.1 send-community extended
[P42625|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P42626|Normal] address-family l2vpn evpn
[P42627|Heading 3] neighbor route-reflector-client
[P42628|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P42629|Normal] Use this command to configure the router as a BGP route reflector and configure the specified neighbor as its client.
[P42630|Body Text] Use the no parameter with this command to indicate that the neighbor is not a client.
[P42631|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P42632|Normal] neighbor NEIGHBORID route-reflector-client
[P42633|Body Text] no neighbor NEIGHBORID route-reflector-clien

[TABLE 1756] rows=4 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	NEIGHBORID	(A.B.C.D\|TAG)	-
R3	IP_ADDR	Specifies the address of the BGP neighbor in IPv4 format.	IPv4 Address
R4	TAG	Name of an existing peer-group. For information on how to create peer groups, refer to the neighbor peer-group and neighbor remote-as commands. When this parameter is used with a command, the command applies on all peers in the specified group.	-

[P42634|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P42635|Normal] Address Family Configuration
[P42636|Heading 4] Default
[P42637|Normal] N/A
[P42638|Heading 4] Usage
[P42639|Normal] Route reflectors are a solution for the explosion of iBGP peering within an autonomous system. By route reflection the number of iBGP peers within an AS is reduced. Use the neighbor route-reflector-client command to configure the local router as the route reflector and specify neighbors as its client.
[P42640|Body Text] An AS can have more than one route reflector. One route reflector treats the other route reflector as another iBGP speaker.
[P42641|Heading 4] Examples
[P42642|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)#router bgp 100
Switch(config-router)#address-family l2vpn evpn
Switch(config-router-af)# neighbor 10.10.0.72 route-reflector-client
[P42643|Heading 4] Related Commands
[P42644|Normal] N/A

[P43049|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P43050|Normal] Interface Configuration
[P43051|Heading 4] Default
[P43052|Normal] Enable priority-based flowcontrol on priority 3
[P43053|Heading 4] Usage
[P43054|Normal] Use the priority-flow-control interface Configuration command to set the interface’s ability to send pause frames to on or off on the specialed priorities.
[P43055|Heading 4] Examples
[P43056|Normal] This example shows how to enable priority-based flowcontrol on the interface:
[P43057|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal

Switch(config-if)# priority-flow-control mode on
[P43058|Normal] This example shows how to enable priority-based flowcontrol on the interface(auto negotiating with the peer):
[P43059|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# interface eth-0-1 
Switch(config-if)# priority-flow-control mode auto

[P43368|Heading 3] efd notify enable
[P43369|Heading 4] Command Purpose
[P43370|Normal] Use this command to configure EFD notify function.Use the no form of this command to unconfigure EFD notify function.
[P43371|Heading 4] Command Syntax
[P43372|Normal] efd notify enable IP_ADDR ( PORT | )
[P43373|Body Text] no efd notify enable

[TABLE 1792] rows=3 cols=3
R1	Parameter	Parameter Description	Parameter Value
R2	IP_ADDR	IP address of the server	IPv4 Address
R3	PORT	UDP port used by server	1-65535

[P43374|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P43375|Normal] Global Configuration
[P43376|Heading 4] Default
[P43377|Normal] The feature is disabled.
[P43378|Body Text] The default UDP port is 20007 if not specifed.
[P43379|Heading 4] Usage
[P43380|Normal] After EFD notify enabled, the new elephant flow will be notified to server, the format of the data in the UDP packet is:
[P43381|Body Text] |—-rsv—- | ver| code|
[P43382|Body Text] |———length———–|
[P43383|Body Text] |—type—-|——len—-|
[P43384|Body Text] |———-value———–|
[P43385|Body Text] ……
[P43386|Heading 4] Examples
[P43387|Normal] This example shows how to configure EFD notify:
[P43388|Terminal Display] Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# efd notify enable 10.10.10.1

[P43412|Normal] Use this command to enable EFD black hole route, specify the gateway address and route tag.Use the no form of this command to disable EFD black hole route, unspecify the gateway address and route tag.

[P43415|Body Text] no efd black-hole-route

R3	TAG_VALUE	Tag of black hole route	0-4294967295

[P43416|Heading 4] Command Mode
[P43417|Normal] Global Configuration
[P43418|Heading 4] Default
[P43419|Normal] None
[P43420|Heading 4] Usage
[P43421|Normal] Enable EFD black hole route feature, a black hole route would be created for it when a flow
[P43422|Body Text] is detected as elephant flow, it’s next-hop would be pointed to the configured gateway address.
[P43423|Heading 4] Examples
[P43424|Normal] This example shows how to enable efd black hole route:
[P43425|Terminal Display] Switch# efd black-hole-route gw 1.2.3.4 tag 876
